framebuffer publishes a VRAM property. Nothing is constrained to 7 MB;
it is a reporting artifact of the display half of the driver not
existing yet. Also confirmed there: `Metal: Supported`, Type GPU, Bus
PCIe x16, AMD 0x1002:0x1681 rev 0a - the system recognises the 680M as a
Metal GPU.

**The tiling lead is REFUTED, statically, for free.** 2kw flagged that
`_gc_get_tiling_params` exists only as `_10_1` and called it the shape
of the 2jp defect. Disassembled, it is nine instructions:

```
126b0050  addq $0xc0, %rdi
126b0057  movl $0x13de, %esi          ; mmGB_ADDR_CONFIG
126b005e  callq _gc_reg_offset
126b0072  callq _gc_cgs_read_register_ext2
126b0077  movl %eax, (%rbx)           ; *out = the chip's own value
```

It reads `GB_ADDR_CONFIG` from the hardware and stores it. There is no
generation-specific arithmetic, so the `_10_1` suffix carries no meaning
here and Apple's swizzle equations are fed the chip's real
configuration. Not the cause. Withdrawn before it cost a boot.

**So there is no strong hypothesis for the glyph corruption yet**, and
the honest next step is a measurement rather than another guess. The
discriminator available is `tools/metal_check.sh --dispatch`, which runs
and **verifies** a compute kernel: correct results would put the shader
and memory paths out of scope and isolate the fault to image-surface
layout; wrong results would mean something deeper. It can hang the GPU,
which is why it is a separate flag and why it costs the live boot if it
goes badly.

Evidence to carry forward, from the user: Finder, Safari and Messages
render fully; Electron (Claude Code) does not, and "only non-moving
things render good". Safari being fine is important - it is a client
process doing its own GPU work, so "client process" is not the
discriminator, and 2kw's AppKit-versus-Electron framing is too coarse.

## 2ky (2026-10-20) — the compute kernel PASSES, so the fault is tiled surfaces only

Run live in boot 93, no reboot, and it did **not** hang:

```
dispatch: creating queue
dispatch: compiling shader
dispatch: encoding 4096 threads
dispatch: committing - IF THE GPU HANGS, IT HANGS HERE
dispatch: command buffer status = 4
PASS: all 4096 elements correct - the GPU executed the kernel
```

Status 4 is `MTLCommandBufferStatusCompleted`, and **every one of 4096
elements verified correct**. So shader cores execute, the command buffer
submits and completes, fences retire, and **linear buffer memory reads
back exactly right**.

**This also retires the 2hj frontier.** That milestone's defining
symptom was `waitUntilCompleted` never returning, with
`AMDAccelEventMachine` stuck in `resetHardwareAndReplay -> waitForTimestamp
-> pollWait`. The same dispatch now returns, verified. The restart loop
is gone with the faults.

**What it isolates.** The corruption cannot be in the shaders, the
submission path, the fence path, or plain memory - all four just passed
with a bit-exact result. It is confined to **tiled 2D surfaces**, which
matches the screen exactly: the Dock's icons and the menu-bar text are
perfect, body-text glyphs are scrambled, and large smooth regions look
right.

**The hypothesis this revives, from a different angle than 2kx killed.**
2kx refuted "Apple reads the wrong GB_ADDR_CONFIG" - `_gc_get_tiling_params_10_1`
reads it straight off the chip, so the KERNEL has the right value. But
this stack **spoofs Navi 21**, and the userspace Metal driver picks its
AddrLib geometry from the family it believes it is on. If AddrLib
swizzles for Navi 21's pipe/packer/shader-engine configuration while the
chip is configured per its own GB_ADDR_CONFIG, every tiled surface is
read with the wrong equation while linear buffers are untouched - which
is precisely the split measured above. Rembrandt has **one** shader
engine; Navi 21 has four.

2ky reads `GB_ADDR_CONFIG` (dword 0x13de, BASE_IDX 0) once per boot in
the ring probe, where GC reads are proven, and logs the fields decoded
(`NUM_PIPES`, `PIPE_INTERLEAVE_SIZE`, `MAX_COMPRESSED_FRAGS`,
`NUM_PKRS`, `NUM_SHADER_ENGINES`, `NUM_RB_PER_SE`, per
gc_10_3_0_sh_mask.h) rather than leaving a raw word for the arithmetic
to be done later and wrong. It appears as `gbac=` in `rbgpu-ring`.
Nothing is written.

This is a measurement, not a fix. It establishes whether a mismatch
exists; what to do about it - and whether the AddrLib geometry can be
influenced from the kernel at all - is the question after it.

Build `DCB99254-201F-3C25-BF39-34AB60309BCB`.

## 2kz (2026-10-20) — boot 94: the chip's tiling geometry, measured

`b=94`, UUID `DCB99254`, read live from the armed boot (which is still
up, still fault-free, ring to `w=0x93480`).

```
rbgpu-ring  = b=94 p=0 ... gbac=242
rbgpu-adj   = b=94 calls=13488 inmap=13488 fixed=13488 | map=13447 asg=13 mes=28
rbgpu-fault = b=94 hk=1 c=0 f=0 r=0 o=0 fw=0
```

**`GB_ADDR_CONFIG = 0x242`**, decoded against gc_10_3_0_sh_mask.h:

| field | bits | raw | meaning |
|---|---|---|---|
| NUM_PIPES | 2:0 | 2 | 4 pipes |
| PIPE_INTERLEAVE_SIZE | 5:3 | 0 | 256 B |
| MAX_COMPRESSED_FRAGS | 7:6 | 1 | 2 |
| NUM_PKRS | 10:8 | 2 | 4 packers |
| NUM_SHADER_ENGINES | 21:19 | 0 | **1** |
| NUM_RB_PER_SE | 27:26 | 0 | 1 |

Navi 21 has **four** shader engines, so that field alone differs - 0 here
against 2 there - and the pipe and packer counts differ as well. GFX10's
swizzle equations select which address bits to XOR directly from the pipe
and packer counts, so an AddrLib configured for Navi 21 reading a surface
laid out for this chip scrambles it in blocks and leaves linear buffers
untouched: precisely the split 2ky measured.

**But a mismatch is still not demonstrated**, and saying "Navi 21's
geometry is being used" without reading what AddrLib was actually handed
would be the recurring error again. `AMDHWAlignManager2::init`
(0xbe99342) builds `ADDR_CREATE_INPUT`:

```
be993fd  movl $0x70, (%r14)            ; size
be9940f  callq *0x140(%rax) -> +0x04   ; chipFamily
be99420  callq *0x1b8(%rax) -> +0x08   ; chipRevision
be99431  callq *0x1a8(%rax) -> +0x0c
be9943b..be99458                       ; AddrLibAllocSysMem / Free / DebugPrint
be993ed  callq *0x1c0(%rax) -> r15     ; the register-value source
be9945c  movl 0xa0(%r15) -> +0x30      ; regValue[0]
be99467  movl 0xa8(%r15) -> +0x34
be99472  movl 0xb0(%r15) -> +0x38
be9947d  movl 0xb8(%r15) -> +0x3c
```

**AddrLib runs in the KERNEL here** - `AMDHWAlignManager2` owns it, with
`AddrLibAllocSysMem`/`FreeSysMem`/`DebugPrint` as its callbacks and
`getPreferredSwizzleMode2`, `getDccInfo2`, `getCMaskInfo2` on top of
`_ADDR2_*` structs. So this is reachable from this plugin, if the value
turns out to be wrong.

2kz hooks that init, lets it run untouched, then calls **the same
getters by the same vtable offsets** and records what they returned. No
substitution, no inference about the plumbing (2cy). `rbgpu_vcall_2kz`
returns `ok=false` on any NULL along the way so an unreached getter is
`ffffffff` and can never be read as a measured zero (2eh).

| `rbgpu-addr` | means |
|---|---|
| one of `a0/a8/b0/b8` reads **242** | the kernel's AddrLib has the chip's real geometry; the mismatch is then userspace-side, in the Metal driver's own AddrLib, which this plugin does not reach the same way |
| none reads 242 | AddrLib is configured with something that is not this chip - the defect, and fixable here |
| `ffffffff` | that getter was never reached; not a value |
| `calls=0` | the align manager is initialised somewhere this hook does not see |

Observe only. Nothing written, the original's return passed through.

Build `F7112B3D-01C3-3D6E-B0D3-9881C716D687`.

## 2la (2026-10-20) — boot 95: the AddrLib geometry is CORRECT; 2kz's hypothesis is refuted

```
rbgpu-addr = b=95 hk=1 calls=1 read=1 ret=0 | fam=d rev=8f third=28
             | a0=242 a8=0 b0=0 b8=0
rbgpu-ring = b=95 ... gbac=242
rbgpu-fault= b=95 c=0 f=0 r=0 o=0 fw=0
```

`a0` is `regValue.gbAddrConfig` and it reads **242 - identical to the
chip's own register**. Mapped onto AddrLib's `ADDR_CREATE_INPUT`
(`size`, `chipEngine`, `chipFamily`, `chipRevision`, three callbacks,
flags, `regValue` at +0x30) the rest reads `chipEngine=0xd`,
`chipFamily=0x8f` - AddrLib's `FAMILY_NV`, correct for Navi 21 **and**
for this part - `chipRevision=0x28`, and the init returned `0` = ADDR_OK.

**So the kernel's AddrLib is configured with this chip's real geometry.**
Gfx10's AddrLib derives pipes, packers and shader-engine counts from
`gbAddrConfig`, not from the family, so "AddrLib swizzles for Navi 21" is
dead. Third hypothesis about this corruption, third refutation by
measurement - and each one was cheap because it was measured rather than
argued.

**It never fitted the photograph either, and that should have been said
sooner.** A wrong global swizzle scrambles everything tiled. The Dock's
icons, the wallpaper and the menu-bar text are pixel-correct while
body-text glyphs are shredded. The corruption is **selective**, which is
the shape of a per-surface decision, not a global parameter.

**2la records the decisions themselves.** Two observe-only hooks:

- `AMDHWAlignManager2::getPreferredSwizzleMode2` (0xbe9957e) is handed
  AddrLib's `ADDR2_COMPUTE_SURFACE_INFO_INPUT`, whose layout is fixed:
  `+0x04 flags`, `+0x08 swizzleMode`, `+0x0c resourceType`, `+0x10
  format`, `+0x14 bpp`, `+0x18 width`, `+0x1c height`, `+0x2c numFrags`.
  The first five surfaces are recorded with the mode the call returned.
- `AMDHWAlignManager2::getDccInfo2` (0xbe99750) is called **only** when
  DCC is being laid out, so its call count alone settles whether
  compression is in the picture at all.

| `rbgpu-surf` | means |
|---|---|
| `dcc calls=0` | compression is not in use; DCC excluded |
| `dcc calls>0` | live suspect, and forcing it off is the next boot |
| per-surface rows | the actual layout decisions, to compare against what the chip supports |
| `hk=0` on either | that hook did not take; its zero is the hook, not the driver |

Both originals run and their results pass through untouched; nothing is
written.

Gates: both defined in AMDRadeonX6000 (2c); routed nowhere else (2kn);
rule 9 clean - `getDccInfo2` opens `48 85 f6 0f 94 c1` (testq, sete, no
branch in the first five bytes), `getPreferredSwizzleMode2` opens
`55 48 89 e5 41 56 53` (2gb). **The `nm` cross-check earned its keep
again**: both names were first written with a 31 length prefix where the
class needs 33, and `solveSymbol` would have returned 0 for both (2kr).

Build `78B2F3A5-84B0-39E3-AB91-C4063BBC1087`.

## 2lb (2026-10-20) — boot 96: DCC is EXCLUDED, and the modes are named

```
rbgpu-surf = b=96 swz hk=1 calls=50 | dcc hk=1 calls=0 ok=0
 | 1920x1080 b32 f26 t1 fl20 s0->1b
 | 1920x1080 b32 f26 t1 fl20 s0->1b
 | 8192x4320 b32 f26 t1 fl0  s9->1b
 | 1920x1080 b32 f26 t1 fl0  s9->1b
 | 64x64     b32 f26 t1 fl0  s9->16
```

**`dcc calls=0` with `hk=1` and 50 swizzle calls in the same boot: DCC is
never laid out at all.** Compression is excluded as the cause, and the
positive control is in the same note - the DCC hook took, it simply was
never called. One suspect dead without a guess.

**The modes, decoded against AddrLib's `AddrSwizzleMode`:**

- `0x1b` = 27 = **`ADDR_SW_64KB_R_X`** - 64 KB **rotated**, X variant
- `0x16` = 22 = `ADDR_SW_4KB_D_X` - 4 KB displayable, X variant
- inputs: `s0` = `ADDR_SW_LINEAR`, `s9` = `ADDR_SW_64KB_S`

Everything large gets `64KB_R_X`, **including an 8192x4320 surface** -
141 MB at 32 bpp, the shape of a glyph/texture atlas. The 64x64 surface
gets a different mode, which is itself the per-surface variation the
screen demands.

`_X` means the swizzle XORs pipe and packer bits into the address; `_R_`
means **rotated**, which on GFX10 distributes across shader engines. This
chip has **one** shader engine (2kz: `NUM_SHADER_ENGINES=0`); Navi 21,
which this stack spoofs, has four. That is the single geometry field that
genuinely differs, and rotation is the first suspect that is per-surface
rather than global - which is what the photograph requires, with icons
and wallpaper perfect and glyphs shredded.

**2lb tests it with one variable changed.** `-rbgpunorotate` remaps
**27 -> 25** (`ADDR_SW_64KB_R_X` -> `ADDR_SW_64KB_S_X`). Both are 64 KB
and both are `_X`, so the pipe/packer arithmetic is bit-for-bit
identical; only the rotation differs. No other mode is touched, so any
change on screen can only come from that.

| outcome | means |
|---|---|
| text renders | rotation is the fault, on a 1-SE part |
| nothing changes | rotation excluded; `remapped=` proves the swap happened |
| worse / no desktop | `_S_X` is not a valid substitute here; revert |

`rbgpu-surf` now carries `rot=` (1 armed, 2 observe-only) and
`remapped=`, so an unarmed boot cannot be read as a null result (2eh).

Still not claimed: that rotation IS the cause. Three hypotheses about
this corruption have been refuted by measurement already (2kx, 2kz, and
DCC here); this one is a test, not a conclusion.

Build `58BAC460-ECD2-322F-8C20-1FE7D021B0AB`. New boot-arg:
`-rbgpunorotate`.

## 2lc (2026-10-20) — boot 97: rotation excluded, and SURFACE LAYOUT is excluded by the photograph

```
rbgpu-surf = b=97 swz hk=1 calls=21 | dcc hk=1 calls=0 ok=0 | rot=1 remapped=9
             | 1920x1080 b32 f26 t1 fl20 s0->1b | ... | 64x64 b32 f26 t1 fl0 s9->16
rbgpu-fault= b=97 c=0 f=0 r=0 o=0 fw=0
```

`rot=1 remapped=9` - the remap was armed and **fired on nine surfaces**,
swapping `ADDR_SW_64KB_R_X` for `ADDR_SW_64KB_S_X`. The user: "text is
unreadable still same artifacts too". **Rotation is excluded**, with the
positive control in the same note. (The recorded rows still read `->1b`
because `e->ret` is stored before the remap; `remapped=` counts the
changes.)

**And surface layout is excluded outright - by the photograph, not by a
boot.** In boot 93's picture the Claude Code window's dark background,
its sidebar, the traffic lights and the sidebar's coloured legend squares
are all correct, while the body text **inside that same window** is
shredded. Those pixels are in **one surface**. A wrong swizzle or tiling
mode corrupts a surface uniformly; correct rectangles and scrambled
glyphs cannot come out of the same buffer from a layout error.

So 2lb's negative was predictable and the boot was avoidable. Recorded
as such: the deduction was available in the image from the moment it
arrived, and three hypotheses (2kx tiling params, 2kz AddrLib geometry,
2lb rotation) were all aimed at a global layout parameter that the
evidence already ruled out. **The recurring error in a new dress - not
reading a value without establishing its meaning, but failing to read the
evidence already in hand before designing the next experiment.**

**What the evidence actually supports.** The fault is in the DRAWING
operation, not the destination:

- compute kernels PASS bit-exact (2ky), so shaders and linear memory work
- zero VM faults, so addressing is right
- rectangles, gradients, icons and the wallpaper draw correctly
- Finder, Safari and Messages render text **fully** - so glyph drawing
  through Apple's own text path works
- Claude Code (Electron/Skia) does not - and Skia rasterises its own
  glyphs and **uploads them as textures**

The one mechanism in play for Skia and not for the native apps is the
**client texture upload path** - the linear-to-tiled conversion done when
a client writes a texture. Candidates already visible in `nm`:
`AMDAccelResource::pageTextureWithStretchNoVendBuf`,
`AMDAccelResource::MSAATextureWrite` / `MSAATextureRead`,
`AMDBltMgr::MetadataRetiling`, `AMDAtomicBlitManager::doMetadataRetiling`.

Not claimed: that the upload path is the cause. It is where the evidence
points, and the next step is to measure it rather than to change it.

## 2ld (2026-10-20) — the split is WHO WRITES THE PIXELS, and linear is the decisive test

The user's app test killed 2lc's framing and produced much better
evidence. Safari on Wikipedia: **every glyph correct** - article body,
links, sidebar, the Appearance panel. Terminal, which is **native**:
scrambled. So "native versus Electron" is dead.

And in the same Safari window, **the Wikipedia globe image in the
infobox is shredded into blocks** while the text around it is perfect.

That re-cuts the evidence along a line that fits everything:

| who writes the pixels | result |
|---|---|
| **the GPU** - Safari's text via CoreGraphics, window chrome, the wallpaper, compositing | correct |
| **the CPU** - a decoded PNG uploaded with `replaceRegion`, Terminal's own glyph atlas | scrambled |

The GPU applies the swizzle in hardware, so anything it writes is
self-consistent. A CPU upload into a tiled surface is tiled **in
software by the userspace Metal driver**. If that software uses Navi 21's
pipe/packer geometry while the surface is laid out for this chip's, CPU
writes land shuffled and GPU writes do not - within one surface, which is
the only hypothesis so far that produces correct rectangles beside
scrambled glyphs.

**It also explains why four kernel-side findings all measured correct**
(2kx tiling params, 2kz AddrLib geometry, 2lb rotation, and the UBM
tables below): the kernel is right, and the disagreement is in
userspace, in `AMDRadeonX6000MTLDriver`.

Checked and clean on the way, so neither is a suspect:
`AMDGFX10Hardware::getUbmSwizzleMode` tail-jumps to
`AMDGFX10AlignManager::getAddrSwizzleMode` (0xbec184a), a 32-entry table
at `0xbf4efa0` which is **identity for every supported mode** (27 -> 27)
with `0x21` meaning unsupported; `AMDNavi21Hardware::setupAndInitializeHWCapabilities`
(0xbeca1a8) sets only a handful of flags (`0x11ec` at `+0x20840`, three
bytes/words), no geometry.

**2ld is the decisive test and it needs no new theory.** `-rbgpulinear`
forces every surface to `ADDR_SW_LINEAR` (0) through the hook 2la already
installed. Linear has **no swizzle at all**, so a CPU writer and a GPU
reader agree trivially.

| outcome | means |
|---|---|
| glyphs and the image come back correct | the fault IS a CPU/GPU tiling disagreement; direction of the fix settled |
| still scrambled with every surface linear | **swizzle is excluded entirely** and the cause is elsewhere |
| no desktop | linear is not accepted for these surfaces; revert the arg |

Either answer is worth the boot, which is more than could be said for
2lb. `forced=` counts the substitutions so an unarmed boot cannot be
read as a null result.

Caveat recorded before the boot: if the userspace driver computes its own
mode rather than taking the kernel's, forcing the kernel's value creates
a *different* disagreement rather than removing one - in which case the
result is "worse or unchanged", and that too distinguishes the
hypotheses.

Build `1905E486-807D-3407-AF84-9EE979F7436F`. New boot-arg:
`-rbgpulinear`.

## 2ld CONFIRMED (2026-10-20, boot 98) — forcing linear fixes ~80%

```
rbgpu-surf = b=98 swz hk=1 calls=66 | dcc hk=1 calls=0 ok=0
             | rot=2 remapped=0 lin=1 forced=66
rbgpu-fault= b=98 c=0 f=0 r=0 o=0 fw=0
```

`lin=1 forced=66` - every one of 66 surfaces forced to `ADDR_SW_LINEAR`,
with `rot=2 remapped=0` so rotation was off and this was a clean single
variable.

The user: "it worked 80%... the widgets render good... the top has no
artifacts the top dock is visible now with only one artifact near an app
icon". **Text is still unreadable**, in Claude Code and in Terminal.

**So the swizzle line is CONFIRMED.** Linear removes any possible
CPU/GPU disagreement about tiling, and with it goes most of the
corruption. 2ld's hypothesis - that CPU-written pixels are tiled in
software with the wrong geometry while GPU-written pixels are not - is
supported by direct experiment, not argument.

**And the pattern of what was fixed locates the rest.** The things that
came right - widgets, Dock, menu bar, the desktop's artifact regions -
are **WindowServer-drawn surfaces**, which are allocated through the
kernel and so pass `getPreferredSwizzleMode2`, the hook that was forced.
The things still wrong - Claude Code's and Terminal's glyphs - live in
**app-owned textures**. Sixty-six surfaces is far too few to be every
texture in the system, so client textures are taking their layout
somewhere this hook never sees.

**The reachable candidate is the client resource path.**
`AMDAccelResourceAddr2::initialize(IOAccelNewResourceArgs*, unsigned long
long)` (0xbe56894) is what runs when an application creates a texture -
`IOAccelNewResourceArgs` is the struct userspace passes in. If the
tiling/swizzle is dictated there by userspace and honoured by the
kernel, that is both the explanation and a place this plugin can reach.

Checked clean on the way, so neither is a suspect:
`AMDGFX10Hardware::setupAndInitializeHWCapabilities` (0xbead3e0) reads
`GB_ADDR_CONFIG` (0x13de), 0x13df, 0xd4 and 0xd5 from the chip and
derives its counts with popcount code (`0x55555555`, `0x33333333`,
`0x0f0f0f0f`, `imull $0x1010101`, `shrl $0x18`) - from hardware, not
hardcoded; and `AMDNavi21Hardware`'s override adds only flags.

**`-rbgpulinear` should stay IN for now.** It is a real and large
improvement. It is also a performance cost - linear surfaces defeat the
tiling the hardware wants - so it is a diagnostic crutch, not the final
answer. The final answer is to make the CPU-side tiling agree with the
chip, which keeps tiling and its performance.

Still unexplained: why text specifically, rather than every client
texture. Terminal and Claude Code both draw glyphs through an atlas they
own; whether other client textures are also wrong and simply less
visible is not established.

## 2le (2026-10-20) — find where client textures get their layout

Boot 98 located the remainder: what `-rbgpulinear` fixed is
WindowServer-drawn and passes the kernel's `getPreferredSwizzleMode2`;
what it did not fix is app-owned textures, and 66 surfaces cannot be
every texture in the system.

`AMDAccelResourceAddr2::initialize(IOAccelNewResourceArgs*, uint64)`
(0xbe56894) is what runs when an application creates a resource, and
`IOAccelNewResourceArgs` is the struct **userspace** passes in.

**2le does not guess the field.** The offset of any tiling or swizzle
member is unknown, so the hook dumps the first 24 dwords of the args for
the first four resources and the layout is read off the data. Choosing
an offset from a struct name and acting on it is exactly 2cy's error;
this boot is to FIND the field, not to change it. Observe only - the
original runs first and its result passes through.

| `rbgpu-res` | means |
|---|---|
| `calls=0` | client textures do not come through Addr2; the Addr1 variant is in use |
| `calls` far above `rbgpu-surf`'s 66 | this IS the path app textures take |
| the dwords | width, height, format and - the question - a userspace-chosen tiling field |
| `hk=0` | the hook did not take; the zero is the hook, not the driver |

Gates: defined in AMDRadeonX6000 (2c); routed nowhere else (2kn); rule 9
clean - `55 48 89 e5 41 57 41 56 53 50` (2gb); mangled name
cross-checked against `nm` (2kr).

**Asked and answered: does DCN 3.1.2 fix the text?** No. The corruption
happens when an application writes glyph pixels into its own texture,
long before anything reaches the display controller; DCN scans out the
already-composited framebuffer at the end of the chain and cannot repair
bytes written wrong upstream. What DCN would bring is separate and real:
a genuine AMD framebuffer, the 7 MB VRAM figure corrected (2kx), mode
setting, external outputs, brightness, multiple displays, a hardware
cursor - and eventually tiled scanout, which matters because
`-rbgpulinear` is currently paying bandwidth for linear surfaces.

Build `D2B77001-49B4-3FBE-8279-E8443B9255FA`.

## 2lf (2026-10-20) — boot 99 names the entry client textures actually use

```
rbgpu-res  = b=99 hk=1 calls=2495 null=335 rows=4
             | r0 40,0,10001,1,1a000,0,1a000,0
             | r1 40,0,10001,1,1000,0,1000,0
rbgpu-surf = b=99 swz hk=1 calls=61 | lin=1 forced=61
```

**`calls=2495` against 61.** Client resources are forty times more
numerous than the surfaces that pass `getPreferredSwizzleMode2`, so they
are the bulk of the system's textures **and they are not getting their
layout from that path**. The first four rows are plain buffers - `0x1a000`
and `0x1000` repeated as a size pair, no width or height - so the early
resources are allocations, not the glyph atlases; the full 24-dword rows
went only to the log, which the 2es rule means did not survive.

**The two align-manager entries differ in kind, and that is the answer:**

```
getPreferredSwizzleMode2(in)     CHOOSES a mode               61 calls
getSurfaceInfo2(in, out)         COMPUTES the layout for the mode
                                 ALREADY SET in in->swizzleMode
```

Client textures arrive with their mode **already chosen** - by userspace -
and only ever pass `getSurfaceInfo2` (0xbe99638). Forcing the chooser
could never reach them, which is precisely what boot 98 showed:
WindowServer's surfaces came right, app glyphs did not. The 80/20 split
was not a coincidence, it was these two code paths.

**2lf hooks the one they use.** `+0x08` is `swizzleMode` in
`_ADDR2_COMPUTE_SURFACE_INFO_INPUT` **on evidence, not assumption** - 2la
logged that field for five surfaces and read coherent values (0 = LINEAR,
9 = 64KB_S). Under `-rbgpulinear` the hook rewrites it to 0 **before**
the original runs, so the layout is computed for linear and the CPU and
GPU agree. Without the arg it counts and records only.

`rbgpu-si` carries `modes=`, a bitmask of every mode arriving (bit 27 =
64KB_R_X, bit 0 = LINEAR), so what userspace is choosing is recorded
whether or not the force is armed.

| outcome | means |
|---|---|
| `forced>0`, glyphs readable | the fix; and the CPU/GPU tiling disagreement is fully characterised |
| `forced>0`, still scrambled | the layout was not what corrupted them; the CPU-side tiling is computed wholly in userspace, out of this plugin's reach |
| `calls=0` | client textures do not use Addr2's align manager either |

Gates: defined in AMDRadeonX6000 (2c); routed nowhere else (2kn); rule 9
clean - `48 85 f6 0f 94 c1`, testq and sete with no branch in the first
five bytes (2gb); mangled name cross-checked against `nm` (2kr).

Build `18EA0E63-AB04-3F6A-8E27-1372BB1A2B4B`. No new boot-arg -
`-rbgpulinear` arms both forces.

## 2lg (2026-10-20) — boot 100: client texture layout is computed in USERSPACE

Two captures from the same live boot, the second after the applications
were up:

```
early  rbgpu-res = calls=551  | rbgpu-surf = calls=26 | rbgpu-si = calls=26 forced=0 already=26 modes=00000001
later  rbgpu-res = calls=5458 | rbgpu-surf = calls=68 | rbgpu-si = calls=68 forced=0 already=68 modes=00000001
```

User: "texts are the same still".

**`getSurfaceInfo2` was called 68 times - exactly as many as
`getPreferredSwizzleMode2` - against 5458 client resources.** Every
single call already carried `swizzleMode = 0`, because our own force on
the chooser fed it; `modes=00000001` is bit 0 alone, so **no other mode
ever arrived**, and `forced=0` because there was never anything to
force.

The counts being *equal* is the finding: every `getSurfaceInfo2` follows
a `getPreferredSwizzleMode2` on the same kernel-allocated surface. The
other ~5400 client resources never touch the kernel's align manager at
all.

**So client texture layout is computed entirely in userspace, in
`AMDRadeonX6000MTLDriver`, and the kernel is never asked.** This is the
branch 2lf pre-registered as "out of this plugin's reach", and it
explains the whole pattern: every kernel-side value measured correct
(2kx, 2kz, 2la, the UBM tables, the HW capabilities) and every
kernel-side force changed only what the kernel owned - WindowServer's
surfaces, the 80% that came right in boot 98.

The second capture matters methodologically: the first was taken three
minutes in, before the applications had created their textures, and
`calls=551` could have been read as "clients do not use this path" when
it only meant "not yet". Re-capturing live in the same boot turned a
weak reading into a settled one, and cost nothing - the boot was already
running. Worth repeating whenever a count is the evidence.

**The remaining in-kernel avenue**, before anything drastic: userspace
must learn the chip's geometry somehow, and if it asks the kernel the
answer can be corrected there. `IOAccelDevice2::get_config(IOAccelDeviceConfigData*)`
(0x14e20282, IOAcceleratorFamily2) is that channel, with
`IOAccelDevice2::get_device_info(IOAccelDeviceInfoReturnData*)`
(0x14e2072e) beside it.

Two outcomes to keep apart, and neither is established:

- if `IOAccelDeviceConfigData` carries tiling geometry, correcting it is
  reachable and safe-ish
- if it carries only a chip/family identifier that userspace uses to
  select hardcoded AddrLib parameters, then changing it collides with
  the Navi 21 spoof the whole stack depends on, and the honest options
  narrow to patching the userspace driver with Lilu's user patcher - a
  different and much larger undertaking

**`-rbgpulinear` stays IN.** It is 80% of the corruption gone and costs
only bandwidth.

## 2lh (2026-10-20) — `get_config` carries no geometry; the remaining fix is userspace

`IOAccelDevice2::get_config(IOAccelDeviceConfigData*)` (0x14e20282)
disassembled in full. The struct it fills is 0x40 bytes:

```
+0x00  accel->0xc90, munged: (lo16) | ((v >> 9) & 0x1000)
+0x04  accel->0xc98
+0x08  accel->vtable[0x868]()        (64-bit)
+0x10  accel->0xca8                  (64-bit)
+0x18  accel->0x178
+0x20  accel->vtable[0x990]()        (64-bit)
+0x28  accel->vtable[0xa90]()        (64-bit)
+0x30  accel->0xd10                  (64-bit)
+0x38  accel->0xd18                  (u16 -> u32)
+0x3c  accel->0xd1a                  (u16 -> u32)
```

**No tiling geometry in it** - no pipe count, no packer count, no shader
engine count, no `GB_ADDR_CONFIG`. It is generic accelerator
configuration. And the accelerator publishes no geometry property in the
IORegistry either (checked against the live capture: the only matches
are `RBGPULoad` and `assigned-addresses`).

**So nothing in the kernel tells userspace this chip's geometry**, and
userspace computes client texture layout itself (2lg). The remaining
conclusion is that `AMDRadeonX6000MTLDriver` derives its AddrLib
parameters from the chip family it believes it is on - and this stack
spoofs **Navi 21**, which has four shader engines against this part's
one (2kz).

**What is established, and what is not.** Established: the kernel is
never asked, via `get_config` or the IORegistry. Not established: that
userspace hardcodes per family rather than obtaining the geometry
through some other external method not yet examined. The conclusion
above is the best reading of the evidence, not a measurement, and it
should be labelled as such until something confirms it.

**Options from here, none of them small:**

1. **Patch the userspace driver** with Lilu's user patcher, correcting
   the AddrLib parameters inside `AMDRadeonX6000MTLDriver`. The direct
   route, and a new phase of the project - a userspace graphics driver
   is delicate and nothing in this plugin has touched one yet.
2. **Spoof a closer part.** Apple ships `AMDRadeonX6000_AMDNavi23Hardware`
   and `AMDNavi23Display` beside the Navi 21 classes. If some supported
   Navi 2x part's AddrLib geometry matches this chip's 4 pipes / 4
   packers / 1 SE, spoofing that instead would fix userspace tiling with
   no userspace patching at all. Cheap to state, expensive to try: the
   entire bring-up - firmware, PSP, SMU, the RLC sub-images, every fix in
   this journal - is built on the Navi 21 path.
3. **Leave `-rbgpulinear` in and move to DCN 3.1.2.** 80% of the
   corruption is already gone for a bandwidth cost, and the display half
   of the driver is untouched, independently valuable, and does not
   depend on any of this.

Nothing here changes the standing results: the CP halt is fixed, VM
faults are zero across five boots, and an armed boot reaches a
composited desktop that stays up.

## 2li (2026-10-20) — THE DISPLAY HALF WAS NEVER ASKED TO START

Decision recorded first: the user chose option 3 (DCN) over re-spoofing
as Navi 23 - "our setup is too stable to ditch for Navi23" - and ranked
userspace patching (option 1) second for later. Option 2 is parked, not
dead.

**And DCN turns out not to be the first problem.** Four facts, all read
live:

- `kextstat` shows **no framebuffer kext loaded at all**
- `AMDSupport` is `matched, active, busy 0 (1 ms)` with **no children**
- **no `AtiFbStub` instance exists** (the only hit in ioreg is a zero
  count in `IOKitDiagnostics`)
- `AMDFramebuffer.kext` matches `IOProviderClass = AtiFbStub`,
  `IONameMatch = display` - so with no stub it can never match

The chain that should build a display is
**controller -> `AtiFbStub` -> `AMDFramebuffer` -> DCN**, and it never
begins. `AMDRadeonX6000Framebuffer.kext` carries the controllers, and
their personalities match on **real PCI ids**:

```
AMDRadeonNavi21Controller  IOPCIMatch 0x73A01002 0x73A21002 0x73A31002
                                      0x73AB1002 0x73AE1002 0x73AF1002 0x73BF1002
AMDRadeonNavi23Controller  IOPCIMatch 0x73E01002 0x73E31002 0x73FF1002
AMDGPUWrangler             the same Navi ids, score 60000, IOFramebuffer
```

This GPU is **`0x16811002`** (`device-id = <81160000>` live) and matches
none of them. So the controller never matches, nothing publishes a stub,
and **DCN is never programmed because nothing ever asks it to**. That -
not a DCN fault - is why the panel is still on `IONDRVFramebuffer` and
why System Profiler reports the boot framebuffer's 7 MB (2kx).

**2li gives the display half the same treatment the accelerator half
already gets:** make Apple's personality match. IOPCIFamily honours a
`device-id` property injected on the device node, so the peer sets it to
**0x73A0**, the first id `AMDRadeonNavi21Controller` accepts.

**Opt-in and reversible (`-rbgpufbmatch`)**, because it changes what
matches on that node - potentially including things that work today. The
accelerator reaches its personality through `LoadAccelerator`,
`LoadHWServices` and `ATY,Belknap` rather than the device id, so it
should be unaffected; that is a reading of the existing code, not a
measurement, and this boot tests it.

| outcome | means |
|---|---|
| an `AtiFbStub` and `AMDFramebuffer` appear | the chain starts; DCN work proper begins |
| controller matches but no stub | the controller runs and fails later - a real DCN question at last |
| nothing matches | the id is not what gates it; read `fbmatch` in the diag |
| accelerator breaks / no desktop | the device id was load-bearing elsewhere; drop the arg |

Also extracted for this phase, neither previously analysed:
`build/re/AMDFramebuffer` (7.0 MB), `build/re/AMDSupport` (7.9 MB) and
`build/re/AMDRadeonX6000Framebuffer` (10.1 MB), all from
**SystemKernelExtensions.kc** - not the boot collection, which is why
`kc_extract.py` found nothing there at first.

Build `BDF97C50-EA4B-3700-876E-85A12C4E4A7E`. New boot-arg:
`-rbgpufbmatch`.

## 2lj (2026-10-20) — boot 101: the device-id route is INCOMPATIBLE with this stack

`-rbgpufbmatch` cost the accelerator and bought no framebuffer. Read live
from the boot:

```
device-id              = <a0730000>          (the spoof applied)
rbgpu-arm              = consumed, LoadAccelerator = Yes   (the boot armed)
rbgpu-boot             = 100                 (NO note written - nothing
                                              reached powerUpHW)
instantiated on IGPU   = RembrandtGPUPeer, AMDSupport, .Display_boot,
                         AMDRadeonX6000_AMDRadeonHWServicesNavi
NOT instantiated       = AMDRadeonX6000_AMDNavi21GraphicsAccelerator
AtiFbStub / AMDFramebuffer = still none
```

The user: "its unaccelerated... back to like when the kext was off".

**The cause is this plugin's own design.** The stack does not pretend to
be another device - it makes Apple **accept 0x1681**:

```
kern_start.cpp:977   if (g_spoof_ttl_mode && ret == 0 && dev_id == 0x1681)
kern_start.cpp:6452  table[target_idx].deviceId = 0x1681;   // deviceTypeTable
kern_start.cpp:6568  *(uint32_t *)(table[...].data + 0x10) = 0x1681;
                                                          // DeviceCapabilityTbl
```

Every one of those patches inserts or keys on **0x1681**. With the
IOKit `device-id` reporting `0x73A0`, Apple's stack asked about a device
our patches had never prepared, the TTL spoof hook did not fire, and the
accelerator could not come up. HWServicesNavi still matched - it is the
chooser - but it built nothing.

**So `device-id` injection is the wrong instrument here**, and the
pre-registered "accelerator breaks / drop the arg" row is the one that
came up. The finding is worth the boot: it rules out the obvious route
and names the right one.

**The right shape, by the project's own convention:** make Apple's
*personality* accept this device, rather than making the device claim to
be Apple's. `AMDRadeonNavi21Controller` is a personality in
`AMDRadeonX6000Framebuffer.kext` with
`IOClass = AMDRadeonX6000_AmdRadeonControllerNavi21`,
`IOProviderClass = IOPCIDevice`, `IOMatchCategory = ATIFramebuffer`. A
personality declared by THIS kext with the same `IOClass` and
`IOPCIMatch 0x16811002` would instantiate Apple's controller against our
device with the device id untouched - the same philosophy as patching
`deviceTypeTable` to contain 0x1681 rather than lying about the chip.

Unexamined, and required before trying it: whether the controller class
is reachable from another kext's personality (it needs
`OSBundleLibraries` on `com.apple.kext.AMDRadeonX6000Framebuffer`, which
lives in **SystemKernelExtensions.kc**, not the boot collection - an
EFI-loaded kext may not be able to link against it at all). If it cannot,
the route is patching the personality in the prelinked collection, which
is OpenCore's job rather than this plugin's.

`-rbgpufbmatch` goes **OUT**. The code stays, gated and inert, with this
entry as the reason.

## 2lk (2026-10-20) — the kernel DOES supply the geometry, and 2lh was wrong

2lg/2lh concluded "client texture layout is computed in userspace, out of
this plugin's reach". **That is refuted.** The conclusion rested on one
channel: 2lh read `IOAccelDevice2::get_config`, found its 0x40-byte struct
carried no geometry, and generalised to "the kernel never supplies it". There
is a second channel, it carries exactly the geometry AddrLib needs, and it is
a single `memcpy` in a function whose name says so.

**The recurring error, 27th instance: absence in one place read as absence
everywhere.** The same shape as 2kx/2la/2lc three milestones earlier, and the
same cost - two milestones spent concluding the fix was unreachable.

### How the channel was found

`AMDRadeonX6000MTLDriver` lives in the dyld shared cache, and this machine has
no extractor (no Xcode, `dyld_shared_cache_util` absent). `tools/re/dyldcache.py`
is new: it builds a vm->file map from all seven subcaches' mappings, finds an
image by path in `imagesText`, parses its Mach-O load commands in place, and
writes a compact Mach-O (5.5 MB of the 155 MB image) whose file offsets are
repacked so `objdump` reads it at the cache's own VM addresses. `LC_SYMTAB`
survives in the cache, so 20 282 symbols come out by name;
`tools/re/mtldis.sh` disassembles one by regex.

789 of those symbols mention `Addr`. The driver carries **its own complete
AddrLib** - `AddrCreate`, `Addr2ComputeSurfaceInfo`, `Addr2ComputeDccInfo`,
the Gfx10 HWL.

### The chain, end to end, all static

```
AMDRadeonX6000_AMDAccelDevice::getHardwareInfo(_sAMD_GET_HW_INFO_VALUES*)
  0xbe47ca4
    movq  0x108(%rbx), %rax          ; hw
    movq  0x1a38(%rax), %rdi
    movq  (%rdi), %rax
    callq *0x1c0(%rax)               ; -> a cached struct pointer
    movl  $0x204, %edx               ; 516 bytes
    callq memcpy                     ; -> the caller's buffer
```

then, in userspace:

```
gfx10_HwInfoInitData(GFX10_HwInfoRec*, _sAMD_GET_HW_INFO_VALUES*, uint)
  0x7ffb08cb4218  movl 0xa0(%rsi), %r9d
  0x7ffb08cb421f  movl %r9d, 0xa4(%rdi)     <- the ONLY write to +0xa4
                                               in the whole function

amdMtl_InitAddrLibInterface(AMD_AddrLibInterfaceRec*, AMDCommonHwInfoRec const*)
  0x7ffb08c9409f  in.size         = 0x70
                  in.chipFamily   = hwInfo->0x00
                  in.chipRevision = hwInfo->0x10
                  in.hClient      = the interface rec
                  -> AddrCreate(&in, &out)

amdMtl_HWL_InitAddrLibHwRegFields(_ADDR_CREATE_INPUT*, AMDCommonHwInfoRec const*)
  0x7ffb08bfde4d  six instructions, the whole function:
                    movl $0xd, 0x4(%rdi)        ; chipEngine = 0xd
                    movl 0xa4(%rsi), %eax
                    movl %eax, 0x30(%rdi)       ; regValue.gbAddrConfig
```

**So the swizzle equation every client texture is tiled with comes from one
dword: `_sAMD_GET_HW_INFO_VALUES + 0xa0`.** It is copied verbatim, twice, with
no transformation, from a kernel struct this plugin can reach.

### The struct, named by Apple's own error strings

`getHardwareInfo` validates the record and kprintfs one of two format strings
before returning `0xE00002BC`. They name the fields:

```
0xbf3deda  "Invalid values - refClkFreq: 0x%llx sysClkFreq: 0x%llx
            memClkFreq: 0x%llx cgRefClkFreq: 0x%llx"
0xbf3df56  "Invalid values - deviceID: 0x%x numRasterPipe: 0x%llx
            numShaderPipes: 0x%llx"
```

against the offsets the compares use:

```
+0x00  uint16  deviceID            +0xc0  uint64  refClkFreq
+0x08  uint32  (-> chipFamily)     +0xc8  uint64  sysClkFreq
+0x18  uint64  numRasterPipe       +0xd0  uint64  memClkFreq
+0x20  uint64  numShaderPipes      +0xd8  uint64  cgRefClkFreq
+0xa0  uint32  GB_ADDR_CONFIG
```

This is a derivation of field names from Apple's own diagnostic text, not an
assumption about struct layout.

### Why this fits the symptom exactly

The measured split has been stable for four boots: window chrome, Dock,
menu-bar text and widgets correct; app body-text glyphs scrambled, in the
**same surface** as correct chrome. Kernel-laid-out surfaces pass through
`AMDHWAlignManager2::getSurfaceInfo2`, which uses the chip's real
`GB_ADDR_CONFIG` (`a0=242`, 2ky - 4 pipes, 4 packers, 1 SE). Client textures
never touch it (2lf: 68 kernel surfaces against 5458 client resources). If
`+0xa0` carries Navi 21's config instead - 4 shader engines where this chip
has 1 - the two halves of one screen are tiled with two different equations,
which is what the photograph shows.

### A second, independent reason to read this struct

Apple rejects its own record if any clock is zero. **`gfx_min = gfx_max = 0`
has been standing since 2di**, so `sysClkFreq = 0` is live, and would mean
userspace never receives a valid hardware-info record at all. The return code
is recorded beside the fields so one boot answers both questions.

### What was built

`hooked_gethwinfo_2lk`, **observe only**. It calls the original first, then
records the first call's whole sample - return code, deviceID, family,
numRasterPipe, numShaderPipes, `+0xa0`, and the four clocks - to `rbgpu-hwi`,
beside the chip's own `GB_ADDR_CONFIG` as the ring probe read it
(`g_rb_2ky_gbac`, newly captured at phase 0). The note states the verdict in
words - `MATCH(hypothesis dead)`, `DIFFER(this is the defect)` or
`UNCOMPARABLE` - so the comparison cannot be done later and wrong.

**No correction is written.** Which correction is right depends entirely on
what `+0xa0` holds, and 2kr already cost a boot to reasoning out an
arithmetic fix before measuring the value it operates on. If `+0xa0` reads
`0x242` the hypothesis is dead and a fix written now would have been wrong.

Gates: defined in AMDRadeonX6000 (`nm -m`, 2c); routed nowhere else, grepped
(2kn); rule 9 clean - opens `55 48 89 e5 41 57 41 56 41 54 53 48 85 f6`, first
branch at +0x0e (2gb); mangled name cross-checked against `nm` (2kr).

Every path out says something (rule 14): `hk=0` for a hook that did not take,
`NO SAMPLE` for a boot where userspace never asked, `null=` for Apple's own
NULL-struct path.

Not claimed: that `+0xa0` is wrong. That is what the boot measures.

## 2lk CONFIRMED-NEGATIVE (boot 102) — the geometry is right on BOTH sides

The hypothesis is dead, and the fallback it named is dead too. Both closed in
one boot plus one static read.

```
rbgpu-hwi = b=102 hk=1 calls=40 null=0 ret=00000000 dev=1681 fam=00000028
            ras=4 shd=6 gbac=00000242 hw=00000242 MATCH(hypothesis dead)
            | ref=10000 sys=20000 mem=20000 cg=10000
```

`b=102` is a new nonce (2gd) and `rbgpu-boot` went 101 -> 102, so this is
this boot's evidence. `hk=1 calls=40 null=0` - the hook took and userspace
asked forty times, so `MATCH` is a measurement and not silence.

**`gbac = hw = 0x242`.** Userspace receives this chip's own
`GB_ADDR_CONFIG`, byte for byte what the ring probe reads off the register.
The one-dword theory of 2lk is refuted on direct evidence.

### Two things settled for free

1. **`ret=00000000` - Apple ACCEPTS its own record**, and all four clocks are
   nonzero (`ref=0x10000 sys=0x20000 mem=0x20000 cg=0x10000`). So
   `gfx_min = gfx_max = 0`, standing since 2di, does **not** propagate into
   the hardware-info struct and does not deny userspace a valid record. That
   half of 2lk's reason for existing is closed as a negative.
2. **`ras=4 shd=6`** - numRasterPipe 4, numShaderPipes 6. Six WGPs is this
   chip's 12 CUs. The kernel is reporting the 680M's real topology, not Navi
   21's.

### The fallback lead, killed statically

2lk said MATCH "sends the search to chipFamily/chipRevision, which AddrLib
also keys its HWL selection on". `rbgpu-hwi` gives `fam=00000028` for the
kernel struct's `+0x08`, and 2kz measured the **kernel's** AddrLib create
input as `fam=d rev=8f third=28` - chipEngine 0xd, chipFamily 0x8f
(AddrLib's `FAMILY_NV`), chipRevision 0x28. `0x28` is not a family value, so
for one moment it looked like userspace was being handed 0x28 as its family.

It is not. `gfx10_HwInfoInitData`'s family selection is a cascade of
`cmpl $N, %r10d ; ja next` - **ranges**, not exact matches - over
`N = 0x9, 0x13, 0x27, 0x31, 0x3b, 0x45`, with `r10d = kernel->0x08 = 0x28`:

```
cmpl $0x27 -> ja   (0x28 > 0x27, skip)
cmpl $0x31 -> fall through, 0x28 <= 0x31, TAKE:
  0x7ffb08cb4411  movabsq $0x80000008f, %r10
  0x7ffb08cb441b  movq    %r10, (%rdi)      ; chipFamily = 0x8f, +0x04 = 0x8
  0x7ffb08cb441e  movl    $0x1, 0x8(%rdi)
```

and `chipRevision` is `hwInfo+0x10`, written at `0x7ffb08cb40eb` from the same
`kernel->0x08` = **0x28**.

So the four values AddrLib is created with:

| input | kernel (2kz) | userspace (2lk + static) |
|---|---|---|
| chipEngine | 0xd | 0xd (hardcoded, `0x7ffb08bfde51`) |
| chipFamily | 0x8f | 0x8f (immediate, the `<=0x31` arm) |
| chipRevision | 0x28 | 0x28 (`kernel->0x08`) |
| gbAddrConfig | 0x242 | 0x242 (`kernel->0xa0`, measured) |

**Identical on both sides.** There is no AddrLib configuration difference
anywhere in this stack, and `movq $0x0, (%rdi)` - the `family = 0` fallback
arm that would have been the defect - is not reached.

### What this costs and what it buys

It costs the whole 2lg -> 2lh -> 2lk line: the remaining corruption is **not**
a global layout parameter, on either side of the kernel boundary. That is now
the fourth global-parameter hypothesis to die (2kx tiling params, 2la kernel
AddrLib geometry, 2lc rotation, 2lk userspace geometry), and all four were
excluded in advance by the same evidence - the photograph showing correct
window chrome and scrambled glyphs **in one surface**. The variant named in
2lk's own writeup ("read the evidence already in hand before designing the
next experiment") applies to 2lk itself.

It buys four facts that are now settled rather than assumed: userspace's
AddrLib inputs, Apple's acceptance of the hw-info record, the real topology
the kernel reports, and the exclusion of 2di from this path. And it buys
`tools/re/dyldcache.py`, which makes the userspace driver readable at all.

### Where that leaves the frontier

Both AddrLibs agree, so a client texture is written by the CPU and read by
the GPU through the *same* layout equation. Self-consistent surfaces cannot
scramble from a layout mismatch. So either

- the surfaces that scramble are not laid out through AddrLib at all, or
- they are laid out correctly and corrupted by something else - the glyph
  atlas's producer, a blit/compute path's own addressing, or DCC metadata on
  a render target (`dcc calls=0` excluded DCC for the 74 *kernel* surfaces
  only, never for client ones).

The next measurement is the first userspace observation this project has
made: log what `amdMtl_HWL_DetermineSwizzleMode` (0x7ffb08d35a11) picks for
each client texture, and what `Addr2ComputeSurfaceInfo` returns for it.
Lilu's user patcher is back on the table - for **observation**, which is what
it should have been used for first.

Not claimed: that the layout is correct for client textures. Only that the
AddrLib *configuration* is identical on both sides, which removes the reason
to expect it to be wrong.

## 2ll / 2lm (2026-10-21) — observing userspace's choice, and the one lever

The request was a userspace observation hook on `DetermineSwizzleMode` and
`Addr2ComputeSurfaceInfo`. **That hook cannot exist.** Lilu's user patcher
(`kern_user.hpp`) offers `BinaryModInfo` / `BinaryModPatch`: a find/replace of
bytes in a loaded image, with `onProcLoad`'s callback firing once per binary
load in the kernel, not per call in userspace. There is no mechanism for
userspace code to report back into the kext. So userspace can be **forced**
but not **read**.

Observation therefore moved kernel-side, where userspace's choice arrives
anyway, and the userspace lever was built as what it actually is.

### 2ll — the mode client resources end up with

`AMDAccelResourceAddr2::initialize` (0xbe56894) builds a client resource, and
its own code names the field:

```
be569b4  movl $0x0, 0x1dc(%r15)
be569bf  movq 0x250(%r15), %rdi
be569cb  callq *0x1b8(%rax)
be569d8  andl $0x1f, %eax          <- 5 bits, an AddrSwizzleMode's full range
be569de  orl  %eax, %ecx
be569e0  movl %ecx, 0x1dc(%r15)
be569f3  callq *0x1c8(%rax)
be569f9  shll $0x5, %eax
be569fc  andl $0x60, %eax          <- bits 5:6, a second field beside it
```

So `res + 0x1dc` bits 0:4 hold the resource's swizzle mode. The offset is
read off Apple's instructions and the 5-bit width is what identifies it as a
mode; neither was chosen from a struct name (2cy).

**It rides inside the existing 2le hook.** 2le already routes `initialize`,
and a second `RouteRequest` on a function this plugin has already routed
panics Lilu outright (2kn) - so `rbgpu_resmode_record_2ll` is called from
inside `hooked_resinit_2le` rather than from a route of its own.

A **histogram over every call**, not a few rows: 2le dumped four resources'
args and the note truncated them to eight dwords, while the log it also wrote
did not survive, because the published RBGPULog ends at the last refresh
(2es). Counting 4287 resources cannot be truncated into a wrong reading the
way two rows of dwords can. New note `rbgpu-mode`; `res` is validated as a
kernel VA before dereference (rule 19); seen=0 and hk=0 each say so in words
(rule 14).

### 2lm — the userspace force, unarmed

`amdMtl_HWL_DetermineSwizzleMode` (0x7ffb08d35a11) is the client-side chooser,
the userspace counterpart of the `getPreferredSwizzleMode2` that
`-rbgpulinear` forces. Two things had to be measured before a patch could be
written, and both were:

**1. The return value IS the mode, not a status.** All nine call sites were
located by scanning `__text` for `e8` displacements to the function; each does
`movl %eax, %ebx` and passes `%eax` onward as a mode (0x7ffb08d5f22a, then
`movl %eax, %edx` into the following call). The `uint&` seventh parameter is a
separate out-field, and at entry the first stack argument is at `rsp+8` -
confirmed from the callee's own `0x10(%rbp)`/`0x18(%rbp)`/`0x20(%rbp)` reads
after it pushes `%rbp`, and from the caller pushing the `leaq`'d reference
last. So the stub returns 0 in `%eax` **and** writes 0 through the
out-reference, which the caller's frame would otherwise leave uninitialised.

**2. A short find pattern would have patched the wrong function.** Measured
against the driver's own `__text`:

```
14 bytes (the bare prologue)  2099 occurrences
20 bytes                        97 occurrences
24 bytes                         1 occurrence
32 bytes                         1 occurrence
```

The 14-byte prologue `55 48 89 e5 41 57 41 56 41 55 41 54 53 48` is 2099
functions in a system Metal driver. The pattern is 32 bytes.

**Scoped to Terminal alone**, and **OUT of boot-args**. This rewrites a system
driver in every process it reaches, and a wrong stub there costs the login
session; Terminal is both the reported symptom and a blast radius that cannot
take down the desktop. Nothing is registered unless `-rbgpumtllinear` is set,
so an unarmed boot carries no user patcher at all.

### Why they are not armed together

One variable per boot. 2ll is observe-only and answers a question 2lm's
result would be read against: if client resources already read `m0` with
`-rbgpulinear` in, the kernel's resources are linear and the scrambled glyphs
are not a kernel-side layout choice, which changes what forcing userspace
would even mean. 2lm is built, documented and left for the boot after.

Not claimed: that forcing userspace to LINEAR will fix the text. That is the
experiment, and its negative - text still scrambled with mode 0 on both sides
- would exonerate layout entirely and send the search downstream, which is
worth as much as the positive.

## 2ll measured (boot 103) — AMBIGUOUS, and the ambiguity is the finding

```
rbgpu-mode = b=103 hk=1 seen=12224 bad=0 | m0=12224 | hi 0/12224/0/0 | lin=1
rbgpu-res  = b=103 hk=1 calls=12224 null=333 rows=4
```

`b=103` against boot 102, `rbgpu-arm` consumed, loaded UUID
`652BFDC8-D935-3B1A-879F-1D43FD0DBE88` == `build/out`. `seen` equals
`rbgpu-res calls` exactly and `bad=0`, so every resource was inspected and no
pointer was refused. The boot is healthy: `rbgpu-fault c=0 f=0 r=0 o=0 fw=0`,
`rbgpu-mew NEVER HALTED`, `rbgpu-adj fixed=8947/8947`.

**Every client resource reads mode 0, and bits 5:6 read 1, across all 12224.**

### Why that is not yet "client resources are linear"

Perfect uniformity across 12224 samples is **evidence against the field being
per-resource at all.** Client textures differ in type, size and format; a
genuine per-texture layout choice should vary. Two readings fit the data
equally:

1. every client resource really is laid out linear, or
2. `res + 0x1dc` is a device-level constant read 12224 times, carrying nothing
   about an individual texture.

Declaring (1) would be the recurring error again - a value read without first
establishing what makes it meaningful - and this time the trap is uniformity
masquerading as unanimity.

### One confound IS excluded

`res + 0x1dc` is filled from `(res->0x250)->vt[0x1b8]()`. If that slot were
the `getPreferredSwizzleMode2` that `-rbgpulinear` forces, `m0=12224` would be
this plugin's own patch reflected back. It is not: 2la's hook on that function
counted **70** calls this boot (`rbgpu-surf calls=70`), against 12224
resources. A hook taken 70 times cannot be what answered 12224 queries, so
`vt[0x1b8]` is a different, unhooked accessor and `m0` is Apple's own value.

That rescues the measurement from being circular. It does not separate (1)
from (2).

### The discriminator, and it is cheap

Read the same note with **`-rbgpulinear` OUT**. If the histogram still reads
`m0=` everything, the field is a constant and 2ll is retired as an instrument.
If it spreads - `m27` (64KB_R_X), `m25`, `m9` - then it IS per-resource, it
was linear only because of the force, and the question becomes why linear
client resources still render scrambled glyphs.

That boot also answers something the user has not seen since 2ld: what the
desktop looks like with no linear crutch at all, now that the halt is fixed
and faults are zero. It removes a boot-arg rather than adding one, which is
the cheapest possible experiment.

### What 2lm's status becomes

Unchanged - still built, still unarmed, still OUT. Forcing userspace to LINEAR
is only meaningful once it is known whether the resources reaching the kernel
are already linear, and that is exactly what reading (1) vs (2) decides. Had
2lm been armed this boot alongside 2ll, neither note could have been read.

Not claimed: that the glyph corruption is or is not a layout problem. Both
readings above remain open.

## 2ll SETTLED (boot 104, -rbgpulinear OUT) — per-resource, and 4% are tiled

```
rbgpu-mode = b=104 hk=1 seen=4788 bad=0 | m0=4598 m2=8 m22=125 m27=57
             | hi 0/4788/0/0 | lin=2
rbgpu-si   = b=104 hk=1 calls=83 forced=0 already=0 modes=08400004 | lin=2
rbgpu-surf = b=104 swz calls=83 | rot=2 remapped=0 lin=2 forced=0
```

Gates: `rbgpu-boot` 103 -> 104, `rbgpu-arm` consumed, `-rbgpulinear` absent
from live boot-args (`grep -c` = 0), loaded UUID
`652BFDC8-D935-3B1A-879F-1D43FD0DBE88` == `build/out`. Health unchanged:
`c=0 f=0 r=0 o=0 fw=0`, `NEVER HALTED`, `adj fixed=10386/10386`,
`hwi gbac=242 hw=242`.

**The histogram spreads, so `res + 0x1dc` IS per-resource.** Boot 103's
reading (2) - a device-level constant read 12224 times - is dead, and 2ll
stands as an instrument. `rbgpu-si modes=08400004` is bits 2, 22 and 27,
exactly the non-zero modes the histogram counts, from an independent hook.

**190 of 4788 client resources carry a tiled layout:** 125 in mode 22
(4KB_D_X), 57 in mode 27 (64KB_R_X), 8 in mode 2. The other 4598 are linear
without anything forcing them.

### A correction: boot 103's "confound excluded" was WRONG

2ll's boot-103 writeup argued that `-rbgpulinear` could not be reaching
`res + 0x1dc`, because 2la's hook on `getPreferredSwizzleMode2` counted 70
calls against 12224 resources, and "a hook taken 70 times cannot be what
answered 12224 queries".

That does not follow, and the data refutes it. Boot 103 recorded **zero**
non-`m0` out of 12224. If ~96% of client resources were natively linear - the
proportion boot 104 measures - roughly 500 tiled ones should have appeared.
They did not, so the arg **does** drive client resources to linear.
`vt[0x1b8]` is therefore reading a mode the align manager has **cached**,
which those 70 calls set and many resources then share, rather than a fresh
per-call answer.

The error was treating a call-count mismatch as proof of independence. A
cache between the hook and the reader breaks that inference completely, and
nothing had established there was no cache. Twenty-eighth instance, and the
first one caught by its own follow-up boot rather than by a later milestone.

### What it buys

The fix shape changes, and improves. `-rbgpulinear` is a blanket force that
costs bandwidth on all 4788 resources to correct 190 of them. If the glyph
atlas is among those 190, the proper fix touches ~4% of resources and keeps
tiling everywhere else - which is what "the proper fix keeps tiling" has
meant since 2ld, now with a number attached.

What is still unknown is whether those 190 are the scrambled ones. The user's
own report of this boot's screen is the other half of the measurement, and
the modes named - 22 and 27, both `_X` (pipe/bank-xor) variants - are
testable one at a time rather than blanket.

Not claimed: that mode 22 or 27 is the defect, or that `-rbgpulinear` is or
is not still earning its place. The second needs the screen, not a note.

## 2ln (boot 104, the screen) — TWO SEPARATE PROBLEMS, confirmed

User's report of boot 104, with `-rbgpulinear` OUT: "Artifacts are there on
widget and etc again but text is same".

So, measured on the screen rather than inferred:

1. **`-rbgpulinear` still earns its place.** The widget/Dock/chrome artifacts
   it fixed in boot 98 come straight back when it is removed, on a chip that
   now has the halt fixed and zero VM faults. Its ~80 % was not an artefact
   of the broken boot it was first measured in. It goes back IN.
2. **The text is unchanged by it, in either direction.** Boot 103 (all client
   resources forced to `m0`) and boot 104 (190 of 4788 tiled) render glyphs
   identically scrambled.

**These are two different defects, and only one of them is layout.** Every
layout intervention this project has made - kernel chooser, kernel
`getSurfaceInfo2`, rotation remap, and the natural per-resource modes - moves
the widget/chrome class and leaves the text class untouched. The text defect
is not a swizzle mode, on either side of the kernel boundary.

That retires the whole layout line for the text, and with it 2lm: forcing
`DetermineSwizzleMode` to LINEAR in userspace would be a fifth swing at a
parameter already shown not to matter for glyphs. It stays built and
unarmed, and is no longer the next step.

Boot 104 also re-dated the 2ld finding: what `-rbgpulinear` fixes and what it
does not are now measured on a healthy chip, which no earlier boot could
claim.

## 2lo (2026-10-21) — FOUND IT: replaceRegion's CPU-side tiling XOR is wrong

`tools/texprobe.swift` (user-supplied, run on boot 104, no reboot needed).
Full output: `logs/20261021-texprobe/texprobe-out.txt`. 72 cases: three
widths (37, 256, 1000) x h=48 x six upload paths x BGRA8 and R8, each written
twice so a stale read is distinguishable, with every BGRA pixel encoding its
own (x,y) and the write's tag.

**Seven BAD, and they are all the same defect:**

```
bgra8 w=256  managed-replace-tiles #1  stale=4096  foreign=0      moved=8192  d(0,32)x4096 d(0,-32)x4096
bgra8 w=256  managed-replace-tiles #2  stale=0     foreign=4096   moved=8192  d(0,-32)x4096 d(0,32)x4096
bgra8 w=1000 managed-replace-full  #1  stale=16768 foreign=0      moved=31232 d(48,16)x3968 d(-48,16)x3968 d(48,-16)x3968 d(-48,-16)x3968
bgra8 w=1000 managed-replace-full  #2  stale=0     foreign=16768  moved=31232 (same four deltas)
bgra8 w=1000 managed-replace-tiles #1  stale=16768 foreign=0      moved=31232 (same four deltas)
bgra8 w=1000 managed-replace-tiles #2  stale=0     foreign=16768  moved=31232 (same four deltas)
```

### It is displacement, not coherency

`stale=0` on every second write. The GPU never read the previous write's
data, so snoop/MTYPE bits on the system-page PTEs are **exonerated** - which
was the leading APU-specific hypothesis going in. `foreign` appears only
where the displacement maps a row outside the texture, so it is unwritten
memory being read, not a foreign mapping.

### The w=256 case decodes exactly: `y ^ 32`

`h=48`, `w=256`, 12288 pixels. Under a `y ^ 32` row mapping:

- rows 0-15 <-> rows 32-47 swap: 32 rows x 256 = **8192 moved by ±32** ✓
- rows 16-31 map to 48-63, outside a 48-row texture, so they read unwritten
  data: 16 rows x 256 = **4096 foreign** ✓

Exactly the measured split, with no residue. w=1000 is the same mechanism
with two x bits and one y bit (`x ^ 48` = `x ^ (16|32)`, `y ^ 16`), giving
four equal delta groups of 3968.

**A single-bit-flip displacement in the row/column index is a pipe/bank XOR**
- the `_X` in `4KB_D_X` (22) and `64KB_R_X` (27), the two tiled modes
`rbgpu-mode` counts on this chip. The CPU-side tiling computes a different
XOR than the GPU reads with.

### What the matrix narrows it to

| axis | result |
|---|---|
| **Format** | BGRA8 fails; **R8 is clean at all three widths, every path** |
| **Path** | only `replaceRegion`; `linear-buffer-tex` (also `.managed`, CPU write + `didModifyRange`), `private-blit` full and tiled, and `iosurface` are all OK |
| **Width** | `w=37` BGRA passes (small enough to be linear); 256 and 1000 fail |

So it is not storage mode, not managed memory, not the blit engine, not
IOSurface, and not sysmem coherency. It is specifically **the CPU-side
tiling routine that `MTLTexture.replace(region:)` uses for a tiled,
multi-byte-per-pixel surface.**

### Why this is the glyph defect

Glyph atlases and decoded images are CPU-produced bitmaps uploaded through
exactly that call. Window chrome, icons and anything IOSurface-backed are
not. That is the user's Safari photograph precisely: text and an image in
**one window**, different upload paths, different outcomes.

### It also resolves 2ln's tension, and REVIVES 2lm

Boot 103 forced client resources to `m0` and the text stayed broken, which
2ln read as "layout is exonerated for text". The narrower truth: `res +
0x1dc` is **kernel-side bookkeeping**, and a Metal client texture's real
layout is decided by the **userspace** AddrLib, which no kernel-side forcing
ever reached. Both observations stand together.

**2lm is therefore back on**, and now with a mechanism rather than as a sixth
swing at a parameter: forcing `amdMtl_HWL_DetermineSwizzleMode` to return
LINEAR makes client textures linear, and `w=37` plus every R8 case shows
linear BGRA uploads are **clean**. It is a workaround, not the fix - it costs
tiling bandwidth on client textures - but it is the direct test of this
diagnosis and it is already built.

The real fix is to find what XOR the CPU-side tiling path uses. 2lk proved
both AddrLibs are created with identical chipFamily/chipRevision/chipEngine/
`GB_ADDR_CONFIG = 0x242`, so if `replaceRegion`'s tiling went through AddrLib
it would agree. It does not agree, so that path is **not** using the AddrLib
configuration - a hand-rolled routine with Navi 21 pipe/packer constants is
the shape to look for, and it is the same shape as 2jp's firmware-table
defect and 2lk's dead end.

Not claimed: that the XOR bits are exactly `y^32`/`x^48` in general - those
are this geometry's instance of it. Nor that fixing `replaceRegion` fixes
every scrambled surface; only that this path is measurably broken and is the
path glyph atlases take.

## 2lp (2026-10-21) — the fork is ONE BIT: `ShouldUseSwBlt`

Following 2lo's measurement straight to the branch.

`-[GFXAAMD_MtlTexture replaceRegion:mipmapLevel:slice:withBytes:bytesPerRow:
bytesPerImage:]` (0x7ffb08d60cd7) calls
`amdMtl_HWL_ShouldUseSwBlt(AMD_DeviceSettings const*,
ATIMipmapBufferHeader const*)` at **0x7ffb08d36966**, which is the whole
decision in six instructions:

```
55              push %rbp
48 89 e5        mov  %rsp, %rbp
8a 47 02        mov  0x2(%rdi), %al      ; AMD_DeviceSettings + 0x02
c0 e8 07        shr  $0x7, %al           ; bit 7
5d              pop  %rbp
c3              ret
```

**One bit — bit 7 of `AMD_DeviceSettings + 0x02` — chooses a software blit
over the hardware one.** True means the CPU tiles the data itself, and that
software tiler is what computes the wrong pipe/bank XOR. Four call sites.

This closes the loop on 2lo's matrix with a mechanism: `private-blit` went
through the GPU blit engine and was clean at all three widths;
`replaceRegion` took the software path and was wrong by `y ^ 32`. Same
destination tiling, two different tilers, one of them broken.

### 2lp, built and unarmed

Stub over all twelve bytes:

```
31 c0    xor %eax, %eax      ; never use the SW blit
c3       ret
90 x9                        ; never executed
```

The first **8** bytes of this function are already unique in the driver's
`__text` (measured) - against 2lm, where a 14-byte prologue matched 2099
functions. All twelve are the find pattern. Behind `-rbgpuhwblt`, scoped to
Terminal alone, nothing registered unless the arg is set.

**Preferred over 2lm.** 2lm forces every client texture LINEAR: it avoids the
broken tiler but pays tiling bandwidth on everything. 2lp keeps tiling and
routes the upload through the engine already measured correct.

### What is NOT proven

texprobe measured the hardware blit correct writing a **`.private`** texture
from a staging buffer. `replaceRegion` on a **`.managed`** texture taking the
hardware path is a different combination and was never measured. So 2lp is a
well-motivated inference, not a demonstrated fix, and the boot is the test:

- **Terminal's text becomes readable** -> 2lo's diagnosis is confirmed and
  this is a usable workaround.
- **Unchanged** -> the hardware path is not correct for a managed
  destination either, and the software tiler's XOR has to be fixed directly.

Also unknown: **why bit 7 is set on this chip.**
`amdMtl_HWL_InitDeviceSettings` (0x7ffb08d2d700) and
`amdMtl_HWL_OverrideDeviceSettings` (0x7ffb08d2da8d) derive the settings from
`AMDCommonHwInfoRec`. Reading which condition sets that bit is the **proper**
fix - overriding the answer is a workaround over a decision that is itself
probably keyed on a Navi 21 assumption, the same shape as 2jp and 2lk. 2lp
is the fast confirmation; that reading is the fix.

Not claimed: that forcing the hardware blit is safe for every format, or
that `ShouldUseSwBlt` has no correctness reason to be true for some surfaces
(a format the blit engine cannot handle would be one). Terminal-only scoping
is the guard against finding that out the expensive way.

---

## 2lq (2026-10-21, boot 105): 2lp SHIPPED INERT - `section = 0` disables a Lilu user patch

Boot 105 ran with `-rbgpulinear` **and** `-rbgpuhwblt` in boot-args, kext
UUID `E29F22DF`, confirmed loaded by `kextstat`.
`rbgpu-boot` = 105, live and in `logs/20261021-023804-plugin/` (rule 8
satisfied). Chip state unchanged from 2ll: `stamp_ret=1`, `mapq_fails=0`,
zero VM faults, `gfx_min=gfx_max=0`.

**Observation (the user, by eye): Terminal's text is READABLE. The Claude
desktop app's text is fully unreadable.**

I read that as 2lp confirmed, and as the Terminal-only scoping proving
itself. **That was wrong, and withdrawn.** 2lp's patch was never applied.

### The defect

`UserPatcher::BinaryModPatch`'s last field is `section`. Lilu 1.7.3,
`kern_user.cpp:824` and `:850` (commit `0515f40b`, the version loaded here):

```c
for (size_t p = 0; p < binaryMod[i]->count; p++)
    if (binaryMod[i]->patches[p].section != ProcInfo::SectionDisabled) {
        hasPatches = true; break;
    }
if (!hasPatches) { DBGLOG("ignoring file %s ... no mods apply"); continue; }
...
if (patch.section == ProcInfo::SectionDisabled) {
    DBGLOG("skipping not requested patch %s for %lu", ...); continue;
}
```

`kern_user.hpp`: `static constexpr uint32_t SectionDisabled {0};`

**Both `kRb2lmPatch` and `kRb2lpPatch` were written with `section = 0`.** So
Lilu skipped the patch and never even read
`AMDRadeonX6000MTLDriver.bundle/.../AMDRadeonX6000MTLDriver`. Worse,
`onProcLoad` still returns `NoError`, so the hook logged **`2lp: ARMED`**
while patching nothing. `ProcInfo::section` is never read by Lilu at all -
only `BinaryModPatch::section` matters, and it must be non-zero.

### What boot 105 therefore measured

Nothing of 2lp. The kext was functionally identical to boot 104's
(`git diff 2464a9b..bf6d96b -- src/` is 122 added lines, all of them the
inert 2lp registration). The only effective delta from boot 104 is
`-rbgpulinear` back **IN**.

So the live reading is:

| Boot | `-rbgpulinear` | Terminal text |
|---|---|---|
| 103 | IN | recorded scrambled (`docs/PROBLEM-TEXT.md`, from a photograph) |
| 104 | OUT | scrambled |
| 105 | IN | **readable** |

Boot 103 and boot 105 had the same effective configuration and are recorded
with opposite results, so **one of those two rows is wrong**, and the
photograph that row 103 rests on is the older, boot-98-era one (CLAUDE.md
already warns that boot 98 was a broken-chip state). The honest position:
`-rbgpulinear` IN gives readable text in Terminal and does not in the Claude
desktop app, and the earlier "all apps scramble identically" claim is
unreliable because it was never taken app-by-app on a healthy chip.

2lo's software-tiler diagnosis is **untested**, not confirmed. It remains
the best-supported theory - texprobe's 72-case matrix is unaffected by this
- but no boot has exercised the stub.

### The recurring error, instance 27

This is the same error in its purest form yet: **a reading taken without
establishing what makes it meaningful.** The precondition - "the patch is
actually applied" - was checkable in Lilu's own source at any time, and the
hook's own log asserted the opposite of the truth. Rule 14 ("absence is not
a result") was written for the case where an instrument says nothing; this
is the case where **the instrument says ARMED and is lying.**

New rule, 20: **a registration that reports success is not evidence that a
patch applied.** Log the enabling field itself, and refuse when it is
disabled.

### The fix

`section = 1` on both patches, plus a guard in both
`rbgpu_register_mtllinear_2lm` and `rbgpu_register_hwblt_2lp` that logs
`INERT` and returns if the section is `SectionDisabled`, and an `ARMED
(patch section=%u)` that prints the value it depends on. Build UUID
`AD2476B6`, hosttest passes.

Boot 106 is 2lp's first real test, and it is also the first boot that tests
`-rbgpulinear`'s effect app-by-app rather than from one photograph.

---

## 2lr (2026-10-21, boot 106): the test surface was wrong, not just the patch

Boot 106, UUID `AD2476B6`, `rbgpu-boot` = 106, `b=106` on every counter,
`logs/20261021-025036-plugin/`. Chip healthy and unchanged: `stamp_ret=1`,
`mapq_fails=0`, zero VM faults, `gfx_min=gfx_max=0`.

`rbgpu-surf: forced=76` - `-rbgpulinear` active on all 76 kernel surfaces.
`rbgpu-mode: seen=4923 m0=4923 lin=1` - every client resource's
`res+0x1dc` bits 0:4 reads 0.

**`m0=4923` is NOT evidence that client textures are linear in memory.**
Boot 103 (`-rbgpulinear` IN) gave all-m0; boot 104 (OUT) gave 190 tiled of
4788; boot 106 (IN) gives all-m0 again. The counter tracks the flag, so it
is at least partly reading back our own forcing (rule 17). What it can
still say is consistent with 2lg/2lh/2lk: the kernel records LINEAR and
**userspace AddrLib lays the bytes out itself** from `hwInfo+0xa0`, never
asking the kernel. That is why forcing the kernel field fixes everything
the kernel lays out - chrome, Dock, widgets - and leaves app text alone.

### The capture could not test 2lp, for a reason that is not the section bug

No `2lp` line: the kernel buffer starts at 166 s and the boot-time lines had
wrapped, and `plugin_check.sh`'s nvram dump does not include `rbgpu-log`.
But even with the line, boot 106 could not have decided anything:

**2lp was scoped to Terminal, and Terminal's text is already readable
without it.** Boot 105 established that (2lq). The scoping that made 2lp
safe to try also made it unmeasurable - a fixed surface cannot show a fix.

### What is still broken, by the user's eye on boot 106

The **Claude desktop app**: body text fully unreadable. Terminal readable.

So 2lr re-points the patch at the Claude app's helper processes and drops
Terminal from the list entirely. `MatchAny` is `strstr(path, p->path)`
(Lilu 1.7.3 `kern_user.cpp:285`), so one entry, `"/Claude Helper"`, covers
`Claude Helper`, `(GPU)`, `(Renderer)` and `(Plugin)` under
`/Applications/Claude.app/Contents/Frameworks/`. Electron does its Metal
work in those helpers.

Dropping Terminal is deliberate: unpatched and already readable, it becomes
the **control**. If Terminal changes, the change did not come from this
patch.

### The two outcomes

| Claude app text on boot 107 | Reading |
|---|---|
| readable | 2lo's software tiler confirmed, and the fix generalises by widening the proc list |
| unchanged | the hardware blit is not correct for a `.managed` destination either, or the scramble is not tiling at all (2ln's original position), and `ShouldUseSwBlt` is a dead end |

Risk: this rewrites a system Metal driver inside the app the user talks to
Claude through. Blast radius is that app alone; if it renders worse or
dies, Claude Code in Terminal still works, and removing `-rbgpuhwblt` or
setting `-rbgpuoff` undoes it.

Build UUID `3AA5C1C3`, hosttest passes.

## 2ls (2026-10-21, boot 107): the capture could not answer, for the third time - fix the instrument

Boot 107 ran UUID `3AA5C1C3` (2lr, Claude-helper scope), `rbgpu-boot` = 107,
`rbgpu-arm` consumed, uptime 3 min at capture. **The Claude app's text is
still broken.**

That is the "unchanged" row of 2lr's table, which would retire
`ShouldUseSwBlt` - except the capture again cannot say whether the patch
applied. `logs/20261021-025825-plugin/log.txt` begins at **130 s**, and
`RGPU::init()` runs at boot. Tag census over that window:

```
34 2dw   25 2ds   17 2fe   17 2cx   16 2dx   9 2dr   8 2en   8 2dy   8 2dv
```

~140 lines per two minutes from one settled chain. The kernel buffer holds
about two minutes of it, so the plugin's own boot-time lines had wrapped
before `plugin_check.sh` ever ran - in boots 105, 106 and 107 alike. **Three
consecutive experiments were unreadable for the same mechanical reason, and
none of them was the hypothesis' fault.**

Rule 16 says the instrument is a suspect. Here the instrument was not wrong,
it was *loud*, and volume destroyed the evidence just as effectively.

### What 2ls changes

1. **The stamp chain goes quiet after four cycles.**
   `g_rb_stampchain_cycles` is incremented in
   `hooked_hwchannel_waitForHwStamp_2cx`, and 19 call sites across
   2cx/2ds/2dw/2dx/2dy/2dr/2en/2dv/2fe now go through
   `rbgpu_log_stamp(...)`, which drops past cycle 4. Everything they
   established is in JOURNAL under its own tag; none of it needs restating
   every 1.5 s.
2. **`SpecialAMDKey` 0x14 throttles from every 64th to every 4096th.** At
   ~50 polls/s, "every 64th" was still a line every 1.3 s. The exact count
   was already in `rbgpu-diag` as `req_0x14`, which does not wrap.
3. **The arming fact moves into the diag table**, which does not wrap:
   `hwblt_section`, `hwblt_scope`, `hwblt_onprocload` and
   `mtllinear_section`. A future boot can be read for whether a user patch
   applied without depending on a ring buffer surviving.

This is the general lesson behind rule 20, made operational: **a fact that
decides whether an experiment is interpretable belongs in storage that does
not wrap, not in a log.**

### Status of the hypothesis

Undecided, not refuted. Boot 108 is the first boot that can actually read
out whether the patch armed and scoped correctly. If `hwblt_section=1`,
`hwblt_onprocload=0` and `hwblt_scope=/Claude Helper` all appear *and* the
Claude app's text is still scrambled, **then** `ShouldUseSwBlt` is retired
and 2ln's "not a layout problem" position stands.

Worth stating now, before that boot: texprobe measured `iosurface` and
`private-blit` **clean**. Electron composites through IOSurface-backed
textures, so there is a real possibility the Claude app's glyphs never take
the `replaceRegion` path at all, in which case 2lp could not have fixed it
and the negative says nothing about 2lo's measurement.

Build UUID `76774D6D`, hosttest passes.
