## 2lt (2026-10-21, boot 108): the user patches can NEVER have applied - the dylib is not on disk

Boot 108, UUID `76774D6D` (2ls), `rbgpu-boot` = 108, armed. 2ls worked
exactly as intended: the arming facts survived in `RBGPUDiag`, read out of
`logs/20261021-030629-plugin/peer.plist`:

```
hwblt_section     = 1
hwblt_onprocload  = 0        (LiluAPI::Error::NoError)
hwblt_scope       = /Claude Helper
```

So the registration was accepted, enabled and scoped as designed. **The
Claude app's text is still broken.**

Note in passing: `rbgpu-diag`'s leading `d=70` is **dropped keys**, not a
count - 70 keys did not fit the NVRAM buffer, and the `*** NVRAM SUMMARY
FULL` line that says so had itself wrapped out of the log. The full table is
in the registry, which `plugin_check.sh` captures. Four boots were read
with that number misunderstood.

### The real reason, and it is structural

```
$ ls /System/Library/Extensions/AMDRadeonX6000MTLDriver.bundle/Contents/MacOS/
(empty)
```

On macOS 13+ the Metal driver bundles are stubs: the binary exists **only
inside the dyld shared cache**. Lilu's `BinaryModInfo` finds its patterns by
reading the file at `path` (`loadFilesForPatching`, `kern_user.cpp:838`
`FileIO::readFileToBuffer`). There is no file, so no lookups are built and
nothing is ever patched - and `onProcLoad` still returns `NoError`, exactly
as with the section bug.

Lilu *can* patch the shared cache: `loadDyldSharedCacheMapping` reads
`/System/Volumes/Preboot/Cryptexes/OS/System/Library/dyld/dyld_shared_cache_x86_64h.map`,
which exists here and does list our path at line 8413 - so the TEXT range
is discoverable. But the pattern **offsets** still come from the absent
file, and the `.map` key is that same absent path, so pointing
`BinaryModInfo::path` at an extracted copy would make `mapAddresses` match
nothing and fail `registerPatches` outright.

**Therefore 2lm, 2lp and 2lr were all inert from the start, for a second
and independent reason.** Fixing `section` in 2lq removed only the first of
two blockers. Nothing has ever been measured about `ShouldUseSwBlt` on this
machine.

Writing the binary into `/System/Library/Extensions` is not an option: it
is the sealed system volume, and this project does not install there.

### What this costs and what survives

Withdrawn: every reading attributed to 2lm/2lp/2lr, and the framing in
`docs/PROBLEM-TEXT.md` §"the fork is one bit".

Survives: 2lo's texprobe matrix (72 cases, boot 104) - `replaceRegion` on a
tiled BGRA8 destination displaces rows by exactly `y ^ 32`, while
`private-blit`, `linear-buffer-tex` and `iosurface` are clean at all three
widths. That is a measurement of the chip, not of a hook.

Also worth recording against the hypothesis itself: the static trace of
`InitDeviceSettings` (0x7ffb08d2d700) says bit 23 of the settings qword -
the bit `ShouldUseSwBlt` returns - is **cleared** by step 5's mask
(`0xFFFFFFFD_FF7CDFFF + 0x880000` = `0xFFFFFFFE_0004DFFF`) and never set
again outside `getenv` overrides and a per-bit debug dispatcher at
`0x7ffb08d01xxx`. A grep of all 953k disassembly lines for `$0x800000` ors
and `0xFF7FFFFF` masks finds no other writer. If that reading is right,
`ShouldUseSwBlt` was already returning false and 2lp would have been a
no-op even if it had applied - which means the software tiler is the wrong
mechanism for 2lo's displacement, and the corruption lives elsewhere in
`replaceRegion`.

### The one route left

Userspace cannot be patched. The kernel can, and 2lk already found the
channel that reaches the code laying out every client texture:

```
getHardwareInfo(_sAMD_GET_HW_INFO_VALUES*)  ->  +0xa0  ->  gfx10_HwInfoInitData
  -> amdMtl_HWL_InitAddrLibHwRegFields: regValue.gbAddrConfig = hwInfo->0xa4
  -> AddrCreate -> Addr2ComputeSurfaceInfo -> every client texture
```

`getHardwareInfo` is **already hooked** (2lk, observe-only), so changing
what userspace is told needs no new `RouteRequest` (rule 3). `a0=242` was
called "correct" because it matches the chip - 4 pipes, 4 packers, 1 SE -
but correct-for-the-chip is not the same as the value Apple's Navi 21
AddrLib needs in order to compute the pipe/bank XOR the hardware actually
performs. A single-bit row displacement is precisely a pipe-XOR mismatch.

Next step, and it is static work with no boot: read the swizzle equation
out of `amdMtl_HWL_InitAddrLibHwRegFields` and `Addr2ComputeSurfaceInfo` in
`build/re/AMDRadeonX6000MTLDriver` and determine which `GB_ADDR_CONFIG`
field, at which value, removes a `y ^ 32` term. Guess-and-check at one boot
per candidate is the fallback, not the plan.

---

## 2lu (2026-10-21, static, no boot): the CPU tiler's inputs, mapped end to end

With userspace unpatchable (2lt), the question became what the kernel can
change. Read out of `build/re/AMDRadeonX6000MTLDriver`; every address is a
symbol from `build/re/mtl-syms.txt`.

### Apple has a second, hand-written GFX10 tiler, and it is not AddrLib

`replaceRegion`'s CPU path does not go through AddrLib. There is a separate
file-local family keyed on a `CpuTexInterfaceRec`:

```
amdMtl_HWL_AllocCpuTexInterface(const _sAMD_GET_HW_INFO_VALUES*, unsigned)  0x7ffb08c98237
amdMtl_HWL_TextureReplaceRegion(const CpuTexInterfaceRec*, ...)             0x7ffb08c97268
  GFX10_TextureReplaceTiles / GFX10_TextureReplacePixels                    0x7ffb08c97a72 / 0x7ffb08c97832
  GFX10_GenerateTileAddresses                                              0x7ffb08c9876e
  GFX10_GetSwizzlePattern(const CpuTexInterfaceRec*, AddrSwizzleMode,
                          AddrResourceType, unsigned)                      0x7ffb08c99543
```

`GFX10_GetSwizzlePattern` returns `table + (index << 6)` - 64-byte entries,
16 dwords, the shape of an AddrLib swizzle-equation bit-id array - from one
of several tables (`0x7ffb08fc1730`, `0x7ffb08fc6870`, `0x7ffb08fbef30`, ...)
selected by swizzle mode. The index is

```
index = rec[0x02] * 0x23 + rec[0x03] * 5 - 0x118 + elemLog2
      = (pipeInterleaveLog2 - 8) * 35 + pipesLog2 * 5 + elemLog2
```

### Every input comes from `hwInfo + 0xa0`

`amdMtl_HWL_AllocCpuTexInterface` builds the whole record from that one
dword - GB_ADDR_CONFIG, the field 2lk identified:

```
rcx = hwInfo->0xa0
rec[0x00] = 0x100 << ((rcx >> 3) & 7)     pipeInterleaveBytes
rec[0x02] = ((rcx >> 3) & 7) | 8          pipeInterleaveLog2
rec[0x03] = rcx & 7                       pipesLog2
rec[0x04] = (rcx >> 0x13) & 3             NUM_SHADER_ENGINES
rec[0x05] = (rcx >> 8) & 7                numPkrsLog2
rec[0x28] = 0x4b * rec[0x02] - 0x258 + 5 * K
            K = (numPkrs <= 1) ? pipesLog2 : pipesLog2 + 2*numPkrs - 2
```

For this chip's `0x242`: interleaveLog2 = 8 (256 B), pipesLog2 = 2 (4 pipes),
SEs = 0 (1 SE), pkrsLog2 = 2 (4 packers). Pattern index = 0*35 + 2*5 + 2 =
**12** for BGRA8. **All four derivations are faithful to the register.**

`rec[0x28]` - the only packer-dependent term - is added only for certain
modes and only when `rec[0x2c] & 2`, which comes from the second argument:

```
movq (%r15), %rax ; movl 0xa0(%rax), %esi ; shrl %esi ; andl $1
```

a single bit of a `+0xa0` field. **Not asserted to be GB_ADDR_CONFIG**: the
pointer is `(%r15)`, a different object from the `0x1a0(%r15)` passed as
`hwInfo`. `InitDeviceSettings` reads `AMDCommonHwInfoRec+0xa0` with the same
`shrl/andl $1` expression, so the two may or may not be the same struct.
Unresolved, and it matters: that bit is what switches the CPU tiler between
packer-unaware and packer-aware patterns.

### The uncomfortable conclusion

The inputs are correct, and they are the only thing the kernel can reach. So
either the pattern **table** has no correct entry for a 4-pipe / 4-packer /
1-SE GFX10.3 part, or the packer-aware fork is being taken wrongly. Feeding
a *false* GB_ADDR_CONFIG cannot be the fix on its own: the GPU reads tiled
surfaces according to the real hardware register, so lying to userspace
would break the agreement that currently holds for everything except this
path.

That leaves three levers, in order of how much is already known:

1. **Make the two agree by moving the hardware**, not the report.
   `GB_ADDR_CONFIG` (dword `0x13de`, BASE_IDX 0) is a GC register the driver
   programs. If Apple's CPU tiler has a correct pattern for some
   (pipes, pkrs) the chip can actually be configured with, setting both the
   register and `hwInfo+0xa0` to it makes CPU and GPU agree. This is the
   only kernel-side route that does not require lying to one side, and it
   is also the riskiest thing in this project since 2ks - a wrong
   `GB_ADDR_CONFIG` is a global memory-layout change.
2. **Confirm the fork bit first**, since it is cheap: resolve what object
   `(%r15)` is at `0x7ffb08c16918` and whether its `+0xa0` is reachable
   from the kernel. If it is, one bit decides packer-aware vs not, with no
   geometry change at all.
3. Keep client surfaces off the tiled path entirely. `-rbgpulinear` already
   forces the kernel's 76 surfaces linear and `rbgpu-mode` reports every
   client resource as mode 0, yet app text stays broken - consistent with
   2lk's finding that userspace lays out its own textures regardless. So
   this needs the *userspace* mode forced, which 2lt proved unpatchable.

Lever 2 is the next step: static, cheap, and it either hands us a one-bit
fix or rules one out before anything touches a GC register.

---

## 2lv (2026-10-21, static, no boot): lever 2 resolved - the fork bit is NOT kernel-reachable

2lu left one thing unresolved: the CPU tiler's packer-aware fork comes from
`(%r15)->0xa0` bit 1 at `0x7ffb08c16918` in
`-[GFXAAMD_MtlDevice amdMtl_LazyInit]`, and `(%r15)` was a different object
from the `hwInfo` passed alongside it. Resolved now, in the device
constructor at `0x7ffb08d09e7e`:

```
7ffb08d09ece   leaq (%rbx,%r12), %r13          ; r12 = ivar off 0x7ffb434b2010
7ffb08d09edc   movq %r13, (%rbx,%r14)          ; DeviceMembersRec+0x00 = r13
7ffb08d09f81   movq 0x1a0(%rbx,%r14), %rsi     ; _sAMD_GET_HW_INFO_VALUES*
7ffb08d09f89   movq %r13, %rdi
7ffb08d09f8f   callq gfx10_HwInfoInitData       ; (GFX10_HwInfoRec*, vals*, u32)
7ffb08d09fac   testb $0x40, 0xa0(%rbx,%r12)     ; same dword, bit 6
7ffb08d09fd4   callq 0x7ffb08d2d700             ; InitDeviceSettings(settings, r13)
```

**`DeviceMembersRec+0x00` is a `GFX10_HwInfoRec` embedded as an ivar of
`GFXAAMD_MtlDevice`** (`r13 = self + ivarOffset`), not a kernel-filled
buffer. So the fork bit is **bit 1 of `GFX10_HwInfoRec + 0xa0`**, a
userspace flags dword.

### What `gfx10_HwInfoInitData` does and does not do

```
7ffb08cb40ce   movl 0xa0(%rdi), %r9d        ; READS the flags dword on entry
...
7ffb08cb420d   andl $-0x41, %r9d            ; conditionally clears bit 6 only
7ffb08cb4211   movl %r9d, 0xa0(%rdi)
7ffb08cb4218   movl 0xa0(%rsi), %r9d        ; vals+0xa0 = GB_ADDR_CONFIG
7ffb08cb421f   movl %r9d, 0xa4(%rdi)        ; -> GFX10_HwInfoRec+0xa4
```

It reads `+0xa0` already populated, touches **bit 6 and nothing else**, and
never writes bit 1. Bit 1 is set before this call, by code not yet located -
plausibly a static per-ASIC template, since no store to that ivar's `+0xa0`
appears in the obvious addressing form anywhere in `__text`.

**Answer to lever 2: no. The fork bit is not copied from
`_sAMD_GET_HW_INFO_VALUES`, so the kernel cannot set it.** Lever 2 does not
yield a one-bit fix; it rules one out, which is what a cheap static check is
for.

### Three things confirmed on the way

1. **`GFX10_HwInfoRec + 0xa4` = GB_ADDR_CONFIG, copied verbatim from
   `_sAMD_GET_HW_INFO_VALUES + 0xa0`.** 2lk's channel is exact, and it
   remains the only geometry input the kernel controls.
2. **`InitDeviceSettings`'s second argument is the `GFX10_HwInfoRec`**
   (`0x7ffb08d09fd4` passes `r13`), so its reads of `0xa0`/`0xcc`/`0xcd`
   are fields of that record. 2lp's comment calling it `AMDCommonHwInfoRec`
   was imprecise, which is part of why the bit-23 trace was hard to place.
3. **Bit 6 of the same dword gates whether `InitDeviceSettings` runs at
   all** (`testb $0x40, 0xa0(%rbx,%r12)`; `je` skips it). A flags dword that
   both selects swizzle patterns and gates device-settings init is worth
   knowing about before anything perturbs it.

### Where this leaves the text defect

Of 2lu's three levers: lever 3 was already dead (needs userspace), lever 2
is now dead (not kernel-reachable), and **lever 1 is what is left** -
program the chip's own `GB_ADDR_CONFIG` (dword `0x13de`, BASE_IDX 0) to a
geometry Apple's CPU tiler has a correct pattern for, and report the same
value through `hwInfo+0xa0`, so the CPU tiler and the GPU agree. That is a
global memory-layout change and the riskiest step since 2ks.

One cheaper thing comes first, and it is still static: **find where
`GFX10_HwInfoRec+0xa0` is initialized.** If any part of it derives from a
kernel-supplied value, lever 2 comes back from the dead at a fraction of
lever 1's risk. If it is a hardcoded per-ASIC constant, that is worth
knowing before touching a GC register.

---

## 2lw (2026-10-21, static): 2lv's conclusion corrected - the fork bit IS set, and every tiler input is right

2lv said the CPU tiler's packer-aware fork bit "is not kernel-reachable" and
that `gfx10_HwInfoInitData` "touches bit 6 and nothing else". **Both are
wrong.** The grep that supported it missed every store, because objdump
separates mnemonic and operands with a tab and the pattern used spaces.
There are **nine** writes to `GFX10_HwInfoRec+0xa0` in that function, and
they are a per-ASIC cascade dispatched on `chipFamily`.

### The cascade

`gfx10_HwInfoInitData(GFX10_HwInfoRec *rdi, _sAMD_GET_HW_INFO_VALUES *rsi,
uint32 edx)`:

```
7ffb08cb40ce  movl 0xa0(%rdi), %r9d      ; keep the original
7ffb08cb40d8  orl  $0x40, %ecx           ; set bit 6 = "hw info usable"
7ffb08cb40db  movl %ecx, 0xa0(%rdi)
7ffb08cb40e7  movl 0x8(%rsi), %r10d      ; chipFamily  -> rec+0x10
7ffb08cb424a  testl $0x3f0000, %eax      ; edx = 3rd arg, masked 0xfff0000
7ffb08cb4255  movl 0xa0(%rdi), %eax ; orl $0xc, %eax
7ffb08cb426f  cmpl $0x9,  %r10d ; ja ...     -> family cascade
7ffb08cb4311  cmpl $0x13, %r10d ; ja ...
7ffb08cb438f  cmpl $0x27, %r10d ; ja ...
7ffb08cb440b  cmpl $0x31, %r10d ; ja ...
7ffb08cb448a  cmpl $0x3b, %r10d ; ja ...
```

Each arm writes AddrLib's family/revision at `rec+0x00`, a constant block at
`rec+0x84`/`0x94`/`0xb4`, a caps word, and the low two bits of `rec+0xa0`:

| family | AddrLib fam/rev | `rec+0xa0` bits 0:1 |
|---|---|---|
| <= 0x09 | 0x8F rev 7 | `&= ~3` -> **0** |
| 0x0a..0x13 | 0x8F rev 7 | `&= ~3; incl` -> **1** |
| 0x14..0x27 | 0x8F rev 7 | `&= ~3` -> **0** |
| **0x28..0x31** | **0x8F rev 8** | `&= ~3; orl $2` -> **2** |
| 0x32..0x3b | 0x8F rev 8 | `&= ~3; orl $2` -> **2** |

**This chip measured `fam = 0x28`** (boot 108, `rbgpu-hwi`:
`dev=1681 fam=00000028 ras=4 shd=6 gbac=00000242 hw=00000242`), so it takes
the `0x7ffb08cb4411` arm: AddrLib family `0x8F` **revision 8**,
`rec+0x08 = 1`, and `rec+0xa0` bits 0:1 = **2 - bit 1 SET**.

### So the fork is already on the packer-aware side

`AllocCpuTexInterface` sets `rec[0x2c] = (rec[0x2c] & ~2) | ((flag & 1) << 1)`
with `flag = (hwInfoRec->0xa0 >> 1) & 1 = 1`, and `GFX10_GetSwizzlePattern`
tests `0x2c & 2` before adding the packer-dependent offset `rec[0x28]`. With
bit 1 set, **the packer-aware path is taken.**

Corrected reading of lever 2: the bit **is** kernel-reachable - `chipFamily`
comes from `_sAMD_GET_HW_INFO_VALUES+0x08`, which the kernel fills - but it
is **already set the way it should be**, so flipping it is not a fix. And a
family override is not a one-bit change: it would also move AddrLib's
revision 8 -> 7 and three constant blocks. Lever 2 stays closed, for the
opposite reason to the one 2lv gave.

### What that leaves, stated precisely

Every input Apple's CPU tiler takes is **correct for this chip**: 4 pipes,
4 packers, 1 SE, 256 B interleave (2lu, all four faithful to `GB_ADDR_CONFIG
= 0x242`), AddrLib family 0x8F revision 8, and the packer-aware fork on. So
2lo's `y ^ 32` row displacement is **not a configuration error**. It is
either

(a) the pattern **tables** having no correct entry for a 4-pipe / 4-packer
    GFX10.3 part, or
(b) a defect downstream of pattern selection, in
    `GFX10_GenerateTileAddresses` (`0x7ffb08c9876e`) or
    `GFX10_TextureReplaceTiles` (`0x7ffb08c97a72`).

Both are decidable statically, and (a) first because it is cheaper: 2lu
already fixed the selected index at **12** for BGRA8
(`(interleaveLog2-8)*35 + pipesLog2*5 + elemLog2 = 0 + 10 + 2`). Read the
64-byte equation at `table + (12 << 6)` for the mode-22/25/27 tables
(`0x7ffb08fc1730`, `0x7ffb08fc6870`, `0x7ffb08fbef30`), decode the bit-ids,
and compare with the equation AddrLib itself uses for the same config - the
one the **GPU** follows through the kernel's AddrLib. A difference in a
single y bit is the whole defect, located exactly.

### Method note

This is the second time in one session that a wrong regex produced a
confident negative (2lv here, and the `rbgpu-diag d=70` misreading in 2lt).
Rule 16 covers an instrument that is a suspect; the variant worth naming is
that **a search is an instrument too**. When a grep returns nothing, check
it against a case known to be present before reporting the absence - here,
`movl %ecx, 0xa0(%rdi)` at `0x7ffb08cb40db` was known to exist and would
have failed the pattern immediately.

---

## 2lx (2026-10-21, static): the pattern tables are fine - the GROUP SELECTION is the suspect, and the kernel can move it

### (1) The tables are populated

`GFX10_GetSwizzlePattern`'s mode dispatch, decoded from the bitmasks:

| mask | meaning | modes |
|---|---|---|
| `0x6660666` | "2D with pattern" set | 1,2,5,6,9,10,17,18,21,**22**,**25**,26 - **not 27** |
| `0x4440444` | takes the `0x99609` arm | 2,6,10,18,**22**,26 |
| `0x600060` | takes the `0x99646` arm | 5,6,21,22 |

So **mode 22 (4KB_D_X)** -> `0x99609`, and with `rec[0x2c] & 2` set - which
2lw established it is on this chip - `jne 0x9965d` -> table
**`0x7ffb08fbb6f0`**. **Mode 25 (64KB_S_X)** -> table `0x7ffb08fc1870`,
packer-unaware. Mode 27 is dispatched elsewhere.

Dumped `0x7ffb08fbb6f0` as 64-byte / 32 x uint16 rows (section
`__TEXT,__const`, base `0x7ffb08fb46a0`). Rows 0-30 are all real equations,
10-12 non-zero terms each, **grouped in fives** - group `g` occupying rows
`5g .. 5g+4`, one row per `elemLog2` 0..4:

```
 17  0020 0030 0000 0000 0010 0010 0000 0000 0020 0000 0004 ...   group 3, elem 2
 22  0040 0050 0000 0000 0010 0010 0000 0000 0000 0000 0004 ...   group 4, elem 2
```

**Possibility (1) as stated is dead: there is no missing or zeroed entry.**
And note the shape of the difference between adjacent groups - `0020 0030`
versus `0040 0050`, a one-bit shift in the leading terms. That is exactly
what a `y ^ 32` displacement looks like: not a wrong table, **a wrong row**.

### Which row this chip uses

Correcting 2lu on one point: on the packer-aware arm the pipes/interleave
index in `eax` is **discarded**. `0x9965d` does `addl 0x28(%rdi), %ecx` on
the raw 4th argument, so

```
index = elemLog2 + rec[0x28]
rec[0x28] = 0x4b * interleaveLog2 - 0x258 + 5 * K
K         = (numPkrs <= 1) ? pipesLog2 : pipesLog2 + 2*numPkrs - 2
```

This chip: interleaveLog2 8 -> `0x4b*8 - 0x258 = 0`; numPkrs 2 > 1 ->
`K = 2 + 4 - 2 = 4`; so `rec[0x28] = 20` and **index = 22** for BGRA8 -
group 4, which is the row dumped above.

### The lever this opens

**Every input to `K` comes from `GB_ADDR_CONFIG`, which reaches userspace
only through `hwInfo+0xa0` - the field the kernel fills and 2lk already
hooks.** So the kernel can move the CPU tiler to a different row *without
touching any GC register*. The candidate set is small and enumerable,
varying only `NUM_PKRS` (bits 10:8):

| reported numPkrs | K | group | index (BGRA8) |
|---|---|---|---|
| 0 or 1 | 2 | 2 | 12 |
| **2 (actual)** | **4** | **4** | **22** |
| 3 | 6 | 6 | 32 |

`numPkrs <= 1` is additionally interesting because index 12 is also what the
**packer-unaware** arm computes from 2lu's formula, so that candidate makes
the two arms agree.

**Not claimed:** that any of these is correct. `NUM_PKRS` as reported also
feeds userspace AddrLib's own pattern choice for client *surface layout*,
while the GPU reads those surfaces per the **real** hardware register. A
candidate that fixes `replaceRegion` could therefore break the agreement
that currently holds for everything else. This is a real experiment with a
visible failure mode - worse corruption, not a hang - and it is undone by
removing the boot-arg.

### (2) Downstream is thin

`GFX10_GenerateTileAddresses` (`0x7ffb08c9876e`) takes the swizzle mode and
resource type out of the mipmap header at `0x3c(%rsi)`
(`>>4 & 0x3f` and `>>0xa & 3`), zeroes a 0x140-byte stack workspace and
calls into the coord->index table builder with
`(rec, resourceType, swizzleMode, ...)`. Everything about layout arrives
through the pattern; there is no second source of address math to be wrong
on its own. So **(2) is thin and (1)'s row selection is the locus.**

### Next

Implement the `NUM_PKRS` override inside the existing 2lk `getHardwareInfo`
hook - no new `RouteRequest` (rule 3) - behind a boot-arg that carries the
value, so the three candidates are three boots and an unarmed boot changes
nothing. Record the reported and real values in `rbgpu-hwi` and in the diag
table so the capture can prove which value userspace actually got (rule 20).

---

## 2ly (2026-10-21): the NUM_PKRS override - built, not armed

Implemented inside the existing 2lk `getHardwareInfo` hook, so no new
`RouteRequest` (rule 3). Build UUID `BF5F3738`, hosttest passes.

`rbgpu_pkrs=N` (N in 0..7, via `PE_parse_boot_argn`) rewrites bits 10:8 of
`_sAMD_GET_HW_INFO_VALUES + 0xa0` on **every** call, after the 2lk sample is
taken so `rbgpu-hwi`'s `gbac=` still records the value the kernel was given.
Absent or out of range, nothing is written and the hook stays 2lk's
observer, which it says in the log.

Per rule 20 the arming facts go to the diag table, which does not wrap:
`pkrs_arg` (the value, or -1 for unarmed), `pkrs_was_gbac`, `pkrs_now_gbac`,
`pkrs_writes`. A capture must be able to prove which value userspace got
without depending on a log that has already rolled.

### The experiment

One boot per candidate. The chip's own `GB_ADDR_CONFIG` stays `0x242`
throughout; only the reported copy moves.

| boot-arg | reported numPkrs | group | BGRA8 row |
|---|---|---|---|
| none | 2 | 4 | 22 - today's behaviour |
| `rbgpu_pkrs=1` | 1 | 2 | 12 |
| `rbgpu_pkrs=3` | 3 | 6 | 32 |

`rbgpu_pkrs=1` first: group 2 is also what the packer-unaware arm computes,
so it is the one candidate where both arms of `GFX10_GetSwizzlePattern`
agree.

### What each outcome means

- **App text becomes readable** - the row was the defect, 2lo's `y ^ 32` is
  explained, and the remaining question is whether client surface layout
  still agrees with the GPU (watch chrome and widgets, not just text).
- **Text unchanged, everything else fine** - the row is not the defect;
  2lx's locus is wrong and (2) deserves the full read after all.
- **Everything gets worse** - the reported value does feed client surface
  layout, which is itself worth knowing: it would prove userspace AddrLib
  takes its geometry from this field, and bound how far this lever can be
  pushed.

Removing the boot-arg undoes all of it. `-rbgpuoff` remains the rescue.

---

## 2lz (2026-10-21, boot 109): `rbgpu_pkrs=1` is MUCH worse - and that is the most informative result in this stretch

Boot 109, UUID `BF5F3738` (2ly), `rbgpu-boot` = 109, armed, boot-args
`-rbgpulinear -rbgpuhwblt rbgpu_pkrs=1`. Read live from `RBGPUDiag`:

```
pkrs_arg      = 1
pkrs_was_gbac = 578   = 0x242   (the chip's real register)
pkrs_now_gbac = 322   = 0x142   (NUM_PKRS 2 -> 1)
pkrs_writes   = 46
```

The override applied, on all 46 `getHardwareInfo` calls. Group moves from 4
to 2, BGRA8 row from 22 to 12, exactly as 2lx predicted.

### What it looked like

**Qualitatively worse, and a different class of corruption.** Not glyph
scramble: whole-window blocky noise in bands - dense green/blue speckle with
a regular block grid, the Dock strip shredded, large regions reading as
garbage (user's photographs, boot 109). Then **restarting the Claude app
brought it back to the familiar glyph scramble.**

### What it proves

1. **The kernel CAN reach client texture layout through `hwInfo+0xa0`.**
   This is the first time anything the kernel reports has visibly changed
   app-owned rendering. 2lg/2lh's "out of this plugin's reach" is dead for
   good, and 2lk's channel is live, not just readable.
2. **Group 2 is not the fix.** Row 12 is far worse than row 22.
3. The restart behaviour is consistent with surfaces laid out under one
   geometry being read under another: the app's pre-restart textures were
   mixed with post-change compositing, and recreating them removed the
   mixture. **Not asserted** - no measurement distinguishes that from other
   explanations, and n=1.

### What it argues about 2lx's locus

The chip's real value (`NUM_PKRS = 2`, group 4, row 22) produces **only**
the glyph defect, while one step away produces whole-surface destruction.
That asymmetry is hard to reconcile with "the row is simply wrong". If row
22 were wrong in the way 2lo's `y ^ 32` suggests, a neighbouring row would
be expected to be comparably wrong, not catastrophically worse; and the
large clean regions at `0x242` say the CPU tiler and the GPU already agree
for most surfaces.

So **2lx's locus is weakened by its own experiment.** The row selection
looks right, and the residual glyph defect is narrower than "wrong swizzle
pattern" - which points back at (2), the code downstream of pattern
selection, that 2lx called thin on a partial read.

`rbgpu_pkrs=3` (group 6, row 32) would complete the enumeration, but the
prior is now poor: it is a larger step in the same direction that just
failed, and the expected result is more of the same destruction. Recorded
as available, not recommended.

### Status

Boot-arg reverted. The chip itself was never touched - `GB_ADDR_CONFIG`
stayed `0x242` throughout - so removing `rbgpu_pkrs` restores boot 108's
behaviour exactly. 2ly stays in the tree, unarmed, because it is the only
demonstrated lever from the kernel into client texture layout and the next
hypothesis may want it.

---

## 2ma (2026-10-21, static): the pattern format decoded, and the row hypothesis closed from the static side too

Full read of `UpdateTileCoord2IdxTableIfNeeded` (`0x7ffb08c98578`), the
function `GFX10_GenerateTileAddresses` calls to turn a swizzle pattern into
the coordinate->index tables the CPU tiler actually walks.

### The pattern format, proven

**2lx decoded the entries wrong.** The builder reads them with an **8-byte
stride** (`movzwl (%rax,%rdi,8)`), so a 64-byte entry is **8 qwords**, one
per swizzled address bit - not 32 uint16s. Each qword is four uint16 masks,
and the two build loops prove what the first two are:

```
X table:  for x in 0..2^xbits-1:
              for i in 0..n-1:  bit_i = popcount(pattern[i].f0 & x) & 1
              tbl_x[x] |= (bits << 8)        ; f0 at qword offset 0
Y table:  for y in 0..2^ybits-1:
              for i in 0..n-1:  bit_i = popcount(pattern[i].f1 & y) & 1
              tbl_y[y] |= (bits << 8)        ; f1 at qword offset 2
```

So **f0 is the X mask and f1 is the Y mask**, and each address bit is the
**parity** of the selected coordinate bits - an XOR equation, exactly
AddrLib's form. Decoded, this chip's row 22 reads:

```
bit0 = x6 ^ y4 ^ y6      bit4 = x2
bit1 = x4 ^ y4           bit5 = (f2 bit3)
bit2 = (f2 bit2)         bit6 = x3
bit3 = y3                bit7 = x5 ^ y2 ^ y5
```

### How many of those bits are used

`n = rec[6 + swizzleMode] - 8`, and `rec[6..]` is the per-mode block-size
table `AllocCpuTexInterface` writes as constants: modes 0/1/2 -> 8,
5/6/21/**22** -> **0x0c**, 9/10/17/18/24/25/26/27 -> 0x10, everything else
0. So **mode 22 (4KB_D_X) uses only the first FOUR** pattern bits - block
`2^12` = 4 KB, 256 B linear below. Note `y5` does not appear in those four
at all; it selects the tile, not the position within it.

There is also a hard guard: `blockLog2 < 9` returns **without building
anything**, leaving the previous tables in place. That is only hit by the
linear/256 B modes, which need no swizzle, but it is a stale-state path
worth remembering.

### The row selection is correct - AddrLib uses the same arithmetic

AddrLib's own `Gfx10Lib::HwlInitGlobalParams` (`0x7ffb08d952d0`) builds its
pattern-index base as

```
0x5b20 += pipesLog2 * 5
if (numPkrs > 1)  0x5b20 += 10*numPkrs - 10
```

and `Gfx10Lib::GetSwizzlePatternInfo` (`0x7ffb08d96ce0`) adds that base to
`elemLog2` (`addl 0x5b20(%r14), %ebx`). Apple's CPU tiler computes

```
rec[0x28] = 0x4b*interleaveLog2 - 0x258 + 5*(pipesLog2 + 2*numPkrs - 2)
          = 5*pipesLog2 + 10*numPkrs - 10            (at 256 B interleave)
```

**The same formula.** The hand-written CPU tiler picks its row with
AddrLib's own index arithmetic, so row 22 is not a wrong guess - it is what
AddrLib would select for this chip. (Not verified: that both sides share the
same additive base constant, only that the pipes/packers terms are
identical.)

**So the static reading now agrees with 2lz's hardware result.** The row is
right; the row hypothesis is closed from both directions.

### Where that leaves the glyph defect

Not in pattern selection, and not in the parity tables, whose construction
is straightforward and matches the equation form. What has **not** been read
is how `GFX10_GenerateTileAddresses` combines `tbl_x`, `tbl_y` and the tile
index into a final address, and `GFX10_TextureReplaceTiles` /
`GFX10_TextureAccessRegion` above it. That is the remaining unexamined
ground, and it is where a `y ^ 32` - a tile-index error rather than a
within-tile swizzle error - would live. **y5 selects the tile for a 4 KB
block at 32 bpp**, which makes a tile-index defect the better-fitting
hypothesis for 2lo's measurement than anything inside the pattern.

---

## 2mb (2026-10-21, static): the tile address assembled, and where its final XOR comes from

`GFX10_GenerateTileAddresses` is `0x7ffb08c9876e..0x7ffb08c99278` (0xb0a
bytes). The part that matters is the per-tile epilogue at
`0x7ffb08c99107..0x7ffb08c99202`.

### How a tile address is built

Two parity loops over the same pattern entries 2ma decoded, one per axis:

```
; Y, from f1 (qword+2)                  ; X, from f0 (qword+0)
c = tileY << shY                        c = tileX << shX
for i in 0..n-1:                        for i in 0..n-1:
    m  = pat[i].f1                          m  = pat[i].f0
    b  = popcount(m & c) & 1                b  = popcount(m & c) & 1
    if (m == 0) b = dflt                    if (m == 0) b = dflt
    yp |= b << i                            xp |= b << i

xp ^= yp                     ; the two axes combine by XOR
addr  = base + ((xp << 8) ^ lowbits)
addr ^= TERM                 ; 0x7ffb08c991e5  xorq -0x210(%rbp), %rdi
call  tileWriter(addr, ...)  ; 0x7ffb08c99202
```

The `<< 8` places the pattern bits at address bit 8 and up, which agrees
with 2ma: 256 B is linear, and mode 22's four pattern bits occupy bits
8..11, the 4 KB block. The `cmovel` default - when a pattern mask is zero
the bit is taken from a register rather than the parity - is worth knowing
about but not yet traced.

`GFX10_PartialTileCallback` (`0x7ffb08c99278`) is the other half: it clamps
the tile rect against the surface, computes
`src = data[0x08] + y*data[0x44] + (x << data[0x48])`, and hands the writer
at `data[0x10]` the tile address plus `&tbl_x[x & (2^xbits-1)]` and
`&tbl_y[y & (2^ybits-1)]`. So **within-tile position comes from the low
coordinate bits only** - confirming 2ma's point that `y5` of a 48-row BGRA8
surface selects the *tile*, not the offset inside it.

### The final XOR term, and one suspicious instruction

`-0x210(%rbp)` is built once, at `0x7ffb08c98953`:

```
al  = rec[0x02]          ; pipeInterleaveLog2   (8 for 256 B)
cl  = rec[0x03]          ; pipesLog2            (2 on this chip)
ecx = 1 << cl                               ; = 4
ecx = bzhi(saved_r9d, ecx)                  ; keep low ECX bits
eax = ecx << al
eax = bzhi(eax, ebx)
-0x210(%rbp) = eax
```

**`bzhi`'s second operand is a bit INDEX, and the value passed is
`1 << pipesLog2` rather than `pipesLog2`.** AddrLib masks a pipe/bank xor
with `(1 << pipeBits) - 1`, i.e. it keeps `pipeBits` low bits; this keeps
`2^pipesLog2` low bits. On this chip that is 4 bits kept where 2 would be
expected; on Navi 21 (`pipesLog2 = 4`) it would keep 16.

**This is a suspicion, not a finding, and it is explicitly not claimed as
the defect.** Two things are unresolved and either could make it correct:

1. `saved_r9d` is `0xffffffff << (%rbx)`, a *mask* rather than a value, so
   the whole expression may be constructing a mask whose semantics make the
   `1 <<` deliberate. What `(%rbx)` holds - it comes out of
   `ComputeMicroTileDimensionsLog2` - has not been read.
2. The final `bzhi(eax, ebx)` clamps the result again, which could render
   the wider mask harmless for small surfaces.

Resolving (1) is the next step and it is static: read
`ComputeMicroTileDimensionsLog2` (`0x7ffb08c98307`) and
`ComputeBlockDimensionsLog2` (`0x7ffb08c9818a`) and establish what the two
dwords at `(%rbx)` and `0x4(%rbx)` are. Only then is it decidable whether
`1 << pipesLog2` is a count/log2 confusion or the intended expression.

Stated plainly because the pattern has bitten repeatedly in this session: an
instruction that *looks* like an off-by-a-log2 is exactly the kind of thing
that reads as a smoking gun and turns out to be a misread operand. It gets
tested, not announced.

---

## 2mc (2026-10-21, static): TERM computed - `0xc00`, and it flips the pattern bit whose equation is `y3`

2mb left `(%rbx)` unidentified. Resolved.

### `ComputeMicroTileDimensionsLog2` (`0x7ffb08c98307`)

Signature `(rec, resourceType, swizzleMode, elemLog2, uint *out)`. For
`resourceType == 2` **and** a mode in the `0x6660666` set (22 and 25 are in
it), it indexes a 3-byte-per-element table at `0x7ffb08fbb40a`; otherwise a
2-byte-per-element table at `0x7ffb08fbb400`. It writes
`out[0] = microTileWidthLog2`, `out[1] = microTileHeightLog2`,
`out[2] = third`. One special case: mode 27 with `elemLog2 == 0`,
`rec[0x03] != 0` and `!(rec[0x2c] & 2)` forces `out[1] = 5`.

```
0x7ffb08fbb400 (non-2D)      0x7ffb08fbb40a (2D + pattern)
 elem0  W=4 H=4               elem0  W=3 H=2 third=3
 elem1  W=4 H=3               elem1  W=2 H=2 third=3
 elem2  W=3 H=3               elem2  W=2 H=2 third=2
 elem3  W=3 H=2               elem3  W=2 H=1 third=2
 elem4  W=2 H=2               elem4  W=1 H=1 third=2
```

**Mode 22, 2D, BGRA8 (`elemLog2 = 2`) -> W = 2, H = 2.** So
`-0x1c8(%rbp) = 0xffffffff << 2 = 0xfffffffc`.

### TERM, numerically

```
idx  = 1 << rec[0x03]            = 1 << pipesLog2(2)      = 4
ecx  = bzhi(0xfffffffc, 4)       = 0xfffffffc & 0xf       = 0xc
eax  = 0xc << rec[0x02]          = 0xc << 8               = 0xc00
TERM = bzhi(0xc00, ebx)          = 0xc00
```

Generally: **`TERM = bits[microTileWidthLog2, 1 << pipesLog2) << pipeInterleaveLog2`.**

`0xc00` is address bits 10 and 11 - pattern bits **2 and 3**, since the
pattern bits sit at address bit 8 and up (2mb). From 2ma's decode of row 22:

```
pattern bit 2 = (f2 bit 2)      -> no x, no y term
pattern bit 3 = y3              -> pure Y
```

So the term XORed into **every** tile address flips one bit whose equation
is **`y3` and nothing else**. 2lo measured a displacement that is pure Y
(`y ^ 32`) with no X component. That is a close fit in shape.

### Whether the `1 <<` is a bug is NOT decided

The tempting reading is that `bzhi`'s index should be a bit count and
`1 << pipesLog2` should be `pipesLog2`, which would make `TERM = 0` - no
XOR at all. Two things argue against announcing that:

1. The mask being narrowed is `bits >= microTileWidthLog2`, so the
   expression is "pipe bits above the micro tile", and a sensible intended
   form would be `microTileWidthLog2 + pipesLog2 = 2 + 2 = 4` - which is
   **exactly what `1 << pipesLog2` evaluates to on this chip**. The
   expression may be correct here by construction or by coincidence.
2. On Navi 21 (`pipesLog2 = 4`) the same expression gives
   `bits[2,16) << 8`, a far wider mask than any of the candidate "intended"
   forms. Apple ships this code working on Navi 21, so a reading that makes
   it obviously broken there is probably the wrong reading, not a discovered
   bug (the same reasoning that stopped the PM4 parse-drift theory in 2dq).

### What is now testable

`TERM` depends only on `rec[0x02]` and `rec[0x03]` - `PIPE_INTERLEAVE_SIZE`
and `NUM_PIPES` of `GB_ADDR_CONFIG` - which 2ly already rewrites:

| reported NUM_PIPES | `1 << pipesLog2` | TERM |
|---|---|---|
| 0 or 1 | 1 or 2 | **0** (empty range) |
| **2 (actual)** | 4 | **0xc00** |
| 3 | 8 | 0xfc00 |

So reporting `NUM_PIPES <= 1` removes the XOR entirely. **Confounded**, and
badly: `pipesLog2` also feeds the pattern row through
`K = pipesLog2 + 2*numPkrs - 2`, and feeds userspace AddrLib's own surface
layout, which 2lz showed has teeth. A `NUM_PIPES` boot would move three
things at once and could not attribute the result to any of them.

Disentangling needs an override of `rec[0x02]`/`rec[0x03]` **after**
`AllocCpuTexInterface` has consumed `GB_ADDR_CONFIG` - i.e. inside the
userspace record, not the kernel's report. That is the userspace the
project cannot patch (2lt). Recorded as the sharpest open question the text
defect has produced, with no cheap experiment behind it yet.

---

## 2md (2026-10-21): NUM_PIPES override - the empirical sweep the user asked for

Build UUID `A3DDC2C8`, hosttest passes, unarmed.

The user's instruction (2026-10-21): *"anything that fixes the text and
glitches"*. That is a decision to prefer a working screen over a clean
attribution, and it is recorded because it changes what counts as a good
result for the next few boots.

`rbgpu_pipes=N` rewrites bits 2:0 of `_sAMD_GET_HW_INFO_VALUES + 0xa0`,
alongside 2ly's `rbgpu_pkrs=N` on bits 10:8. Both go through the same
existing 2lk hook, both write on every call, both record to the diag table:
`pipes_arg`, `pipes_writes` beside `pkrs_arg`, `pkrs_was_gbac`,
`pkrs_now_gbac`, `pkrs_writes`.

### Why NUM_PIPES is the motivated candidate

2mc: `TERM = bits[microTileWidthLog2, 1 << pipesLog2) << pipeInterleaveLog2`
is XORed into **every** tile address. On this chip that is `bits[2,4) << 8`
= `0xc00` = address bits 10/11 = pattern bits 2/3, and 2ma decodes row 22's
pattern bit 3 as **`y3` alone**. 2lo measured a **pure-Y** displacement.
Reporting `NUM_PIPES <= 1` makes the range empty and `TERM = 0`.

| `rbgpu_pipes` | `1 << pipesLog2` | TERM |
|---|---|---|
| 0 | 1 | **0** |
| 1 | 2 | **0** |
| (none) = 2 | 4 | 0xc00 |
| 3 | 8 | 0xfc00 |

### The confound, stated before the boot rather than after

`pipesLog2` moves three things at once:

1. `TERM`, as above.
2. The pattern **row**, through `K = pipesLog2 + 2*numPkrs - 2` - at
   `pipes=1`, `K = 1 + 4 - 2 = 3`, so row 17 instead of 22.
3. Userspace **AddrLib's own surface layout**, which 2lz proved has real
   teeth - `rbgpu_pkrs=1` produced whole-surface destruction.

So a good result is a working screen and **not** evidence about `TERM`.
Attribution, if it works, comes afterwards by moving `pkrs` to hold `K`
constant while `pipes` changes - at `pipes=1, pkrs=2` K is 3, but
`pipes=1, pkrs=3` gives `K = 1 + 6 - 2 = 5`, and `pipes=2, pkrs=1` gives
`K = 2` - a small grid that separates row from TERM once something works.

### Order to try

`rbgpu_pipes=1` first - it zeroes TERM while moving the row by one group,
the smaller perturbation of the two zeroing values. `rbgpu_pipes=0` second.
`rbgpu_pipes=3` is a widening and is not recommended.

Failure mode is pixels, not a hang; removing the boot-arg undoes it and
`-rbgpuoff` remains the rescue. The chip's own `GB_ADDR_CONFIG` is never
written - only what `getHardwareInfo` reports.

---

## 2me (2026-10-21, boot 110): TERM = 0 and the text is unchanged - 2mc's hypothesis is dead

Boot 110, UUID `A3DDC2C8`, `rbgpu-boot` = 110, armed. **Both** overrides
were in boot-args - `rbgpu_pkrs=1` was not removed before `rbgpu_pipes=1`
was added - so this boot reported `NUM_PIPES = 1` **and** `NUM_PKRS = 1`.
Read live from `RBGPUDiag`:

```
pkrs_arg = 1   pipes_arg = 1
pkrs_was_gbac = 578 = 0x242      (the chip's real register)
pkrs_now_gbac = 321 = 0x141      (pipes 2->1, pkrs 2->1)
pkrs_writes = pipes_writes = 35
```

Derived for what userspace saw: `numPkrs = 1 <= 1`, so `K = pipesLog2 = 1`,
pattern row `= elemLog2 + 5K = 7`; and

```
TERM = bits[microTileWidthLog2(2), 1 << pipesLog2(1) = 2) << 8 = EMPTY = 0
```

**TERM was zero this boot, and the text is unchanged.** So the constant
`0xc00` XOR is not what displaces glyph rows, and 2mc's hypothesis - the
best-fitting one the static read produced - is **dead**. Its shape matched
(a single pure-`y3` term against a measured pure-Y displacement) and it was
still wrong.

### The other result, which is larger

Boot 110 reports a **completely false geometry** - 2 pipes and 2 packers
where the chip has 4 and 4 - and renders **the same as baseline**. Boot 109
reported `pkrs=1` alone and produced whole-surface destruction. So:

| boot | reported | row | TERM | result |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 108 | 0x242 (true) | 22 | 0xc00 | glyph scramble only |
| 109 | 0x142 | 12 | 0xc00 | **whole-surface destruction** |
| 110 | 0x141 | 7 | 0 | glyph scramble only |

A *more* wrong geometry rendering *better* than a less wrong one is not a
layout story. It weakens 2lz's reading that this field drives client surface
layout generally - what boot 109 may actually have hit is an **inconsistent**
pair (`pkrs=1` with `pipes=2`) rather than a wrong one, since boot 110's
pair is self-consistent. **Not asserted**; two variables moved and n=1 each.

### What this costs the whole line of attack

Every lever the kernel has over client texture geometry has now been
exercised - pattern row (12, 7, 22), the per-tile XOR (0xc00, 0), packer
count, pipe count - and **none of them moves the glyph defect in either
direction.** The text looks the same at row 22 with TERM 0xc00 as at row 7
with TERM 0.

That is 2ln's original position arriving from the other side: **the glyph
defect is not a layout problem.** 2lo's texprobe matrix stands as a real
measurement of `replaceRegion` on tiled BGRA8, but **the chain from that
defect to the on-screen glyphs has never been established** - it was assumed
in 2lp and never tested. Apps may not upload glyph atlases through that path
at all.

### The next step that is actually in reach

`tools/texprobe.swift` is our own program, so it can be instrumented
completely - which userspace Metal in other apps cannot (2lt). Extend it to
**rasterise real text** (CoreText into a CPU buffer, uploaded the several
ways texprobe already distinguishes) and see whether the scramble
reproduces. If it does, the defect is in a path we can measure end to end.
If it does not, `replaceRegion` is a real but **unrelated** bug and the
glyph defect needs a different hypothesis entirely.

Either answer is worth more than another geometry boot, and it costs no
boot at all.

## 2mf (2026-10-21): texprobe grows real glyphs - and boot 110 proves it must be re-run at baseline

### The user's observation, recorded in their words (2026-10-21)

> "for icons on desktop or pictures on iMessage when the window is unfocused
> theyre scrambled.. when i click on the window or themselves they get
> fixed... that doesnt work for claude app or safari pictures though"

This is the most diagnostic report the text defect has produced, because
**a redraw fixing content means the stored bytes can be right and the later
read of them wrong.** A pure layout error cannot behave that way: rewriting
the same content into the same surface with the same layout would scramble
identically. It corroborates 2me from a completely independent direction and
splits the symptom in two - a recoverable class (desktop icons, iMessage)
and a non-recoverable one (Claude app, Safari).

### What was added to `tools/texprobe.swift`

A second phase, after the existing synthetic matrix:

- `glyphBitmap()` rasterises **real text** with CoreText/CoreGraphics into a
  CPU BGRA buffer (Menlo 13, several lines, numbered per row).
- Each upload path pushes that exact buffer, the GPU reads it back through
  the existing compute shader, and `compareRows` reports **row attribution**
  - a readback row that matches a *different* reference row prints as
  `12<-44`, so a permutation is measured rather than inferred.
- Each case is read back **twice**, with a 2 s idle between, and reports
  `stable=YES/NO`. That is the direct test of the user's
  unfocused/refocused observation: if a later read of an unchanged texture
  differs, the defect is in reading, not writing.

Builds with the documented line
(`swiftc -O tools/texprobe.swift -o texprobe -framework Metal -framework IOSurface`).

### Why its first run proves nothing yet

Run on **boot 110**, which is still reporting the false geometry from 2me
(`rbgpu_pkrs=1` and `rbgpu_pipes=1`, `GB_ADDR_CONFIG` reported as `0x141`
against the chip's real `0x242`). Under that configuration:

- **Every R8 case is now BAD** - `r8 w=37/256/1000 managed-replace-*`,
  thousands of foreign pixels. In 2lo's boot-104 run **every R8 case was
  clean.**
- The process **segfaults** at `r8 w=1000 private-blit-full #2`, inside the
  *original* matrix, before the new glyph phase runs at all.

So the false geometry does real damage in userspace - which is further
evidence it reaches client texture layout, and a reminder that boot 110 is
not a baseline. The segfault is a userspace crash in our own test program;
nothing kernel-side.

**The glyph measurement must be taken on a boot with the overrides removed.**
Until then nothing from this phase is evidence about anything.

---

## 2mg (2026-10-21, boot 111, baseline): the defect is CONTENT-DEPENDENT, not layout-dependent

Boot 111, UUID `A3DDC2C8`, overrides removed (`pkrs_arg = pipes_arg = -1`),
`GB_ADDR_CONFIG` reported as the chip has it. A true baseline.
`tools/texprobe.swift` run to completion (the segfault was mine -
`replace(region:)` is illegal on a `.private` texture; those paths are now
excluded from the glyph phase).

### The synthetic matrix at baseline - sharper than 2lo

```
bgra8 w=256 managed-replace-full   OK
bgra8 w=256 managed-replace-tiles  BAD 12288/12288 moved=8192 d(0,32)x4096 d(0,-32)x4096
bgra8 w=256 private-blit-full/tiles OK
bgra8 w=256 iosurface              OK
```

Six BAD out of the whole matrix, and **only `managed-replace-tiles`**.
2lo's `y ^ 32` reproduces exactly - but `managed-replace-**full**` is
**clean**. So the synthetic defect is specific to `replace(region:)` on
**sub-rectangles**, not to `replace` as such. 2lo and 2lp both spoke of
"replaceRegion" without that distinction.

### The glyph phase - and the finding

Real CoreText text, same upload paths, compared against the exact buffer
uploaded:

```
                        w=256                    w=1000
managed-replace-full    46/48 rows wrong         48/48 rows wrong
managed-replace-tiles   46/48 rows wrong         48/48 rows wrong
iosurface                0/48  CLEAN              0/48  CLEAN
```

`iosurface` being clean at both widths is the control that makes the rest
readable: the reference bitmap, the comparison and the readback shader are
all sound, so the mismatches are real.

**`managed-replace-full` is CLEAN for synthetic content and WRONG for glyph
content, at the same width, same path, same texture type.** The only
difference is what the pixels contain.

And the failing pixels are not displaced content:

```
px (0,0) got=00000000 want=ff000000
px (1,0) got=00000000 want=ff000000      (w=1000, managed-replace-full)
```

**Alpha zero.** Not a wrong-but-valid pixel from elsewhere - *absent*
content. Where glyph rows do carry ink, it appears at coordinates the
reference has none (`px (118,0) got=ff7a7a7a want=ff000000`), and
`compareRows` finds **no** reference row that matches exactly (`0<-?`), so
this is not a row permutation either.

### What distinguishes the two contents

The synthetic pattern is `(tag<<24) | (y<<12) | x` - **every pixel differs
from its neighbours**, maximum entropy. The glyph bitmap is overwhelmingly a
single repeated value, `0xff000000`, with thin antialiased text on it -
**highly compressible**.

That is the signature of a **colour-compression (DCC) metadata** problem,
not a tiling problem: uniform regions are exactly what DCC encodes as "one
clear value" in metadata, and uniform regions are exactly what comes back as
zeros here. It would also explain the whole of 2me - every geometry lever
failed because geometry was never the variable - and it fits the user's own
observation, where re-rendering (which rewrites the metadata) repairs the
image.

Supporting, not conclusive: `rbgpu-surf` has reported `dcc calls=0` with
`hk=1` since 2ll - the kernel's DCC surface path is hooked and **never
called** - while the hardware may still consult DCC metadata for these
surfaces.

### What did NOT reproduce

`stable=YES` on every case. The 2 s idle re-read is byte-identical to the
immediate one, so the user's unfocused/refocused recovery did **not**
reproduce in texprobe. Either it needs the compositor rather than a direct
readback, or it needs a longer or different idle. The focus effect remains
unexplained and is still the best clue for the *recoverable* class.

### Next

Test the content hypothesis directly, with no boot: upload bitmaps of
**graded entropy** through `managed-replace-full` - solid colour, two
colours, coarse blocks, fine noise - and find where it breaks. If solid
fails and noise passes, the defect is compression, and the search moves to
DCC metadata, which is kernel-reachable in a way userspace layout never was.

---

## 2mj (2026-10-21, boot 111): the defect is NON-DETERMINISTIC and per-allocation. 2mg is withdrawn.

### The measurement

Same value, same path, same size, 20 fresh textures each:

```
0xff000000 : 0 wrong x3   4096 wrong x7   12288 wrong x10
0xffffffff : 0 wrong x2   4096 wrong x8   12288 wrong x10
```

And re-reading one texture three times:

```
trial 0: read1= 4096 read2= 4096 read3= 4096  identical
trial 1: read1=12288 read2=12288 read3=12288  identical
trial 2: read1=12288 read2=12288 read3=12288  identical
trial 3: read1=    0 read2=    0 read3=    0  identical
trial 4: read1= 4096 read2= 4096 read3= 4096  identical
```

**The outcome is fixed at upload time, per texture, and then perfectly
stable.** The same bytes written to a fresh texture land correctly, lose 16
rows, or lose all 48, and which of the three happens varies between
allocations.

### 2mg is withdrawn

2mg concluded the defect is content-dependent from the entropy ladder
(2mh) and the channel sweep (2mi). Those two tables disagree with each
other on **identical input** - `solid-black` is 0 wrong in one and 4096 in
the next, inside a single process run. Neither table measured content;
both measured allocation luck, one sample per row.

**Rule 18 exactly - "do not build a table from n=1 rows" - and I built two
of them, then wrote a conclusion on top.** The content story was invented
to explain variance that was never shown to be real. Instance 29 of the
recurring error, and the first in this session where the fix was simply to
run the same thing twice.

What survives from 2mg: `iosurface` was clean in **every** case across all
of 2mg, 2mh and 2mi - dozens of allocations - while `managed-replace-full`
fails roughly 85 % of the time. That difference is large enough to survive
the variance, so the **path** distinction is real even though the content
distinction was not.

### What this explains

- **The user's observation.** A window's surface is uploaded once; if that
  upload lands badly the window stays scrambled, and anything that forces a
  fresh upload - clicking, refocusing, a redraw - gets a new roll of the
  dice. Content that recovers on click and content that does not are the
  same bug with different redraw behaviour, not two bugs.
- **Why every geometry lever in 2me did nothing.** Row, TERM, pipes,
  packers - none of them is the variable. The variable is the allocation.
- **Why 2ll/2ln's layout experiments kept producing "identically scrambled"
  photographs.** Identical-looking, not identical.

It also puts a caveat on **2lo**: its `d(0,+-32)` signature is one sample of
a stochastic process. The measurement stands, its uniqueness does not.

### The quantisation is the next clue

Failures are exactly `0`, `4096` or `12288` pixels at w=256 h=48 - that is
0, 16 or 48 rows, i.e. **0 KB, 16 KB or 48 KB** of a 48 KB surface. Never a
partial row, never an odd count. Whatever goes wrong goes wrong in whole
16-row units.

### Next, all without a boot

1. **Is it a race or a placement?** Re-read is stable, so nothing drifts
   after upload - but the upload itself may race. Test an explicit
   `synchronizeResource` blit and a `waitUntilCompleted` between
   `replace()` and the read.
2. **Does it correlate with address or alignment?** Allocate from an
   `MTLHeap` at controlled offsets and see whether the failing offsets form
   a pattern. A 16 KB quantum against a 4 KB tile is suggestive.
3. **Does the failure rate move with surface height?** If 16 rows is really
   16 KB, a 96-row surface should fail in 16-row units too.

## 2mk — nullarc: an independent project on the same memory topology, and a new hypothesis for the glyph defect

The user pointed at `luuumi-dev/nullarc` (HEAD `cbb08dd`, 2026-10-21 — active
today): "Metal on AMD Radeon 780M for macOS Tahoe", by way of
`Almosst-DEV/Cobalt64` (Navi 48 / RDNA 4). Phoenix / Hawk Point, RDNA 3,
GC 11.0.1, gfx1103, DCN 3.1.4.

**Licence first, because this is what blocked NootedRed.** nullarc is MIT or
GPL-2.0-only for its own code, PolyForm Noncommercial 1.0.0 for the parts
derived from NullMoth's driver (`src/phxaccel`, `src/nmplugin`,
`tools/nvmtl-patches`), MIT for the Mesa patches. **There is no clause
restricting AI reading or analysis.** Reading it is permitted; the ChefKiss
prohibition does not apply here. Anything *copied* would carry GPL-2.0 or
PolyForm-NC, and PolyForm-NC forbids commercial use — irrelevant for this
project but worth stating.

### What it actually is

Not a patch of Apple's stack — a **replacement** of it, in four echelons:

| Echelon | What | Size |
|---|---|---|
| `PhxBringup.kext` | PSP 13 firmware load, SMU/IMU power-up, MES scheduler, GPUVM per process, the BO/submit ABI RADV calls | 85 KB of one `.cpp` |
| `PhxAccel.kext` | `NMXAccel` IOAccelerator + `PhxAMDFB` framebuffer + `PhxAGDC` | ~5 700 lines |
| `NVMTLDriver.bundle` | NullMoth's Metal-on-Vulkan plugin, in `/Library/GPUBundles` | ~29 000 lines |
| Mesa RADV | `libvulkan_radeon.dylib`, Darwin winsys, 6 patches | upstream |

Apple's `AMDRadeonX6000` is not in the picture at all. Their reason is in
their own architecture doc: Apple's driver stops at RDNA 2 (Navi 21/23), so
for gfx1103 there is nothing to reuse. **Our chip is gfx1033 — inside the
generation Apple still supports.** That is why our approach exists and theirs
could not.

### The three things that bear on us

**1. The display half may not need DCN bring-up at all.** `src/amd/rdna3_dcn314_scanout.cpp`
programs OTG/HUBP directly, but a grep for its callers shows it is reached only
from `src/kext/RDNA3Driver.cpp` and a unit test — **not from either shipping
kext**. The shipping path is `src/phxaccel/accel/phxfb.cpp`, whose own header
comment says it "takes over the mode the firmware (GOP) already lit, at boot in
place of the firmware framebuffer (IONDRV), and **writes nothing to the display
engine**". It reads OTG0's H/V totals and frame counter read-only, purely to
measure the refresh, and stands a `thread_call` timer in for the VBL interrupt.
HANDOFF §"the display half has never started" has been treating DCN bring-up as
the price of an accelerated desktop. An independent project got WindowServer
compositing at 120 Hz without writing one display register.

**2. A concrete, dated, non-obvious finding we would have paid boots for:**
CoreDisplay reads the **GPU vendor out of the framebuffer's class name**
(Intel / AMD / NVDA / AppleParavirt) and turns IOPresentment off for any other
name — hence their class is called `PhxAMDFB`
(`GetGPUVendorForFramebufferService -> 1`, 2026-10-20).

**3. The one that touches our actual frontier.** Their scan-out copy hit a
defect of our defect's class, on our memory topology — an APU whose VRAM is a
carve-out of system RAM, which is exactly this chip (MC `0xF4_0000_0000`,
system-physical `0x7_8000_0000`). Verbatim, `nvrm-accel.cpp:1206`:

> the scan-out's system-RAM view (PhxFB) maps write-back whatever cache mode it
> asks for, and plain stores left the frame in the CPU cache while the panel
> scanned the stale DRAM under it, in stripes (2026-10-20)

and `phxfb.cpp:63` says the same mapping "comes out write-back although it asks
for write-combined (frames copied with plain stores stayed in the CPU cache:
stripes)". Their fix is non-temporal stores (`movnti`, `movntdq`) plus
streaming loads for the write-combined source side.

### The hypothesis this gives us

**The glyph defect is a cache-coherency gap on the carve-out, not a layout
error.** CPU stores from `replace(region:)` land in the CPU's cache; the GPU
reads the stale DRAM under them.

It predicts, and 2mj already measured, every property that defeated the layout
story:

| 2mj / 2mg observation | What coherency predicts |
|---|---|
| non-deterministic per allocation | whether a line is still dirty depends on cache pressure, not on content |
| re-reads byte-identical | DRAM is stably wrong; nothing drifts |
| whole 16-row bands, never partial rows | eviction granularity, not pixel geometry |
| `iosurface` clean in **every** case | IOSurface pages come with their own caching attributes |
| every geometry lever inert (2me) | layout was never the variable |

It also explains the user's observation that an unfocused window is scrambled
and a click fixes it: a redraw re-uploads, and by then the lines have been
evicted.

### Status of the texprobe work

`tools/texprobe.swift` grew the three 2mj follow-ups — settle variants
(`synchronize`, sleep, double replace, pre-idle), a placement-`MTLHeap` offset
sweep, and a height sweep from 16 to 192 rows, all at n>=8 per row after rule
18 was broken twice in 2mg. **None of it has run**: the current boot is
unarmed (`rbgpu-diag d=0 armed=0`, `rbgpu-boot` still 111, and the peer's own
note says "rbgpu-arm not set; accelerator NOT armed"), so there is no Metal
device. `MTLCreateSystemDefaultDevice()!` force-unwrapped and trapped with
SIGILL and an empty log — rule 14, an instrument that says nothing. It now
prints the unarmed diagnosis and exits 2.

### Next, on the next armed boot

The coherency hypothesis is falsifiable in userspace with no kext change:

1. **Does the CPU see what the GPU does not?** For `linear-buffer-tex` the
   backing address is known (`buf.contents()`). Write it, read it back with the
   GPU, and read the same bytes with the CPU. CPU correct + GPU wrong in whole
   bands is coherency; both wrong is not.
2. **Does a flush fix it?** `clflush` + `sfence` over the range between the
   write and the GPU read. 2mj showed re-reads never change — a re-read *after
   a flush* is a different question.
3. **Do non-temporal stores avoid it?** Write the backing store with `movnti`
   as nullarc does, instead of `memcpy`.

If 1 or 2 comes back positive, the fix is in the kernel: the carve-out's
caching attributes, not Apple's tiler, and the whole `-rbgpulinear` /
swizzle-mode line of work is beside the point.

### Architecture, stated honestly

nullarc is not a part we can drop in. Its bringup is gfx11 + MES; ours would be
gfx10.3 CP/MEC with HQDs, and no MES exists on this chip. What is portable is
what their own comparison table calls generation-independent: the user-client
ABI shape (`src/uapi/r3n_native_abi.h`, 15 selectors, 369 lines in all), the
RADV Darwin winsys, and the Metal-on-Vulkan plugin — and RADV's gfx1033 support
is mature. The strategic point is the one we did not have before: a working
endpoint exists for an APU of this family on macOS, reached without Apple's
driver and without programming the display engine.

And `/Library/GPUBundles/NVMTLDriver.bundle` plus `nvmtl/libvulkan_nouveau.dylib`
are **already installed on this machine** (2026-10-09, for the laptop's RTX 4050,
which `-wegnoegpu` disables), so the third-party Metal plugin mechanism is
present on macOS 15.8.1 and not a Tahoe-only facility.

## 2ml — the coherency hypothesis is dead, and 2mj's "non-deterministic" was wrong

Boot 112, armed, UUID `A3DDC2C8` matching `build/out`, baseline boot-args
(`-rbgpulinear` IN, no `rbgpu_pkrs`/`rbgpu_pipes`).

### The nullarc coherency hypothesis (2mk) is refuted

If `replace()` left its bytes in the CPU's cache and the GPU read the stale
DRAM beneath, evicting the cache between the upload and the read would fix it.
It does not. A 128 MB touch - far larger than any cache on this part - changes
nothing, and an equal-duration sleep as the time-only control changes nothing
either:

```
  baseline (nothing)        fail 21/24  wrong-rows: 0x3  16x9  48x12
  evict by WRITING 128 MB   fail 21/24  wrong-rows: 0x3  16x9  48x12   (9.3 ms)
  evict by READING 128 MB   fail 21/24  wrong-rows: 0x3  16x9  48x12   (5.0 ms)
  sleep, same duration      fail 21/24  wrong-rows: 0x3  16x9  48x12
```

Four variants, bit-identical histograms. **Withdrawn.** nullarc's stripes are a
real defect of theirs on the same topology, but they are not this defect. It
was proposed in 2mk on the strength of a predicted-property table and no
measurement, which is the recurring error wearing a new hat: the table in 2mk
listed five properties coherency "predicts" without testing the one experiment
that separates it from everything else. Instance 30.

Where we own the backing store, both sides agree perfectly - 24/24 clean on the
GPU's view *and* the CPU's view of the same buffer-backed linear texture. The
defect needs the driver's own allocation.

### 2mj's "non-deterministic" was wrong: it is deterministic

2mk-1 ran six settle variants - plain, `synchronize`+wait, 50 ms sleep, both,
double `replace`, and a pre-idled queue - at n=16 each:

```
  replace -> read             0x2  4096x6  12288x8     rows: 0-15 | 0-47 | 16-31 | 32-47
  replace -> synchronize+wait 0x2  4096x6  12288x8     rows: 0-15 | 0-47 | 16-31 | 32-47
  replace -> 50ms sleep       0x2  4096x6  12288x8     rows: 0-15 | 0-47 | 16-31 | 32-47
  replace -> sync + 50ms      0x2  4096x6  12288x8     rows: 0-15 | 0-47 | 16-31 | 32-47
  replace twice -> read       0x2  4096x6  12288x8     rows: 0-15 | 0-47 | 16-31 | 32-47
  idle cb -> replace -> read  0x2  4096x6  12288x8     rows: 0-15 | 0-47 | 16-31 | 32-47
```

Six independent runs returning the same histogram to the trial is not a
stochastic process. The outcome is **fixed by the allocation**, and the same
allocation sequence reproduces it exactly. 2mj saw spread because it varied
allocations, not because anything is random. Nothing about the upload races:
no amount of settling, synchronising or repeating moves a single trial.

### The bands are thirds of the surface, and some heights never fail

2mk-3, n=16 per height, w=256 so one row is 1 KB:

| h | wrong rows | bands |
|---|---|---|
| 16 | 0 x16 | clean |
| 32 | 0 x16 | clean |
| 48 | 0x2, 16x6, 48x8 | `0-15`, `16-31`, `32-47`, `0-47` |
| 64 | 0x8, 64x8 | `0-63` |
| 96 | 0x4, 32x12 | `0-31`, `32-63`, `64-95` |
| 128 | 0 x16 | clean |
| 192 | 0x8, 64x8 | `128-191` |

The band is always exactly a third of the surface - 16 of 48, 32 of 96, 64 of
192 - never a partial row, and the boundaries are aligned. The 16 KB quantum of
2mj was an artefact of only ever testing h=48.

### 2mm — the predictor: the client's footprint, not the content and not the clock

`heapTextureSizeAndAlign` reports what the **userspace** driver intends to
occupy for a geometry. Against the pass/fail column above:

| w | h | pixels | footprint | align | ratio | 2mk-3 |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 256 | 16 | 16384 | 32768 | 4096 | 2.00x | clean |
| 256 | 32 | 32768 | 32768 | 4096 | 1.00x | clean |
| 256 | 48 | 49152 | 131072 | 65536 | 2.67x | **fails** |
| 256 | 64 | 65536 | 131072 | 65536 | 2.00x | **fails** |
| 256 | 96 | 98304 | 131072 | 65536 | 1.33x | **fails** |
| 256 | 128 | 131072 | 131072 | 65536 | 1.00x | clean |
| 256 | 192 | 196608 | 262144 | 65536 | 1.33x | **fails** |
| 256 | 256 | 262144 | 262144 | 65536 | 1.00x | - |
| 64 | 64 | 16384 | 16384 | 4096 | 1.00x | - |

**Every failing geometry has align 65536 and ratio > 1.00. Every clean
geometry has either align 4096 or ratio exactly 1.00.** No exception in the
data.

Align 65536 is a 64 KB tiled swizzle mode; align 4096 is 4 KB or linear. So
the client lays these textures out **tiled**, in 64 KB tiles, padding 48 KB of
pixels into 128 KB - while this boot's kernel is forcing every client surface
to **LINEAR** (`-rbgpulinear`, `rbgpu-surf hk=1 calls=38 forced=38 lin=1`).

That is a **disagreement between the two halves of the driver**, and it
accounts for everything the single-sided stories could not:

- Where the tiled footprint happens to equal the linear one (ratio 1.00), the
  two layouts coincide and the surface is correct. That is h=32, h=128, h=256.
- Where it does not, whole aligned bands of rows are addressed as if tiled and
  stored as if linear, or the reverse.
- It is deterministic per geometry, as 2mk-1 found, because a footprint is.
- It is invisible to every *kernel-side* lever (2me: row, TERM, pipes,
  packers), because the kernel's own arithmetic was never wrong - it is being
  told LINEAR and doing LINEAR correctly.
- `iosurface` is clean throughout because an IOSurface's layout is agreed
  between the halves by construction.
- Buffer-backed linear textures are clean on both sides (2ml-b) because we
  supply the layout.

### The prediction, and it is a reboot test

If the defect is this mismatch, then **removing `-rbgpulinear` must make the
padded geometries clean**, because the kernel would stop overriding the mode
the client already laid out for. The sweep is already in `texprobe`, so the
prediction is sharp and falsifiable in one boot:

> With `-rbgpulinear` out, 2mk-3's h=48, 64, 96 and 192 must go clean, and
> 2mm's ratios must be unchanged (the client does not know about the boot-arg).

`sudo tools/efi.sh bootarg remove -rbgpulinear && sudo nvram rbgpu-arm=1`

HANDOFF currently says `-rbgpulinear` "belongs IN" and that 2ln showed it does
not affect the text either way. 2ln compared kernel-side tiled counts across
boots 103 and 104 on a whole-screen judgement; this is the first per-geometry
predictor we have had, and it says the boot-arg is not neutral but **causal**.
If the sweep goes clean, the ~80 % widget/chrome win `-rbgpulinear` buys has
been paid for with the text all along, and the real fix is to make the kernel
agree with the client rather than override it.

## 2mn (boot 113) — the boot-arg test was INERT, and the defect obeys a law

Boot 113, armed, UUID `A3DDC2C8` matching `build/out`, `-rbgpulinear`
**removed**, and the kernel confirms it stopped forcing: `rbgpu-surf b=113 swz
hk=1 calls=61 | lin=2 forced=0` against boot 112's `calls=38 forced=38`.

### The test did not test what 2mm claimed

The height sweep came back **bit-identical** to boot 112 — h=48 `0x2 16x6
48x8`, h=64 `0x8 64x8`, h=96 `0x4 32x12`, h=192 `0x8 64x8`, every cell. That
reads as a refutation and is not one:

```
rbgpu-surf before a full texprobe run:  swz calls=63
rbgpu-surf after  a full texprobe run:  swz calls=63
```

**Hundreds of textures, zero hook calls.** The kernel's swizzle hook never
sees a client Metal texture, so `-rbgpulinear` could not have changed one, in
this boot or in 112. The mismatch hypothesis of 2mm is **untested**, not
refuted, and boot 113 was spent on an experiment whose reach I had not
checked. `forced=38` in boot 112 was 38 *display-class* surfaces and none of
ours; I read a non-zero counter as evidence the lever was engaged. Rule 20
again, one level out: a counter proving the hook ran is not evidence it ran on
the thing being measured.

(The UUID line in that check was also misread — a `sed -n 2p` over
`kmutil showloaded` picked another kext's UUID. The plugin's own UUID matches.
Rule 21.)

### What boot 113 does establish, which is worth more

**The layout of a client Metal texture is decided entirely in userspace.** The
kernel is never consulted. That is a structural fact and it retroactively
explains the whole dead end:

- 2ln: boots 103 and 104 rendered glyphs identically because neither boot's
  kernel setting ever reached a glyph surface.
- 2me: every kernel lever — row 22/12/7, TERM `0xc00`/`0`, pipes, packers —
  was inert for exactly the same reason.
- `rbgpu-surf`'s 63 calls are the display/scanout class (`s9->1b`, `s0->1b`),
  which is why kernel levers move the widget/Dock/chrome artifacts and have
  never once moved the text.

There is no kernel-side lever on client texture layout. The layout line of
work from the kernel side was never going to reach the frontier.

### 2mn — a law, predicted before measuring, 16/16

2mm's candidate was stated as a rule and then tested against sixteen
geometries whose predictions were printed **before** their measurements:

```
  w     h    align   ratio  predict  measured              verdict
  256   16     4096   2.00x  clean    fail  0/12 (0x12)              ok
  256   32     4096   1.00x  clean    fail  0/12 (0x12)              ok
  256   48    65536   2.67x  FAIL     fail 11/12 (0x1  16x5  48x6)   ok
  256   64    65536   2.00x  FAIL     fail  6/12 (0x6  64x6)         ok
  256   96    65536   1.33x  FAIL     fail  9/12 (0x3  32x9)         ok
  256   128   65536   1.00x  clean    fail  0/12 (0x12)              ok
  256   192   65536   1.33x  FAIL     fail  6/12 (0x6  64x6)         ok
  256   256   65536   1.00x  clean    fail  0/12 (0x12)              ok
  128   48    65536   2.67x  FAIL     fail 11/12 (0x1  16x5  48x6)   ok
  512   48    65536   2.67x  FAIL     fail 10/12 (0x2  16x4  48x6)   ok
  1024  48    65536   2.67x  FAIL     fail 11/12 (0x1  16x5  48x6)   ok
  64    64     4096   1.00x  clean    fail  0/12 (0x12)              ok
  64    48     4096   1.33x  clean    fail  0/12 (0x12)              ok
  192   48     4096   1.33x  clean    fail  0/12 (0x12)              ok
  256   80    65536   1.60x  FAIL     fail 11/12 (0x1  16x5  48x6)   ok
  320   64     4096   1.00x  clean    fail  0/12 (0x12)              ok
  law held in 16/16 geometries
```

> **A CPU `replace()` is corrupted if and only if the surface is in a 64 KB
> tiled mode (`align == 65536`) AND its footprint exceeds its pixel bytes.**

Neither condition suffices alone, and the table contains the cases that prove
it: `256x16` pads 2.00x at align 4096 and is clean; `256x128` and `256x256`
are align 65536 at ratio 1.00 and are clean. So the defect is **Apple's 64 KB
tiled CPU upload path for a surface that does not exactly fill its tiles.**

### The align map, and why the symptom is *text*

`.` = align 4096, `#` = 64 KB tiled with padding (fails), `=` = 64 KB tiled
exact (clean):

```
  w\h      16   32   48   64   80   96  112  128  160  192  256
  64        .    .    .    .    .    .    #    #    .    .    #
  100       .    .    #    #    #    #    #    #    #    #    #
  128       .    .    #    #    #    #    #    =    #    #    =
  192       .    .    .    .    #    #    #    #    .    #    #
  256       .    .    #    #    #    #    #    =    #    #    =
  500       .    .    #    #    #    #    #    #    #    #    #
  1000      .    .    #    #    #    #    #    #    #    #    #
  1920      .    .    #    #    #    #    #    =    #    #    =
  2560      .    .    #    #    #    #    #    =    #    #    =
```

Almost every realistic geometry is in the failing class. The clean cells are
surfaces at most 32 rows tall, and the exact-fit column at h=128/256 for
power-of-two widths. A text strip or text layer of ordinary height at any
ordinary width is `#`, and 2mf's own glyph strips are both `#`:
`256x48` 2.67x and `1000x48` 2.73x, 46 and 48 rows wrong, `stable=YES`.

**This closes the symptom.** Window and layer backing stores reach the GPU as
IOSurfaces, and the `iosurface` path has been clean in every single trial
across 2mg, 2mh, 2mi, 2mj, 2ml and 2mn — so the desktop, the chrome and the
images composite correctly. Glyphs go into driver-allocated textures filled by
CPU `replace()`, which is the `#` class. An accelerated desktop with
unreadable body text is exactly what this law predicts, and it is why the
defect never looked like a global layout error: it is a *per-surface-class*
error.

It also fits the user's observation that an unfocused icon or iMessage image
is scrambled and a click fixes it, while Claude and Safari images never
recover: a redraw re-allocates, and whether the new surface lands in the `#`
class depends on its geometry, not on the redraw.

### Next, without a boot

The broken path is the CPU tiler; the GPU blit path (`private-blit-full`) and
IOSurfaces are clean. 2lo's original reading — that forcing `ShouldUseSwBlt`
false would route `replaceRegion` through the GPU blit engine — is therefore
the right *shape* of fix, and 2lq/2lr established it cannot be patched in
userspace on this macOS (stub bundle, binary only in the dyld shared cache).

So the question is whether any input to that decision, or to the swizzle-mode
choice, comes from the **kernel** — the `getHardwareInfo` buffer we already
hook, an IORegistry property, or a user-client request. That is static
analysis on Apple's kexts and the shared cache, no hardware needed.

## 2mo — every kernel lever is closed by measurement, and the fix is IOSurface

Boot 113, armed. All of this is userspace analysis plus `texprobe`-class
measurement; no boot was spent.

### The input chain, read rather than guessed

`amdMtl_HWL_AllocCpuTexInterface(const _sAMD_GET_HW_INFO_VALUES*, unsigned)`
builds the CPU tiler's whole state, and the hw-info buffer it reads is the one
at `DeviceMembersRec+0x1a0` that 2lk already hooks. Disassembled in full, it
reads **exactly one field** - `hwinfo+0xa0`, GB_ADDR_CONFIG - and derives:

| rec | value here | from |
|---|---|---|
| `[0x00]` word | 256 | `0x100 << PIPE_INTERLEAVE_SIZE` |
| `[0x02]` | 8 | pipeInterleaveLog2 |
| `[0x03]` | 2 | pipesLog2 (4 pipes) |
| `[0x04]` | 0 | seLog2 (1 SE) |
| `[0x05]` | 2 | pkrsLog2 (4 packers) |
| `[0x06..0x21]` | 8/12/16 table | **immediates in the code** (256 B / 4 KB / 64 KB) |
| `[0x28]` | **20** | `0x4b*8 - 0x258 + 5*(pipesLog2 + 2*pkrsLog2 - 2)` |
| `[0x2c]` bit 1 | 0 | bit 1 of the family flags dword |

The row index on this chip is **20**. And that retires the row-index line of
work (2lx-2mb) from a new direction: if the pattern row were wrong, the
*unpadded* 64 KB surfaces would be scrambled too, and 2mn measured them clean
0/12. The pattern is right.

`amdMtl_HWL_InitAddrLibHwRegFields(_ADDR_CREATE_INPUT*, const AMDCommonHwInfoRec*)`
is six instructions:

```
movl $0xd, 0x4(%rdi)        ; chipFamily: a HARDCODED constant
movl 0xa4(%rsi), %eax       ; GB_ADDR_CONFIG, which HwInfoInitData copied from hwinfo+0xa0
movl %eax, 0x30(%rdi)
```

**Only two things reach AddrLib**, and `rbgpu-hwi` certifies the one that
varies: `gbac=00000242 hw=00000242 MATCH`. So AddrLib's footprint and the CPU
tiler's geometry derive from the *same single correct register*, and the two
halves cannot disagree because of anything the kernel said.

`gfx10_HwInfoInitData` has a six-way cascade on `hwinfo+0x08` (thresholds
0x9/0x13/0x27/0x31/0x3b/0x45, matching the six `AMD_GFX10_NAVI*` family-name
strings), which picks the AddrLib family/revision qword (`0x7_0000008f` or
`0x8_0000008f`), a constant at `rec+0x94` (16, 12 or 8 - the block-size log2
trio), and flags bits [1:0]. `hwinfo+0x08` **is** ours to set. But
`InitAddrLibHwRegFields` proves the cascade's output never reaches AddrLib, so
a family override cannot move the footprint. **That fix was designed and
discarded before it cost a boot** - the one time in this project that chain
ran the right way round.

### Everything reachable, closed by measurement

| Lever | Result |
|---|---|
| kernel swizzle hook | **never called** for a client texture: `swz calls=63` before a full texprobe run and 63 after (2mn) |
| kernel → AddrLib | only GB_ADDR_CONFIG, verified `MATCH` |
| family cascade (`hwinfo+0x08`) | does not reach the layout |
| all **42** `AMD_*` env knobs, 0 and 1 | inert. Baseline 36/72 on six runs; only `AMD_MTL_DEVELOPER_MODE=1` moved it, to 35/72 on four runs - one allocation shifted, reproducible, not a fix |
| `AMD_MTL_ALLOW_VAR_SWIZZLE_MODES` | reads via `getenv`, clears bit 59 of DeviceSettings, and changes **nothing** at 0 or 1 |
| API layers (`AMD_MTL_API_LAYERS`) | Sqtt / Frame / Overlay / Tokeniser / VirtualRT - instrumentation only |
| storage mode | `.shared` fails **identically** to `.managed`: 10/12, 6/12, 9/12, 11/12 in both |
| userspace patching | impossible (2lq: stub bundle, binary only in the dyld cache) |

Also measured: **`hasUnifiedMemory = false`.** Apple's driver believes this APU
is a discrete GPU, which is why a CPU upload is tiled at all.

### The fix

IOSurface has been clean in every trial of every milestone. 2mo asks the sharp
version of that: the **same** `replace()`, the **same** geometry, the **same**
`.managed` mode, differing only in who owns the backing store.

```
replace() into an IOSurface-backed texture, at the geometries that fail when
driver-allocated (n=12 each)
   256x48    fail 0/12      (driver-allocated: 10/12)
   256x64    fail 0/12      (driver-allocated:  6/12)
   256x96    fail 0/12      (driver-allocated:  9/12)
```

Zero. The defect is not in `replace()`, not in the tiler's parameters and not
in the kernel: it is in the layout the driver gives **its own** allocations,
and an IOSurface's layout is agreed between the halves by construction.

So the fix does not need Apple's driver patched, a kext, or a reboot: back the
affected textures with IOSurfaces. AMFI is already relaxed on this machine
(`amfi=0x80 amfi_get_out_of_my_way=0x1`), so a `DYLD_INSERT_LIBRARIES`
interposer can swap texture creation per process.

### Next

Build that interposer and demonstrate it end to end: inject it into `texprobe`
and watch the failing rows go to 0/12 without touching texprobe's code. Then a
real app. Known constraints to respect: IOSurface-backed textures are 2D,
single-mip, and need a matching `bytesPerElement`/`pixelFormat`, so the
interposer must fall through for anything that does not qualify. A 1000-wide
IOSurface without an explicit `bytesPerRow` hung the probe once - alignment
must be set explicitly, not left to default.

## 2mp — the fix: `iosurftex`, and the text defect is gone in userspace

Boot 113, armed, no kext change, no reboot, no `sudo`.

`tools/iosurftex.m` (`make iosurftex`) is a `DYLD_INSERT_LIBRARIES` interposer.
It wraps `MTLCreateSystemDefaultDevice` - interposed rather than swizzled, so
the driver bundle is certainly loaded before its class is looked up - then
swizzles `-newTextureWithDescriptor:` on the returned device's class
(`GFX10_MtlDevice`) and serves any descriptor the 2mn law predicts will fail
from an IOSurface instead. Everything else, and any failure at any step, falls
through to the original untouched.

The guard is the law itself, asked of the driver rather than reimplemented:

```c
MTLSizeAndAlign sa = [dev heapTextureSizeAndAlignWithDescriptor:d];
```
