## 2r5 — both of 2r4's reads, answered: the map is EMPTY, and "selector 1" is an AGDC device attribute

No boot. One new oracle (`make agdcinfo`), run non-root in a second.

### 1. What `%r13d` holds — and the enclosing function is not the one 2r4 named

Symbolized with `atos` (slide measured this run, 0x6137000) after teaching
`dscsym.sh`/`dscsym_many.sh` to dlopen IOPresentment and IOKit and giving
`dscinv.sh` an `IOPresentment` case — **449 functions**:

```
0x7ff812e8ad03 -> ioPresentmentCreateAssociationMap(sioPresentmentDeviceMap**) + 1491
```

So the function running at 2r4's addresses is
**`ioPresentmentCreateAssociationMap`** (`0x7ff812e8a730`, 0x18dc bytes), not
`ioPresentmentFindAGDCMatch`. That name survives only as the **os_log function
string** at `0x7ff812ea14f7`, which every log site in the inlined helper
passes as its `%s` — the helper was inlined into its caller. 2r4 read the
string correctly and attributed the code to it; the enclosing symbol is the
association-map builder, which is a more useful fact, because that map is
exactly what `IOPresentmentCreateForRegistryID` searches.

The query, read instruction by instruction, every stub resolved by
chained-pointer decode + `atos` (14 of them: `IOServiceMatching`,
`IOServiceGetMatchingServices`, `IOIteratorIsValid`, `IOIteratorNext`,
`IOServiceOpen`, `IOConnectCallMethod`, `IOServiceClose`, `IOObjectRelease`,
`IOObjectRetain`, `IORegistryEntryGetName`,
`IORegistryEntryGetRegistryEntryID`, `IOMasterPort`, `os_log_type_enabled`,
`_os_log_impl`):

```
7ff812e8ac33   lea   "AppleGraphicsDeviceControl" ; -> IOServiceMatching
7ff812e8ac4e   call  IOServiceGetMatchingServices ; else log "gms %#x"
7ff812e8acb8   call  IOIteratorIsValid            ; must == 1
7ff812e8acc9   call  IOIteratorNext               ; -> %r13d   <-- THE ANSWER
7ff812e8ad67   call  IORegistryEntryGetName
7ff812e8ad73   movabsq $0x72656c676e617257       ; "Wrangler"
7ff812e8ad87   movabsq $0x555047656c707041       ; "AppleGPU"
7ff812e8ad94   movzbl -0x2500(%rbp)              ; the NUL at [16]
7ff812e8ada1   je    7ff812e8af98                ; name == "AppleGPUWrangler" -> SKIP
7ff812e8adb1   call  IORegistryEntryGetRegistryEntryID
7ff812e8ad12   call  IOServiceOpen(svc, mach_task_self_, 2, &conn)
7ff812e8ae54   call  IOConnectCallMethod(conn, 1, …, out, &outLen)
7ff812e8ae6a   movl  -0xf8(%rbp), %eax ; out+0x28
7ff812e8ae72   cmpl  $0x1, %eax
7ff812e8ae75   ja    <skip>                      ; out+0x28 must be 1 or 2
7ff812e8afc9   …record (service, registryID) in the map, stride 0x30, max 16
```

**`%r13d` is a service matching the CLASS `AppleGraphicsDeviceControl`** —
`IOServiceMatching` sets `IOProviderClass`, which matches by `metaCast`, so
subclasses qualify — **minus the one named `AppleGPUWrangler`**, rejected by an
exact 17-byte compare done as three xors.

### 2. Measured live, non-root: there is exactly ONE, and it is the wrangler

`make agdcinfo` reproduces that query byte for byte, including the name test
written the way the code writes it rather than as `strcmp`:

```
[1] name="AppleGPUWrangler" class=AppleGPUWrangler registryID=0x100000537
    -> SKIPPED by the name test
matched 1, skipped 1, candidates 0
```

So **`AppleGPUWrangler` IS an `AppleGraphicsDeviceControl` subclass** — which
also explains why the wrangler imports `AppleGraphicsDeviceControl::gMetaClass`
and both AGDC constructors (2r0 read the imports and guessed subclasses; this
measures it) — and **`AppleGraphicsDeviceControlPlugin` is NOT**: it is live
(`id 0x100000545, registered, matched, active`) and does **not** appear in the
match. Control for the instrument (rule 26): `ioreg -c IOUserClient -r -d1`
matches **431** services, none of which is exactly an `IOUserClient`, so `-c`
does follow the superclass chain. (My first control was `-c IOUserClient -d1`
without `-r`, which prints only the root and proved nothing — the depth is
measured from wherever the tree is rooted.)

**Zero candidates survive. The association map is EMPTY.**

### 3. `0x10000003` is MACH_SEND_INVALID_DEST — a send to port 0

Not an `IOReturn` and **not** a user-client status, as 2r4 supposed:

```
/Library/Developer/CommandLineTools/SDKs/MacOSX.sdk/usr/include/mach/message.h:807
#define MACH_SEND_INVALID_DEST          0x10000003
```

And the chain that produces it is complete. There are **three** LEA sites to
the error string `0x7ff812ea2880` (cache-wide `ripall`, 7 mappings), each in a
distinct outlined cold block, each with exactly one caller
(`dsc.py callxref`):

| cold block | caller | enclosing function |
|---|---|---|
| `0x7ff812e9f34b` (`.cold.1`) | `0x7ff812e8aee1` | `ioPresentmentCreateAssociationMap` — the selector-1 failure |
| `0x7ff812e9f3af` (`.cold.3`) | `0x7ff812e8b6d5` | `ioPresentmentCreateAssociationMap` — the **IOServiceOpen** failure |
| `0x7ff812e9f617` (`.cold.2`) | `0x7ff812e8c50b` | `IOPresentment::IOPresentmentCreateForRegistryID` |

The second inlined query is **`ioPresentmentPopulateIOFramebufferEntries`**
(its own os_log name string, `0x7ff812ea15e8`). It looks a framebuffer's GPU up
in the map built by the first — stride 0x30, matched on registry ID at
`0x18(%rdi,%rsi)` — and when there is no entry it leaves the service id **0**
(`movl $0x0, -0x2578(%rbp)` at `0x7ff812e8b3be`) and opens *that*:

```
7ff812e8b6a3   call  IOServiceOpen(-0x2578(%rbp), mach_task_self_, 2, &conn)
7ff812e8b6d5   call  7ff812e9f3af    ; -> "Unable to get AGDC information. %#x"
```

The tool's control closes it:
`IOServiceOpen(MACH_PORT_NULL, mach_task_self(), 2, &c)` returns **exactly
`0x10000003`**. So boot 150's
`(IOPresentment) Error: Unable to get AGDC information.  Return code: 0x10000003`
is **a mach send to port 0 because the association map is empty** — not a
misbehaving user client, and not a missing property. Those would need different
repairs; this one needs a *second AGDC service*.

### 4. The two selectors name themselves — and 2r1 is half-corrected

The os_log format strings on these calls' own paths:

| VA | string |
|---|---|
| `0x7ff812ea1512` | `kAGDCVendorInfo %#x %#x %#zx` |
| `0x7ff812ea15ca` | `kAGDCVendorInfo %#llx %#x %#x` |
| `0x7ff812ea1667` | `kAGDCVendorInfo failed %#llx %#x %#zx` |
| `0x7ff812ea1625` | `kAGDCGPUCapability %#llx %zu %u` |
| `0x7ff812ea1645` | `kAGDCGPUCapability %#llx %#x %#zx` |

So **selector 1 is `kAGDCVendorInfo`** (0x2c-byte reply, `+0x28` ∈ {1,2},
a u16 at `+0x24`) and **selector 0x980 is `kAGDCGPUCapability`** (0xdc-byte
reply, non-zero count at `+0x30`, then 8-byte entries from `+0x3c`).
2r1 was right that those names appear **0 times** in `AppleGPUWrangler` and
`AppleGraphicsDeviceControl`; it was wrong to conclude the names were only
2qm's reading of a string table. They are IOPresentment's own labels for these
two calls, printed three bytes from the failing branch. 2qr's *motivation* is
restored; 2r1's *measurement* stands unchanged.

### 5. The kernel side: there is no "type-2 user client" to implement

`AppleGraphicsDeviceControl::newUserClient(task, secID, type, props, &out)`
(`0x13dfd45e`, symbols intact in this kext) has **no switch on `type` at all**
— unlike `IOGraphicsAccelerator2::newUserClient`, which 2ql decoded as a jump
table. It is IOService's canonical implementation with two changes:

```
prop = this->copyProperty(gIOUserClientClassKey)      ; vt[0x2a8]
  cast to OSSymbol, else cast to OSString -> OSSymbol::withString
                                          -> this->setProperty (vt[0x258])
  neither                                 -> kIOReturnUnsupported 0xE00002C7
obj = OSMetaClass::allocClassWithName(sym)             ; NULL -> 0xE00002BD
safeMetaCast(obj, AppleGraphicsDeviceControlClient::metaClass) ; NULL -> 0xE00002C7
obj->vt[0x8e8](task, secID, TYPE)   ; initWithTask     ; false -> 0xE00002BC
obj->vt[0x960](this, task, TYPE)    ; authorizeTask    ; false -> 0xE00002E2
obj->vt[0x670](this)                ; attach           ; false -> 0xE00002BC
obj->vt[0x5c0](this)                ; start            ; false -> 0xE00002BC
*out = obj; return 0
```

`gIOUserClientClassKey` identified by measurement, not by resemblance: the
wrangler's own `IOUserClientClass` property reads **`AppleGPUWranglerClient`**
in ioreg. And `0xE00002E2` from `authorizeTask` is exactly what `agdcinfo`
measured unprivileged, so that constant is now placed.

**And "selector N" is not a dispatch index.**
`AppleGraphicsDeviceControlClient::externalMethod` (`0x13dfae20`) builds an
`AGDCClientState_t` from `client+0xf0..0x120` with the
`IOExternalMethodArguments*` at `state+0x38`, then forwards **every** selector
to `AppleGraphicsDeviceControl::UserKernelTransfer(selector, state)`
(`0x13dfd600`), which unwraps the arguments —
`structureOutputDescriptor` at `args+0x68` else `structureOutputSize` at
`+0x60`; `structureInputDescriptor` at `+0x40` else `structureInputSize` at
`+0x38`; both ≤ 0x4000000 or `0xE00002EA`; `prepare`/`map`/`getVirtualAddress`
for the descriptor cases — and calls

```
filtered_doDeviceAttribute(api = 3, attribute = selector, in, inLen, out, &outLen, state)
```

`agdc_filtered_api_t` complete, from the four callers:
**0 = getDeviceAttribute, 1 = setDeviceAttribute, 2 = doDeviceAttribute,
3 = UserKernelTransfer.**

So **IOPresentment's "selector 1" and "selector 0x980" are AGDC device
attributes 1 and 0x980**, and the thing to implement is the attribute
protocol, not a user client.

In `filtered_doDeviceAttribute` (`0x13dfbf02`), the two differ:

- **0x980 (`kAGDCGPUCapability`)** is handled explicitly (`0x13dfc29e`):
  `bzero(local, 0xdc)`, require a state and `*outLen == 0xdc`, then call
  **virtual slot `0x858`** with `(0x980, in, inLen, &local, &outLen)`. A
  vendor subclass must implement that slot. (`vendor_doDeviceAttribute`,
  `0x13dfd3d4`, is the sibling that calls **slot `0x850`**.)
- **1 (`kAGDCVendorInfo`)** is **not** in the explicit list. The `attr <= 0x7f`
  group (`0x13dfc40a`) handles only **3, 0x10 and 0x20**, so attribute 1 falls
  to the default at `0x13dfd1f1`, which takes an `IORecursiveLock`, indexes a
  16-slot plugin table at `0x13e00940` by `(attr >> 2) & 0x3c0` — slot **0**
  for attribute 1 — retains the plugin there, requires the slot's `+0x18`
  (max attribute) ≥ attr, requires `agdc->0xa0` **and** `agdc->0xa8` non-NULL
  (else `0xE00002D8`), and then calls
  **`AGDCPlugin::doPluginAttribute(agdc, attr, in, inLen, out, outLen, state)`**.

Two side confirmations fell out. Attribute **0x301** at `0x13dfc474` is
`movzwl (%r10),%eax; movw %ax,0xb0(%rdi)` — **2r1's reading of the wrangler's
`0x301` call as a SET that pushes the GPU id INTO AGDC, confirmed from AGDC's
own side.** And live, `ioreg -c AGDCPlugin -r -d1` matches exactly one service,
**`AGDCPluginDisplayMetrics`** (`!registered, !matched`), while
`AppleGraphicsDeviceControlPlugin` is not an `AGDCPlugin` at all.

### What this costs, stated before anyone starts building

`__ZTV26AppleGraphicsDeviceControl` spans `0x13dff478`..`0x13dffd30` = **0x8b8
bytes = 279 pointers**, so a subclass needs a ~277-method instance vtable plus
the metaclass vtable 2qy showed is also required (its `alloc()` is pure virtual
on the base). That is on top of implementing the attribute protocol — at
minimum slot `0x858` for `kAGDCGPUCapability` and a plugin path for
`kAGDCVendorInfo` — in a class whose superclass lives in a different kernel
collection, i.e. through 2qy's runtime-metaclass route, with Apple's code
calling our methods and **no fail-safe**. `SCOPE-FRAMEBUFFER.md` §6 counted one
vtable for a smaller class; this is strictly larger.

And it still does not answer what 2qn proved no client probe can:
whether IOPresentment works *past* the gate, since `IONDRVFramebuffer`
implements neither `IOPresentmentBindIOAccelSurfaceToResource` nor
`SetPlaneState`.

### Tooling

- `dscsym.sh` / `dscsym_many.sh` dlopen IOPresentment and IOKit; a failed
  dlopen prints and is skipped rather than silently renaming every address.
- `dscinv.sh IOPresentment` (base `0x7FF812E88000`, len `0x1C000` from
  `dyld_info -segments`): 449 functions.
- `make agdcinfo` — the oracle above. Its two load-bearing answers need no
  root; the third (would the wrangler itself answer attribute 1?) returned
  `kIOReturnNotPermitted` unprivileged, as the tool pre-stated, and needs
  `sudo ./build/out/agdcinfo` to be decided.

### Next

The display half is now closed as a **decision**, not a read. Either accept
2ql's verdict and leave the desktop on software compositing, or take on a
~277-slot runtime `AppleGraphicsDeviceControl` subclass that also implements
the attribute protocol — with the post-gate question still open behind it.
One cheap thing is left and it is the user's to run:
`sudo ./build/out/agdcinfo`, which says whether an AGDC user client on this
machine answers attribute 1 at all.

## 2r6 — the universal fix's one silent failure, closed

No boot. The debt named in 2op's loose threads: *"hardening the universal fix
with a visible signal when an OS update moves the driver."*

**The defect was rule 14 on the plugin's most-travelled path.** 2on's design
is fail-safe — every site is read back and compared before anything is
written, so an OS update that moves `amdMtl_HWL_DetermineSwizzleMode` leaves
the desktop *unpatched* rather than wrongly patched. Correct, and silent: the
counters were published at the **end** of `rbgpu_mtlk_on_exec`, after the
stage-B detour, so in exactly that case the function returned at `if
(!caveOk)` and `mtlk_patched`, `mtlk_failed` and `mtlk_cavehits` were **all
absent**. Absent is indistinguishable from "the hook never ran" — which is the
rule 14 mistake, committed on the one path that runs ~2000 times a boot. The
only trace was a `rbgpu_log` line for the first 8 execs, and 2qw already
established that a log that lands only in a capture is not enough.

Three changes, all in `src/plugin/kern_start.cpp`:

1. **`g_mtlkLastMatch`**, set inside `rbgpu_mtlk_place` on **every** call
   (1 = original found, 2 = already placed, 0 = neither, 0xFFFF = the read
   itself failed). The diag key of the same meaning is written only while the
   report budget lasts, so after 8 execs this global is the only carrier.
2. **`mtlk_moved`** counts `g_mtlkLastMatch == 0` — the read succeeded and
   **neither** pattern is there. That is the signature an OS update produces,
   and it is a different thing from a failed read, a NULL task map or an
   unsolved symbol, each of which already had its own key.
3. **`rbgpu_mtlk_counters()`** publishes
   `mtlk_cavehits`/`mtlk_patched`/`mtlk_failed`/`mtlk_moved` on **every** path
   out. Throttled to the first 64 scoped execs, then every 256th: the comment
   on `g_mtlkReportBudget` warns that `rbgpu_diag_set_num` takes a lock and
   scans the whole key table, and rule 16 says the instrument is a suspect, so
   this must not become the slowest thing in the plugin. 64 execs is already
   enough to make a "nothing was ever patched" verdict certain, and the tail
   sampling keeps the final counts honest for ~8 extra writes per boot.

**The visible signal is `mtlk_moved_verdict 1`**, set once per boot when 8
scoped execs have all missed the pattern with `mtlk_patched == 0`, with a log
line naming the cave (`RBGPU_MTL_CAVE_VM`, its anchor) and the detour
(`RBGPU_MTL_FN_VM`) unslid, plus this boot's slide — so the next session can
re-derive both against the new `AMDRadeonX6000MTLDriver` and edit
`src/plugin/rbgpu_mtlcave.h` without spending a boot to find out where things
went. `plugin_check.sh` dumps the whole `RBGPUDiag`, so the new keys appear in
every capture with no script change.

Built: hosttest all passed, UUID moved `5C3D0EA9` -> `C3FEAF28`, no new
compiler warnings in the edited region (the `-Wsign-conversion` lines are all
pre-existing, around line 1040 and below).

**Not verified on hardware.** Nothing here changes what is written — the
write path, the ordering and the read-back are untouched — but the throttle
arithmetic and the new counters are only *claimed* correct until a boot shows
`mtlk_patched` still counting up and `mtlk_moved` absent. The honest reading
of a normal boot after this: `mtlk_moved` and `mtlk_moved_verdict` should both
be **absent**, `mtlk_cavehits` should be in the low thousands and
`mtlk_patched` should track it. If `mtlk_moved_verdict` is 1, the desktop will
have artifacts and the log line says what to do.

## 2r7 — the `av=N fail=N` debt, paid: the reading was wrong, not the driver

No boot. One disassembly, as §6 said it would take.

`rbgpu-vmid` has printed `av=N fail=N` with the two **equal** in every boot
that ever read it, and the standing note said "every `assignVMID` reports
failure by the hook's own criterion while VMIDs are plainly handed out".

`AMDRadeonX6000_AMDHWVMM::assignVMID` is at **`0xbe91376`** in
`build/re/AMDRadeonX6000`, and it has **exactly one `retq`** (`0xbe914f3`).
The instruction two before it is:

```
be914d2   testl %r14d, %r14d        ; the vmid the context already had
be914d5   je    be914f4             ; 0 -> do the invalidate work
be914d7   movq  -0x40(%rbp), %rax   ; the `bool *` out-parameter
be914db   testq %rax, %rax
be914de   je    be914e3
be914e0   movb  %r12b, (%rax)       ; *flag = (freshly assigned)
be914e3   movb  $0x1, %al           ; <-- THE RETURN VALUE
be914e5   addq  $0x48, %rsp
...
be914f3   retq
```

and `0xbe914d7` is reached from **every** path: the already-assigned early
exit (`je` at `0xbe914d5` not taken), the invalidate-submitted exit (`je` at
`0xbe91538`), the no-channel exit (`je` at `0xbe9154e`) and the full path
(`jmp` at `0xbe915b6`).

**So `assignVMID` returns `bool`, and it always returns `true`. There is no
failure return in the function.** `av == fail` never meant "every call
failed"; it meant **every call succeeded**, counted by a hook whose criterion
was `r != 0`. This is 2ha in its purest form — *a return code is not a result
until the code that sets it has been read* — and the thing that made it
plausible for fifteen milestones is that `0 == success` is the right
convention for `IOReturn`, which this function does not use.

The declaration was wrong twice over. A C++ mangled name **does not encode the
return type**, so `uint32_t (*)(void *, void *, uint32_t *, void *, void *,
void *)` was an assumption with nothing behind it; and the SysV ABI defines
only **`%al`** for a `bool` return, so the upper 24 bits of what the hook read
as a `uint32_t` were whatever the previous computation left in `%eax` — here
the assigned VMID, via `movl %eax, -0x64(%rbp)` at `0xbe914bc`. That is why a
boot could report a `fail` value that was not even 1.

Fixed: the hook and the original's type are both `bool`, and the counter is
kept **under its old key** so existing captures stay comparable, now counting
`r == false`. The disassembly says that cannot happen, so from here a nonzero
`fail` means the driver changed and everything else in that note should be
re-derived before it is trusted — which is now written into the note's own
legend.

Built: hosttest all passed, UUID moved `C3FEAF28` -> `442DF066`. The four
`-Wshadow` warnings are pre-existing and unchanged (4 before, 4 after,
measured by stashing).

Also corrected in `docs/HANDOFF.md` §6, where it had been standing wrong since
2qw: **"the diag table is full at `d=73`"**. The cap is **768**, and the table
seeds `diag_max`/`diag_used` into slots 0 and 1 before any real key. Rule 14's
actual requirement — check `diag_used` against `diag_max` before concluding
from an absent key — is what replaces it.

## 2r8 — root is refused for an ENTITLEMENT, not a capability; only WindowServer holds it

`sudo ./build/out/agdcinfo` (boot of 2026-10-25). Output is in the session;
the load-bearing lines:

```
[1] name="AppleGPUWrangler" ... -> SKIPPED by the name test
    IOServiceOpen(type 2)        = 0xe00002e2 (kIOReturnNotPermitted)
matched 1, skipped 1, candidates 0
== 2. control: IOServiceOpen(MACH_PORT_NULL, ..., 2) = 0x10000003
```

So **as root, the wrangler's own AGDC user client still returns
`kIOReturnNotPermitted`** — the same `0xe00002e2` the unprivileged run gave.
2r5 pre-stated the unprivileged refusal as inconclusive; the root refusal is
the new fact, and it means `sudo` is not the missing privilege.

`AppleGraphicsDeviceControlClient::authorizeTask` (`0x13dfaf46`) says why,
read whole:

```
copyClientEntitlement(task, "com.apple.private.applegraphicsdevicecontrol")  ; 0x13dfafb8
  present -> authorized
else copyClientEntitlement(task, "com.apple.private.gpuwrangler")            ; 0x13dfaff3
  present -> authorized
else IOLog("AGDCC: Unauthorized client '%s' blocked (%s)") ; return FAIL     ; 0x13dfb0cd
```

(entitlement strings `0x13dfdd9c` / `0x13dfddc9`, the block message
`0x13dfdde7`, all confirmed by reading `(__TEXT,__cstring)`). **The gate is a
code-signing entitlement, which `sudo` does not grant** — uid 0 and an
unprivileged process both lack those two private entitlements, so both are
refused identically. The one holder of
`com.apple.private.applegraphicsdevicecontrol` on this system is
**WindowServer** (its name is a literal `0x13dfde16` in the very same
function, used only to format the block message), which is exactly the process
boot 150 saw take the failure. So **no tool a user can run from a shell can
probe attribute 1**, root or not; only WindowServer opens this client.

This does not touch 2r5's verdict. The association map is empty because our
only AGDC service is `AppleGPUWrangler`, which IOPresentment skips by name —
a **missing per-GPU `AppleGraphicsDeviceControl`**, not an access problem. The
entitlement gate only closes the measurement, not the diagnosis.

### The one Apple lever, flagged and NOT pursued

`authorizeTask`'s first branch (`0x13dfaf72`) is
`cmpb $-0x1, 0x13e00884; jne <skip the parse>`, and when that cached byte is
`0xFF` it runs `PE_parse_boot_argn("agdc_entitle", &b, 1)` (string
`0x13dfdd8f`) and stores `b != 0` back. When the resulting flag at
`0x13e00884` is non-zero, the check at `0x13dfb016`
(`cmpb $0x0, 0x13e00884; jne <authorized>`) **bypasses the entitlement test
entirely.** All **three** references to that byte are inside `authorizeTask`
(`0x13dfaf72`, `0x13dfafa8`, `0x13dfb016`) — `ripxref` over the whole AGDC
`__text` finds no others — so the blast radius is this one function.

**Not pursued, and it is the user's call if ever:** `agdc_entitle` is an
Apple-internal development boot-arg that disables a code-signing authorization
check across AGDC; it is untested here, and before arming it one would need to
read **what sets `0x13e00884` to `0xFF`** (the initial-sentinel guard) and
whether that path even runs on a release kernel — it was not spent on this
turn. It would at most let a user-run tool reach `authorizeTask`; it would
**not** create the missing AGDC service, so it answers the measurement
question and nothing about the diagnosis. Noted so it is in the record, not
proposed.

## 2r9 — tiled client render targets and linear kernel surfaces are different paths

2026-10-25. **No reboot, no kext load, no boot-arg or NVRAM write.**
Continued the second loose thread in HANDOFF §2 rather than building the
unapproved runtime AGDC subclass. The display blocker from 2r5/2r8 stands.

### Preconditions, recorded before treating anything as a new boot

`rbgpu-boot` is **154**, the SAME boot as the latest disk capture. This is
additional userspace measurement on that existing accelerated boot, not boot
155 and not a new test of the pending plugin. `kextstat` reports loaded UUID
**16A3402E-96BD-3DDB-BA76-4F6D4FF094BB**, while `build/out` is
**442DF066-9584-3FD2-BB1E-2B5CABB2DD0C**. Therefore **2r6's diagnostic
hardening and 2r7's bool fix remain unverified on hardware**. Live
`RBGPUDiag`: `armed=1`, `diag_used=524 < diag_max=768`, `linear_force=1`,
`mtlk_patched=14903`, `mtlk_cavehits=14965`, `mtlk_failed=74` at the recorded
snapshot. Those counters move as processes exec; they are not a new boot nonce.
`rbgpu-mcreg` is now absent (read-only check), so 2qy's deletion is no longer
pending on this boot.

Evidence directory: **`logs/20261025-2r9-texturepath/`**. `preconditions.txt`
holds the loaded/built UUIDs, live boot-args and diagnostics. The final runs
are the six **`<width>x<height>-{control,watched}.txt`** files.

### The question 2oo left behind

2oo explained the need for both fixes as kernel LINEAR disagreeing with
userspace tiling until the userspace fix also selected LINEAR. But `fix`
deliberately keeps render targets tiled, and they work. The missing premise
was whether a plain Metal texture's backing allocation is a kernel texture
layout at all. A count of resources whose `+0x1dc` reads 0 cannot answer that
without identifying their resource type and format.

### First read the initializer's actual branch

In `AMDAccelResourceAddr2::initialize` (`0xbe56894`):

- The base `AMDAccelResource::initialize` copies **`args+0x68`**, one byte,
  into the resource's format byte (`res+0x1b4`) at **`0xbe4de84`**.
- Back in the Addr2 override, **`0xbe56958`** zero-extends that low byte into
  `%edx`. At **`0xbe569a6`**, `testl %edx,%edx; sete %cl`, combined with
  `negb %al; setno %al; orb %cl,%al; jne 0xbe56a14`, bypasses the swizzle
  lookup when **format is zero**. The other condition restricts the lookup
  to resource type **0x80** (`negb` overflows only for byte 0x80).
- Only the non-bypassed path at `0xbe569b4` clears `res+0x1dc`, calls
  `res->0x250->vt[0x1b8](0)` at `0xbe569cb`, and stores its low five bits.
  **The histogram reads that resource field, not a client image descriptor.**
- `IOAccelResource2::init` independently stores the supplied type byte at
  `res+0x14`, **`0x14e3447e`**. Types are not guessed from allocation sizes.

These instructions give a testable distinction; they do not identify what
Metal actually passes. That was measured next.

### The two new tools and their controls

**`tools/resourcewatch.c`**, `make resourcewatch`: per-process interposition
on **`IOAccelResourceCreate`**, observe-only. Its three-argument signature
and pointer return were read from unslid **`0x7ff80d33ce77`**: it forwards
the second and third arguments unchanged to `IOConnectCallMethod`, selector
0. The interposer reads at most `min(size,0x108)` through
`mach_vm_read_overwrite` on its own task, logs a failed/short read explicitly,
calls the original with unchanged arguments and returns its unchanged handle.
It prints both an initial loaded line and final intercepted-call/failure
counts, so zero intercepted calls means **INCONCLUSIVE**, not no allocations.
No patch to the driver's instructions and no launchd environment.

**`tools/texturepath.m`**, `make texturepath`: a shared-buffer control, plain
shader-read texture, plain render-target texture and IOSurface-backed render
target, bracketed with BEGIN/END markers. Read the *texture's own GPU image
descriptor* too: Objective-C runtime metadata gives the `GFX10_MtlTexture`
ivar **`_gfx10` at +0x2c8**, and its full type encoding names
`texImgRsrcDesc.SQ_IMG_RSRC_WORD3.SW_MODE`. Four 3-bit channel selectors and
two 4-bit mip levels precede its five bits, hence **`(WORD3 >> 20) & 31`**.
The tool resolves the ivar offset at runtime, checks the class/type encoding
and instance bounds, and reports **INCONCLUSIVE** on an unknown layout. The
metadata dump is saved in `ivars.txt`; the mode was not inferred from the
footprint or from a variable named `swizzle`.

An initial uniform-clear check passed, but **cannot expose a permutation of
tiles**. It was replaced before drawing the conclusion. The final tool draws
a fullscreen triangle whose fragment shader encodes x/y into all RGB
channels, blits the private render target to a shared buffer, waits for
completion, and compares **every pixel** with the CPU formula (one UNORM
quantization level allowed). The initial `control.txt`/`watched.txt` are
preliminary uniform-clear runs, superseded by the six dimension-named logs.
This remains a test of the allocation/layout distinction, **not an oracle
for the original application text defect** (texprobe's limitation stands).

### What arrived at the kernel, at all three sizes

64×64, 640×480 and 1024×768, each in a fresh process with and without the
observer; all with the existing system policy and `linear_force=1`:

| API object | IOAccelResourceCreate type | format byte +0x68 | Own GPU descriptor SW_MODE |
|---|---|---|---|
| Plain shader-read texture | 0x40 | 0 | 0 at all three sizes |
| Plain render target | 0x40 | 0 | **6**, **10**, **10**, respectively |
| IOSurface-backed render target | 0x82 | 0x0f | 0 at all three sizes |

The plain-RT phase contains **one** create, so the corresponding allocation
is unambiguous; its requested byte count agrees with `allocatedSize` (e.g.
**1,310,720** for 640×480). Its `vendor104` is 0x1000; no per-texture format
is handed to the kernel in that request. The shader-read phase includes
first-use allocations, so the table classifies the backing type/format,
not every incidental allocation's ownership.

Every watched run intercepted **13** calls, all successful. Both controls
and watched runs have the same descriptor modes. Every patterned render
completed; **0 mismatches out of 4,096 / 307,200 / 786,432 pixels**, twice
each, for **2,195,456 checked pixels** total. The two tiled descriptor values
are directly observed, not deduced from the successful rendering.

Reproduce on an accelerated boot without root:

```
make texturepath resourcewatch
env -u DYLD_INSERT_LIBRARIES ./build/out/texturepath 640 480
env DYLD_INSERT_LIBRARIES="$PWD/build/out/resourcewatch.dylib" ./build/out/texturepath 640 480
```

### What is closed, and what is still owed

**Closed for the measured plain-texture path:** the kernel's linear force
does not recompute this render target's texture layout. It allocates raw
backing memory; the userspace driver keeps the tiled layout in its own GPU
descriptor. A zero in the backing resource's `+0x1dc` is therefore compatible
with a tiled client texture. **2oo's blanket kernel/userspace disagreement
explanation is withdrawn**, including the matching source comment, now
corrected. The boot-131/132 experiment still proves both fixes are needed;
no hook or policy was removed.

**Still owed:** why the `_X` family is wrong, and exactly which AppKit backing
surface/lifecycle makes the kernel force fix Terminal. The IOSurface control
shows a separate allocation path, but these scratch allocations do not trace
CoreAnimation's backing-store lifecycle. Nothing here advances the missing
AGDC protocol or turns on Metal display compositing.

Both new tools built with **`-Wall -Wextra -Werror`**; the six final runs
exited 0 and `git diff --check` passed. Only a comment changed in the plugin;
no plugin build or hardware configuration was changed by this milestone.

## 2ra — framebuffer work: the missing per-GPU AGDC bridge is implemented and built

2026-10-25. The user clarified **"continue the GPU framebuffer work"**.
Returned to 2r5's measured blocker and implemented its missing service. This
is a kernel change prepared for a user-run boot test, **not a claim that the
framebuffer or Metal display compositing now works**. No kext was loaded,
no EFI installed, and no boot-arg or NVRAM variable changed in this turn.

### The vendor protocol has an exact reference implementation here

`AMDRadeonX6000Framebuffer` names both methods; no need to invent the replies:

- **`AmdAgdcServices::getVendorInfo`, 0xbffb59a**: require output size 0x2c,
  zero the reply, +0x00 = 0x30000, +0x04 = "AMD", +0x24 = 0x1002,
  **+0x28 = 2**. The separate `AmdGpuWrangler::getVendorInfo` at
  **0xc010918** instead writes **7**, which is deliberately excluded by
  IOPresentment's {1,2} role test. This is why renaming the existing wrangler
  would not supply the per-GPU reply even if its name gate were removed.
- **`AmdAgdcServices::getGpuCapability`, 0xbffb712**: output size 0xdc,
  count +0x30, PCI entry +0x34, framebuffer array +0x3c. The cached struct is
  at service+0x140; stores at **0xbffb9b8/0xbffb9cf** populate those entries
  from the controller's actual objects. Controller vtable slots were checked
  by name: +0x8b8 = getPciDevice, +0x8c8 = getNumFramebuffer, +0x8d0 =
  getFramebuffer. So these are **kernel object pointers**, not registry IDs.
- **`AGDC::filtered_doDeviceAttribute`, 0x13dfd167** converts the PCI pointer
  through `IORegistryEntry::getRegistryEntryID`, then the framebuffer array
  (bounded to eight), before copying 0xdc bytes to the client's output at
  **0x13dfd1bf**. That conversion must remain in the call chain. Returning
  registry IDs from the vendor callback would make Apple dereference IDs as
  pointers; bypassing the filter with the kernel form would leak addresses.

`src/common/rb_agdc.h` now builds the exact vendor reply and a conservative
one-framebuffer capability reply, using the real objects. Optional feature
masks are zero: no invented link, VRR, DSC, brightness or modeset support.

### The runtime class is smaller than the "277 methods" description implied

**`src/plugin/rbgpu_agdc.cpp`** watches the real AGDC kext (bundle id and path
verified against its installed Info.plist). It clones the live **0x8b8-byte
instance vtable** and **0xe8-byte metaclass table**, preserving their address
points at +0x10. Static analysis checked every overridden/relevant slot:

| Instance slot | Treatment |
|---|---|
| 0x00 / 0x08 | Replace abstract D1/D0 traps with base-D2/IOFree wrappers |
| 0x38 | Return our registered runtime metaclass |
| 0x5c0 / 0x770 | Preserve Apple's start / newUserClient, verify by symbol |
| 0x850 | Replace the sole `__cxa_pure_virtual` with our vendor callback |
| 0x858 | Preserve Apple's state-to-arguments vendor wrapper |

The metaclass allocator is overridden at **0x88**. Everything else is copied,
not reimplemented. The live constructor receives our metaclass; the allocator
calls `instanceConstructed`, just as the SDK's generated constructors do.
`OSObject::free` at **0xffffff8000a4b880** was read before choosing destruction:
it obtains the virtual metaclass, calls `instanceDestructed`, and then dispatches
the deleting destructor. Our wrapper must not decrement the count twice.

Runtime guards separately solve and compare the six relevant instance slots
and metaclass allocator, table bounds/terminators and all callable entries;
the only pure virtual must be slot 0x850. The routed filter's first eight
bytes must be **55 48 89 e5 41 57 41 56**, with no branch in the displaced
prefix. Every mangled name was checked defined in the extracted AGDC binary,
and the whole-plugin search found no pre-existing route.

### Keep Apple's user client and its entitlement check

`newUserClient`, `AppleGraphicsDeviceControlClient` and `authorizeTask` are
unchanged. 2r8's root-entitlement result stands. Attribute **1** ordinarily
falls into the global plugin table, so the new filtered-method hook supplies
it **only when this == our service**. All other services and all other
attributes, particularly 0x980 with its pointer conversion, call the original.
Unsupported vendor operations return Unsupported; they are not faked successful.

The service is **RembrandtGPUAGDC**, attached to our actual 1002:1681 PCI
device, and its capability reply names the existing IONDRVFramebuffer.
There is no framebuffer takeover or new static AGDC/IOGraphicsFamily import.
The bridge itself writes no DCN registers. Apple's newly reachable presentation
code remains untested and may still fail or blank the panel.

### Startup, arming and lifetime

The existing `enableController` route hands off the framebuffer after calling
the original. Registration runs on a thread-call worker, outside that hook.
It waits boundedly for the superclass to be **registered**, not merely nonzero
BSS (2qv), and for AppleGPUWrangler to exist before entering AGDC::start's
otherwise unbounded wait. Either kext/framebuffer arrival order can wake it.
It verifies class size **0x110** and IOService superclass before constructing.

`preModLoad` / metaclass ctor / `postModLoad` reuse 2qy's successful protocol.
No diagnostics or returns occur while the stalled-class lock is held;
postModLoad is unconditional, including a NULL pre handle. The instance is
initialized and attached, then Apple's AGDC::start publishes it. Its initial
reference stays pinned for the boot **even if start returns false**, because
2pl already proved cross-kext registrations outlive an IOKit start failure.

**OFF unless -rbgpuagdc AND one-shot rbgpu-agdc.** The fail-closed one-shot
must be consumed before the filtered hook is installed or any runtime class is
registered. The already verified IOP gate patch still needs **its own**
one-shot in that boot. Full user-run commands and recovery are in
**`docs/SPEC-AGDC-BRIDGE.md`**; no install/activation was done here.

`agdc_stage`, `agdc_error`, `agdc_oneshot`, `agdc_started` and the separate
**`agdc_user_vendor` / `agdc_user_cap`** counts go at the front of the existing
NVRAM hot-key list. Base AGDC::start calls the vendor callback too, so a vendor
count alone must not be mistaken for a WindowServer query. The last requested
attribute and last unsupported vendor attribute are also recorded. Every
refusal has a numeric error plus a readable reason. plugin_check now captures
`rbgpu-agdc`, avoiding 2qy's missing-one-shot-key instrumentation defect.

### Validation and the actual next step

**`make plugin` passes**, including the existing ASan/UBSan hosttest and its
300,000 parser mutations. New protocol tests exercise NULL/zero identities,
every invalid size through 0xdd with unchanged-buffer checks, guard bytes,
AMD identity/role, pointer offsets and zero optional features. A mutation
changing GPU role **2 to 7** makes the new tests fail, as required. The new
plugin translation unit compiles under `-Werror`; no new warning there.

**`tools/check_imports.py` resolves 362/362 imports** through the existing
IOPCIFamily and kpi libraries. `nm -u` has IOMallocZero/IOFree as positive
controls and **no AGDC or IOFramebuffer imports**. Info.plist gained no
dependency. Shell syntax and `git diff --check` pass. UUID moved from
**442DF066… to 902BE8B3-FA45-3CA3-AABD-94E526538A31**. Build log saved to
`logs/20261025-2ra-agdc/build.txt`.

**Next: the user-run boot test of this build, with AGDC and IOP both armed.**
First require a new boot nonce and matching loaded UUID, then
`agdc_mc_post=0`, `agdc_mc_ok=1`, `agdc_started=1`, `iop_verify=1` and a live
RembrandtGPUAGDC service. User-attribute counters show whether IOPresentment
actually queried it. A service publishing is only partial success: the real
verdict is a created display pipe, IOSurface-backed display surfaces and
Metal display compositing. If it stops on another attribute or on plane/bind
support, that is the next framebuffer implementation task. It has not been
tested on hardware, and nothing in these host checks proves that final chain.

## 2rb — boot 155 refused the bridge before registration: the kernel symbol helper selected a zero-length range

2026-10-25. User supplied `logs/20261025-173030-plugin` and
`logs/20261025-173052-compositor/compositor.txt`. Read the saved boot nonce
first: **155**, after 154. Loaded UUID **902BE8B3-FA45-3CA3-AABD-94E526538A31**
agrees with the 2ra build. This was a real armed test of the intended build.

### What ran, and what did not

The IOP input patch landed: **iop_verify=1**, iop_match=1, iop_patched=1,
iop_oneshot=0. The AGDC bridge did **not** get as far as its one-shot:
**agdc_error=1**, agdc_say="required symbols/ranges", agdc_fb_seen=1,
agdc_wait_load=1; rbgpu-agdc is still **1**, while rbgpu-iop and rbgpu-arm
are absent. No runtime AGDC class registration or service start was attempted.
This is a defect in our preparation code, not a negative hardware answer.

The diagnostic table has room: **522 used / 768 max**. The NVRAM summary's
`d=105` is its separate truncation count, and its numeric values are hex:
`diag_max=300`, `diag_used=20a`. It is not a full IORegistry diag table.

### The existing log contains the exact cause

`logs/20261025-173030-plugin/log.txt`, all four at **17:28:29.580–.581**:

```
patcher: address 0xFFFFFF8011449940 is out of range 0x0000000000000000 with size 0
patcher: address 0xFFFFFF801144A190 is out of range 0x0000000000000000 with size 0
patcher: address 0xFFFFFF801144A290 is out of range 0x0000000000000000 with size 0
patcher: address 0xFFFFFF8011475800 is out of range 0x0000000000000000 with size 0
```

These are OSMetaClass's ctor, preModLoad, postModLoad and __cxa_pure_virtual,
all valid kernel symbols. `third_party/Lilu/Lilu/Headers/kern_patcher.hpp`
**209–224** defines the overload the new helper called:

```
solveSymbol(id, name, start, size):
    addr = solveSymbol(id, name)
    if addr >= start && addr < start + size: return addr
    code = InvalidSymbolFound
    return 0
```

2ra's helper supplied its default **base=0, size=0** for kernel symbols but
still called this FOUR-argument overload. The underlying symbol lookup
succeeded, then the empty range necessarily rejected it. The prior static
ABI tests checked names/slots/prologue but never exercised this helper's
choice of overload. That gap cost boot 155.

### Fix and regression

`src/plugin/rbgpu_agdc_lookup.hpp` now resolves with Lilu's **two-argument**
API, records the raw result, and applies **explicit bounds only to kext
symbols**. Bounds use `address >= base && address-base < size`, avoiding
base+size overflow. Null results and the existing kernel/kext pointer-floor
checks still refuse. No class, reply layout, hook target or arming policy
changed.

`tools/hosttest/agdc_lookup_test.cpp` exercises the exact failing case: a
valid kernel address with no supplied range, plus valid/outside/empty kext
ranges, preserved rejected addresses and a missing symbol. It runs under
ASan/UBSan as part of `make hosttest` / `make plugin`. Mutating the resolver
back to `solveSymbol(id,name,base,size)` makes the regression fail, including
the kernel lookup and raw-address assertions. The real Lilu implementation
above is the basis for that mock's overload behavior.

Also repaired the instrument's refusal path: **every one of the ten input
addresses** is recorded in RBGPUDiag, alongside callback base/size. The helper's
own logs were absent from the saved log ring because early lines were evicted;
only Lilu's unified-log warnings survived. **agdc_solved** now records the
accepted inputs, expected **0x3ff / 1023**; bits 5–8 are the four kernel
inputs. It is NVRAM-hot. `agdc_bad_slot` identifies a failed instance-slot
check. Future early refusals no longer require recovering overwritten logs
just to tell which input was missing.

### The compositor capture does not answer a new display question

It measured a live accelerator/Metal device, nonzero acceleratorPort 0x2203,
135.63 Hz callback pacing and **0 flips / 0 swaps**. But **render_update=0**
and no compositor frames were sampled: its own verdict is **INCONCLUSIVE:
the display may have been idle**. No inference that Metal display compositing
works or fails is made from that sample. The bridge's preparation refusal is
already the decisive finding for this test; another compositor sample before
fixing it would not exercise the missing service.

Incidental existing-fix validation, not the framebuffer task: `rbgpu-vmid`
now reads **av=2611 fail=0**, the first hardware confirmation of 2r7's bool
return correction. 2r6's normal path publishes mtlk_patched=1788,
mtlk_cavehits=1792 and mtlk_failed=7, with both moved keys absent and capacity
available. That verifies ordinary counter publication, not the unexercised
OS-update/moved-pattern failure path.

### Build and next boot

`make plugin`: host tests and the new lookup regression pass. The new module
builds with -Werror. `tools/check_imports.py` resolves **362/362** symbols;
`git diff --check` passes. UUID moved **902BE8B3… →
667372BC-502F-31A6-BFF2-60E61AAAF29F**. Log:
`logs/20261025-2rb-agdc/build.txt`.

**Next is the SAME AGDC+IOP boot test with the rebuilt kext**, not another
experimental branch. The flags are already present from boot 155. The user
installs the rebuild, checks EFI status, rearms IOP and rbgpu-arm (both were
consumed), and leaves/reasserts rbgpu-agdc=1. Then capture plugin_check before
another reboot. Require agdc_solved=0x3ff, agdc_error=0, agdc_mc_post=0,
agdc_mc_ok=1, agdc_started=1 and iop_verify=1 before interpreting the next
presentation failure. No EFI, NVRAM, kext load/unload or reboot was performed
by the agent in this turn.

WindowServer's display errors. Recovered a broader historical log into

a concrete presentation blocker; it does not yet explain every GPU progress

## 2rd — `AGDCLinkConfig_t` identified: it is a PUBLIC struct, and IOPresentment validates none of its timing

2026-10-26. No boot, no build. Static only, against `build/re/AMDRadeonX6000Framebuffer`
(`__text 0xbfcc6a0 + 0x1ed164`, which is the image 2rc's addresses live in) and
the dyld cache.

### 1. The reply layout, from `getLinkConfig` itself

`__ZNK30AMDRadeonX6000_AmdAgdcServices13getLinkConfigEP16AGDCLinkConfig_tm`
at **`0xc009184`** — the symbol is intact, so the name is Apple's. Guards
first: `out != NULL`, `len == 0xb0` exactly (`cmpq $0xb0,%rdx; jne` at
`0xc0091a0`), and `out[0] <= this->0x170 - 1` (the framebuffer count, an
**unsigned** compare, so count 0 would wrap and reject everything). Then
`fb = this->0x118->vt[0x900](out[0])` and `link = this->0x118->vt[0x8e8](fb->0xec)`
must both be non-NULL, and `fb->0xd0 != 0`.

The fill is a near-verbatim block copy from `fb->0x1c` to `out+0x10`, i.e.
shifted by exactly **-0xc**, in four groups: **7 dwords**, **3 unaligned
`movq`s**, **18 dwords**, **8 `movzwl`/`movw` halves**. That shape is
`IODetailedTimingInformationV2` from the **public**
`IOKit/graphics/IOGraphicsTypes.h`, whose own groups are 10 dwords (3 of them
`__reservedA`), 3 `UInt64`s, 18 dwords, 9 `UInt16`s — and `-0xc` is exactly
`sizeof(__reservedA[3])`.

Verified by `offsetof`, not by counting header lines (2q4's rule), with the
timing base hypothesised at `out+0x04`:

```
sizeof(V2) = 0xa0 ; 0x04 + 0xa0 = 0xa4   <- exactly the next written field
horizontalScaledInset              reply+0x10   (first copied dword)
signalLevels                       reply+0x28   (seventh, last before the u64s)
pixelClock / minPixelClock / maxPixelClock
                                   reply+0x2c / 0x34 / 0x3c  (the three movqs)
horizontalActive                   reply+0x44
verticalBlankingExtension          reply+0x88   (eighteenth, last dword)
pixelEncoding                      reply+0x8c   (first half)
verticalBlankingMaxStretchPerFrame reply+0x9a   (last half copied)
verticalBlankingMaxShrinkPerFrame  reply+0x9c   (NOT copied - left zero)
```

Every one matches the disassembly. So:

```c
struct AGDCLinkConfig_t {                        // 0xb0 bytes
    uint32_t                      framebufferIndex;  // +0x00  (input; see §2)
    IODetailedTimingInformationV2 timing;            // +0x04, sizeof 0xa0
        // __reservedA[0]    @ +0x04 = AGDC link id, 0xFFFFFFFF = none
        // __reservedA[1..2] @ +0x08 = AGDC flags (u64; only the low byte is built)
    uint32_t                      streamIndex;       // +0xa4
    uint32_t                      field_a8;          // +0xa8  <- fb->0xf0
    uint32_t                      streamState;       // +0xac  translateAmdStreamState()
};                                                   // sums to exactly 0xb0
```

**AGDC reuses `__reservedA[3]`, which the header documents as "Init to 0",
for its own link id and flags.** That is why the copy is shifted by 0xc.

Two details worth having, both corrections to 2rc's wording:
`+0xa4` is **not** a "stream address" — it is `fb->0xec + 1`, zero when
`fb->0xec == 0xff` (`cmpl $0xff; cmovel`), i.e. a 1-based **stream index**;
and the flags byte at `+0x08` is assembled as
`0x08 | (linkId != -1 ? 0x10 : 0x02) | ((link->vt[0x150](0xd) & 1) << 2) | fb->0x719`,
so **bit 3 is unconditionally set** and bit 4 vs bit 1 are mutually exclusive.

### 2. IOPresentment checks the IOReturn and ONE bit. Nothing else.

`__GatherAGDCLogicalDeviceCapabilities` at **`0x7ff812e9781a`**, read whole
(0x1c2 bytes):

* `this->0x20` must be non-NULL and `->0x10` non-zero, else **0x808**.
* The buffer is `this+0x2c`, bzero'd to 0x3fc, and **IOPresentment writes the
  framebuffer index itself**: `this->0x2c = deviceRecord->0x50`. We do not
  choose it.
* `IOConnectCallMethod(conn, 0x921, NULL, 0, inStruct = this+0x2c, 0xb0,
  NULL, NULL, outStruct = this+0x2c, &outLen = 0xb0)` — **input and output are
  the same buffer**, which is why 2rc's blanket "inSize must be 0" guard
  rejected it.
* `jne → 0x80e` on any non-zero IOReturn; `je → 0x80e` if `outLen` came back
  zero. Those are the only two failure tests.
* It then copies `reply+0x10 .. reply+0x9b` — the entire timing body — into
  its own cache at `this->0x19b0c..`, with `movups`/`movq`/`movl`/`movw`.
  **It inspects no field of it.**
* `r14d = 0` (success), then `testb $0x1, reply+0x08` — and on either branch
  the function returns **0**.

So **the timing values cannot make this stage fail.** The stage's only
behavioural output is flags bit 0.

And the cache it fills is, within this image, **write-only**: `0x19b00`,
`0x19b0c` and `0x19b10` appear at exactly three sites, all three inside this
one function, all three stores, and `0x19b00`'s address is never taken
(grep over the whole 32 292-line `__text` disassembly). The neighbouring
`0x19c78` *is* read — `addq $0x19c78,%r15` at `0x7ff812e959dd` feeds
`CFNumberCreate(alloc, 3, &value)` → `CFDictionarySetValue` → `CFRelease`
(all three stubs resolved by chained-pointer decode + `atos`), so that one is
published into a capabilities dictionary. **Not established, do not gloss:**
"write-only in this image" is not "nothing ever reads it" — the object could
be handed to a consumer elsewhere. But no consumer exists in IOPresentment and
no pointer to the block is formed there.

### 3. Flags bit 0 opts INTO more unimplemented protocol

The bit-0 branch calls `0x7ff812e98af6`, which sets `this->0x19c78 = 2` and
issues selector **0x925** with a **0xc-byte** in/out struct; if *that* reply's
bit 0 is set it issues a further **0x24-byte** request. AMD's dispatch table
at `0xbfec050` is a table of **int32 offsets from its own base**, not
pointers (`machoread.ptr()` masks them to 30 bits and makes them look like
`0x3ffff...`; reading them as `int32` reproduces 2rc's `0x921 → 0xbfebd9f`
exactly). Decoded:

| attr | stub | tailcalls |
|---|---|---|
| 0x921 | 0xbfebd9f | `getLinkConfig(AGDCLinkConfig_t*, 0xb0)` |
| 0x925 | 0xbfebdc6 | `getPortStatus(AGDCPortStatus_t*, 0xc)` |

So **leave flags bit 0 clear.** With it clear the gather returns success
immediately after the copy and claims nothing; with it set we promise a port
sub-protocol the bridge does not implement. Bit 3 should still be set, because
AMD sets it unconditionally.

### 4. What this changes about the next step

The 0x921 reply does **not** need DCN registers, and it does not need
invention either. `IODetailedTimingInformationV2` is exactly what
`IOFramebuffer::getTimingInfoForDisplayMode` produces (inside
`IOTimingInformation`), and this plugin **already routes**
`IONDRVFramebuffer::getInformationForDisplayMode` (2ou/2q4) and already holds
the framebuffer pointer. So the truthful source for every timing field is the
boot framebuffer's own current mode — read-only, no register access, no
fabricated value, and nothing in the stage branches on it anyway.

2rc's "an offline all-zero reply cannot describe the running panel" remains
the right instinct and is now sharper: a zero reply would **pass** this stage
and poison IOPresentment's cache, which is precisely the failure that would be
hard to find later. Fill it from the framebuffer.

**What this does NOT do**, stated plainly: it makes one request succeed. The
next stage is still 0x711 / `getFbExtendedCapability` with a 0x196c-byte
structure and truthful plane capabilities, and the bind/transaction/scanout
backend after it. Nothing here touches boot 156's frozen panel, the
`checkGPUProgress` channel errors, or the 138 "Attempting to get capabilities
when none exist" messages. No hardware was touched and no boot was spent.

## 2re — 0x921 answered from the boot framebuffer's own timing

2026-10-26. No boot. Builds and host tests only; **not verified on hardware.**

2rd established the layout and that IOPresentment validates none of it. This
implements the reply.

### Reachability is now traced, not inferred

2rc recorded `agdc_last_attr = 0x921` from the *filter* hook and said the
return code was never recorded, so "0x921 reaches the vendor callback" was a
static inference. It is now a traced path through Apple's
`filtered_doDeviceAttribute`: 0x921 is `> 0x703`, `<= 0x922`, `> 0x711`, so
`0x13dfc32b`, where `0x921 - 0x800 = 0x121 > 3` takes `ja` to `0x13dfc5b8`;
it is neither 0x712 nor 0x713, so `jne` to the default at `0x13dfd1f1`; it is
outside the 0x4000 range so `ja` to `0x13dfd204`; `r14b` is still 0 (only the
0x411c path sets it) so `je` to **`0x13dfcf0d`**, which is

```
13dfcf23   callq *0x858(%rax)      ; esi = attribute
```

— the vendor slot the bridge overrides. The argument order at that call is
`(this, attr, in, inLen, out, outLenPtr, state)`, matching the bridge's
callback exactly.

### One correction to my own first cut

I had required `in_size == 0xb0` for 0x921. **Apple does not check inLen at
all** — `getLinkConfig` validates only the output length (`cmpq $0xb0,%rdx` at
`0xc0091a0`) — and input and output are the same userspace structure, so my
check would have invented a refusal the protocol does not have. Removed; the
0xb0 is enforced where Apple enforces it, on the output. A host test now
passes `in_size` of 0 and 0x196c and requires both to succeed, and a wrong
*output* length to refuse without writing.

### What is supplied, and what is refused

`rb_agdc_link_config` in `src/common/rb_agdc.h` — freestanding, bounded,
host-tested. It reads the framebuffer index where Apple reads it (out of the
**output** buffer, because IOPresentment wrote it there), refuses anything but
index 0 since the bridge advertises one framebuffer, copies the V2 body to
+0x04 **first** and only then overwrites the two AGDC overlay words, so the
reused `__reservedA` slots cannot survive.

Refusals, every one of them preferring silence to a fabrication:

* **no timing → Unsupported.** Not a zero fill. 2rd measured that a zero reply
  would *pass* the gather and poison IOPresentment's cache.
* `kIODetailedTimingValid` clear, or zero `horizontalActive`/`verticalActive`
  → refuse (rule 13: the struct is only meaningful when the driver says it is
  filled in).
* flags bit 0 set → refuse, because that claims selector 0x925
  (`getPortStatus`). The builder enforces it so the policy cannot be lost at a
  call site.

The timing source is `IONDRVFramebuffer::getCurrentDisplayMode` +
`getTimingInfoForDisplayMode`, both **defined** in IONDRVSupport (rule 1,
`nm`) and **neither routed** anywhere — `processNDRV` resolves and *calls*
them, so rule 3 is untouched and nothing is patched. The solve sits **before**
the `-rbgpuvbl`/`-rbgpufbaccel` gate, because the bridge is armed
independently of both; a failed solve clears the patcher error so the later
routes in that function are unaffected, publishes both raw results (2rb's
lesson), and leaves 0x921 refused.

`kIODetailedTimingValid = 0x80000000` and `IOAppleTimingID` being `UInt32`
(so the detailed union starts at +0x08) were both read out of the SDK header,
not recalled. They are local `constexpr`s, not an `#include`, so no import is
added and the 2oz trap stays shut.

The bridge reports **one framebuffer with no AGDC link and no stream**: link id
`0xFFFFFFFF`, stream index 0, stream state `0x80000000` — Apple's own values
for "none" and "unknown", and an honest description of what the bridge knows.
Whether anything past this stage requires a real link is **not established**;
this stage does not check, and both are single named constants so one boot's
evidence can change them in one line.

### A test that passed for the wrong reason

The first bit-0 assertion did not trip when the guard was deliberately
removed: the buffer was 0xa5-filled, so the *index* check refused first and
masked it. That is rule 26 applied to a test rather than a search. Fixed by
zeroing the index before each single-guard assertion. Re-verified by breaking
each guard in turn: wrong timing offset **5** failures, bit 0 permitted **3**,
NULL timing not refused **1**, index check removed **1**.

### Build

`make hosttest` and `make plugin` pass, ASan/UBSan and the parser mutations
included. Imports **362 of 362**, the same count as 2rc, through the same
dependencies — `grep -c 'IOGraphicsFamily\|IONDRVSupport' src/plugin/Info.plist`
is **0**. No new compiler warning in any edited file (the 42 that remain are
pre-existing). UUID moved `758BFD86…` → **B8E38412-6CD7-374A-8762-BA53B460AE77**.
Ten new diag keys; boot 156 used 550 of 768, so capacity is not at risk and
`diag_used`/`diag_max` still self-report.

**Nothing here is measured on hardware.** It makes one request answerable from
real values. It does not create a display pipe, and the next stage — 0x711 /
`getFbExtendedCapability`, 0x196c bytes, truthful plane capabilities — plus the
bind/transaction/scanout backend are still absent, as are explanations for boot
156's frozen panel, the `checkGPUProgress` channel errors and the 138
"Attempting to get capabilities when none exist" messages. Activation is
unchanged (`-rbgpuagdc` + `-rbgpuiop` + the one-shots); read `agdc_tim_src 3`,
`agdc_tim_err 0` and `agdc_link_result 0` first, and `agdc_tim_h`/`agdc_tim_v`
must be the panel's own numbers or nothing downstream means anything.

## 2rf — 0x711 answered, and the whole stage needs ONE capability

2026-10-26. No boot. Static reads, host tests and a build; **not verified on
hardware.**

### The structure, closed by its own arithmetic

`getFbExtendedCapability` (`0xbfecb62`, symbol intact) shows
`AGDCFBGetExtendedCapability_t` is a **query**, not a dump:

```
+0x00  u8   framebuffer index   (Apple reads it with movzbl)
+0x04  u32  capability type     (the switch value)
+0x08  u32  count - IN the caller's capacity, OUT the number filled
+0x0c  AGDCFBExtendedCapabilitesEntry_t entries[8], 0x32c each
```

The sizes close it: `getFbCapabilityForScaler` bzeroes `entry+0x08` for
**0x324** bytes, so an entry is 0x32c; `8 * 0x32c = 0x1960`, `+ 0xc = 0x196c`
— both the length Apple's filter demands and the capacity **8** IOPresentment
pre-loads into `+0x08`. Three numbers that were measured separately agreeing is
what makes this a layout rather than a guess.

Apple's switch implements **five** types — 1 CSC (inline), 2 Gamma, 4 Degamma,
0x10 Scaler, 0x8000 Cursor — and returns `kIOReturnUnsupported` for anything
else, with a NULL display path giving `kIOReturnNoDevice` and a zero
`fb->0x719` giving Unsupported. `getFbCapabilityForRotation` exists
(`0xbfed23e`) and is **not** in this switch, so it is reached from some other
attribute; unchased.

### IOPresentment asks for all sixteen bits and needs exactly one

`__GatherAGDCDisplayPipelineCapabilities` (`0x7ff812e979dc`) issues **sixteen**
0x711 queries, one per type bit — 0x10, 0x8, 0x4, 0x2, 0x1, 0x40, 0x20, 0x200,
0x80, 0x100, 0x400, 0x800, 0x1000, 0x2000, 0x4000, 0x8000 — each into its own
0x196c buffer at a different offset in its object, each with capacity 8. Eleven
of those sixteen are types **Apple itself does not implement**, so most of these
queries fail on a real AMD Mac too, and the gather is built to tolerate it:

* `0x808` when there is no device or a zero device count.
* `0x2006` from exactly **two** sites, and both belong to the **first** query,
  type **0x10, the scaler**: a non-zero IOReturn (`0x7ff812e97b1c`, and even
  that is only fatal while `this->0x434` bit 0 is clear), and a returned
  **count of zero** (`movl 0x69f8(%rbx),%eax; testl; je 0x7ff812e98ad3`).
* Every later query's failure just rewrites `outLen` and falls into the next
  one, and the last is preceded by `xorl %r14d,%r14d`, so **even its failure
  returns success**.
* A count of 9 or more is clamped to 8 rather than rejected.

**So the entire stage reduces to: answer type 0x10 with count >= 1.** As with
0x921, IOPresentment reads nothing out of the entries here — only the count,
which it stores at `this->0x42c` before setting `this->0x434` bit 0.

### What the bridge answers

`rb_agdc_extcap` / `rb_agdc_scaler_entry` in `src/common/rb_agdc.h`,
freestanding and host-tested. It reads the index and type **where Apple reads
them**, out of the structure itself, preserves `+0x00`/`+0x04`, rewrites
everything from `+0x08`, and reproduces Apple's own **no-scaling** entry
(`0xbfed05a`): the identity word `0x00080004`, a 1 at `entry+0x1c` and
`+0x1a4`, the two extents twice over in each of two blocks, and the constants
`0x00050005` and 4. The extents come from the same real timing 0x921 uses —
`horizontalActive` at V2+0x40 and `verticalActive` at V2+0x50.

Refusals, again preferring silence to a fabrication: any type but 0x10 →
Unsupported **without writing a byte**; index not 0 → refuse; no timing, or a
zero active dimension → refuse, because there is nothing truthful to say about
a scaler without the panel's size. Only entry 0 is claimed, and entries 1..7
are required to be entirely zero — IOPresentment offered room for eight and a
stale byte there would be a capability nobody implements.

**NOT ESTABLISHED, and deliberately not guessed:** which slot in each pair is
width and which is height. Apple takes them from `fb->0x720` and `fb->0x71c`,
and `updateStreamComposition` (`0xbfe9270`) shows `0x71c` pairing with `0xc0`
and `0x720` with `0xc4` in a letterbox fit — which fixes the *pairing* but not
the axis names, and `populateScalingCapabilities` (`0xbff5d84`) writes the
scaling table from `fb->0xc0`/`0xc4` in the same order without naming them
either. It cannot change this entry's meaning: **source and destination
extents are equal, so transposing both pairs still says 1:1**, and a host test
asserts that equality rather than the axis assignment. Both numbers are
published as diag keys.

### Two guards that the tests did not actually catch

Deliberately breaking each guard (the project's rule for a new test) found two
that passed for the wrong reason:

* Removing the type check didn't fail a test — it failed the **build**,
  `-Werror=unused-but-set-variable`. A real guard, but not the one claimed.
  Re-broken as `type == 0xdeadbeef`, which compiles: **34** failures.
* Removing the `+0x08`-onward zero fill changed nothing, because the test
  started from an already-zeroed buffer. The test now pre-fills that region
  with `0x5c` and requires it rewritten: **5684** failures.

Final verification, each break in turn: hactive/vactive **3**, count **2**,
an entry field **2**, type guard **34**, zero fill **5684**.

### Build

`make hosttest` and `make plugin` pass. Imports **362 of 362**, unchanged
again, and `grep -c 'IOGraphicsFamily\|IONDRVSupport' src/plugin/Info.plist`
is **0**. No new warning in any edited file. UUID moved `B8E38412…` →
**5719404C-3236-3851-870C-36A767392FFC**. New diag keys
`agdc_extcap_calls`/`_type`/`_result`/`_answered`; `agdc_extcap_type` exists
specifically so that if the kernel hands the vendor callback a separate zeroed
*output* copy rather than the shared in/out buffer, a boot says so — every type
would then read 0 and be refused for that reason rather than because it is
unimplemented.

**One boot now covers both stages.** Read in order: `agdc_tim_src 3`,
`agdc_tim_err 0`, `agdc_tim_h`/`agdc_tim_v` matching the panel,
`agdc_link_result 0`, `agdc_extcap_type 0x10` and `agdc_extcap_result 0`.
Still absent and not claimed: the bind/transaction/scanout backend, any plane
state, and any explanation for boot 156's frozen panel or the
`checkGPUProgress` channel errors. A published capability is not a picture.

## 2rg — the 0x921 cache is NOT write-only: it IS the display's advertised capability, and Apple computes the refresh rate out of it

Static, no boot. Follows 2rd/2re/2rf, and **corrects 2rd on one sentence that
mattered**: *"copies `reply+0x10..0x9b` into a cache it never reads in this
image."* It reads it twenty-four times.

### The orchestrator

`IOPresentmentCapabilities::__gatherCapabilities()` (`0x7ff812e95370`, 0x104
bytes) is the function above both gathers, and it is small enough to read
whole:

```
if (this == NULL)                       return 0x808;
if (!cmpxchg(this->0x8, 0 -> 1))        return 0x81f;   /* re-entrant */
retry:
  this->0x10 = 0;                                        /* dirty flag */
  ret = __GatherAGDCLogicalDeviceCapabilities();         /* 0x7ff812e9781a */
  if (ret != 0) goto out;                                /* <- the only abort */
  ret = __GatherAGDCDisplayPipelineCapabilities();       /* 0x7ff812e979dc */
  this->0x19c54 = 60.0f;                                 /* 0x42700000 */
  hTotal = (float)(this->0x19b40 + this->0x19b44);
  vTotal = (float)(this->0x19b50 + this->0x19b54);
  if (hTotal * vTotal > 0.0f)
      this->0x19c54 = (float)this->0x19b28 / (hTotal * vTotal);
  this->0x19c58 = this->0x19b40;
  this->0x19c60 = this->0x19b50;
out:
  if (this->0x10) goto retry;
  release lock; return ret (or 0x821 if the release raced)
```

The `ucomiss` operand at `0x7ff812ea3468` reads **`0.0f`** (measured, not
assumed — the neighbouring word is `160.0f`), so that branch is **only a
divide-by-zero guard**, not a plausibility test.

### Which fields those offsets are, by Apple's own names

The cache base is `reply + 0x19afc` (`reply+0x10` → `0x19b0c`, from the copy
in `__GatherAGDCLogicalDeviceCapabilities`), and the V2 struct sits at
`reply+0x04`, so `V2 = cache - 0x19b00`. That makes the formula above:

> **refresh = pixelClock / ((horizontalActive + horizontalBlanking) ×
> (verticalActive + verticalBlanking))**

the textbook refresh-rate identity — which is itself evidence for the
embedding. But it is no longer the only evidence.
`IOPresentmentCreateEndPointDictionary` (`0x7ff812e9550c`) takes the **address**
of fourteen cached fields in turn and makes a CFNumber of each under a CFString
key, and the keys decode to:

| cache | V2 | Apple's key |
|---|---|---|
| `0x19b28` | `0x28` | `PixelClock` |
| `0x19b30` | `0x30` | `MinPixelClock` |
| `0x19b38` | `0x38` | `MaxPixelClock` |
| `0x19b40` | `0x40` | `HorizontalActive` |
| `0x19b44` | `0x44` | `HorizontalBlanking` |
| `0x19b48` | `0x48` | `HorizontalSyncOffset` |
| `0x19b4c` | `0x4c` | `HorizontalSyncPulseWidth` |
| `0x19b50` | `0x50` | `VerticalActive` |
| `0x19b54` | `0x54` | `VerticalBlanking` |
| `0x19b58` | `0x58` | `VerticalSyncOffset` |
| `0x19b5c` | `0x5c` | `VerticalSyncPulseWidth` |
| `0x19b70` | `0x70` | `HorizontalSyncConfig` |
| `0x19b78` | `0x78` | `VerticalSyncConfig` |
| `0x19b84` | `0x84` | `VerticalBlankingExtension` |

Field for field, in order, matching the public `IOGraphicsTypes.h`. **This is
Apple naming the fields rather than us matching offsets**, and it is the
strongest confirmation of the `reply+0x04` embedding so far — stronger than
2rd's shifted block copy and stronger than the `offsetof` sum. The derived
values are published too: `0x19c58`/`0x19c60` as **`LooksLikeWidth`** /
**`LooksLikeHeight`**, and `0x19c54` under **`RefreshTime`**,
**`MinRefreshTime`** and **`MaxRefreshTime`** — three keys, one address, all
the computed value.

So 2rd's claim stands exactly as far as it was measured and no further:
IOPresentment **validates** no timing field. It **consumes** nearly all of
them.

### What that changes in the bridge: one new refusal

The zero-fill hazard 2rd reasoned about is now specific rather than general. A
zero `pixelClock` **passes** the `> 0.0f` guard (because the guard tests the
*totals*, not the clock) and publishes a `RefreshTime` of **0.0 Hz** — where a
zero total would at least have left Apple's own stated 60.0f. So a zero clock
is the one remaining poisoning, and `rb_agdc_link_config` now refuses it,
before touching the output, by the same rule and for a measured reason.

`IOPresentmentGetCurrentEndPointDimensions` (`0x7ff812e96ed6`) independently
justifies the refusal already in place: when `0x19b40` or `0x19b50` is zero it
returns having written **neither** output, leaving its caller's values whatever
they were. It also reveals an override — `*w = 0x19b18 ? 0x19b18 : hActive`,
`*h = 0x19b1c ? 0x19b1c : vActive`, i.e. **`horizontalScaled`** /
**`verticalScaled`** (V2+0x18/+0x1c) win when set. The bridge copies the V2
body wholesale, so whatever the NDRV publishes there is what Apple will use;
that is honest, and it is recorded here rather than silently inherited.

### flags bit 0 is SAFE, and 2rd overstated it

2rd said bit 0 must stay clear because it pulls in "a port sub-protocol this
bridge does not implement." The reachability is right; the danger is not.
`__GatherAGDCLogicalDeviceCapabilities` tests `reply+0x08` bit 0 at
`0x7ff812e979b7` and calls `__GatherAGDCLinkCapabilities(reply+0xa4)`
(`0x7ff812e98af6`), which:

* presets `this->0x19c78 = 2`;
* issues selector **0x925** with a 0xc-byte `{streamAddr, 0}` — on failure, on
  `outLen == 0`, or if `reply+0x08` bit 0 is clear, **returns**;
* issues selector **0x988** with a 0x24-byte buffer — same three exits;
* otherwise sets `0x19c78` from `reply+0x20`: bit 3 → 8, else bit 1 → 4, else
  bit 2 → 1, else 2.

It returns **void**; `r14` (the success code) is zeroed at `0x7ff812e979b4`
*before* the call and is callee-saved across it. And `0x19c78` has **four
writers and ZERO readers in the entire image** (`grep` of the full 0x1c000-byte
disassembly) — the same shape as the cache 2rd mis-called write-only, inverted.
So setting bit 0 would cost two answerable queries and change nothing. It stays
clear because **this bridge knows of no link to describe**, which is a reason
of honesty, not of hazard. Recorded because a wrong reason for a right
decision breaks the next time the decision is revisited.

Also confirmed: `reply+0xa4` and `+0xa8` are **one** field to the consumer —
read with a single `movq` and passed as `AGDCStreamAddress_t` — so the zero the
bridge writes at `+0xa8` is that address's high half, not padding.

### Tests, and each one broken on purpose

Five new offset literals are pinned to the measurement (`RB_AGDC_TIMING_OFF +
RB_AGDC_V2_*` must equal `0x2c`/`0x44`/`0x48`/`0x54`/`0x58`, the reply offsets
`0x19b28`−`0x19afc` etc.), the ramp proves the copy puts each one there, the
zero-clock refusal is asserted to write nothing, and 0x711 is asserted to
**still answer** with a clockless timing so the refusal is provably scoped to
0x921. The index is zeroed first so the clock guard is what fires and not the
index check — the trap the bit-0 guard fell into in 2re.

Broken in turn: removing the clock guard (as `== 0xdeadbeef`, so it still
compiles) **4** failures; shifting `RB_AGDC_V2_PIXELCLOCK` by 4 → **2**;
shifting `RB_AGDC_V2_HACTIVE` by 4 → **6**.

### Build

`make hosttest` and `make plugin` pass; imports **362 of 362** unchanged;
`grep -c 'IOGraphicsFamily\|IONDRVSupport' src/plugin/Info.plist` = **0**; no
new warnings. UUID moved `5719404C…` →
**E56F3227-243C-3F7E-9B29-5B8DD5B5405F**.

New diag keys: `agdc_tim_hblank`, `agdc_tim_vblank`, `agdc_tim_clk`, and
**`agdc_tim_mhz`** — the refresh in millihertz that *Apple's own formula* will
produce from this boot's timing, published whether or not the reply is refused,
so the capture says directly whether the number macOS is about to advertise is
the panel's. `agdc_tim_err` gains **5 = zero pixelClock**.

**Nothing here is verified on hardware.** The reading order for the next boot
is unchanged except for one addition: after `agdc_tim_h`/`agdc_tim_v`, read
**`agdc_tim_mhz`** and compare it with the panel's 143 833 — if it reads 0 or
60 000, the NDRV's detailed timing is incomplete and that, not the bridge, is
the next thing to fix. Still absent: the bind/transaction/scanout backend, all
plane state, and any explanation for boot 156's frozen panel or the
`checkGPUProgress` channel errors.

## 2rh — boot 157 hung three times; the callback was calling into IOFramebuffer, and the capture script finished the job

**BOOT 157 WAS A HANG, NOT A PANIC, AND THE EVIDENCE IS GONE.** All three
resets recorded `previous shutdown cause 5`, not `-128`, and **no `.panic` file
was written** (newest is 2026-10-23). The panel froze, SSH stayed up, the user
power-cycled. That is a deadlock.

**It happened three times because the one-shot did not clear.** `rbgpu-agdc`
survived the boot that consumed it, so the next two boots re-armed and re-hung;
it is absent only now. **2qy had already measured this exact failure**
(`mcr_oneshot 4`, the NVRAM clear silently failing, cause never established)
and I handed over the activation commands anyway, resting the whole rescue on
a mechanism this journal says is unreliable. The one-shot's entire purpose is
that a bad boot is recovered by a power cycle, and that is the job it failed.

### What was lost, and one inference retracted

No `logs/<ts>-plugin` directory from 2026-10-26 exists **at all** - not a
partial one. `plugin_check.sh` creates it at line 12 and writes the NVRAM
breadcrumbs by line 57, so the directory existed in the page cache and **never
reached the disk** before the hard reset.

`rbgpu-diag` is overwritten every boot, so boot 157's block is gone too. I was
one step from reporting `rbgpu-diag-prev` as boot 157's capture. **It is not,
and rule 8 says why: `rbgpu-diag` carries no nonce.** Its contents -
`agdc_user_vendor=4`, `agdc_user_cap=1`, `agdc_last_attr=921`,
`agdc_logical_ret=e00002c7` - are *identical* to boot 156's documented numbers,
and **every key added in 2re/2rf/2rg is absent from it** while `diag_used`
reads 0x224 of 0x300, i.e. 548 of 768 with room to spare. So that block is
boot 156 and says nothing about the boot that hung. Retracted before it became
a finding.

Also corrected, because I told the user the wrong thing to read: **the diag
notes are HEX.** `diag_max=300` is 0x300 = **768**, matching
`RBGPU_MAX_DIAGS`; `diag_used=224` is 548. I had told them to check that
`diag_max` reads 768 as proof the new build was live, which would have made a
correct install look like a failed one.

### The defect, and it is 2re's

`currentTiming()` called `IONDRVFramebuffer::getCurrentDisplayMode` and
`getTimingInfoForDisplayMode` **synchronously from inside
`filtered_doDeviceAttribute`** - that is, on WindowServer's thread, inside a
user-client external method - while both are IOFramebuffer methods that expect
the IOGraphics workloop. A lock-order inversion there produces exactly the
observed symptom: wedged desktop, live kernel, no panic. **CLAUDE.md already
carried the warning in this shape** for `-rbgpuvblpump` ("if that path needs a
lock WindowServer holds the desktop can wedge") and 2re did it anyway, because
"resolved and called, so rule 3 is untouched" answered the *routing* question
and I never asked the *locking* one.

**NOT ESTABLISHED: that the lock is what hung it.** The capture that would have
proved it died with the boot. What is certain is that the structure was wrong.

### The fix: sample once, off the callback

`sampleTiming()` now runs on the bridge's own `thread_call`, **once**,
immediately before `service->start(pci)` - with nothing of ours registered,
no Apple lock held by us, and before WindowServer can query - and copies the
0xa0-byte V2 body into `timingCache`. `vendor()` serves that cache and **calls
nothing**: verified mechanically, `vendor()` no longer mentions
`ndrvCurrentMode`, `ndrvTimingInfo` or any sampler. A failed sample leaves
`timingValid` false and 0x921/0x711 **refuse**, which is 2rd's rule unchanged.
This is the right structure whether or not the lock hypothesis holds, so the
fix does not depend on it.

### Rule 14, on my own refusal path

`currentTiming()`'s first guard - `!ndrvCurrentMode || !ndrvTimingInfo ||
!framebuffer` - returned `nullptr` **with no diag key at all**, so "the symbols
never resolved", "no framebuffer" and "never called" were indistinguishable,
which is the precise failure rule 14 exists for and 2qu restated as *a refusal
path must publish the value it refused*. Now: **6** getters unresolved, **7**
no framebuffer, and `agdc_tim_err` is **seeded to 9** in `rbgpu_agdc_load`
before anything else, so an **absent** `agdc_tim_err` is impossible and 9 means
`sampleTiming()` was never reached. `agdc_tim_cached 1` is the positive
confirmation.

### The instrument was the other culprit — rule 16, twice in one night

`plugin_check.sh:83` ran `/usr/bin/sample WindowServer 3` **unguarded**, added
by me in 2rc. `sample` suspends the target's threads and walks their stacks; a
WindowServer wedged in a kernel call **cannot be suspended**, so `sample`
blocks in the kernel and takes the machine with it - which is what ended two of
the three attempts, each time destroying the capture it belonged to. The script
run to diagnose a hang was causing one.

**A timeout does not make it safe**, and the script already said so about
`ioreg`: killing the wrapper cannot unblock a `task_suspend` already in the
kernel. So the sample is now **OFF by default**, opt-in via
`RBGPU_WS_SAMPLE=1`, with the bounded background-and-poll guard copied from
`rb_ioreg` as a second line only, and a message that states plainly it cannot
recover the thread. `compositor_check.sh`'s `sample` is bounded the same way
but stays on, because that script is only meaningful on a responsive desktop.
Its `pgrep -x WindowServer` also became the `ps -axo` form (rule 23).

And the breadcrumbs are now **`sync`ed immediately** after they are written,
before anything slower or riskier runs - the single change that would have
saved tonight's evidence.

### Build

`make hosttest` and `make plugin` pass; imports **362 of 362** unchanged;
`grep -c 'IOGraphicsFamily\|IONDRVSupport' src/plugin/Info.plist` = **0**; no
new warnings. UUID moved `E56F3227…` → **B5419C66-347A-3123-880D-245FA816F9E4**.
**`src/common` did not change, so no host-test case was added** - the fix is
entirely in the plugin's threading, which the host harness cannot reach. That
is a real gap in coverage, not an argument that none was needed.

**NOTHING HERE IS VERIFIED ON HARDWARE, and the next boot must not rest on the
one-shot.** Take **`-rbgpuagdc` out of boot-args** between experiments: the
bridge needs the arg *and* the key, so without the arg a stuck one-shot is
inert. That, not the one-shot, is the rescue that actually holds.
