## 2ri — 2rh's lock-order inversion is MEASURED FALSE, and the frozen panel predates every line of it

Static, no boot, and it retracts the hypothesis 2rh was built on.

### Neither getter takes a lock

`getCurrentDisplayMode` (`0x15003f50`) is **0x22 = 34 bytes**, whole:

```
testq %rsi,%rsi ; je +0x11 ; movl 0x1e8(%rdi),%eax ; movl %eax,(%rsi)
testq %rdx,%rdx ; je +0x1e ; movl 0x1ec(%rdi),%eax ; movl %eax,(%rdx)
xorl %eax,%eax ; retq
```

Two loads from cached fields, two guarded stores, `return kIOReturnSuccess`.
**No call of any kind.** It cannot block, lock or fail.

`getTimingInfoForDisplayMode` (`0x15003ddc`, 0x174 bytes) calls
`this->vt[0xc10]` once and then `IONDRVFramebuffer::_doStatus` three times,
with codes 0xd, 0x1f and 0x24. `_doStatus` (`0x15001610`) is where any lock
would be, and it has none:

```
if (this->0x218 == 0)            return 0xe00002cd;   /* NDRV not open */
<fill a 0x60-byte request with 0xAA>
if (_ml_at_interrupt_context())  goto CALL;
wl = <0x14fc6858>(this);  if (!wl) goto CALL;
if (wl->vt[0x138]())             goto CALL;           /* gated: fine */
OSReportWithBacktrace("%s::_doStatus(%d) not gated\n", this->0x118, code);
CALL: return this->vt[0xaf0](this, 1, req, 0x85, 4);
```

The stub at `0x10330` resolves through `kc_stubs.py` (1678 of 1678) to
**`_ml_at_interrupt_context`**, and the format string is **Apple's own**, lifted
from the image: **`"%s::_doStatus(%d) not gated\n"`**, next to
`"%s::_doControl(%d) not gated\n"` and `IONDRVFramebuffer.cpp`. So `vt[0x138]`
is an `inGate`/`onThread` **predicate**, and failing it costs **one log line
with a backtrace and nothing else** - every path, including the complaint path,
falls through to the NDRV call. There is no lock, no gate acquisition and no
wait anywhere in it.

**So 2rh's lock-order inversion could not have happened**, and I should not
have let it stand as "the leading hypothesis" while the cheap static read that
refutes it was available the whole time - the exact variant named at the end of
CLAUDE.md's rules: *read the evidence already in hand before designing the next
experiment.*

### And the freeze was never 2re's

The decisive fact was already in CLAUDE.md's own status block:
**"BOOT 156 / 2rc: AGDC REGISTERED AND STARTED; PANEL FROZE."** Boot 156 froze
the panel with `agdc_started=1` and `iop_verify=1` **before 2rd, 2re, 2rf or
2rg existed**. Publishing the bridge is what freezes the panel, and it has done
so from the first boot that published it. 2rh pinned it on 2re's timing call;
that was wrong, and the correction matters because it moves the frontier back
to where it actually is.

### What the night actually was, itemised

1. **The frozen panel** - known since boot 156, **cause still unknown**, and
   untouched by anything in 2rh or 2ri.
2. **`plugin_check.sh`'s unguarded `sample`** - real, mine (2rc), killed the
   machine on two of three attempts and destroyed the capture each time. Fixed
   in 2rh.
3. **The one-shot failing to clear** - real, measured in 2qy, which is why the
   same hang repeated three times. Mitigated in 2rh by keeping `-rbgpuagdc`
   out of boot-args between experiments.
4. **The capture directory never reaching disk** - real; fixed in 2rh by
   syncing the breadcrumbs immediately.

Two of the four are fixed, one mitigated, and **the thing that actually freezes
the screen is none of them.**

### 2rh's fix is still right, now for a measured reason

Sampling once off the callback is not justified by deadlock avoidance, because
there is no deadlock. It is justified because the vendor callback runs on
**WindowServer's thread, which is not the IOGraphics gate**, so calling
`getTimingInfoForDisplayMode` from there earned an `OSReportWithBacktrace` -
three of them, one per `_doStatus` - on **every** 0x921 and 0x711 query. Once,
on our own `thread_call`, costs one set. The structure was still wrong; the
reason was not the one 2rh gave.

### A real second defect, found while reading this

`vendor()`'s `agdc_extcap_type` probe read `out+0x04` behind **`if (out)`
alone** - a NULL check, not a bounds check, which is **rule 19** verbatim. The
type is at +0x04, so the read needs eight bytes of output buffer, and any
caller passing fewer got an out-of-bounds kernel read. Now guarded by
`out && outSize && *outSize >= 8`, with `agdc_extcap_type_short` publishing the
length that was refused instead (rule 14 on the refusal path, 2qu's form).

### Build

`make hosttest` and `make plugin` pass; imports **362 of 362**; Info.plist
graphics deps **0**; no new warnings. UUID → **61BE982B-C074-3B04-A751-0CE18935E5B4**.

**The open question is the one 2rc left and 2rh mislabelled: why does
publishing the AGDC bridge freeze the panel?** It is not the timing path. The
next read is `AppleGraphicsDeviceControl::start` and what the wrangler does
with our service on the `0x13dfd37c` call, since that is the only thing that
runs between a working desktop and a frozen one.

## 2rj — AGDC::start queries OUR vendor twice and branches on the answers; and it holds the kext's only infinite wait

Static, no boot. Asked for: `AppleGraphicsDeviceControl::start` and the
wrangler's `0x13dfd37c` call. Both read; the freeze is **still not explained**,
but two concrete things came out and one forming hypothesis was dropped.

### `0x13dfd37c` is `setDeviceAttribute`, and it is a 36-byte thunk

```
AppleGraphicsDeviceControl::setDeviceAttribute(unsigned, unsigned long *, unsigned long):
    filtered_doDeviceAttribute(api = 1 /* SET */, attr, buf, len, 0, 0, NULL)
```

So **2r1's reading is confirmed from AGDC's own side**: the wrangler is pushing
a value *into* AGDC, not reading one out, and it lands in the very function
this bridge routes.

### `start` has the only blocking wait in the kext, and it is INFINITE

Swept the whole of AGDC through `kc_stubs.py`: **one**
`IOService::waitForMatchingService`, **one** `IOSleep`, 12 `IORecursiveLockLock`
and 14 unlocks. The wait is in `start`:

```
13dfbc8d  leaq "AppleGPUWrangler", %rdi
13dfbc94  xorl %esi, %esi            ; serviceMatching("AppleGPUWrangler", NULL)
13dfbca6  movq $-0x1, %rsi           ; *** timeout = UINT64_MAX ***
13dfbcad  callq IOService::waitForMatchingService
13dfbcb5  callq mach_absolute_time   ; it MEASURES how long it waited
13dfbcc7  callq absolutetime_to_nanoseconds
```

`$-0x1` is an infinite timeout, and Apple instruments the duration, so a long
wait is expected behaviour. **Benign here** - 2r5 measured that
`AppleGPUWrangler` is present and is the only `AppleGraphicsDeviceControl`
match - but worth recording plainly: this bridge calls `service->start(pci)`
from its own `thread_call`, so if that service were ever absent the call blocks
**forever**, on a shared kernel thread, with no timeout and no diagnostic of
ours. `agdc_stage` would sit at 60 and never reach 70.

### `start` calls OUR vendor slot twice, and branches on what we answer

Three re-entries into our code during `start`: `*0x858` at `0x13dfbb60` and
`0x13dfbba1`, and `filtered_doDeviceAttribute` directly at `0x13dfbef6`. The
first two decode completely:

```
*(u64 *)outLen = 0x2c;
vendor(attr = 1, ..., buf);              /* kAGDCVendorInfo */
eax = buf->0x28;
if ((uint32_t)(eax - 1) > 1) goto TAIL;  /* i.e. unless buf->0x28 is 1 or 2 */
    *(u64 *)outLen = 0xdc;
    vendor(attr = 0x980, ..., buf2);     /* kAGDCGPUCapability */
    eax = <field>;
TAIL:
if ((uint32_t)(eax - 7) > 1) goto SKIP;  /* i.e. only for 7 or 8 */
    setProperty("NeedsPolicyDriver", ...);
SKIP:
```

Two things follow, and the first is a genuine cross-confirmation:

* **`vendorInfo+0x28` must be 1 or 2**, measured here in AGDC's own `start`.
  2r5 derived exactly that constraint from the opposite end, out of
  IOPresentment's os_log format ("0x2c bytes, `+0x28` must be 1 or 2"). Two
  independent files, same requirement. **The bridge writes 2**
  (`rb_agdc_vendor`), so it takes the branch that queries 0x980 - correct.
* **The decode of the other value is new**: `+0x28 == 7` - the value this
  bridge's own comment records as what Apple's AMD wrangler reports - **skips
  the 0x980 query entirely** and lands on `TAIL` with `eax = 7`, which is in
  `{7,8}` and therefore **sets `NeedsPolicyDriver`**. So `+0x28` is not a
  version field: it selects between *"I am a policy-driver GPU, do not ask me
  for capabilities"* and *"ask me for capabilities and decide from the reply"*.
  The bridge is deliberately on the second path.

### A hypothesis dropped before it became a claim

Three `*0x858` dispatch sites sit in `filtered_doDeviceAttribute`
(`0x13dfcf23`, `0x13dfd026`, `0x13dfd0a2`), and there is an
`IORecursiveLockLock` at `0x13dfc6ff` whose unlock is not until `0x13dfd0f3`.
That looked like "our callback runs under AGDC's lock", which would have made
every slow thing in `vendor()` a convoy - a tidy story for a frozen panel.

**It is not supported.** 2rd already traced 0x921 as
`0x13dfc32b → 0x13dfc5b8 → 0x13dfd1f1 → 0x13dfd204 → 0x13dfcf0d`, which
**skips `0x13dfc6ff..0x13dfca43` entirely**, and `0x13dfd222`'s lock is past
the `0x13dfd204` hop. So on 0x921's actual path **no recursive lock is held at
our callback**. Recorded as a non-finding rather than quietly dropped, because
this is the second tidy lock story this week and the first one (2rh) reached a
commit before being measured false.

### Where this leaves the freeze

**Still unexplained**, and nothing in 2rh, 2ri or 2rj has touched it - the
panel froze in boot 156 with `agdc_started=1`, before any of the timing code
existed. What is new is that `start` **branches on our replies**, so the
bridge's answers are not merely reported, they configure Apple's object. The
live lead is **`NeedsPolicyDriver`**: find its readers, and find which field
the `TAIL` comparison reads after the 0x980 call (it is `-0x4(%r15)`, four
bytes *below* the capability buffer, so it is not obviously a field of our
reply and must be pinned down before anything is concluded from it).

No code changed in this milestone.

## 2rk - NeedsPolicyDriver is an OPT-OUT, and its absence recruits AppleGraphicsDevicePolicy onto our bridge

2rj's lead, chased and closed, and it reverses 2rj's own reading of the flag.

**The instrument was broken first (rule 26, again).** `strings -a` on the
373 MB `SystemKernelExtensions.kc` **silently under-reports**: it found
`AppleGPUWrangler` **11** times where a byte search finds **32**, and
`NeedsPolicyDriver` **0** times where a byte search finds **4**. A
`grep -rl --binary-files=binary` over the same trees found **neither** string -
control included - so both scans would have produced a confident
"only AGDC has it". The answer came from `mmap` + `bytes.find`.

**Four occurrences, three kexts, and only ONE is a read:**

| file offset | kext | what it does |
|---|---|---|
| `0x13dfdf9f` | `AppleGraphicsDeviceControl` | the string; LEA'd at `0x13dfbbb6` in `AGDC::start` |
| `0x13e0f0c3` | `AppleGraphicsDevicePolicy` | **read** at `0x13e098ce`, **write** at `0x13e0e800` |
| `0x13e392b6` | `AppleMuxControl` | write at `0x13e3299d` |
| `0x13e50a72` | `AppleMuxControl2` | write at `0x13e4c997` |

Boundaries from `kc_extract.py --list`: AGDC `0x13dfa000`, AGDP `0x13e03000`,
AppleMuxControl `0x13e29000`, AppleMuxControl2 `0x13e3e000`,
ApplePolicyControl `0x13e55000`. The scanner was validated before use: it
returns the AGDC site inside `AGDC::start`'s measured range, which 2rj had
already decoded independently.

**THE READER IS `AppleGraphicsDevicePolicy::probe` (`0x13e0989a`), AND THE
SENSE IS INVERTED FROM WHAT 2rj ASSUMED.** Slots named from the boot KC
(`vtslots.py`): `0x278` = `IORegistryEntry::setProperty(const char *, bool)`,
`0x2b8` = `getProperty(const char *)`, `0x670` = `IOService::attach`,
`0x5c0` = `IOService::start`; the GOT entries resolve to
`__ZTV9IOService` and `OSBoolean::metaClass`, and slot `0x128` on OSBoolean's
own vtable is `OSBoolean::getValue` (rule 7: a call through a vtable
**symbol** uses dump offsets, so `*0x5c8(__ZTV9IOService)` is the
**non-virtual super call** `IOService::probe` at address-point `0x5b8`).

```c
IOService *AGDP::probe(IOService *provider, SInt32 *score) {
    *score = 0;
    IOService *r = IOService::probe(provider, score);   /* super, non-virtual */
    *score = 1000;
    if (!r) { *score = 0; return NULL; }
    OSBoolean *b = OSDynamicCast(OSBoolean,
                                 provider->getProperty("NeedsPolicyDriver"));
    *score = 1000;
    if (!b)            return r;      /* ABSENT  -> MATCH, score 1000 */
    if (b->getValue()) return r;      /* TRUE    -> MATCH, score 1000 */
    *score = 0; return NULL;          /* FALSE   -> REFUSE            */
}
```

So an **absent** property is not neutral: it is consent. And
`vt[0x278]` with `edx = 0` is `setProperty(name, **false**)`, so
`AGDC::start` does not "set NeedsPolicyDriver" as 2rj wrote - it **clears**
it, for `vendorInfo+0x28` in {7,8}. Apple's own AMD value opts **out** of the
policy driver; our `2` leaves the property absent and opts **in**.

**AND AGDP MATCHES ON EVERY AGDC.** Its personality is
`IOProviderClass = AppleGraphicsDeviceControl`, `IOMatchCategory =
AppleGraphicsDevicePolicy`, `IOResourceMatch = IOKit` - no PCI match, no
board-id gate at the matching stage. `IOService` provider matching is a
`metaCast`, so a subclass qualifies (2r0's finding, applied here). The two
`AppleMuxControl` personalities are **not** ours - both are
`IOProviderClass = IOACPIPlatformDevice` with `IONameMatch` `GMUX` / `GPUC`,
i.e. a real gmux device this laptop does not have; their `NeedsPolicyDriver`
sites are *writes*, part of the same opt-out pattern (`attach` -> clear the
flag -> `start`), and `AppleMuxControl` is **absent from the live class list**
while `AppleGraphicsDevicePolicy` is present at **0** instances - so AGDP's
kext IS loaded here and simply has nothing to attach to yet.

**WHY THIS IS A FREEZE CANDIDATE, STATED HONESTLY.** Boot 156 published an
AGDC with no `NeedsPolicyDriver`, so `AppleGraphicsDevicePolicy` became
eligible to probe and start on it - a mux/dual-GPU policy driver, on a
single-GPU APU, holding Apple's own display-policy state. That is a NEW
mechanism, reachable only once the bridge publishes, and it fits the one fact
every reading has had to accommodate: the panel froze the first time the
bridge was registered and has frozen every time since. **It is NOT
established that AGDP is what freezes the panel** - it has not been observed
attaching, boot 156's capture never reached disk, and the baseline shows AGDP
at 0 instances against the wrangler (which is itself an AGDC), so something
already stops it there. Do not record this as the cause.

**THE FIX IS ONE PROPERTY, AND IT IS APPLE'S OWN.** The bridge now publishes
`NeedsPolicyDriver = false` between `init()` and `attach()`, exactly where
AGDP's own nested AGDC does it (`0x13e0e800`, between `vt[0x670]` attach and
`vt[0x5c0]` start). `-rbgpuagdcpolicy` leaves the property absent for an A/B
test, and `agdc_policy_optout` publishes which way it went (1 = opted out,
0 = policy driver allowed). New verdict **16** = the property could not be
published, which refuses the whole bridge rather than publishing a service
that invites a driver we did not mean to invite. `src/common` did not change,
so no host-test case was added - this is a property on an IOService the host
harness cannot construct, and that is a coverage gap, not a justification.

**THE TAIL COMPARISON IS `vendorInfo+0x28`, THE SAME SLOT - 2rj's "four bytes
below the capability buffer" is now pinned.** `AGDC::start`'s stack:
buffer 1 is `rbp-0x138` (bzero `0x108`, `*(r15-8) = this` at `rbp-0x140`,
outLen at `rbp-0x148`), so `0x28(%r15)` is **`rbp-0x110`**. For the `0x980`
query `%r15` is **reassigned** to `rbp-0x10c`, so `-0x4(%r15)` is
**`rbp-0x110` again** - the identical slot. The compiler reused the register;
there is no second field. Buffer 2 spans `rbp-0x10c` upward and cannot reach
`rbp-0x110`, so the capability reply **cannot clobber it**. Therefore
`AGDC::start` tests **one** value twice:

```c
vendor(attr=1, out=&buf1, outLen=0x2c);
if ((uint32_t)(buf1.u32[0x28/4] - 1) <= 1u)        /* 1 or 2 */
    vendor(attr=0x980, out=&buf2, outLen=0xdc);    /* reply unread here */
if ((uint32_t)(buf1.u32[0x28/4] - 7) <= 1u)        /* 7 or 8 */
    this->setProperty("NeedsPolicyDriver", false);
```

The `0x980` reply is **never read by `start`** - it is fetched and dropped, so
whatever our capability answer says, `start` branches only on `+0x28`. That
retires the open question 2rj left and removes a field we did not need to
model.

UUID **8CB914E5**; plugin imports **362 of 362**, 0 unresolved;
`grep -c 'IOGraphicsFamily\|IONDRVSupport' src/plugin/Info.plist` = **0**.
**NOT VERIFIED ON HARDWARE.** Reading order gains one line before the timing
block: **`agdc_policy_optout 1`**, and verdict **16** means the bridge refused
rather than published.

## 2rm - OTG0's live timing becomes the 0x921 source, read-only

2rl left 0x921 refusing because `IONDRVFramebuffer` **answers**
`getTimingInfoForDisplayMode` and what it answers is `flags = 0` -
`kIODetailedTimingValid` clear. This builds the fallback the firmware already
made available.

**THE PANEL'S REAL TIMING WAS ALREADY ON DISK, MEASURED IN 2oq/2os:**

```
OTG0_H_TOTAL            0x0000083a   2106
OTG0_H_BLANK_START_END  0x007f07ff   127 / 2047
OTG0_H_SYNC_A           0x003c0000     0 / 60
OTG0_V_TOTAL            0x00000469   1129
OTG0_V_BLANK_START_END  0x0014044c    20 / 1100
OTG0_V_SYNC_A           0x00050000     0 / 5
```

**The field order is established by arithmetic, not by a header this tree does
not have** (`docs/linux-ref` carries `dcn_3_1_2_offset.h` but no `sh_mask`):

```
h: active 2047-127 = 1920   front 2106-2047 = 59, sync 60, back 127-60 = 67 -> 186 = 2106-1920
v: active 1100-20  = 1080   front 1129-1100 = 29, sync  5, back  20-5  = 15 ->  49 = 1129-1080
```

Three independently derived porches summing to the blanking the totals imply,
**on both axes**, is a stronger check than a header would be - and it is what
makes this a decode rather than a guess.

**IT ALSO CORRECTS 2os.** The registers hold the **true** totals, 2106 and
1129; 2os computed the pixel clock from **2107 x 1130**, one too many on each
axis, and with those values the porches above do not sum. Pixel clock is
therefore **341 987 984 Hz (341.988 MHz)**, not 2os's 342 453 428 - a 465 444 Hz
(0.14 %) difference that matters to nothing yet, but the journal's number was
wrong and this is where it is fixed.

**`src/common/rb_otg.h`** is the converter: raw registers in, a 0xa0-byte
`IODetailedTimingInformationV2` body out, freestanding and host-tested. The V2
offsets are derived from the **public** Kernel.framework header's member list
by walking the types (UInt64 is 8-aligned, so `pixelClock` is 0x28 and the
struct closes at 0xa0) - not by counting header lines, which 2q4 already
learned to avoid. All four offsets `rb_agdc.h` independently pinned from the
consumer side agree, and the closing size equals `RB_AGDC_TIMING_SIZE`; the
host test asserts both, so two derivations have to keep agreeing.
`kIOSyncPositivePolarity` (`IOGraphicsTypes.h:1002`) is a local constant
quoting the header, never an `#include` - a compile-time constant cannot add a
kext dependency and 2oz's IOGraphicsFamily trap stays shut
(`grep -c` on Info.plist is still **0**).
The halves of each field pair are read **order-agnostically** (span and lower
edge), so the hardware's naming of "start" versus "end" cannot matter, and
every refusal carries its own code: `RB_OTG_E_HACTIVE` for equal halves,
`_HTOTAL`/`_VTOTAL` for no room to blank, `_HSYNC`/`_VSYNC` for a sync that
does not start at 0, is zero-width, or will not fit, `_REFRESH` for an
unmeasured refresh. An unprogrammed OTG reads zeros and therefore refuses, so
it can never publish a zero timing into Apple's capability cache (2rd/2rg).
**A guard that could not fail was removed before it shipped:** the first cut
also checked `front + sync + back == blanking`, which is an *identity* once
active is `hb_hi - hb_lo` - it can never trip, and a guard that cannot fail is
not a guard. What replaced it are the three checks that do carry information.

**`tools/hosttest/otg_test.c`** runs the converter on this machine's own
register values and asserts 1920/1080, 186/49, 59/60, 29/5, the clock as
`2106*1129*143833/1000` written as arithmetic rather than a constant, both
polarity mappings, that every untouched byte of the 0xa0 body is zero, and
that each refusal both names itself and leaves the output untouched. It also
asserts that the two guards **compose**: a zero V2 body is refused by
`rb_agdc_link_config`, and a converted one is accepted. Three deliberate
breaks of the decode trip **21 / 27 / 1** assertions.

**`rbgpuOtgSample()` in the plugin reads the registers; nothing writes one.**
That is what makes this different in kind from the OTG/HUBP writes CLAUDE.md
reserves to the user: a wrong read reports a wrong number, it cannot blank the
panel. Addressing needed the DMU segment, and the plugin's `g_disc` is a
two-IP stub (MP1 + SMUIO) with no DMU entry - so **segment 2 = `0x34c0`**,
parsed by this project's own `rb_disc_parse` from this machine's real
discovery table (`tests/data/rembrandt-680m-tufa15.bin` -> DMU **3.1.3**,
nbase 5, `base[2] = 0x34c0`), putting `OTG0_CONTROL` at dword `0x5001`.
**Because a constant is an assumption, it is checked:** 2oq's measured
four-register signature - OTG0 with `OTG_MASTER_EN` set and OTG1-3 reading
exactly `0x300` - must hold, and all four values are published either way
(`otg_ctl0..3`, `otg_off_ok`). If it does not hold we are not addressing what
we think we are, and the sampler refuses rather than converting whatever it
read. The refresh is **measured**, not assumed: `OTG0_FRAME_COUNT` across a
100 ms `IOSleep` on the bridge's own `thread_call`, with
`absolutetime_to_nanoseconds` for the real elapsed time, published as
`otg_frames`/`otg_ns` and clamped to 20-400 Hz. That is the method
`RembrandtProbe.cpp` already uses (2os: 10 frames in 69 524 857 ns).
Rule 3 untouched - **nothing is routed** - and rule 17 is the reason the clock
is `hTotal * vTotal * measured refresh` instead of CVT/GTF.

**Keys, in reading order after `agdc_tim_err 3`:** `agdc_otg_bound 1`,
`agdc_otg_src` (0 no sampler, 1 refused, 2 sampled), `otg_err` **0**,
`otg_ctl0`/`otg_off_ok 3`, the six raw registers as
`agdc_otg_htot`/`_hbse`/`_hsa`/`_vtot`/`_vbse`/`_vsa`, `agdc_otg_mhz`,
`agdc_otg_ret` **0**, and then **`agdc_tim_cached 2`** - 2 means the timing
came from OTG0, 1 means it came from the NDRV, so the source is never
ambiguous. `agdc_tim_err` is set to 3 **before** the fallback runs and only
cleared if it succeeds, so a boot where the fallback does nothing reads
exactly as 159 did.

UUID **9028175A**; imports **362 of 362**, 0 unresolved; Info.plist graphics
deps **0**; `make hosttest` and `make plugin` pass. **NOT VERIFIED ON
HARDWARE** - and what a boot can show is bounded: 0x921 and 0x711 answering
does not mean a display pipe exists, because `iop_oneshot 2` in 159 means
IOPresentment never ran at all. Arm **`rbgpu-iop=1` alongside `rbgpu-agdc=1`**
to reach that layer.

## 2rn - BOOT 160: OTG0 WORKED, THE IOP PATCH LANDED, AND THE BRIDGE IS SIMPLY TOO LATE

No black panel, desktop live, `plugin_check.sh` run from inside the boot.
Rule 8/15 clear: `rbgpu-boot` **160** in capture and live, uptime 4 min,
`kextstat` UUID **9028175A** byte-equal to `build/out`, `diag_used` **564** of
**768** so absence still carries information, `agdc_oneshot 0` and
`iop_oneshot 0` - both one-shots cleared.

**THE OTG0 SOURCE WORKS, AND THE SEGMENT CONSTANT WAS RIGHT.**
`otg_err 0`; the four-register signature held exactly as 2oq measured it -
`otg_ctl0 0x11201` with `OTG_MASTER_EN` set, `otg_ctl1/2/3` all `0x300`,
`otg_off_ok 3` - so DMU segment 2 = `0x34c0` is correct on live hardware and
the addressing was not a guess. Every register came back as 2oq recorded it:
`agdc_otg_htot 2106`, `_vtot 1129`, `_hbse 0x7f07ff`, `_hsa 0x3c0000`,
`_vbse 0x14044c`, `_vsa 0x50000`. The converter accepted them
(`agdc_otg_ret 0`, `agdc_otg_src 2`) and produced **`agdc_tim_h 1920`**,
**`agdc_tim_v 1080`**, `agdc_tim_err 0` and **`agdc_tim_cached 2`** - 2 meaning
the timing came from OTG0, exactly as the key was designed to distinguish. The
0x921 refusal of boot 159 is **gone**: `agdc_link_result` is now absent
because nothing refused.

**BUT THE PIXEL CLOCK IS 3.3 % HIGH, AND THE METHOD WAS WRONG, NOT THE
WINDOW.** `otg_frames 15` in `otg_ns 100 977 001` = **148.549 Hz**, against
this panel's 143.833. The panel really delivered **14.52** frames in that
window and an integer counter sampled over a fixed interval can only resolve
+/- one frame, so 15 is a quantisation over-read - and it went straight into
`agdc_tim_clk 353 198 717` where the truth is 341 987 984. **Lengthening the
window only shrinks that linearly and costs delay on a path boot 160 proves is
already too late.** FIXED by changing the method: both endpoints are now
latched on a counter **edge**, so the frame count is exact by construction and
the only residual is the difference between two 100 us polling delays - about
**0.1 %** over 16 frames (~111 ms), a ~30x improvement for the same elapsed
time. `otg_frames`, `otg_ns` and the new `otg_polls` are published so the
arithmetic can be re-checked from any capture instead of trusted.

**THE IOP PATCH LANDED: `iop_verify 1`, `iop_patched 1`, `iop_match 1`,
`iop_saw_ws 1`.** So 2qo's five-byte write went into WindowServer's own memory
and the vendor-mask gate opened, exactly as in boot 150.

**AND THE REAL FINDING IS AN ORDERING RACE, WHICH NO AMOUNT OF CAPABILITY WORK
WOULD HAVE FOUND.** The log, by timestamp, same process and thread:

```
10:11:33.920 WindowServer[161:3a0] (reg) gpu 0xfbc7 ... agdc 0x000000000
                                                        fb0:0 /IONDRVFramebuffer
10:11:33.941 WindowServer[161:3a0] (IOPresentment) Error: Unable to get AGDC
                                   information.  Return code: 0x10000003
10:11:33.982 WindowServer[161:3a0] System set to use IOP but no display pipes
                                   are present
10:11:34.396 WindowServer[161:3a0] Unable to find display pipe for IOFB
                                   service / regID: 0xc703 / 0x1000004af
...
10:12:07.323 SafeEjectGPUService[570] (reg) gpu 0xfbc7 ... agdc 0x100000525
                                                           /RembrandtGPUAGDC
```

**At 33.920 the wrangler's own dump reads `agdc 0`. Twenty-one milliseconds
later IOPresentment asks for the AGDC and fails. Thirty-four seconds later the
same dump reads `/RembrandtGPUAGDC`.** So the bridge is published, paired and
correct - and it arrives after the only question that mattered had already been
answered. `agdc_user_vendor` and `agdc_user_cap` are **absent** this boot,
where boot 159 had 4 and 1: WindowServer gave up before our service existed,
so it never queried it. That also means **0x711 was never exercised**
(`agdc_extcap_*` absent) - not refused, never reached.

**`0x10000003` IS THE SAME CONSTANT AS BOOT 150, AND IT NOW MEANS SOMETHING
DIFFERENT.** 2r5 established it as `MACH_SEND_INVALID_DEST` from
`ioPresentmentPopulateIOFramebufferEntries` opening service id 0 after finding
nothing in an empty association map. In 150 the map was empty because no
per-GPU AGDC existed at all. In 160 it is empty because none existed **yet**.
Same error, different cause - which is why the error string alone was never
going to settle this and the timestamped `debug-gpus` dump is what did.

**SUSPECT, NOT ESTABLISHED, AND IT IS MINE.** 2rm put a **100 ms `IOSleep`**
in `sampleTiming()`, which runs immediately before `service->start()` - i.e. I
added 100 ms of delay to the publish path in the same change that made the
publish matter. Boot 159 published early enough to be queried four times;
boot 160 did not. But 160 also differs by `rbgpu-iop` being armed, which
changes when WindowServer runs and what it asks, so **attributing the miss to
my sleep would be exactly 2qm's error**. Both are live suspects. The edge-
latched measurement above shortens that window and, more to the point, boot 161
will say where the time actually goes: new keys **`agdc_t_presample_ms`**,
**`agdc_t_sampled_ms`** and **`agdc_t_started_ms`**, uptime in milliseconds
from `mach_absolute_time`, directly comparable against the log's own
timestamps. That turns "too late" into "late by N ms, of which the sample cost
M".

**Re-checked:** `fb0:0` reads `/IONDRVFramebuffer` here where 159 read
`/.Display_boot` - an instance-name difference, not a change of driver, and
nothing downstream reads it. `gpuc` is still **0**, as 2r1 predicted.
`agdc_failed_attr 3` / `agdc_failed_ret 0xE00002C7` is attribute **3**, one of
the three Apple handles in its own `attr <= 0x7f` group, refused by us - a new
caller, not WindowServer's 0x921 path, and harmless.

UUID **A83C0170**; imports **362 of 362**, 0 unresolved; graphics deps **0**;
hosttest and plugin pass. Evidence kept at `logs/boot160/`.
**The display pipe is still not created, and the reason is now a schedule
rather than a capability.**

## 2ro - WHAT DELAYS THE PUBLISH: NOTHING OF OURS WAITS, AND THE FRAMEBUFFER DEPENDENCY IS NOW VESTIGIAL

Static, no boot. Three findings, and the third is a defect that blocks the fix.

**1. OUR OWN WAITS DID NOT FIRE.** `run()` (`rbgpu_agdc.cpp:303`) polls every
**100 ms** for up to **100 retries = 10 s**, waiting for the
`AppleGraphicsDeviceControl` metaclass to be registered AND `AppleGPUWrangler`
to exist, and publishes `agdc_wait` on every retry; the un-armed path publishes
`agdc_wait_load`. **Both keys are ABSENT in boot 160's capture** at
`diag_used` **564** of **768**, so absence carries information (rule 14):
`run()` was entered **once**, found the metaclass registered and the wrangler
present on the first try, and went straight through. The 10-second retry
machinery contributed **zero**. So the delay is not in the publish, it is in
**when `run()` is first called at all**.

**2. THE TRIGGER IS `IONDRVFramebuffer::enableController`, AND IT IS THE ONLY
ONE.** `rbgpu_agdc_framebuffer()` has exactly one caller - `kern_start.cpp:8232`,
the tail of `hooked_ndrv_enablectl_2pa`, after the original returns - and it is
what allocates the `thread_call` and enters it (`rbgpu_agdc.cpp:511-513`). The
only other entry is `rbgpu_agdc_load`'s `if (work) thread_call_enter(work)`
(line 481), which can only re-enter a `work` the framebuffer path already
created. **So the publish cannot happen before `enableController` returns, by
construction**, and within our own code that is the whole of the delay by
elimination.
**NOT established, and the log cannot establish it:** that `enableController`
itself runs at ~34 s. The second `debug-gpus` dump reading
`/RembrandtGPUAGDC` is **`SafeEjectGPUService` at 10:12:07**, which bounds the
publish from **above only** - it says the bridge was paired by 67 s of uptime,
not that it was paired at 67 s. The real publish instant is anywhere in
`(33.92, 67.3]`. 2rn's new `agdc_t_presample_ms`/`_sampled_ms`/`_started_ms`
are what close that, and they are the reason not to guess here.

**3. THE FRAMEBUFFER IS NO LONGER NEEDED, AND 2rm IS WHY.** Every use of
`framebuffer` in the bridge:

| line | use | load-bearing? |
|---|---|---|
| 121-131 | `sampleTiming()`'s NDRV getters | **no** - boot 160 measured `flags 0`, and OTG0 supplied the timing instead |
| 240 | a pointer in a diag/log line | no |
| 304 | the `run()` gate | only because of the above |
| 377 | `agdc_fb_id`, a registry id | no |
| 503 | **`pci = fb->getProvider()`** | **yes - this is the one** |

So the single thing the bridge actually needs the framebuffer for is the
`IOPCIDevice`. **And the plugin already holds that device far earlier:**
`src/plugin/Info.plist` matches `RembrandtGPUPeer` on
`IOProviderClass = IOPCIDevice` with an `IOPCIMatch`, and
`RembrandtGPUPeer.cpp:504` does `pciDevice = OSDynamicCast(IOPCIDevice,
provider)` in `start()` - the GPU's own PCI device, attached long before the
boot framebuffer's controller is enabled. **So yes, the bridge can start
earlier, and the handshake for doing so already exists**: `run()`'s bounded
retry loop (currently dead) is exactly the mechanism for "the AGDC metaclass or
the wrangler is not up yet", and `rbgpu_agdc_load`'s re-entry already covers
the other ordering. Starting earlier makes that dead code load-bearing, which
is a point in its favour, not against it - it was written for this case.
**2oy's warning does NOT apply here**, and the distinction matters:
CLAUDE.md says the VRAM publish was deliberately moved out of
`RembrandtGPUPeer::start()` into `enableController` because of the boot-137
race - but that was publishing *properties on the framebuffer*, which genuinely
needs the framebuffer. The AGDC bridge publishes a service on the **PCI
device** and, since 2rm, takes its timing from **OTG0**. Different dependency,
different answer.

**AND ONE DEFECT BLOCKS IT, WORTH FIXING EITHER WAY.** `sampleTiming()` has
**four** early returns that bypass the OTG fallback entirely - `agdc_tim_err`
**6** (getters unresolved), **7** (no framebuffer), **1**
(`getCurrentDisplayMode` failed), **2** (`getTimingInfoForDisplayMode` failed).
The fallback sits on the **fifth** path only, the one where the NDRV answers
and its `flags` lack `kIODetailedTimingValid`. So OTG0 - a complete,
independent timing source that boot 160 proved works - is reachable only when
the NDRV partially succeeds. Publishing before the framebuffer exists would
take path **7** and lose the timing altogether. The fallback belongs behind
**every** NDRV failure, not one of five.

**Order of work, for the same reason 2rl gave:** fix the fallback's
reachability first, because it is correct independently of any re-ordering;
then measure the publish instant with 2rn's timestamps; only then move the
trigger, so the move is made against a measured baseline instead of an
inferred one.

## 2rp - THE OTG FALLBACK IS REACHABLE FROM EVERY NDRV FAILURE, AND THE PUBLISH NO LONGER WAITS FOR THE FRAMEBUFFER

Both changes 2ro named, with the dependency 2rm removed actually taken out.

**1. `sampleTiming()` IS SPLIT, AND THE FALLBACK NOW SITS BEHIND ALL FIVE
FAILURES INSTEAD OF ONE.** It was one function with four early returns -
`agdc_tim_err` **6** (getters unresolved), **7** (no framebuffer), **1**
(`getCurrentDisplayMode`), **2** (`getTimingInfoForDisplayMode`) - that each
bypassed OTG0 entirely, leaving the fallback on the fifth path alone, the one
boot 159 happened to hit. Now `sampleTimingNdrv()` **returns** the code and
`sampleTimingOtg()` gets a turn after any non-zero, so a complete, independent,
already-proven timing source is no longer gated on the NDRV partly succeeding.
New key **`agdc_tim_ndrv_err`** keeps the NDRV's own verdict visible even when
OTG0 then succeeds and `agdc_tim_err` reads 0 - otherwise the fix would have
hidden which source was used and why, which is the error this project keeps
making about its own instruments. `agdc_tim_cached` still says 1 = NDRV,
2 = OTG0.

**2. THE TRIGGER MOVED TO `RembrandtGPUPeer::start()`.** 2ro established that
`rbgpu_agdc_framebuffer()` had one caller - the tail of the
`IONDRVFramebuffer::enableController` hook - and that it was also what
allocated the `thread_call`, so the publish could not precede
`enableController` **by construction**. New entry point
**`rbgpu_agdc_pci(IOService *)`**: the peer hands over its own provider, which
is the device it matched on (`IOProviderClass = IOPCIDevice` + `IOPCIMatch` in
`Info.plist`), validated the same way as before by vendor/device
(`0x1002`/`0x1681`, refusal **6** unchanged), and that is what allocates and
enters the worker now. `run()`'s gate changed from `!framebuffer` to **`!pci`**.
`rbgpu_agdc_framebuffer()` survives but is **demoted**: it supplies the
framebuffer for the NDRV path and `agdc_fb_id`, and only triggers the publish
if the peer somehow did not - so the old ordering still works and is no longer
the only path. New key **`agdc_pci_seen`**.

**What makes this safe rather than merely earlier:** the handshake for "too
early" was already written and, until now, dead. `run()` returns on `!armed`
publishing `agdc_wait_load`, and `rbgpu_agdc_load`'s
`if (work) thread_call_enter(work)` re-enters once AGDC's kext is routed - so
either order works. If the metaclass or the wrangler is not up yet, `run()`
retries every **100 ms** up to **100 times (10 s)** publishing `agdc_wait`.
Both keys were ABSENT in boot 160 because nothing ever waited; they become
load-bearing now, which is what they were written for. **Boot 161 should show
`agdc_wait` NON-ZERO** - if it is still absent, the peer is starting later than
assumed and that is itself the finding.
**2oy's warning does not apply**, and the distinction is the whole reason this
is allowed: it moved the *VRAM property publish* out of the peer because that
needs the framebuffer. This publishes a service on the **PCI device** and takes
its timing from **OTG0**, so it needs neither.

**NOT established, and deliberately not assumed:** that moving the trigger
fixes the race. 2ro showed the publish cannot precede `enableController`; it
did **not** show that `enableController` is what runs at ~34 s, because the
only upper bound in the log is `SafeEjectGPUService` at 10:12:07, which says
"paired by 67 s", not "paired at 67 s". 2rn's `agdc_t_presample_ms` /
`_sampled_ms` / `_started_ms` and the now-live `agdc_wait` are what will say
whether this moved the publish before WindowServer's query at ~33.94 s, and by
how much.

Refusal codes unchanged and still unique (1-16, no collisions);
`RouteRequest` count in the file still **1**, so rule 3 is untouched.
`src/common` did not change, so no host-test case was added - both changes are
plugin ordering and threading, which the host harness cannot reach; that is a
coverage gap, not a justification. UUID **FB501234**; imports **362 of 362**,
0 unresolved; Info.plist graphics deps **0**; hosttest and plugin pass.
**NOT VERIFIED ON HARDWARE.**

## 2rq - 2rp's TRIGGER MOVE HUNG THREE BOOTS AND IS REVERTED

The user: *"i rebooted 3 times it kept the bar filling up over and over but
nothing happend so i added gpuoff"*. Progress bar filling, nothing after it,
three times, recovered only by `-rbgpuoff`.

**WHAT IS ESTABLISHED, WHICH IS LESS THAN I WOULD LIKE.** No `.panic` file was
written - the newest is **2026-10-23**, three days old - so these were hangs,
not panics, same signature as 2rh's boot 157. And **`rbgpu-boot` still reads
160**: the nonce is bumped lazily by the first NVRAM note of the boot
(`rbgpu_boot_seq`, called from the note writer, not from `start()`), so no note
was written in any of the three. **All three one-shots are STILL SET**
(`rbgpu-arm 1`, `rbgpu-agdc 1`, `rbgpu-iop 1`) - never consumed. So the three
boots left **no evidence whatsoever**: no nonce, no panic, no capture. The
cause is **NOT measured** and no guess is recorded as a finding.

**THE LEADING HYPOTHESIS, LABELLED AS ONE.** 2rp called
`rbgpu_agdc_pci(pciDevice)` from `RembrandtGPUPeer::start()`, which IOKit calls
*on the matching thread with the provider busy*, and that path enters a
`thread_call` that does `service->attach(pci)` and `service->start(pci)` **on
that same provider**. Attaching to a provider that is in the middle of its own
`start()` contends for the arbitration the matching thread holds, which is a
textbook re-entrancy deadlock and matches the symptom exactly - IOKit matching
never completes, so the boot never progresses past the bar. Alternatives not
excluded: `rbgpuOtgSample`'s up-to-400 ms of `IODelay` spinning during early
matching, and MMIO reads through `g_hw.ctx` at a point where the AMD TTL
context may be set but the chip not ready. **Nothing here is measured.**

**AND THE LESSON IS THAT CLAUDE.md ALREADY CARRIED THE WARNING.** 2oy moved the
VRAM publish *out* of `RembrandtGPUPeer::start()` for the boot-137 race, and
2rp read that warning, decided it did not apply, and wrote so in the commit -
on the grounds that 2oy was about *needing the framebuffer* while this needed
only the PCI device. **That reasoning was correct about the dependency and
silent about the hazard.** Two different things live at that call site: what
the code needs, and when it is safe to publish an IOService. 2ro answered the
first and I treated it as having answered the second. The reusable form:
**a dependency analysis is not a safety analysis** - "it no longer needs X"
does not establish "it is safe here".

**REVERTED.** `rbgpu_agdc_pci` is gone (0 references in all three files), the
framebuffer hook is the trigger again and sets `pci` and `framebuffer`
together, so `run()`'s `!pci` gate is equivalent to the pre-2rp `!framebuffer`
one. **2rp's part (1) is KEPT**: the `sampleTimingNdrv()`/`sampleTimingOtg()`
split and `agdc_tim_ndrv_err` are pure control flow with no new calls and no
new timing, they fix a real reachability defect, and they are not a suspect for
a boot hang.

**2ro's finding still stands and so does the goal:** the framebuffer is needed
only for its provider, and the publish is still too late for IOPresentment
(boot 160). What 2rp got wrong is *where* earlier is. A point after matching
completes - a matching notification on the PCI device, or a delayed
`thread_call` - is the shape to measure next, and it must be measured rather
than argued, because this is the second time in this sequence that a tidy
static argument reached a commit before hardware saw it.

UUID **45F0E563**; imports **362 of 362**, 0 unresolved; graphics deps **0**;
hosttest and plugin pass. **The one-shots must be cleared before `-rbgpuoff`
comes out**, or the next boot re-arms the bridge immediately.

## 2rr - THE PUBLISH TRIGGER IS A MATCHED NOTIFICATION, WHICH IS APPLE'S OWN IDIOM

The user chose to skip the measure-only boot and go straight at the fix. The
timestamps 2rn added are in anyway, so this boot measures and acts at once.

**THE MECHANISM IS THE ONE THE WRANGLER ITSELF USES.** 2r0 measured
`AppleGPUWrangler` pairing services through **two matching notifications** on
`serviceMatching("IOService")`. `gIOMatchedNotification` fires only after a
service has **matched and started**, on IOKit's notification thread - which is
precisely not the window `RembrandtGPUPeer::start()` sits inside and that 2rq
hung three boots in.

**The service waited for is `AppleGPUWrangler`, because its arrival IS the
readiness condition** `run()` otherwise polls for: the wrangler is itself an
`AppleGraphicsDeviceControl` subclass (2r5), so AGDC's metaclass is registered
by the time it starts, and `AGDC::start`'s infinite
`waitForMatchingService("AppleGPUWrangler")` (2rj) is already satisfied. One
notification replaces a 10-second poll and arrives earlier than
`enableController`.

**THE HANDLER DOES TWO DIAG WRITES AND `thread_call_enter`. NOTHING ELSE.**
That is the whole of 2rq's lesson, encoded. It matters more than it looks:
`addMatchingNotification` fires the handler **immediately and synchronously**
for a service that has *already* matched, so the handler can run on the
kext-load thread that installed it. Because it touches no IOService state, that
is harmless - `attach()` and `start()` happen only in `run()`, on a
`thread_call`, on a plain kernel thread, with our provider long since started.
The worker is allocated at **kext-load time** now so the handler never has to.

**THE PCI DEVICE IS RESOLVED, NOT HANDED OVER.** `resolvePci()` does
`copyMatchingService(serviceMatching("RembrandtGPUPeer"))` and takes the
provider, validating `0x1002`/`0x1681` exactly as before. Our peer's
personality is `IOProviderClass = IOPCIDevice` + `IOPCIMatch 0x16811002`, so
**a peer in the registry is proof its own `start()` already returned** - the
precise fact 2rp assumed instead of establishing. No call crosses from the peer
into the bridge any more (`grep -c rbgpu_agdc` in `RembrandtGPUPeer.cpp` = 0),
so the hazardous call site no longer exists at all rather than being merely
unused.

**The framebuffer hook survives as the fallback** and will not clobber a device
`resolvePci()` already retained - the first cut would have dropped a retain and
could have replaced a good pointer. `agdc_pci_seen` says which path won:
**1 = framebuffer, 2 = peer lookup**.

**IMPORTS WENT 362 -> 364, AND BOTH ARE SAFE:**
`IOService::addMatchingNotification` and `gIOMatchedNotification`, both from
**`com.apple.kpi.iokit` in the BOOT KC** - the same collection the plugin is
injected into, no new kext dependency, and `grep -c` for IOGraphicsFamily in
Info.plist is still **0**, so 2oz's trap stays shut.

**Timeline keys, which is what makes the next boot readable:**
`agdc_t_armed_ms` (AGDC kext routed), **`agdc_t_note_ms`** (the wrangler
arrived - compare against the log's AGDC query at ~33.94 s),
`agdc_t_fb_ms` (enableController, the old trigger),
`agdc_t_presample_ms`/`_sampled_ms`/`_started_ms` (2rn). Plus
`agdc_note_armed 1`, `agdc_note_fired 1`, `agdc_pci_seen`, `agdc_pci_err`
(1 no dictionary, 2 no peer, 3 wrong identity) and `agdc_wait_pci`.
**If `agdc_t_note_ms` lands before `agdc_t_fb_ms`, the trigger moved earlier
and the whole point of this change is measured rather than argued.**

Audited against 2rq, five ways: the handler body is diag + enter only; zero
calls from the peer; `attach`/`start` appear in `run()` only;
`RouteRequest` count still **1** (rule 3); imports 364/364 with 0 unresolved.
UUID **A6A4FDD8**; graphics deps **0**; hosttest and plugin pass.
**NOT VERIFIED ON HARDWARE**, and the rescue is unchanged and must be in reach:
`-rbgpuoff`, with `-rbgpuagdc` out of boot-args between experiments (2rh).

## 2rx — THE MATCHED NOTIFICATION IS RE-LANDED, AND THE AUDIT FOUND THREE DEFECTS 2rr DID NOT HAVE WHEN IT WAS WRITTEN

The user asked for 2rr's trigger back now that 2rw measured the window, and for
an audit against 2rq's lesson first. The audit is the substance of this
milestone: **2rr as written would not have been safe on this tree**, and one of
the three defects is a plausible mechanism for the fourth hang.

**DEFECT 1, AND IT IS THE INTERESTING ONE: `run()` HAD NO MUTUAL EXCLUSION, AND
2rr TAKES ITS LIVE ENTRY POINTS FROM ONE TO THREE.** The restored tree has three
`thread_call_enter` sites but only **one live**, by accident of ordering: `work`
is allocated in the framebuffer hook, so `rbgpu_agdc_load`'s own
`if (work) thread_call_enter(work)` is a no-op (`work` is still NULL) and the
hook's is the only enter. 2rr moves the allocation to kext-load time, which
**activates that dormant enter** and adds the notification handler's — and
`addMatchingNotification` fires the handler **synchronously** for an
already-matched service, so the handler's enter and the one two lines below it
happen back to back. `thread_call_enter` on a call that is already executing
requeues it, and a thread call has no built-in exclusion, so two `run()` bodies
can overlap.
**Why that is not a stylistic objection:** `run()` calls
`preModLoad` / `mcCtor` / `postModLoad`, and 2qx measured that
`OSMetaClass::preModLoad` takes `_sStalledClassesLock` as its first instruction
and **only `postModLoad` releases it**. Two overlapping bodies means two
`preModLoad`s against one lock, a second metaclass constructed into the same
`metaStorage`, and a double `attach`/`start`. 2qx already spelled out the
consequence: **if that lock is not released the next kext load blocks forever,
with no panic and no log** — which is exactly "the bar filling up over and over
but nothing happened", and exactly why all four hangs left `rbgpu-boot` at 160
with no note and no panic file.
**HYPOTHESIS, LABELLED AS ONE, AND IT IS NOT PROVEN:** this is a mechanism that
fits the fourth hang's whole signature, where 2rq's provider-busy story did not.
It does **not** explain the first three (they ran 2rp's tree, which had the old
single-enter shape), and 2rs reconstructed the fourth boot as having
`-rbgpuagdc` **out**, under which none of this code runs — but 2rs labelled that
reconstruction "NOT a measurement". So: a candidate, recorded as one, and
**`agdc_run_reentry` now measures it** rather than leaving it argued.
**THE FIX** is one claim at the top of `run()`:
`if (!OSCompareAndSwap(0,1,&inRun)) { rbgpu_diag_inc("agdc_run_reentry"); return; }`
released **only** on the paths that deliberately ask to be re-entered (no PCI
yet, not armed, and the 100 ms retry), and held forever on every terminal path.
The idiom is the one `RembrandtGPUPeer.cpp` already uses for
`g_rbgpuNvramBusy`. All seven exits were walked individually.

**DEFECT 2: A NULL DEREFERENCE ON THE FAST PATH.** `run()` does
`rbgpu_diag_set_num("agdc_fb_id",framebuffer->getRegistryEntryID())`, and the
entire point of this change is to publish **before the framebuffer exists** —
so `framebuffer` is NULL exactly when the fix works. 2rr's diff never touched
that line because 2rr was written against 2rq's tree, where `run()` still
required the framebuffer two statements earlier. Guarded.

**DEFECT 3: THE OTG0 FALLBACK WAS UNREACHABLE ON THE FAST PATH, SO THE BRIDGE
WOULD HAVE PUBLISHED WITH NO TIMING.** `sampleTiming()` returns
`agdc_tim_err 7` ("no framebuffer") **before** the OTG0 fallback — and with the
notification trigger, 7 becomes the **normal** case. The published 0x921 would
then refuse, which is correct behaviour and a useless result: we would have
traded a late-but-complete bridge for an early-but-empty one. This is precisely
the reachability defect **2rp part (1)** fixed and **2rq explicitly kept**
("pure control flow... no suspect for a hang") before 2rs reverted the whole
tree wholesale. Restored: `sampleTimingNdrv()` returns the code (6/7/1/2/3/4/5,
0 on success) and `sampleTimingOtg()` gets a turn after **every** non-zero one,
with **`agdc_tim_ndrv_err`** preserving the NDRV's own verdict when OTG0 then
succeeds and `agdc_tim_err` reads 0. Without that key the fix would hide which
source the published timing came from.

**A FOURTH, LATENT, FOUND WHILE EDITING:** the framebuffer hook did
`pci = OSDynamicCast(...)` and *then* validated the identity, so a non-matching
device was left in the global `pci` **unretained**. Harmless while `run()` gated
on `framebuffer`; not harmless once it gates on `pci`. Now validated into a
local and assigned only on success, and it will not clobber a device
`resolvePci()` already retained (`agdc_pci_seen`: 1 = framebuffer, 2 = peer).

**WHAT IS KEPT FROM 2rr, UNCHANGED:** `resolvePci()` takes the PCI device from
our own peer in the registry — a peer that matched `IOPCIMatch 0x16811002` is
proof its `start()` returned, the fact 2rp assumed while publishing from inside
that same `start()` — and it runs on a `thread_call`, so there is no matching
thread to contend with. The handler is **two diag writes and
`thread_call_enter`**, nothing else.

**THE 2rq AUDIT, ITEM BY ITEM:** handler body minimal (verified by reading it);
`attach(pci)` and `service->start(pci)` occur at exactly **one site each**, both
inside `run()`, on the thread_call; no call crosses from the peer into the
bridge (`grep -c rbgpu_agdc` in the peer = 0, unchanged); `RouteRequest` count
still **1** (rule 3); refusal codes still unique **1–16**.

**IMPORTS 362 -> 364, AND 2oz's TRAP IS SHUT — CHECKED, NOT ASSUMED.**
`kmutil libraries` resolves **364 of 364** with **0 unresolved** and
**0 from `SystemKernelExtensions.kc`**. Both new symbols —
`IOService::addMatchingNotification` and `gIOMatchedNotification` — resolve to
`com.apple.kpi.iokit` in **`BootKernelExtensions.kc`**, so no new kext
dependency and `grep -c IOGraphicsFamily src/plugin/Info.plist` is still **0**.
UUID moved **A83C0170 -> 932B9FC8**. Hosttest passed, including the agdc cases.

**WHAT THE NEXT BOOT HAS TO SHOW, PRE-STATED.** 2rw's deadline is
**+5452 ms** and the framebuffer hook fired at **+7072 ms**. So, in order:
`agdc_note_armed 1`, `agdc_note_fired 1`, then **`agdc_t_armed_ms` and
`agdc_t_note_ms` against 5452** — if `agdc_t_note_ms` is above it, the wrangler
arrives later than the window implies and that is the finding, not a failure of
this code. Then **`agdc_t_started_ms` below 5452** is the actual goal, with
`agdc_pci_seen` **2** (resolved from the peer, not the framebuffer) and
`agdc_run_reentry` **absent** (or non-zero, which would confirm defect 1 was
real and is now contained). The timing block must still read `agdc_tim_err 0`
with `agdc_tim_cached 2` and `agdc_tim_ndrv_err 7` — NDRV had nothing because
the framebuffer did not exist yet, OTG0 supplied it anyway. And the verdict that
matters: whether `Unable to get AGDC information` and
`Unable to acquire map` are **gone** from the log, with
`agdc_user_vendor`/`agdc_user_cap` present instead of absent.

**NOT VERIFIED ON HARDWARE.** `src/common` did not change, so **no host-test
case was added** — the change is the plugin's control flow and threading, which
the host harness cannot reach. That is a coverage gap, not a justification
(2rh's own words for the same situation). Rescue unchanged: `-rbgpuoff`, and
clear the one-shots before it comes back out.

## 2ry — BOOT 164 WINS THE AGDC RACE, THEN REFUSES 0x921; MAKE THE TIMING SOURCE EARLY TOO

User requested the new commits/handoff and the hang's plugin_check results,
then continued framebuffer work. Evidence is `logs/20261026-133012-plugin`,
not the live recovery boot: capture nonce **164**, loaded UUID
**932B9FC8-49CB-3472-9099-A92D34380236** (2rx), all three one-shots absent,
`iop_verify 1`, `diag_used 0x22f` = **559 of 768**. Live `kern.boottime`
was already **13:30:44**, after this capture, while `rbgpu-boot` still read
164; live RBGPUDiag reads `armed 0` / `agdc_oneshot 2`. Those live values
are recovery controls and are NOT assigned to the hung boot.

**2rx did win the publication race.** In the saved log, displaypolicyd PID142
already sees AGDC registry ID **0x1000004ad** at **13:29:30.463**; its
13:29:30.974 publication dump and WindowServer PID161's **13:29:31.515**
registration both name `/RembrandtGPUAGDC`. There are **zero** occurrences
of `Unable to get AGDC information` or `Unable to acquire map`, against the
known-present registration dump. NVRAM records `agdc_started 1`,
`agdc_user_vendor 4`, `agdc_user_cap 1`, `agdc_logical_calls 3` and
**`agdc_last_attr 0x921` / `agdc_logical_ret 0xe00002c7`**. The bridge was
queried and refused the logical-device timing. In this tree `rb_agdc_reply`
returns Unsupported for implemented 0x921 when its timing pointer is NULL,
and vendor supplies that pointer only when `timingValid` is true. Thus the
cache was invalid. The log has **69** `No plane indices` and **20**
`checkGPUProgress` occurrences. This is progress past the AGDC map failure,
not a working framebuffer, and the GPU-progress errors remain unexplained.

**The capture lost WHY, and it was a shell error, not evidence of a registry
wedge.** Its last file is `display-log.txt`; no sample-status or peer file.
`plugin_check.sh` uses `set -u` but its default-off branch expands
`$RBGPU_WS_SAMPLE` without a default. When unset, the shell exits immediately
at that line, before the registry collection. Fixed to
`${RBGPU_WS_SAMPLE:-}`. The exact production conditional was executed in an
isolated shell with the variable removed: exit 0, skip-status file written,
no sample invoked. `sh -n` passes. The full script was NOT run by the agent.
The depth-one peer plist now saves and syncs immediately after the NVRAM
breadcrumbs, before slower log collection, and the later formatter reuses
it rather than issuing a second potentially blocked walk. `boot-time.txt`
is saved alongside the boot session UUID. Timing verdicts and the completed
plane-answer counter move ahead of old probes in the existing 512-byte
NVRAM summary; `iop_verify` also stays ahead of possible truncation.

**The code's remaining dependency on the late NDRV path is real.** 2rx made
all NDRV failures fall through to OTG, but the OTG function pointer was still
assigned only by `processNDRV`. The early worker can therefore find no
sampler, publish with an invalid cache, and never repair it (sampling is
once, and `finished` prevents another registration). Merely moving the
binding earlier would retain another startup dependency: the sampler used
`g_hw`, populated only by AMD SMU sw_init. The saved NVRAM omitted all the
sampler keys, so it cannot distinguish those early failures from a later
OTG refusal; **the exact failed precondition on boot 164 is NOT measured**.

**Fix:** move the existing edge-latched sampler into
`src/plugin/rbgpu_agdc_otg.cpp`, call it directly with the bridge's retained
PCI device, and delete the source-binding API and its NDRV registration.
It maps **BAR5 only, `kIOMapInhibitCache | kIOMapReadOnly`**, using its own
local map, and releases it on every exit. No AMD context or NDRV callback is
needed. Before reading any register it checks **1002:1681 rev0a**, existing
memory decoding, the virtual address and the aperture length through the
highest of all four OTG control registers. It does not enable decoding or
bus mastering. The DMU segment and four-pipe signature, raw timing decode,
16-frame edge latch and conversion are the same ones boot 163 verified.
After the sample it rejects changed timing/control registers. No register
write, new route, new notification or publication trigger was added.
The sampler error codes retain 1/3/4/5 and gain **6 identity, 7 decoding off,
8 mapping failure, 9 short/invalid mapping, 10 timing changed**; old code 2
(global AMD context absent) is obsolete. `agdc_otg_bound` is obsolete too;
`otg_map_ro 1` and `otg_bar_len` describe the actual mapping instead.

**Validation exercises the production sampler**, compiled with a minimal
IOKit/clock shim under ASan/UBSan. With no NDRV or AMD startup in that
executable it measures the fixture scanout and produces a successful 0x921
with 1920x1080. Cases also cover 32-bit counter rollover, stopped counter,
unreasonable refresh, timing changes, wrong vendor/device/revision, disabled
decoding, mapping failure, short aperture (inaccessible pointer, so an early
read fails hard), NULL address/output/device, unexpected second active OTG,
read-only BAR5 flags and release on every mapped exit. Existing parser,
AGDC, OTG and lookup tests pass, including 300000 parser mutations.

**Next hardware verdict, pre-stated:** all three one-shots armed as on 164;
`otg_err 0`, `otg_map_ro 1`, `agdc_tim_err 0`, `agdc_tim_cached 2`, real panel
geometry/refresh, then **`agdc_link_result 0`** and
**`agdc_extcap_answered > 0`**. The last `agdc_extcap_result` can legitimately
be Unsupported: Apple asks optional types after the mandatory scaler, so
use the successful-answer counter rather than requiring the last query to
succeed. A successful reply still does not prove a display-pipe transaction
or scanout. The actual flip/backend and GPU-progress errors remain open.

Build/import UUID and commit are recorded in the next state block. No EFI,
boot arguments, one-shots, installed kext, live hardware register or reboot
was changed by the agent. **NOT VERIFIED ON HARDWARE.**

**Final build:** `make plugin` passed; UUID moved from installed 932B9FC8
to **0E6F0DCD-FB38-3D8B-BD95-370AF39DDF9B**. Imports **365/365**, no
unresolved and none in SystemKernelExtensions.kc; the new revision-byte
accessor `IOPCIDevice::extendedConfigRead8` resolves through the already
declared IOPCIFamily in BootKernelExtensions.kc. Info.plist graphics
dependencies remain zero. `git diff --check` passes. Existing kern_start
warnings remain; the new sampler compiles without warnings.

earlier hangs never produced.** Attributed by timestamp AND pid (rule 28), the
hung boot that began **14:26:31** reached:

- +3.7 s `kernelmanagerd[122]` probe-bundle check, +3.9 s `Received kext load
  notification: com.rembrandtgpu.plugin`;
- +3.9 s `WindowServer[161:40d]` `(reg) gpu 0xfbc7 flags 0x20 (DG)
  vid.did=1002.1681 b:d:f=54:0:0` — the wrangler registered our GPU;
- +3.9 s to +5 s dozens of `IOAccelDisplayPipe::display_change_handler` events;
- +10 s `PMRD: wrangler->setIgnoreIdleTimer(1)`, +13 s `WindowServer[161:9a8]`
  Multitouch momentum rates around 130–143 Hz, +21 s to +22 s the familiar
  `AMDRadeonX6000 channel ... event timeout` / `is not hung, keep running`
  `checkGPUProgress` noise, +24 s `airportd` scan results, `launchd` reaping
  `mdmclient`;
- **and then the log ends.** Last line **14:26:56.054**. Nothing until
  14:30:51, the next boot.

So the accelerator was **alive**, WindowServer was **running**, and the whole
machine wedged at **~24 s uptime** — the login-window / desktop-composition
stage, which is exactly "the bar filling up and nothing happened". Rule 12
holds: a user power-cycling a frozen boot looks like a hang, and this one is a
hang with the kernel's own log stopping mid-second.

### Boot 163 vs boot 164: identical boot-args, one variable, opposite outcomes

Boot 164's capture (`logs/20261026-133012-plugin`) was still unread. It is the
A/B this project has been missing for five hangs, because
`diff` of 163's and 164's `boot-args.txt` is **empty — byte-identical**. The
only difference between them is 2rx's trigger.

| | boot 163 (2rw, A83C0170) | boot 164 (2rx, 932B9FC8) |
|---|---|---|
| trigger | framebuffer hook, 1732 ms late | matched notification, early |
| `agdc_started` | 1 | **1** (`agdc_stage` `0x46` = 70) |
| wrangler dump | `agdc 0x10000052d /RembrandtGPUAGDC` | `agdc 0x1000004ad /RembrandtGPUAGDC` |
| `agdc_user_vendor` / `_cap` | **absent** | **4 / 1** |
| `Unable to get AGDC information` | present | **0 occurrences** |
| `Unable to acquire map` | present | **0** |
| `Unable to locate service dependencies` | present | **0** |
| `System set to use IOP but no display pipes are present` | present | **0** |
| outcome | **working accelerated desktop** | **HUNG** |

`diag_used` `0x22f` = 559 of `diag_max` `0x300` = 768, so absence in 164 means
something (rule 14). `iop_verify 1`, `iop_patched 1`, `iop_oneshot 0` — the
IOPresentment vendor gate was open and verified from WindowServer's own memory.

**So 2rx worked.** It won the race it was built to win: the bridge published
before WindowServer asked, WindowServer asked (`agdc_user_vendor 4`,
`agdc_user_cap 1`), and **every single AGDC error that boots 160/162/163 logged
disappeared**. IOPresentment got its vendor info and its capability and went
past the gate 2ql, 2qp, 2qq/2qr and 2r5 spent six milestones closing.

**And going past the gate is what hangs the machine.**

### This was pre-stated, and it is now measured

CLAUDE.md has carried the warning since 2qo, unanswered through 2r5:

> *"the post-gate question is still unanswered behind it, because
> `IONDRVFramebuffer` implements neither `IOPresentmentBindIOAccelSurfaceToResource`
> nor `SetPlaneState`, which 2qn proved no client probe can decide."*

Boot 164 decided it. Nothing else distinguishes 163 from 164 — same tree except
the trigger, same args, same one-shots, same hardware, both with
`iop_verify 1`. Open the gate on a framebuffer that cannot serve the
presentment protocol and WindowServer blocks with no panic and no log; leave it
closed and the desktop works, software-composited, exactly as it has since 2pd.
It also retro-fits **boot 156**, which froze the panel with `agdc_started=1`
before any timing code existed, and reconciles **boot 159**, which published and
was queried and lived — because `rbgpu-iop` was unarmed there, so IOPresentment
never ran and there was no post-gate path to enter (2rw established that
arming the IOP patch is what creates the deadline at all).

**The three `0x921` refusals are not the cause.** `agdc_last_attr 921`,
`agdc_last_ret 0xe00002c7` (`kIOReturnUnsupported`), `agdc_logical_calls 3` —
our own refusal, correct per 2rd/2rg, because the early path had no timing. The
hang is downstream of it: IOPresentment tolerates a failed logical-device
gather (2rl measured it aborting the pipeline gather and carrying on), and 164
hung anyway.

### What 2ry did, and what was wrong with it

2ry read boot 164 as *"wins the AGDC race, but has no timing"* and set out to
fix the timing: it deleted `rbgpu_agdc_otg_source`/`agdc_otg_bound`, moved the
sampler into `src/plugin/rbgpu_agdc_otg.cpp`, and gave it its own read-only
BAR5 mapping (`mapDeviceMemoryWithRegister(kIOPCIConfigBaseAddress5,
kIOMapInhibitCache | kIOMapReadOnly)`) so it no longer depends on `processNDRV`
binding a callback or on AMD's `g_hw` being ready.

**That diagnosis is not wrong about the timing, and it is the wrong thing to
have fixed.** The capture's headline was not the missing timing; it was that
every AGDC error had vanished and the machine had hung. 2ry kept the trigger
that caused the hang, added live MMIO and an up-to-400 ms `IODelay` spin to the
earliest path in the plugin, and shipped it to hardware — which hung twice
more, this time without even reaching the peer's first NVRAM note.

**What is kept:** the sampler itself. It is read-only, bounds-checked
(`otg_err 9` on a short BAR), identity-checked against 2oq's four-register
signature (`otg_err 3`), re-reads every register after the measurement
(`otg_err 10`), publishes a key on every exit, and refuses rather than
converting garbage. Not depending on a late callback is a genuine improvement,
and `make hosttest` executes the production sampler with no NDRV or AMD
initialization. It is also no longer on a path that runs by default.

### The fix

**`-rbgpuagdcearly`, OFF by default.** Without it `rbgpu_agdc_load` publishes
`agdc_say = "ARMED (late): waiting for the framebuffer"` and returns before
both triggers 2rx added — `addMatchingNotification` is never installed and the
load-time `thread_call_enter` is never reached — leaving the framebuffer hook
as the sole trigger. That is the pre-2rx shape, byte-for-byte the behaviour
boot 163 booted clean on. `wranglerArrived` also tests `early` before entering
the worker, so a notification that somehow survived cannot publish.

This is **not** a fix for the race. It is a deliberate decision not to win a
race we cannot yet survive winning, recorded as such so the next session does
not re-land the trigger for the third time. **`agdc_early`** is published and
NVRAM-hot: **0 = late (keeps a desktop), 1 = early (boot 164's wedge)**.

**What would make the early path safe is NOT another trigger change.** It is
the thing CLAUDE.md has named as a large body of work since 2pd: an
`IOFramebuffer` that implements `IOPresentmentBindIOAccelSurfaceToResource` and
`IOPresentmentSetPlaneState`, i.e. DCN 3.1.2 written from Linux's `dcn31`.
Until that exists, opening the gate is measured to be worse than leaving it
shut, and that is a result, not a setback: **the display half's blocker has
moved from "we cannot get past the AGDC gate" to "past the gate there is no
backend", and the first of those is now solved.**

### Verification

`make hosttest` passes (SMU, AGDC bounded replies, link-config overlay, scaler
capability, 300 000 parser mutations, the OTG kernel sampler's early-timing,
edge-latch, refusal and unmap cases). UUID **0E6F0DCD -> 5951FC1F**.
`kmutil libraries` resolves **365 of 365**, **0 unresolved**, **0 from
`SystemKernelExtensions.kc`** — the gate adds no import, so 2oz's trap stays
shut. Info.plist graphics dependencies **0**. `RouteRequest` in
`rbgpu_agdc.cpp` still **1** (rule 3). **NOT YET BOOTED.**

Rescue unchanged: `-rbgpuoff`, and clear the one-shots before it comes out.

## 2s0 — Boot 165 verifies 2rz: the gate is shut, the desktop lives, and the BAR5 sampler works on hardware

Capture `logs/20261026-145230-plugin`, run from inside a live accelerated
desktop. Rule 8/15/14 all clear: **`rbgpu-boot` 165**, every one-shot
**consumed** (`rbgpu-arm`/`rbgpu-agdc`/`rbgpu-iop` all `<unset>`, `agdc_oneshot
0`, `iop_oneshot 0`), UUID **5951FC1F** = `build/out`, `diag_used` **0x23f =
575** of **0x300 = 768**, so an absent key carries information. Boot-args: no
`-rbgpuoff`, no `-rbgpuagdcearly`, `-rbgpuagdc` and `-rbgpuiop` in.

### The gate held, and the absences are the proof

**`agdc_early 0`.** `agdc_note_armed`, `agdc_note_fired`, `agdc_run_reentry`,
`agdc_wait` and `agdc_wait_load` are **all absent** — the matched notification
was never installed, the load-time `thread_call_enter` was never reached,
nothing re-entered and nothing waited. `agdc_pci_seen` **1** (framebuffer, not
the peer lookup) confirms the framebuffer hook was the sole trigger, which is
the pre-2rx shape by construction.

### Published late, never queried, desktop alive — boot 163's signature exactly

`agdc_started 1`, `agdc_stage 0x46` (= 70), `agdc_error 0`, `agdc_say` =
*"PUBLISHED: verify IOPresentment in WindowServer"*, `agdc_policy_optout 1`.
`AGDC::start` queried us as 2rj decoded (`agdc_vendor_calls 2`,
`agdc_cap_calls 1`). **`agdc_user_vendor` and `agdc_user_cap` are ABSENT**, and
so are `agdc_link_result` and every `agdc_extcap_*` key — WindowServer never
reached us, so 0x921 and 0x711 were never asked.

**THE CONTROL, and it is the point of the whole change: all four errors are
BACK**, one occurrence each in `display-log.txt` — `Unable to get AGDC
information`, `Unable to acquire map`, `Unable to locate service dependencies`,
`System set to use IOP but no display pipes are present`. Boot 164 had **zero**
of all four and hung. Their return is what says the gate is shut again.

Apple's own dump reads **both** states, which is the clearest single picture of
the race this project has: `gpu 0xfbc7 agdc 0x000000000` three times, then
`gpu 0xfbc7 agdc 0x100000524 /RembrandtGPUAGDC` later in the same log.
Published and paired — after the question.

**The race, measured again and TIGHTER than 163's:** `kern.boottime`
**14:50:32.279**; the question is `WindowServer[162:3a2]` at **14:50:38.608** =
**+6329 ms** (rule 28: timestamp and pid). `agdc_t_armed_ms` **5946**,
`agdc_t_fb_ms` **7134** = `agdc_t_presample_ms`, `agdc_t_sampled_ms` **7249** =
`agdc_t_started_ms`. **Late by 920 ms, of which the sample is 115 ms.** Boot
163 was late by 1732 ms. The trigger is the same; what moved is when the
framebuffer arrived, which is further evidence that a framebuffer-triggered
publish cannot meet this deadline reliably (2ro) rather than evidence of any
improvement.

### 2ry's BAR5 sampler is verified on hardware, first time

This is the part of 2ry that was worth keeping, and it works:

- **`otg_map_ro 1`** — the read-only `mapDeviceMemoryWithRegister(BAR5,
  kIOMapInhibitCache | kIOMapReadOnly)` succeeded.
- **`otg_bar_len 0x80000` = 512 KB** — BAR5's size, measured here for the first
  time, against the `lastByte` the sampler needs (0x14608 = 83 976), so the
  bounds check had 6x headroom rather than passing by luck.
- **The identity check held through the NEW path**: `otg_ctl0 0x11201` with
  `OTG_MASTER_EN`, `otg_ctl1`/`2`/`3` all `0x300`, `otg_off_ok 3` — 2oq's
  four-register signature, so a direct BAR5 read reaches the same registers
  AMD's `g_hw.rreg` did. That equivalence was assumed by 2ry and is now
  measured.
- **Six raw registers bit-identical to 2oq and boot 163**: `agdc_otg_htot`
  2106, `_hbse` 0x7f07ff, `_hsa` 0x3c0000, `_vtot` 1129, `_vbse` 0x14044c,
  `_vsa` 0x50000. `agdc_otg_ret 0`, `agdc_otg_src 2`.
- **The edge latch and the arithmetic audit**: `otg_frames` **16** in `otg_ns`
  **111 205 632** (`otg_polls` 954 of 4000) = **143.8776 Hz**, and
  `2106 * 1129 * 143877 / 1000` = **342 092 602**, reproducing `agdc_tim_clk`
  to the digit. Against the true 341 987 984 that is **+0.0306 %** (boot 163:
  +0.045 %; boot 160's fixed window: +3.278 %).
- Timing block green: `agdc_tim_err 0`, `agdc_tim_cached` **2** (OTG0),
  `agdc_tim_h 1920`, `agdc_tim_v 1080`, `agdc_tim_mhz 143877`.
- **`agdc_tim_ndrv_err 3`** — the NDRV answered with `kIODetailedTimingValid`
  clear (`agdc_tim_flags 0`), exactly as 2rl measured, and 2rx's split is what
  let the OTG fallback carry it. So the key does the job it was added for:
  `agdc_tim_err 0` alone would have hidden which source won.

`iop_verify 1` with `iop_match 1`, `iop_patched 1`, `iop_saw_ws 1` — 2qo's five
bytes landed in WindowServer's own memory again, so the IOP gate was open and
this boot is a true comparison with 164 rather than a repeat of 159.

### Live state, same boot

Read live at 4 min uptime with the nonce checked first:
`AppleGraphicsDeviceControl` **2** instances, `RembrandtGPUAGDC` present,
`AMDRadeonX6000_AMDNavi21GraphicsAccelerator` present. A working accelerated
Mac with the bridge published and paired.

### Instrument note, rule 26

**`ioreg.txt` in a `plugin_check.sh` capture is TWO LINES** — our own
`RembrandtGPU` node and its bundle id, not a registry dump. A grep for
`AMDRadeonX6000_AMDNavi21GraphicsAccelerator` against it returns 0 and that is
a property of the file, not of the boot; the accelerator is in
`igpu-children.txt`, `igpu-raw.txt` and `pci.txt`. This produced a confident
wrong negative here before the control was run. Do not read class presence out
of `ioreg.txt`.

### What this boot does NOT show

It is the deliberate *non*-winning configuration, so it tests nothing past the
gate. No display pipe, 0x921 and 0x711 never asked, `agdc_user_vendor` /
`agdc_user_cap` absent, software compositing unchanged, and the
`checkGPUProgress` channel errors still unexplained. 2rz's verdict stands
untouched: opening the gate needs
`IOPresentmentBindIOAccelSurfaceToResource` and `IOPresentmentSetPlaneState`,
i.e. DCN 3.1.2 from Linux's `dcn31`, and until that exists `-rbgpuagdcearly`
stays out.

## 2s1 — The two afternoon hangs were NOT boot 164's failure, and 2rz over-grouped them

This corrects 2rz and 2s0 on one point, found by reading evidence already on
disk rather than by booting: **the hung boot of 2026-10-26 14:26 failed
EARLIER than boot 164, in a different place, and 2rz treated both as the same
class.** 2rz's fix and verdict stand; its account of the evidence does not.

### Rule 28, and I fell into it once before getting it right

My first pass windowed the afternoon log by `$2 > "14:26:25" && $2 < "14:30:48"`
and read `WindowServer[161]` lines at 14:30:47 as that boot's tail. **They are
the NEXT boot's WindowServer, which was assigned pid 161 again.** Pids are
reused across boots, so a timestamp window alone does not separate boots. The
reliable separator is the **`Darwin Kernel Version` banner**, which prints once
per boot. Boundaries, afternoon: **14:26:29**, **14:30:47**, **14:50:32**.

### The three afternoon boots, separated

| | boot A | boot B | boot C (= boot 165) |
|---|---|---|---|
| kernel banner | **14:26:29** | 14:30:47 | 14:50:32 |
| build | 2ry `0E6F0DCD` | 2ry + `-rbgpuoff` | 2rz `5951FC1F` |
| WS start | `[161:40d]` 14:26:32.113 | `[162:38f]` 14:30:50.104 | `[162:3a2]` 14:50:35.105 |
| compositor line | **NONE of the three** | **`Software` x2** | `Metal` x2 |
| IOPresentment errors | **none** | 1 (`Unable to acquire map`) | all 3 |
| outcome | **HUNG** | usable (plugin off) | **clean** |

**Boot B is `-rbgpuoff`** — the boot I did the diagnosis from — so it is not a
third hang. There were **two** 2ry hangs: boot A, and the one before it that
boot A's `previous shutdown cause 5` reports.

### Where boot A blocked, pinned against boot C as the control

`WindowServer[161:40d]`, boot A's main thread, last logged at
**14:26:38.311** — `(CoreFoundation) Updating Key-Value Observers Of
Preferences`, after MobileGestalt, CoreVideo's pixel-format registry, TCC and
Accessibility. A HID thread (`161:9a8`) kept logging Multitouch momentum rates
until 14:26:44.203, so **the process was alive with its main thread blocked** —
the frozen-panel signature. The whole system then stopped logging at
**14:26:56.054**.

Milestone counts, boot A against boot C:

| string | boot A | boot C |
|---|---|---|
| `Session 257` | 4 | 4 |
| **`CGXConstructVirtualFramebuffer`** | **1** | **7** |
| **`Setting main display`** | **1** | **7** |
| `CGXMainDisplayDevice` | 1 | 1 |
| `debug-gpus` | **0** | present |
| `RembrandtGPUAGDC` | **0** | present |

**So boot A entered WindowServer's display bring-up and blocked inside the
FIRST `CGXConstructVirtualFramebuffer` pass**, where a healthy boot completes
seven. It never reached the compositor decision (all three of
`Metal`/`Software`/`Noop compositor activated` absent, and 2qa/2qd established
all three paths log), never issued an IOPresentment query, and never ran the
wrangler's `debug-gpus` dump. The nonce stayed **164**, so the peer's first
NVRAM note never flushed either.

**Boot 164, by contrast, got through all of that**: `Metal compositor
activated` x2 at +4 s, zero IOPresentment errors, 26 `IOAccelDisplayPipe`
events, and `WindowServer[161]` still servicing XPC and bluetooth at
**13:30:22**, 54 s in, before the user power-cycled a frozen panel. Boot 164
is a late freeze past the gate; boot A is an early block before it.

### The mechanism, as a hypothesis, and the code change that separates it

**NOT ESTABLISHED.** No diag note exists for boot A, so nothing here is
measured from the plugin's own side. But the composition is specific: 2ry put a
`mapDeviceMemoryWithRegister(BAR5, …)` and an **up-to-400 ms `IODelay` poll of
OTG0** on the bridge's early worker, which runs during exactly the window boot
A blocked in. Boot 164 could not reach that code at all — the sampler was then
bound only from `processNDRV`, which is why 164 shows no OTG keys and 2ry was
written to "fix" that. **This is 2rq's own unexcluded suspect, verbatim:**
*"`rbgpuOtgSample`'s up-to-400 ms `IODelay` spin during early matching, and
MMIO through `g_hw.ctx` before the chip is ready."* 2ry moved that spin onto the
early path and the next two boots blocked earlier than anything before.

**The change: `sampleTimingOtg()` now declines on the early path** —
`if (early && !framebuffer)` publishes **`agdc_otg_src 3`** and returns. The
early trigger therefore publishes with **no timing** (`agdc_tim_err 7`, exactly
what boot 164 did and still got past the gate), and the OTG sample belongs to
the late, framebuffer-triggered path that boot 165 measured clean. A future
`-rbgpuagdcearly` experiment then tests **one** variable instead of two.

**This is inert in the default configuration** — `early` is false, so the guard
cannot fire, and boot 165's verified behaviour is unchanged byte-for-byte in
effect. No boot is needed to trust the current default.

### A control this project has never had

**`Software compositor activated` was observed for the first time**, twice, in
boot B (`-rbgpuoff`, no accelerator). 2qd read the three-way logging from the
disassembly and noted boot 149 had *"the Metal line twice and neither other"*;
this is the negative control for that reading, and it confirms it. It also
means **`Metal compositor activated` x2 is the normal signature of an
accelerated boot here and says nothing about which compositor a given display
gets** — boots 163, 164 and 165 all log it, and all three composite in
software (2pd/2qd).

### What this does and does not change

- **2rz's fix is unaffected**: boot 165 verified it, and the early trigger is
  off by default either way.
- **2rz's verdict is unaffected but its evidence is narrower than written**:
  "past the gate there is no backend" rests on **boot 164 alone** — the boot
  that answered IOPresentment, logged no error, and froze. Boot A says nothing
  about past-the-gate, because it never got there. 2rz's status block and
  commit message both imply the two afternoon hangs corroborated 164; they do
  not.
- **One inference in 2rz is now weaker, and it should be**: a hang is not what
  a missing method produces. `IOPresentmentBindIOAccelSurfaceToResource` and
  `IOPresentmentSetPlaneState` being unimplemented would return
