rule 9, exactly as written. `ioreg` finds **0** `RembrandtGPUAGDC` instances.
So the four map conditions have **never been tested against our bridge**, and
`rbgpu_agdc.cpp` already satisfies two of them on paper: it registers a
runtime metaclass whose superclass is `AppleGraphicsDeviceControl` (so
`IOServiceMatching` should match it by `metaCast`) and it is named
`RembrandtGPUAGDC`, not `AppleGPUWrangler`. Untested: the type-2
`IOServiceOpen` (it sets `IOUserClientClass =
AppleGraphicsDeviceControlClient`) and selector 1's `out+0x28`.

### The next experiment, and its one real risk

It needs **no new code**: an armed boot with `-rbgpuagdc` *and* its one-shot
set, then `build/out/agdcinfo` over SSH. Either our bridge appears as a
candidate — in which case the map gets an entry, a `DisplayPipe` is built, the
latch never fires and the whole chain above unwinds — or it is skipped, and
`agdcinfo` names which of the four conditions it failed.

The risk is **timing, and it is tight**. Boot 174 latched at **+6.5 s** after
`kern.boottime`, with the AGDC query 39 ms earlier at +6.47 s. 2rw measured
the bridge's load at **≤ +5128 ms**. So the plain `-rbgpuagdc` path has about
a 1.3 s margin and may well make it. **`-rbgpuagdcearly` stays OUT** — it is
the arg that wedges (2rz) and it is not needed to test this. If the plain path
loses the race, the fix is to make the bridge earlier, not to open the gate
earlier.

### 2t7 addendum — our selector-1 reply is verified compatible, so the experiment needs no code

Read the validation byte by byte rather than trusting 2r5's prose, because
`cmpl $0x1,%eax; ja` alone would accept **0 or 1** and `rb_agdc_vendor` writes
**2** at `+0x28` — which would have made the whole experiment fail silently:

```
7ff812e8ae6a   movl  -0xf8(%rbp), %eax     ; out is -0x120(%rbp), so this is out+0x28
7ff812e8ae70   decl  %eax                  ; <-- THE instruction that decides
7ff812e8ae72   cmpl  $0x1, %eax
7ff812e8ae75   ja    <skip>
```

The `decl` makes the accepted set `{1, 2}`. **2r5's "must be 1 or 2" is
correct and our `+0x28 = 2` passes.** Also confirmed from the same block: the
`IOConnectCallMethod` at `0x7ff812e8ae54` passes `esi = 1`, output buffer
`-0x120(%rbp)`, output length `-0x2568(%rbp)`, and a zero length or non-zero
return goes to the error tail at `0x7ff812e8aebb`.

`rb_agdc_reply` handles attributes 1, 0x980, 0x921 and 0x711, so both map
queries (`kAGDCVendorInfo` = 1, `kAGDCGPUCapability` = 0x980) are answered.
Two of the map's four conditions are now verified statically; the untested two
are the class match and `IOServiceOpen(type 2)`, and both need the boot.

## 2t8 — BOOT 175: the AGDC bridge armed and then waited forever, because winning the framebuffer destroyed its only trigger

Boot 175 set `rbgpu-agdc=1` and the bridge **armed cleanly** — `agdc_error 0`,
`agdc_oneshot 0`, `agdc_stage 0x1e`, `agdc_t_armed_ms 0x1948` (6472 ms), and
the peer's own line: *"one-shot `rbgpu-agdc` consumed; clear OK"*. Boot 174's
`agdc_error 3` / `"UNARMED: no class or service created"` is gone.

And then nothing happened. `agdc_say` read
**`ARMED (late): waiting for the framebuffer`** for the whole boot, `ioreg`
found **zero** `RembrandtGPUAGDC` instances, and `agdcinfo` again reported
`matched 1, skipped 1, candidates 0`.

### The cause, and it is ours

`rbgpu_agdc_framebuffer()` has exactly **one** caller in the whole plugin:
`hooked_ndrv_enablectl_2pa` (`kern_start.cpp:8284`), which is 2pa's route on
**`__ZN17IONDRVFramebuffer16enableControllerEv`**. `RBAMDFramebuffer`
**displaces** `IONDRVFramebuffer` (2sm: same provider, name and
`IOMatchCategory`, score 30000 vs 20000), so that function **never runs**, and
the bridge waited for a framebuffer that could not arrive.

The same function would have refused ours even if it had been reached: its
identity check was a bare `strcmp(…, "IONDRVFramebuffer")` with
`refuse(5,"unexpected framebuffer")` on anything else. Two independent
blockers, both introduced by the framebuffer kext succeeding.

**So `candidates 0` in boot 175 is still NOT a verdict on the bridge** (rule
14) — it is a verdict on its trigger. The four association-map conditions
remain untested.

This is rule 6's shape again — *when a fix moves upstream, remove the
downstream patch it replaces* — inverted: the framebuffer moved upstream of
`IONDRVFramebuffer` and **nothing downstream was updated to follow it**. 2sm
through 2sy changed which class owns the panel and never audited what else was
routed on the old one. 2pa's VRAM publish, 2qv's metaclass read, 2qx and the
AGDC trigger all hang off that one hook; only the AGDC trigger is fixed here,
and **the other three are still on the dead route** — unaudited, and named so
the next session does not have to rediscover them.

### The fix, in build `4E119EEE`

Two changes in `rbgpu_agdc.cpp`, both behind the existing `-rbgpuagdc`, no new
boot-arg:

1. `rbgpuAgdcIsFramebufferClass()` accepts **`RBAMDFramebuffer`** as well as
   `IONDRVFramebuffer`. Listed rather than dropped, because rule 19's point
   holds: a refusal path must be able to say what it refused.
2. The late path now installs its own `gIOMatchedNotification` on
   `RBAMDFramebuffer` (`fbArrived`), mirroring 2rr's wrangler notification.
   `gIOMatchedNotification` fires after the service matched **and** `start()`
   returned true, which is the same "the controller is up" point 2pa's route
   sat at — **a trigger change, not a timing change**, so the 2rz wedge risk
   is unchanged and `-rbgpuagdcearly` stays out.

Per 2rr, `fbArrived` does two diag writes and calls `rbgpu_agdc_framebuffer`
and nothing else, because `addMatchingNotification` fires **synchronously** for
an already-matched service and can therefore run on the installing thread.
New keys: `agdc_fbnote_armed`, `agdc_fbnote_fired`, `agdc_t_fbnote_ms`, and
`agdc_say` now distinguishes *"watching for RBAMDFramebuffer"* from *"NO
framebuffer notification"*.

Build `4E119EEE` (was `C92D436F`): hosttest green, `kmutil libraries` resolves
**0** from `SystemKernelExtensions.kc`, `grep -c IOGraphicsFamily
src/plugin/Info.plist` is **0**.

### Also measured, and it was my error

Boot 175 ran with `armed = 0` and `rbgpu-arm` unset — *"Peer: rbgpu-arm not
set; accelerator NOT armed"* — because the commands handed over named only
`rbgpu-agdc` and `rbgpu-fb`. The accelerator did not load at all that boot, so
nothing about the desktop in boot 175 is evidence of anything. **Rule 9 names
all four one-shots; the hand-over listed two.**

## 2t9 — 2t8 PANICKED TWICE: the NDRV timing getters are called with `framebuffer` as `this`, and 2t8 made that our object

Two boots lost (176, 177), both to a bug I introduced in 2t8. Build
`4E119EEE`, byte-identical panics:

```
panic(cpu 14): Kernel trap at 0x0000000000000000, type = 14=page fault
RIP: 0x0000000000000000   RAX: 0xffffff7fb6e80068   RSI/RDX/R12/R13: 0
  com.rembrandtgpu.plugin : sampleTiming() + 0xcf
  com.rembrandtgpu.plugin : run(void*, void*) + 0x5ad
  mach_kernel : _thread_call_delayed_timer
```

`RIP = 0` is a call through a NULL pointer; `RAX` is a kext address ending
`0x68`, i.e. a vtable slot that was read and found empty. `sampleTiming()` is
three lines, so `+0xcf` is inside the **inlined `sampleTimingNdrv()`**.

### The bug

`ndrvCurrentMode` and `ndrvTimingInfo` are raw pointers to
**`IONDRVFramebuffer::getCurrentDisplayMode`** and
**`getTimingInfoForDisplayMode`** (`rbgpu_agdc.hpp:16-17`), and
`sampleTimingNdrv()` calls them with the global `framebuffer` as `this`. Until
2t8 that was **safe by construction**: the only caller of
`rbgpu_agdc_framebuffer()` was 2pa's route on
`IONDRVFramebuffer::enableController`, so `framebuffer` could not be anything
else. 2t8 added the `RBAMDFramebuffer` notification and made the same code
reachable with **our** object as `this`. `getTimingInfoForDisplayMode`
dispatches virtually through `this`; our vtable has nothing at that slot; the
machine died at +6.4 s, twice, and the second power cycle hung at the progress
bar in between.

2ri's note — *"neither getter takes a lock … getCurrentDisplayMode is 34
bytes, two loads from `this->0x1e8/0x1ec`"* — is why the first getter survived
and the second did not. The guard at the top tested that the **pointers** were
non-NULL and never that the **object** was the right type. Rule 19, almost
verbatim: *a NULL check is not a pointer check*. Here it was not even a NULL
check of the thing that mattered.

### The fix, build `43447D39`

`sampleTimingNdrv()` now returns **8** when `framebuffer`'s class name is not
`IONDRVFramebuffer`. That is correct rather than merely safe: `sampleTiming()`
already falls through to `sampleTimingOtg()` whenever the NDRV path fails, and
OTG reads the panel's timing straight out of BAR5 with no object at all (2rn,
±0.03 %) — so **OTG is the right timing source for our framebuffer**, not a
degraded fallback. New code 8 is distinct from 6 (getters unresolved) and 7 (no
framebuffer) so `agdc_tim_ndrv_err` says which it was.

Audited the rest of the bridge for the same shape: the only other uses of
`framebuffer` are `getRegistryEntryID()` (a genuine virtual on any
`IORegistryEntry`, so both classes are fine), a pointer-to-`uint64_t` cast for
the AGDC reply, and two NULL tests. Nothing else is NDRV-typed.

### The rule this earns

**When a hook's trigger changes, re-check the TYPE of everything the old
trigger guaranteed.** 2t8 reasoned carefully about *timing* — it argued that
`gIOMatchedNotification` fires at the same "controller is up" point as the old
route, which was true and was the right question to ask — and never asked what
else the old route had been silently guaranteeing. It guaranteed the class of
`framebuffer`, which three functions depended on without saying so. The
generalisable form: a route on `Class::method` is an implicit type assertion
for every global it feeds, and moving the trigger voids it.

This also sharpens 2t8's own closing note. It listed 2pa's VRAM publish, 2qv's
metaclass read and 2qx as "still on the dead route, unaudited". That was
recorded as a loose end; it is in fact the same defect class, and 2qv's read in
particular asserts `getClassName() == "IONDRVFramebuffer"` by comment. Those
three must be audited for type, not just for reachability, before anything
re-triggers them.

## 2u0 — 2sy IS REFUTED BY 2pp: `populateAccelConfig` DID run here, published the capabilities, and something we did since stopped it

Static, no boot. This is the most consequential thing found in a while, and it
was found by reading evidence already in hand — the failure mode this journal
names most often.

### The contradiction, stated plainly

**2pp (2026-10-23, boot ~145, journal line 24847)** recorded, from `ioreg` on
**this machine**, on **our** accelerator:

```
"IOAccelDisplayPipeCapabilities" = {"DisplayPipeSupported"=Yes,"TransactionsSupported"=Yes}
+-o IOAccelDisplayPipeUserClient2  ... "IOUserClientCreator" = "pid 162, WindowServer"
```

with `IOAccelTypes` naming `IGPU@0/AMDRadeonX6000_AMDNavi21GraphicsAccelerator`,
and 2pp's own words: *"Apple's accelerator **found our IONDRVFramebuffer**,
bound to it, published the index triple on it, advertises display pipes AND
transactions as supported"*.

**2sv addendum (2026-10-26 23:42)** measured, with the instrument controlled
(rule 26 — `ioreg -l` emits 7973 property lines and does resolve other
`IOAccel*`-shaped names in the same boot):

```
ioreg -l | grep -c IOAccelDisplayPipeCapabilities   ->  0
```

**And 2sv §3 established there is exactly ONE setter of that name** in
`AMDRadeonX6000` — `0xbe3c6f1`, `r13->setProperty(name, r12)` inside
`AMDRadeonX6000_AMDGraphicsAccelerator::populateAccelConfig` — the single other
reference in the image being `IOAcceleratorFamily2`'s **getter**
(`copyCapabilities`, a three-instruction `getProperty` tail call through slot
`0x2e8`).

So the property was published on 2026-10-23 and is absent on 2026-10-26, and
the only thing that publishes it is `populateAccelConfig`.

### What that refutes

2sy concluded: `populateAccelConfig` derefs `accel->0x368` with no NULL check,
`ATIController` never instantiates here, so a call *would panic*; no boot
panicked; **therefore the function never runs**, and "Apple's display-pipe path
is architecturally closed here".

**That inference is dead.** 2pp is a direct observation of the function's own
output. The function ran, published, and did not panic. Therefore at least one
link of 2sy's argument is false — either `accel->0x368` is populated by
something that is not an `ATIController`, or there is a NULL check in the ~50
unread lines of that function, or the cast target is not `ATIController`. Which
one is **not established here**; 2sy's *conclusion* is what is withdrawn, and
the bad step was reasoning from "no panic was observed" to "the code did not
run" without checking whether the code's *effects* had been observed. They had
been, three days earlier, in this same file.

With 2sy withdrawn, **2sw and 2sx are un-superseded** and go back to being
open rather than moot. 2sx's finding stands on its own merits
(`mov byte ptr [rbx+0x47], 0x1` — `CFG_USE_DPT` defaults to ENABLED, so its
absence from the plist is not a gate), and it is now *consistent* with 2pp
rather than irrelevant to it: gate A passed because the default is 1.

### What it means for the goal, which is the point

The display-pipe path is **not architecturally closed on this machine**. It
**worked**, to the extent of both gate flags being published and WindowServer
opening an `IOAccelDisplayPipeUserClient2` against it. So:

* 2s3's two gates (`DisplayPipeSupported`, `TransactionsSupported`) were
  **satisfied** in 2pp.
* The plane count, 2se's blocker, was never reached in 2pp's analysis because
  nobody looked — the property being present means the frontier in that boot
  was the **blob at slot 0x8d0** (2sv §5), not the dictionary.
* And the capabilities are **gone now**. Between 2pp and 2sv this project
  replaced the framebuffer: `RBAMDFramebuffer` displaced `IONDRVFramebuffer`
  (2sl/2sm/2st). 2pp's line says the publish happened while the accelerator was
  bound to `IONDRVFramebuffer`.

**Prime suspect: the framebuffer takeover suppressed the capabilities
publish.** That is the same defect class as 2t8 and 2t9 — winning the panel
voided assumptions downstream that nothing audited — and it would be the third
instance in one session. It is a **suspicion, not a measurement**: no boot has
yet compared the two configurations for this property.

### The A/B that settles it, and both halves are KNOWN-GOOD configurations

No new code, no wedge risk, no `-rbgpuagdcearly`, no AGDC one-shot. One
property, one grep, in two boots this project has already booted cleanly many
times:

```
A:  sudo nvram rbgpu-arm=1 rbgpu-fb=1     (our framebuffer owns the panel)
B:  sudo nvram rbgpu-arm=1                (IONDRVFramebuffer keeps the panel, 2pp's shape)

in each:  ioreg -l | grep -c IOAccelDisplayPipeCapabilities
          ioreg -l | grep -c IOAccelDisplayPipeUserClient2
```

Four outcomes, each decisive:

| A | B | reading |
|---|---|---|
| 0 | 1 | **the framebuffer takeover suppressed it.** Fix is ours and local, and the display-pipe road reopens. |
| 1 | 1 | it is published now too, 2sv's boot differed for another reason, and the frontier is the 0x8d0 blob. |
| 0 | 0 | it regressed between 2pp and now for a reason unrelated to the framebuffer — bisect the plugin changes since 2026-10-23. |
| 1 | 0 | would contradict 2pp; re-check the instrument before believing it. |

Run A first, since it is the configuration the machine is being restored to
anyway, so the first half costs no extra boot at all.

### The rule this earns, stated against myself

**Before concluding that Apple's code does not run, grep this journal for its
observable effects.** 2sy had the disassembly and reasoned forward from it;
2pp had the output and had written it down. The existing rule says *read the
evidence already in hand before designing the next experiment* — this adds the
specific trigger: a claim of the form "that function never executes" is only as
good as a search for what it would have left behind.

## 2u1 — A/B arm B: with `IONDRVFramebuffer` on the panel the capabilities ARE published, today, on the current build

Measured, no risk, in the recovery boot. Configuration established first
(rule 15), because the property alone would not have said which arm this was:

```
boot-args: -rbgpuoff   ABSENT        (rescue removed)
boot-args: -rbgpuownfb ABSENT        <-- so our framebuffer CANNOT arm (needs the arg AND the key)
ioreg -rl -c IOFramebuffer:
  +-o .Display_boot  <class IONDRVFramebuffer, id 0x1000004c9, registered, matched, active>
kextstat: com.rembrandtgpu.plugin 43447D39  (the 2t9 build, loaded)
          com.rembrandtgpu.fb     45588775  (loaded but unarmed)
```

So this is **arm B** of 2u0's A/B — `IONDRVFramebuffer` owns the panel, which is
2pp's shape — and the answer is unambiguous:

```
ioreg -l | grep -c IOAccelDisplayPipeCapabilities   ->  1
ioreg -l | grep -c IOAccelDisplayPipeUserClient2    ->  2
"IOAccelDisplayPipeCapabilities" = {"DisplayPipeSupported"=Yes,"TransactionsSupported"=Yes}
```

**Byte-for-byte what 2pp recorded on 2026-10-23**, reproduced four days later on
a plugin build four days newer. That settles three things:

1. **2u0's refutation of 2sy is confirmed by a live measurement**, not just by
   an old journal line. `populateAccelConfig` runs on this machine, publishes
   both of 2s3's gate flags, and does not panic. 2sy's "architecturally closed"
   is dead for good, and 2sw/2sx stay open.
2. The regression is **not** in the plugin changes between 2026-10-23 and now —
   this build publishes it fine.
3. 2pp was not a fluke or a misread; the configuration is reproducible.

### What this does NOT settle, and it is the whole point

**Arm A has not been run.** The property being present with
`IONDRVFramebuffer` on the panel says nothing about whether it survives
`RBAMDFramebuffer` taking the panel — which is precisely what 2sv measured
absent. Arm A is the measurement; this is its control.

### The shape this is starting to take, stated as a hypothesis

If arm A comes back 0, the two configurations fail at **different, complementary
links**, and neither has ever had both:

| | gate 1 (`UseIOPresentment`, vendor mask) | the two capability flags |
|---|---|---|
| **B** — `IONDRVFramebuffer` | **FAILS** — class name has no "AMD", mask `0x01` (2ql) | **PASSES** — measured here |
| **A** — `RBAMDFramebuffer` | **PASSES** — mask `0x04`, measured in 2t7 | ? — 2sv says absent |

That table is the useful way to hold this: the framebuffer kext bought gate 1
and may have cost the capabilities, and a working desktop needs both at once.
**It is a hypothesis with one cell unmeasured**, and the A arm fills it.

Arm A needs `-rbgpuownfb` back in boot-args (it is currently out, so
`rbgpu-fb=1` alone cannot arm the framebuffer - rule 9's "the feature needs the
arg *and* the key" read in the other direction).

## 2u2 — A/B arm A: the capabilities SURVIVE our framebuffer. 2u0's suspicion is WRONG, and the frontier moves

Measured, no risk, in the arm-A boot. Configuration established first:

```
ioreg -rl -c IOFramebuffer:
  +-o RBAMDFramebuffer  <class RBAMDFramebuffer, id 0x1000004c4, registered, matched, active>
```

So the framebuffer armed and owns the panel - the arm actually took, which is
what makes a zero meaningful (and it was not zero):

```
ioreg -l | grep -c IOAccelDisplayPipeCapabilities   ->  1
ioreg -l | grep -c IOAccelDisplayPipeUserClient2    ->  1
"IOAccelDisplayPipeCapabilities" = {"DisplayPipeSupported"=Yes,"TransactionsSupported"=Yes}
```

**Both keys `Yes`, with `RBAMDFramebuffer` on the panel.** That is 2u0's second
row: present in both arms.

### 2u0's prime suspect is WITHDRAWN

2u0 wrote: *"Prime suspect: the framebuffer takeover suppressed the
capabilities publish … the same defect class as 2t8/2t9, which would be the
third in one session."* **That is measured false.** The publish survives our
framebuffer. The pattern-match to 2t8/2t9 was seductive precisely because two
real instances of it had just been found, and it was wrong - which is worth
recording as its own small lesson: **two confirmed instances of a defect class
make the third feel measured when it is still only guessed.** 2u0 did label it
a suspicion rather than a finding, and that label is the only reason this cost
nothing.

The complementary-failure table 2u1 proposed is therefore also wrong in its
second row, and the corrected version is:

| | gate 1 (`UseIOPresentment` vendor mask) | the two capability flags |
|---|---|---|
| **B** - `IONDRVFramebuffer` | FAILS - mask `0x01`, no "AMD" in the name (2ql) | **PASSES** (2u1) |
| **A** - `RBAMDFramebuffer` | **PASSES** - mask `0x04` (2t7) | **PASSES** (here) |

**Arm A has BOTH.** Nothing in this pair is missing any more, and the
framebuffer kext is a clear net gain: it buys gate 1 and costs nothing here.

### What is still unexplained, and is not being papered over

2sv's addendum measured this same property **absent** on 2026-10-26 23:42,
`ioreg -l | grep -c` = 0, with the instrument controlled (rule 26). The obvious
candidate - an unarmed accelerator in that boot - is **excluded**:
`logs/20261026-234946-plugin/nvram.txt` is boot 171, captured seven minutes
later, and its live `rbgpu-diag` reads `armed=1`.

So 2sv's zero and 2u2's one disagree with no mechanism named. Candidates, none
measured: a different build (2sv predates `770AE129`, `4E119EEE` and
`43447D39`); a timing race where `ioreg` ran before `populateAccelConfig`; or
the `-rbgpuownfb`/one-shot combination differing in a way the capture does not
record. **Rule 14 cuts both ways here** - 2sv's absence was a controlled
measurement and is not dismissed, it is unreconciled, and anything built on
"the capabilities are missing" must now be re-checked against 2u2 instead.

One real difference between the arms, measured and unexplained:
`IOAccelDisplayPipeUserClient2` counts **2** in arm B and **1** in arm A.

### Where the frontier actually is now

With both capability flags published and gate 1 passing, 2s3's two checks are
satisfied in arm A. The chain's remaining break is the one 2t7 named and 2r5
measured, and it is unchanged by any of tonight's work:

```
AGDC association map EMPTY -> IOServiceOpen(port 0) -> 0x10000003
  -> IOPresentmentCreateForRegistryID NULL -> DisplayPipe ctor throws
  -> zero pipes in the map -> gUseIOP LATCHED 0 -> legacy path -> CompositorSW
```

and behind it, still unread, 2se's plane count via the slot-`0x8d0` blob
(2sv §5). The AGDC bridge is the thing that fills the association map, its
trigger was broken (2t8) and its panic is fixed (2t9), and **it has still never
been tested against the map's four conditions** - three of which are verified
statically (class match by metaCast, the name test, selector 1's `out+0x28`
= 2 in `{1,2}`), leaving only the type-2 `IOServiceOpen`.

So the next experiment is unchanged from 2t7's, but its value is higher than it
was: everything downstream of the AGDC map is now known to be in place rather
than hoped to be.

## 2u3 — 2sv §5 ANSWERED and CORRECTED: slot `0x8d0` is `copyCapabilities`, not a vendor blob. There is no second capabilities channel

Static, no boot. 2sv §5 named "the blob produced by **slot 0x8d0** on the
object at `userclient+0xe8`, a **vendor method**" as *the next read*, and
pointed at `AMDRadeonX6000`. Read it, and the premise is wrong.

### The read

The vendor display-pipe class is `AMDRadeonX6000_AMDAccelDisplayPipe` (2s4).
Dumping its vtable (`dumptable.py`, `__ZTV34AMDRadeonX6000_AMDAccelDisplayPipe`,
0xbf94220, 2336 bytes) at **dump offset 0x8e0** — rule 7, call offset
`0x8d0` = dump `0x8e0`:

```
  +0x8c8  __ZN34AMDRadeonX6000_AMDAccelDisplayPipe17submitTransactionEP30IOAccelDisplayPipeTransaction2
  +0x8d0  -> 0x14e5d79e      (inherited, IOAcceleratorFamily2)
  +0x8d8  -> 0x14e5d4be      (inherited)
  +0x8e0  -> 0x14e5d7aa      (inherited)   <-- CALL OFFSET 0x8d0
  +0x8e8  __ZN34AMDRadeonX6000_AMDAccelDisplayPipe16beginTransactionEP12IOAccelEvent
```

`nm` on the extracted `IOAcceleratorFamily2` names all three:

| address | symbol |
|---|---|
| `0x14e5d79e` | `IOAccelDisplayPipe::getDisplayModePipeScalerSetup` |
| `0x14e5d4be` | `IOAccelDisplayPipe::createWorkLoop` |
| **`0x14e5d7aa`** | **`IOAccelDisplayPipe::copyCapabilities()`** |

and its body is the same function 2sv §2 had already read, four bytes further
in at the first instruction after the frame setup:

```
14e5d7aa  pushq %rbp
14e5d7ab  movq  %rsp, %rbp
14e5d7ae  movq  0x88(%rdi), %rdi
14e5d7b5  movq  (%rdi), %rax
14e5d7b8  movq  0x2e8(%rax), %rax
14e5d7bf  leaq  0x16b41(%rip), %rsi     ; "IOAccelDisplayPipeCapabilities"
14e5d7c7  jmpq  *%rax
```

### What that corrects, and what it means

1. **It is not a vendor method.** The entry at call offset `0x8d0` is
   *inherited*; `AMDRadeonX6000_AMDAccelDisplayPipe` overrides the slots on
   either side of it (`submitTransaction`, `beginTransaction`) and leaves this
   one alone. 2sv §5's "a vendor method" and its instruction to read
   `AMDRadeonX6000` were both wrong, and the error is instructive: 2sv
   inferred "vendor" from the *call shape* (`call [rax+0x8d0]` on an object
   reached through a field) without checking whether that slot was overridden.
   **A high vtable offset is not evidence of a vendor override** — rule 7's
   neighbourhood needs the actual dump.
2. **It is the SAME channel, read twice.** 2sv §2 and 2sv §5 were describing
   one function. So `getCapabilitiesData`'s "binary blob" is just
   `copyCapabilities()`'s return value serialised through the two accessors at
   slots `0x158`/`0x118`; the length/bytes reading of those two is 2sv's
   inference and is **still unverified**, but it no longer matters for the
   question being asked.
3. **There is therefore NO second, non-AGDC capabilities channel in the
   kernel.** 2sv §5 was the last candidate found by elimination for where the
   plane count could enter, and it has collapsed into the registry property
   this project has now measured twice (2u1, 2u2) as containing exactly two
   keys: `DisplayPipeSupported` and `TransactionsSupported`. No `PlaneArray`,
   no count.

### So where the plane count comes from is OPEN again, and honestly so

The state of that question, with nothing papered over:

* 2sf measured the userspace dictionary that carries the count
  (`IOPresentmentCapabilitiesStructureFromDictionary`, keyed `PlaneArray`,
  `GammaArray`, …) is built by `__GatherAGDCDisplayPipelineCapabilities` from
  the **AGDC replies**.
* 2sg measured that **no AGDC query carries a plane count** — 0x711 sixteen
  times, 0x921 once, and `__GatherAGDCLinkCapabilities` which 2rg measured
  inert — and that `PlaneArray` is the one group no capability type feeds.
* 2u3 now removes the kernel-side blob that was the remaining candidate.

Three measurements that each exclude a source, and the count is non-zero on
real hardware. **Something in that set is being read wrongly, and the cheapest
way to find out which is to watch the code run rather than to read a fourth
candidate.** None of this is observable until
`IOPresentmentCreateCapabilities` is actually reached, and it is not reached
while the AGDC association map is empty.

### Which makes the AGDC boot the next step on its own merits

Not as a prerequisite to be got out of the way, but because it is the only
instrument that makes the plane-count question answerable at all. Everything
downstream of the map is now known present rather than hoped for (2u2: gate 1
and both capability flags), three of the map's four conditions are verified
statically (2t7, 2t8 addendum), the bridge's trigger is fixed (2t8) and its
panic is fixed (2t9). The static road has run out; this is no longer a choice
between reading more and booting.

Boot 177, `rbgpu-boot = 177` against the previous capture's 174, so the nonce
is new (rule 8). Capture on disk: `logs/20261027-042201-plugin`. It **wedged**,

### THE PLANE COUNT IS NOT ZERO - 2se/2sf/2sg's whole line of inquiry is RETIRED

Every one of the 58 `DisplayPipeState` dumps opens:

```
-------------------DisplayPipeState-------------------
Plane Index: 0
Source Color Space: <CGColorSpace ...> (sRGB IEC61966-2.1)
Rotation Angle: 0 degrees
Matrix / LUT R,G,B [0..0.500489..1] with 1024 entries / LiT R,G,B with 3 entries
```

**A plane exists and is being enumerated.** So 2se's "the plane count is a
byte at pipe+0x10, a count of 0 means nothing can ever be staged" was never
the gate here, 2sf's hunt for what feeds `PlaneArray` was answering a question
that had no teeth, and 2sg's "the plane count does not come from AGDC" is
consistent with it coming from nowhere we needed to supply. **2u3's three
mutually-exclusive measurements are reconciled the cheapest possible way: the
count was never the problem.** 2u3 said the way to find which measurement was
wrong was to watch the code run; the answer is that none of them was wrong and
the inference built on top of them was.

### What Apple says the blocker IS, in its own words

New in this boot, and never seen before in this project:

```
04:21:23.303  [ERROR] - DisplaySurface Size: (1920x1080) Format:BGRA
04:21:23.303  [WARN]  - Display: 0x5b81c5c0 woke on GPU: AMD
04:21:23.303  [ERROR] - Attempting to get capabilities from plane with no gamma   (x7)
04:21:23.305  [ERROR] - Fallback GPU Display Pipe transaction submission failed
04:21:23.305  [ERROR] - Transaction Target State
```

and in every dump, the single unresolved operation, unchanged since 2sa:

```
    Dirty        Fetch  - Pipe          <- routing through the pipe
    Dirty        System Gamma  - Unknown   <- THE ONE THAT DOES NOT RESOLVE
    Dirty        EOTF  - GPU
```

`Clean` still never appears in 58 dumps, and the transaction submission now
fails **with a named cause**: the plane has **no gamma capability**.

### This is precisely the suspect 2sc/2sd could not eliminate

2sd eliminated capability types 1 (CSC), 4 (Degamma) and 0x8000 (Cursor) by
answering all five and measuring a byte-identical log. It explicitly could not
eliminate **type 2 (Gamma)**, because 2sc had to substitute its channel count
(`vt[0x1b8](0xf)`, on an object we lack) and "an empty gamma capability is
plausibly indistinguishable from a refused one". **Apple has now printed the
distinction.**

### And we did not even answer it this boot

```
boot-args: -rbgpuagdccaps   ABSENT
agdc_extcap_all = 0   agdc_extcap_answered = 3   agdc_extcap_gated_n = 0x2d
```

So type 2 was **gated off**. The next experiment is therefore a single
variable, needs no new code, and carries a sharp prediction: arm
`-rbgpuagdccaps` and `Attempting to get capabilities from plane with no gamma`
must change. If it does, gamma is the blocker and the question becomes what a
*correct* gamma capability contains. If it does not, the message is about
something other than our AGDC reply and the capability interface is the wrong
lever after all.

**Stated plainly because rule 17 demands it**: `-rbgpuagdccaps`'s gamma answer
contains a SUBSTITUTED channel count (2sc). It is legitimate as a diagnostic -
that is what 2sc built it for - and **no reading from it may be narrated as a
hardware fact**. It tells us whether the message responds to that input, and
nothing more.

### Standing risk, unchanged

Boot 177 wedged, as boots 156/164/169/170 did. 2s8 holds: the wedge writes its
NVRAM note, consumes its one-shots, and a plain power cycle comes up clean.
`-rbgpuoff` remains the rescue. The capture surviving on disk is what makes
these boots affordable.

## 2u5: boot 178 — the gamma arm LANDS on the AGDC side, and the display-side verdict was lost to a +28 s capture

Boot 178 (`rbgpu-boot = 178`, new nonce, `armed = 1`, kern.boottime
04:26:42) ran 2u4's single-variable experiment: `-rbgpuagdccaps` present in
`boot-args.txt`, everything else as boot 177.

**The arm took, and the capability negotiation changed exactly as predicted:**

| key | boot 177 | **boot 178** |
|---|---|---|
| `agdc_extcap_all` | 0 | **1** |
| `agdc_extcap_answered` | 3 | **15** |
| `agdc_extcap_calls` | 48 | 48 |
| `agdc_extcap_gated` / `_gated_n` | 0x8000 / 45 | **absent** |
| `agdc_failed_calls` | 46 | **34** |
| `agdc_last_ret` | 0xE00002C7 | **0** |

48 calls is 16 types × 3 rounds. 3 answered was one type per round (Scaler);
**15 is five types per round** — 1 CSC, 2 Gamma, 4 Degamma, 0x10 Scaler,
0x8000 Cursor. `agdc_failed_calls` falls by **exactly 12** = 4 new types × 3
rounds, and `agdc_extcap_gated_n` disappears because nothing is gated off any
more. So **type 2 (Gamma) was answered this boot**, which is the one thing 2u4
asked for. Everything else held identical: `agdc_say = "PUBLISHED"`,
`agdc_error 0`, `agdc_stage 0x46`, `agdc_user_vendor 4`, `agdc_user_cap 1`,
`agdc_tim_ndrv_err 8` with OTG timing (1920×1080, 342287571 Hz, 143959
mHz), `agdc_link_result 0`, `fb_vbl_on 1`, `otg_err 0`.

**But the experiment's actual readout is MISSING, and the capture is why.**
`display-log.txt` is **0 bytes**, and so is `display-log-errors.txt` — the
`log show` succeeded and matched nothing. The capture ran at
04:27:10, **28 s into the boot**; boot 177's ran at **46 s** and got 2225
lines. Live `kern.boottime` now reads 04:27:45, i.e. the machine was power
cycled 63 s into boot 178, so **that boot is gone and its display log cannot
be recovered**. Rule 10 saved the diag and nothing else.

**Stated per rule 14: the zero is not a result.** Two readings fit it and this
capture cannot separate them — (a) the log store had nothing flushed at +28 s
and WindowServer's pipe activity came later, or (b) boot 178 never got as far
as WindowServer's display-pipe work at all. `framebuffer.plist` is 4261 bytes,
so `RBAMDFramebuffer` existed; that bounds nothing about WindowServer.
So **`Attempting to get capabilities from plane with no gamma` is neither
confirmed changed nor confirmed unchanged**, and 2u4's prediction is still
open.

**The repeat costs no new code and no new arg** — the arm is already in
boot-args and already measured to take. What it needs is the capture **later
in the boot**, which is a procedure change, not a build:

> **New rule, paid for here:** `plugin_check.sh` reads NVRAM, which is ready
> immediately, and the unified log, which is not. A capture taken before
> WindowServer has run is a capture with the display half silently blank.
> **Check `wc -l display-log.txt` against a known-present control in the same
> capture before concluding anything from it** — exactly rule 26's shape,
> applied to a log window instead of a grep.

Also recorded: the display-side question has never been answered with the
gamma arm on. 2sd's A/B (boot 170) answered five types too, but that was
**before** gate 1 was won and before a `DisplayPipe` existed, so its
byte-identical display log says nothing about boot 178's configuration.

### 2u5 addendum: boot 178 wedged, and the capture is now self-checking

The user reports boot 178 **wedged like 156/164/169/170/177**. That bounds the
0-byte display log usefully: boot 177 wedged too and still logged **2225
lines** at +46 s, so the wedge does **not** suppress WindowServer's logging —
the +28 s capture window does. Reading (b) from 2u5 ("the boot never got as
far as WindowServer's display-pipe work") is therefore **not supported**; the
log was simply not flushed yet. The zero still carries no information about
gamma.

Two things follow, and the second is a fix rather than a note.

**1. The wedge survives answering Gamma.** That is weak and stated as weak: a
wedge is the observable in every armed, gate-open boot since 2rz, so its
recurrence distinguishes nothing on its own. What would distinguish is the
`plane with no gamma` line, which is exactly what was lost.

**2. `tools/plugin_check.sh` now measures its own log window.** The display
capture gained an unfiltered `process == "WindowServer"` **control** written to
`display-log-control.txt`, and the script waits 15 s and retries up to six
times while that control reads 0. Three outcomes are now distinguishable where
boot 178 had one:

- control 0 → the script prints `WARNING: the control is ZERO, so
  display-log.txt carries NO information` and says not to reboot on it;
- control > 0 and predicate 0 → it prints `that IS a result`;
- both > 0 → the capture is what it has always been.

Verified live: the control predicate returns 13 876 lines in the current boot,
and `bash -n` passes. This is rule 26 applied to a log window instead of a
grep, and it is the first time the script checks an instrument of its own.

The repeat is unchanged otherwise: `-rbgpuagdccaps` is **already in
boot-args** and already measured to take (`agdc_extcap_answered 15`), so the
next boot needs no `efi.sh` step — only the one-shots, and the capture run
**once WindowServer is up**, which the script will now tell the user.

## 2u6: boot 179 — the gamma arm MOVED the error, and the new wording names the field 2sc substituted

Boot 179 (`rbgpu-boot = 179`, new nonce, `armed = 1`, boot 14:43:53, capture
14:44:35 = **+42 s**) is 2u4's experiment with a capture that works. The new
control proves the window this time: `display-log-control.txt` **2693 lines**,
`display-log.txt` **2245**. 2u5's blank was the window, nothing else.

Arm identical to 178: `agdc_extcap_all 1`, `agdc_extcap_answered 15`,
`agdc_failed_calls 34`, `agdc_last_ret 0`, `agdc_say = "PUBLISHED"`,
`agdc_error 0`, `agdc_stage 0x46`, `agdc_user_vendor 4`. Chain still open:
`Unable to get AGDC information` **0**, `no display pipes are present` **0**,
`Unable to find display pipe` **0**, `Metal compositor activated` **2**,
`CompositorSW` **0**.

**2u4's prediction is CONFIRMED, and sharply.** The message did not merely
change count — it changed **text**, with the same ×7 multiplicity:

| | boot 177 (gamma gated OFF) | **boot 179 (gamma answered)** |
|---|---|---|
| `Attempting to get capabilities from plane with no gamma` | **7** | **0** |
| `Attempting to get 3-channel gamma table capabilities from plane with no 3-channel gamma table support` | 0 | **7** |
| `...3-channel linearization table capabilities from plane with no 3-channel linearization table support` (WARN) | 0 | **1** |
| `Fallback GPU Display Pipe transaction submission failed` | present | 57 |
| `Transaction Target State` | present | 57 |
| `DisplayPipeState` dumps | 58 | 57 |
| `Clean` | 0 | **0** |

So the gamma capability **does** reach CoreDisplay, and what it now rejects is
the capability's **channel count** — which is exactly the field 2sc had to
substitute and labelled as substituted (`vt[0x1b8](0xf)`, value **0**, on an
`AmdFbDisplayPath` we do not have). Apple asks for a 3-channel table; we said
zero channels; it says so in words.

**That REFUTES 2sf's reading of where CoreDisplay gets gamma from.** 2sf/2sd
concluded, from 2sd's byte-identical display log, that "type 2's substituted
channel count was never going to matter, because that is not where CoreDisplay
reads gamma from" (journal line 35513). Boot 179 measures the opposite: the
AGDC type-2 reply is read, and its channel count is the field under test. 2sf's
*disassembly* of the dictionary and its key groups stands; the inference that
the AGDC type bits do not feed it does not. The reason 2sd saw no change is
that 2sd ran **before gate 1 was won and before a `DisplayPipe` existed**
(2t7/2u4) — there was no consumer in that boot to read the reply. 2sd is
therefore not a null result about capabilities either; it is a null result
about a boot with no pipe.

**The dumps also got richer, which is independent corroboration.** Boot 177's
`DisplayPipeState` carried `LUT: R` alone. Boot 179's carries `Rotation Angle`,
a 3×3 `Matrix`, `LUT: R/G/B` (1024 entries each) **and `LiT: R/G/B`** (3
entries each). Those are the CSC, gamma and linearization groups appearing
because we now answer their types. The operation list is complete and, of
eight operations, **seven resolve** — `Fetch - Pipe`, `EOTF - GPU`, and
`Scale / Rotate / Linearize / CSC / Regamma - None` — with exactly one left:

```
    Dirty        System Gamma  - Unknown
```

**So the frontier is now one field, named by Apple, in code we already own.**
`rb_agdc.h`'s gamma reply writes a channel count of 0; CoreDisplay wants 3.

**Stated before anyone acts on it (rule 17):** changing 0 to 3 is **still a
substitution**, not a measurement — we would be asserting a three-channel
gamma table we cannot program, exactly the risk 2sc named when it chose
Apple's smallest branch ("copying AMD's real numbers would claim hardware
gamma … and if `Commit` then chose the hardware pipe on the strength of it the
result would be worse than the wedge"). The honest framing is that boot 179
turns that caution from a general worry into a **specific, testable** one: the
error names the field, so a single-field change is a single-variable
experiment, and it must be journalled as a substituted value whatever it
produces. The `LiT: R/G/B - 3 entries` line and the linearization WARN say the
same thing about `LinearizationArray`.

Unchanged and still unexplained: `fb_vbl_ot_armed` absent (`diag_used` 549 of
768, so rule 14's check passes and the absence carries information — nothing
has ever been queued), and the wedge itself.

## 2u7: the error's one and only emitter, read — and it is NOT the channel count, it is a NULL table

Static read, no boot. 2u6 ended by saying the next change is one field; this
corrects *which* field before anyone spends a boot on it.

The new string `Attempting to get 3-channel gamma table capabilities from plane
with no 3-channel gamma table support` lives at **`0x7ff80415456f`** (found by
`Cache.read` + `bytes.find`, start-of-string per rule 26). `dsc.py ripall`
across all seven cache files finds **exactly one** RIP-relative site:
`0x7ff80405df8e`, a `lea` feeding the log call — inside
**`CoreDisplay::IOPCapabilities::GammaChannelTableEntryCountAndType()`**
(`0x7ff80405ddd8`, named in `build/re/CoreDisplay-funcs.txt`). So 2sc's comment
at `rb_agdc.h:277` named the right consumer all along, and 2sf talked itself
out of it (2u6).

**What the function actually decides.** After a NULL check on `this->0x8` and
on `[this->0x8 + 0xb0] -> 0x90 -> 0x88` (the array count, `rax`; zero takes a
*different* error at `0x7ff80405dfb1`), it walks an array with **stride 0x38**
from `0x90(%rcx) + 0x30`, and per entry reads two slots:

- `%rdi = [entry + 0x10]` — a **format bitmask**
- `%rsi = [entry + 0x30]` — the value it will return

It then picks the entry with the widest accepted format, in this order, each
guarded by the best-so-far count in `%rdx`:

| bit of `entry+0x10` | entry count it claims |
|---|---|
| 9 | 0x10 (16) |
| 8 | 0xc (12) |
| 7 | 0xa (10) |
| 6 | 8 |
| 4 | 8 |
| 3 | 8 |

and the winner's `%rsi` is kept in `%r14`. The **last three instructions before
the error** are the whole predicate:

```
7ff80405df7f:  testq %r14, %r14
7ff80405df82:  jne   0x7ff80405dfd1          ; success
7ff80405df84:  xorl  %r14d, %r14d
7ff80405df87:  leaq  0xf6541(%rip), %rdi     ; function/file name
7ff80405df8e:  leaq  0xf65da(%rip), %rdx     ; the error string
7ff80405df95:  movl  $0x2d8, %esi            ; Apple's source line 728
```

**So the complaint is `entry+0x30 == 0`, not a channel count.** And our format
bitmask is already accepted: `rb_agdc_gamma_entry` writes `0x10` at `+0x10`,
which is **bit 4**, one of the six the table above lists. That is why the error
*moved* rather than staying put — the entry is now found and its format
honoured, and the one thing missing is the value at `+0x30`.

**Stated plainly, because 2u6 came one step from getting this wrong:** 2u6
inferred from the new wording that the field under test was
`RB_AGDC_GAMMA_CHANNELS` (`rb_agdc.h:278`, our substituted 0, written to our
entry's `+0x28`). **That inference is NOT supported.** The slot Apple reads is
`+0x30` of a **0x38-stride CoreDisplay array**, which is not our 0x32c-stride
AGDC entry; nothing read so far maps our `+0x28` onto it. 2u6's measurement
stands in full — the error text changed, so the AGDC type-2 reply *is* consumed
— but its closing sentence named a field it had not traced. This is the
recurring error again (reading a value without establishing what makes it
meaningful), caught this time before it cost a boot rather than after.

**The one read that closes it** is the field mapping:
`__GatherAGDCDisplayPipelineCapabilities` (`0x7ff812e979dc`, the address
`rb_agdc.h:182` has cited since 2rf) → the gamma branch → which slot of our
reply it copies into the dictionary's `GammaArray` entry, and which key then
lands at `+0x30`. The dictionary's gamma keys are already known (2sf, journal
line 35489): `GammaArray`, `FixedFormat`, `GammaValue`, `NumberOfElements`,
`Elements`. `NumberOfElements` is the obvious candidate for `+0x30` and
`FixedFormat` for `+0x10` — **candidate, not conclusion**; the read decides it.
No boot is needed for any of this, and no boot should be spent until it is done.

## 2u8: `UseIOPGamma` read and ELIMINATED, and `useiop` gained the gamma quartet

Static, plus one live oracle run. No boot.

`CoreDisplay-funcs.txt` lists **`UseIOPGamma(CGXDisplayDevice const*)`** at
`0x7ff8040ea95c`, which is the obvious candidate for `System Gamma - Unknown`
and had never been read. It is short:

```
7ff8040ea962:  movq  0x8(%rdi), %rax
7ff8040ea966:  callq *0x200(%rax)          ; device vtable slot 0x200 -> %ebx
7ff8040ea96e:  callq 0x7ff804057b40        ; UseIOPresentment()
7ff8040ea973:  testb %al, %al
7ff8040ea975:  je    <return 0>
7ff8040ea977:  leal  -0x2(%rbx), %ecx
7ff8040ea97a:  rorl  %ecx
7ff8040ea97e:  cmpl  $0x7, %ecx
7ff8040ea981:  ja    <return 0>            ; jump table at 0x7ff8040ea9e4
```

So it **calls `UseIOPresentment()` itself** — which 2t7 proved true here,
unpatched — and then switches on `%ebx`, the value from device vtable slot
`0x200`, which the branch bodies compare against **4, 8 and 0x10**: the same
AMD / NVDA / AppleParavirt bits as `gSystemGPUVendors`. Each vendor branch does
`movb $0x1, %al; cmpb $0x0, <byte>; jne <return 1>` against one of four bytes
at **`0x7ff843bac76f`–`0x772`**, immediately after `useIOP_onIG`'s
`0x7ff843bac76e` (`tools/useiop.m:24`).

**The names were one string block away.** Dumping the strings around
`displaySurfaceUsesIOSurface` prints `CoreDisplay::InitializeUserDefaults()`'s
whole key list, and beside `useIOP`, `useIOP_onIG/onAMD/onNVIDIA/onAPV` sit
**`useIOP_gamma_onIG`, `useIOP_gamma_onAMD`, `useIOP_gamma_onNVIDIA`,
`useIOP_gamma_onAPV`**. Same quartet, same shape, same domain.

`tools/useiop.m` now reads all four the way it already reads the others, so
this is an oracle rather than a reading of the binary. Live, this machine:

```
   useIOP_gamma_onIG     = 1  (absent -> default)
   useIOP_gamma_onAMD    = 1  (absent -> default)  <- ours
   useIOP_gamma_onNVIDIA = 1  (absent -> default)
   useIOP_gamma_onAPV    = 1  (absent -> default)
```

**A non-zero byte takes the `jne <return 1>` branch**, so with the default of 1
`UseIOPGamma` returns **1** for an AMD device whenever `UseIOPresentment()` does
— which it does (2t7). **`UseIOPGamma` is therefore ELIMINATED as the cause of
`System Gamma - Unknown`**, and nobody should spend a `defaults write` or a
boot on it. Worth saying because the temptation was real: a per-vendor
preference named `useIOP_gamma_onAMD` reads exactly like the switch one wants
to find, and it is already on.

**So 2u7's conclusion stands unchanged and is now the only live lead**: the
sole emitter is `GammaChannelTableEntryCountAndType`, and its predicate is
`entry+0x30 != 0` over a 0x38-stride array whose format bitmask at `entry+0x10`
our `0x10` already satisfies. The next read is what **fills** that array.
Where it is NOT: `__GatherAGDCDisplayPipelineCapabilities`'s own body, which
2rg/2sg already read in full — its sixteen 0x711 calls go through four imported
stubs (`0x7ff812ea00f6`, `0x7ff812ea02b8`, `0x7ff812ea0306`, `0x7ff812ea039c`,
16/16/32/32 calls, all `jmpq *GOT`), so the per-type field copying is not in
that function either. The array belongs to `CoreDisplay::IOPCapabilities`
(`this->0x8 -> +0xb0 -> 0x90 -> 0x88` is its count), and its constructor is the
thing to read — `CapabilitiesForClients` (`0x7ff80405d582`) and the destructor
(`0x7ff80405d4f8`) bracket it in the function list.

## 2u9: Apple's own gamma producer re-read field by field — `+0x28` is an ELEMENT COUNT, and Apple's second entry hardcodes 0x200

Static, kernel side, no boot. `nm -m build/re/AMDRadeonX6000Framebuffer`
resolves `0xbfecda8` to
`AMDRadeonX6000_AmdAgdcServices::getFbCapabilityForGamma(AmdFbDisplayPath*,
unsigned int&, AGDCFBExtendedCapabilitesEntry_t*)` — **the Framebuffer kext,
not `AMDRadeonX6000`**, which is why the address is absent from the latter's
text (noted so the next reader does not repeat the lookup).

2sc read this function and took its smallest branch. Read field by field now,
with the write **widths** attended to:

**Entry 1** (`%rbx` = the entry):

| write | offset / width | value |
|---|---|---|
| `movl $0x88005, (%rbx)` | +0x00 dword | `0x00088005` |
| `movq $0x1, 0x4(%rbx)` | +0x04 **qword** | 1 (so +0x08 = 0) |
| `movq $0x1000000000, 0xc(%rbx)` | +0x0c **qword** | +0x0c = 0, **+0x10 = 0x10** |
| `movl $0x0, 0x14(%rbx)` | +0x14 dword | 0 |
| `movq $0x3f80000000000000, 0x20(%rbx)` | +0x20 **qword** | +0x20 = 0, **+0x24 = 1.0f** |
| `vt[0x1b8](0xf)`, `cltq`, `movq %rax, 0x28(%rbx)` | +0x28 **qword** | the substituted field |

`rb_agdc_gamma_entry` reproduces every one of those correctly, including the
two values that are only visible once the qword writes are split
(+0x10 = 0x10 and +0x24 = 1.0f). The segment count comes from
`vt[0x118](0x17) + 1` on a *different* object (`this->0x118` → `vt[0x920]()`),
and the +0x28 value from `vt[0x1b8](0xf)` on another (`this->0x118` →
`vt[0x938]()`) — both `AmdFbDisplayPath`-side objects we do not have.

**Entry 2 — written only when the segment count is >= 2** — is the find:

| write | offset within entry 2 | value |
|---|---|---|
| `movl $0x88005, 0x32c(%rbx)` | +0x00 | `0x00088005` |
| `movq $1, 0x330(%rbx)` | +0x04 qword | 1 |
| `movl $0, 0x338(%rbx)` | +0x0c | 0 |
| `movq $1, 0x33c(%rbx)` | +0x10 qword | **1** |
| `movq this->0x2e798 \| 0x40, 0x344(%rbx)` | +0x18 qword | device flags OR 0x40 |
| `power(2.0, -25)` → `movss 0x34c` | +0x20 float | `powf(2, -25)` |
| `power(2.0, 7)` → `movss 0x350` | +0x24 float | `powf(2, 7)` |
| `movq $0x200, 0x354(%rbx)` | +0x28 qword | **0x200** |

So **`+0x28` is the entry's ELEMENT COUNT**, and Apple's own second entry
states it as a literal **0x200 = 512** — a 512-entry segmented gamma table —
while `+0x10` carries a format word (0x10 for entry 1, 1 for entry 2). That
reading is consistent with 2u7's consumer: CoreDisplay accepts our format word
(bit 4 of `+0x10`) and then finds the count behind it empty.

**Which makes the next experiment materially better than the one 2u6 proposed,
and cheaper to justify.** 2u6 wanted to invent a channel count. Instead,
raising `RB_AGDC_GAMMA_SEGMENTS` from 1 to **2** makes `rb_agdc.h` write
Apple's second entry, whose element count is **Apple's own literal 0x200** and
whose two floats are **Apple's own `powf` constants** — nothing invented. The
single remaining substitute in entry 2 is the device-flags qword
(`this->0x2e798`), for which 2sc's convention already uses 0, leaving
`0 | 0x40 = 0x40` — Apple's own OR, with the unavailable term zero.

**Still not established, and it matters (rule 13/17):** that CoreDisplay's
`entry+0x30` *is* this `+0x28` after translation. The chain
`this->0x8 → +0xb0 → +0x90 → {+0x88 count, +0x90 array}` walks a **0x38-stride
CoreDisplay array**, not our 0x32c AGDC entry, and the translation step is
still unread — `IOPresentmentCapabilitiesStructureFromDictionary`
(`0x7ff812e8df1c`, 911 lines, 36/30/10 calls through three imported stubs)
references the gamma keys through CFSTR constants rather than direct string
leas, so neither `ripall` on `GammaArray` (`0x7ff812ea0ed3`) nor a chained-
pointer-blind qword search for its `__cfstring` finds the site. That is a
tooling gap, not a dead end, and it is the honest reason this entry proposes an
experiment rather than claiming a cause.

**What the experiment is, stated so it stays a single variable:** one constant,
`RB_AGDC_GAMMA_SEGMENTS 1u` → `2u` in `src/common/rb_agdc.h`, plus the second
entry's builder; `-rbgpuagdccaps` already armed and already measured to take
(2u6); the prediction is that
`Attempting to get 3-channel gamma table capabilities from plane with no
3-channel gamma table support` changes again. If it does, the count is the
field and `System Gamma` has a chance of leaving `Unknown`. If it does not,
the translation step above is where the next read has to go, and no further
boot should be spent before it.

### 2u9 addendum: built, in `AA4E5167`

`src/common/rb_agdc.h`: `RB_AGDC_GAMMA_SEGMENTS` **1 → 2**, a new
`rb_agdc_gamma_entry2()` carrying Apple's eight fields, and three named
constants — `RB_AGDC_GAMMA_ELEMENTS 0x200`, `RB_AGDC_GAMMA_MIN_F 0x33000000`
(`powf(2,-25)`, exponent 127−25 = 0x66) and `RB_AGDC_GAMMA_MAX_F 0x43000000`
(`powf(2,7)`). The gamma arm of `rb_agdc_extcap` gained the same capacity
guard the degamma arm has always had, so a count of 2 can never be published
into a buffer that fits one. `RB_AGDC_GAMMA_CHANNELS` is **untouched** at 0:
entry 1 keeps its substitute, so the only new values in the reply are Apple's
own literals plus `0 | 0x40`.

Hosttest extended per the standing rule, and **checked to fail when what it
guards is broken**: with `RB_AGDC_GAMMA_ELEMENTS` temporarily 0 it reports
`FAIL AGDC:248: le(g2+0x28,4)==0x200`; restored, `hosttest: all passed`. The
case checks all eight fields of entry 2, re-checks that entry 1 is still entry
1 (format word 0x10, count still the substitute), and checks the refusal at a
one-entry capacity.

Build **`AA4E5167`** (was `43447D39`, so the UUID moved). `kmutil libraries -p`
resolves **0** from `SystemKernelExtensions.kc` and
`grep -c IOGraphicsFamily src/plugin/Info.plist` is **0** — both standing
post-plugin-change checks pass.

The boot needs **no boot-arg change**: `-rbgpuagdccaps` is already in and
already measured to take (2u6). It needs the plugin reinstalled to the EFI,
the one-shots, and the capture taken once WindowServer is up — which
