2w4 - THE KERNEL HALF OF OUR OWN CAPTURE WAS ONE FUNCTION NAME, AND BEHIND IT
      WERE THE DISPLAY GATE AND THE WEDGE
================================================================================
2026-10-27. No boot. Boot 185's window re-queried, 213 lines recovered.

**2w3's FAULT-absence argument was unsound, and this corrects it.** 2w3
concluded that `init_framebuffer_resource` had not failed because its three
FAULT exits were absent from `display-log.txt`. But that capture's kernel
clause was `eventMessage CONTAINS "checkGPUProgress"` - a **literal single
function name** - so no other IOAcceleratorFamily2 message could ever appear
and the absence carried nothing. Rule 26, twice in two milestones: 2w2 lost
eight boots to the log LEVEL, 2w3 nearly lost a conclusion to the
PREDICATE. The reading was right; its control was not.

Re-queried by **sender** over boot 185's window (18:55:59 boot,
18:57:30 the next one; both Darwin banners checked, rule 28) - saved as
`logs/20261027-185657-plugin/kernel-accel-log.txt`:

    senderImagePath CONTAINS "IOAcceleratorFamily2"
      OR senderImagePath CONTAINS "AMDRadeonX6000"

FAULT-level messages persist across a reboot, which is the only reason this
was recoverable at all - INFO ones do not (2w2).

--- 1. `display_change_handler` logs EVERY notification, with its number ----

`IOAccelDisplayPipe::display_change_handler` (`0x14e5cab4`) logs at os_log
type **0x11 = FAULT** on entry and on completion, printing the event, and
calls `IOGraphicsAccelerator2::find_vram_descriptor()` **unconditionally**
before dispatching. Boot 185, 13 notifications:

    18:56:04.974  event 1    DisplayModeWillChange
    18:56:04.974  event 2    DisplayModeDidChange
    18:56:04.975  event 40   OnlineChange
    18:56:04.985  event 1, 2
    18:56:04.991  event 91   WSAAWillExitDefer
    18:56:04.991  event 93   WSAADidExitDefer
    18:56:05.034  event 90   WSAAWillEnterDefer
    18:56:05.034  event 92   WSAADidEnterDefer
    18:56:05.408  event 1, 2
    18:56:05.543  event 91, 93

The numbers are `kIOFBNotify*` from `IOFramebuffer.h` - 40 OnlineChange
(the handler's own `cmpl $0x28` arm confirms it), 90 WSAAWillEnterDefer,
**91 WSAAWillExitDefer**, 92 WSAADidEnterDefer, **93 WSAADidExitDefer**.
So our framebuffer's notification delivery is working, `found_framebuffer`
ran, and `find_vram_descriptor` ran thirteen times with a non-zero
framebuffer count.

(Also found: `find_vram_descriptor`'s call from `found_framebuffer`
(`0x14e21278`) happens **before** `0x108` is incremented, so on the first
framebuffer `getFramebufferCount()` reads 0, the loop body never runs and
`accel->0x180` is left NULL by that call. It is the handler's own calls that
can fill it.)

--- 2. TWO OF THE THREE GATES ARE NOW ELIMINATED --------------------------

**The defer gate (`pipe->0x282`) is OPEN.**
`IOAccelDisplayPipe::wsaaDidExitDefer` (`0x14e5dfe6`) ends
`xorl %eax,%eax; movb %al,0x2ac; movb %al,0x282; movb $0x1,%al` - it zeroes
the byte **unconditionally** and returns true. Event 93 last fired at
**18:56:05.543**, and the submit failures run **18:56:05.516 -> 18:56:07**
and again at **18:56:39** and **18:56:55**. A flag cleared at .543 cannot be
what fails a call at 18:56:55.

**The isActive gate (`pipe->0x298`) is OPEN**, now against a real control:
213 IOAcceleratorFamily2 FAULT lines in the window, from the same thread
(`kernel[0:3a4]`), and **not one** from `init_framebuffer_resource`, whose
every failure exit logs at that level.

**So the gate is `accel->0xc78 & 0x2` - the accelerator-enabled bit** - by
elimination, from the log alone. `enableAccelerator()` is its only setter and
is called only from `IOAccelDisplayMachine::display_mode_did_change`, which
skips it (while still running the per-pipe loop) when **`accel->0x180 == 0`**.

The vendor gate above it is now named too: `display_mode_did_change`'s
`callq *0x870(%rax)` is dump offset 0x880 (rule 7) =
**`AMDRadeonX6000_AMDAccelDisplayMachine::displayModeDidChange()`**
(`0xbe48428`), which returns
`AMDRadeonX6000_AMDAccelDisplayMachine::set_display_mode_and_vram()`. If that
returned false, the pipe loop would be skipped too - and it was not, so it
returned true at least once. Note `machine->0x180` in AMD's code is its own
back-pointer to the accelerator (set in `init`), not the same field.

--- 3. THE WEDGE, NAMED FOR THE FIRST TIME -------------------------------

Starting at **18:56:11.410** - six seconds after the first submit failure -
and repeating every ~5-6 s until 18:56:50:

    (AMDRadeonX6000) channel 52 GFX event timeout;        pending stamps [1..289]
    (AMDRadeonX6000) channel 12 SDMA0_PAGE event timeout; pending stamps [1..191]
    (AMDRadeonX6000) channel 53 SDMA0_PAGE event timeout; pending stamps [1..184]
    (AMDRadeonX6000) channel N is not hung, keep running                     x18
    (IOAcceleratorFamily2) checkGPUProgress - Signaling hardware error on
                           channel 12 / 25 / 52 / 53                         x22
    (IOAcceleratorFamily2) signalHardwareError: GPURestartSignaled /
                           GPURestartEnqueued                            x22 each
    (IOAcceleratorFamily2) hardwareErrorEvent: setting restart type to 2     x22
    (IOAcceleratorFamily2) restart_channel: GPURestartSkipped                x18
    (IOAcceleratorFamily2) restart_channel: no channel associated with
                           stamp_idx N (type 2)                              x18

Work IS submitted - stamps 1..289 on GFX, 1..191 and 1..184 on SDMA0_PAGE -
and **never retires**. The timeout fires, AMD's own hang check answers *"not
hung, keep running"*, the restart path cannot find the channel for the stamp
and skips, and the whole cycle repeats. That is the wedge, and it is a
**stamp-retirement** failure, not a display one: it begins **after** the
display-pipe failures, not before.

Also new and unexplained: **`IOAccelSurface::set_id_mode(uint32_t,
uint32_t): Surface mode contains bad bits`**, four times at 18:56:05.034 -
in the same 1 ms as WSAAWillEnterDefer, and ~0.5 s before the first submit
failure.

--- 4. INSTRUMENT FIXED ---------------------------------------------------

`tools/plugin_check.sh`'s `dl_pred` now matches by **sender**
(`IOAcceleratorFamily2`, `AMDRadeonX6000`) instead of one function name, and
the summary prints the kernel-line count plus a `display_change_handler`
count, with a WARNING when the kernel count is zero against a non-zero
total. `display_change_handler` logs once per notification unconditionally,
so it is a genuine known-present control for the kernel half - the same
shape rule 26 asks for, applied to a predicate rather than a level.

2w5 - BOOT 186: THE PROBE NEVER RAN, AND THE TWO ELIMINATIONS RECONFIRMED
================================================================================
2026-10-27, logs/20261027-230204-plugin, boot 186, armed, captured at +3m21s.

Identity first (rules 8/15/33/34): `rbgpu-boot` **186** (new), `armed 1`,
`agdc_oneshot 0`, `iop_oneshot 0`, `diag_used` **564** of 768 so absences are
informative, boot 22:58:45 and the capture at 23:02:04 - **and the loaded
plugin is `D8B1115C`**, the build that carries the probe, with
`-rbgpuaccelprobe` present in boot-args (token 49).

**AND NOT ONE `ax*` KEY EXISTS.** Not even `ax_say`, which
`rbgpu_accelprobe_start()` writes unconditionally once the arg check passes.
The cause is the **call site**, not the probe: 2w3 added
`rbgpu_accelprobe_start()` next to `rbgpu_heartbeat_start()` in
`kern_start.cpp` because a grep found that name, and never read what gates
it -

    if (stage >= 40) {
        ...
        if (checkKernelArgument("-rbgpubeat")) {
            rbgpu_heartbeat_start();
            rbgpu_accelprobe_start();      <-- 2w3 put it here
        }
    }

`-rbgpubeat` has not been in boot-args since 2fg answered its question, so
the branch is dead. Rule 16 applied to a probe's own call site: **a probe
needs a call site that runs whenever ITS arg is set, not one borrowed from a
neighbour.** Moved to `RembrandtGPUPeer.cpp` immediately after
`rbgpu_diag_set_num("armed", ...)`, which runs in the peer's `start()` on
every boot; build **`D69D9B33`**.

2w7 - BOOT 188: THE PROBE ANSWERS, AND IT REFUTES 2w4/2w5. THE GATE IS
      `pipe->0x298`, AND 2w3 MISCOUNTED THE EXITS.
================================================================================
2026-10-27, logs/20261027-232901-plugin, boot 188, armed.

Identity: `rbgpu-boot` **188**, `armed 1`, `agdc_oneshot 0`, `iop_oneshot 0`,
`agdc_error 0`, `diag_used` **613** of 768. The capture is **incomplete** -
six files, no `kexts.txt` and no `display-log.txt`, because the box rebooted
~40 s into `plugin_check.sh` - but rule 15 is satisfied another way: the
`ax*` keys exist at all, and **only build `D69D9B33` can produce them**. The
hot-key ordering also paid off: `ax0_*` and `ax2_*` both survived into the
512-byte note.

**ALL THREE SAMPLES AGREE, 25 / 45 / 75 s:**

    ax{0,1,2}_enabled   1        accel->0xc78 & 0x2  -- SET
    ax{0,1,2}_flags     2
    ax{0,1,2}_vram      1        accel->0x180        -- non-NULL
    ax{0,1,2}_vmap      1        accel->0x188        -- non-NULL
    ax{0,1,2}_defer     0        pipe->0x282
    ax{0,1,2}_active    0        pipe->0x298         -- CLEAR
    ax{0,1,2}_b280      0
    ax{0,1,2}_b299      0
    ax{0,1,2}_gate      3        "pipe NOT active (0x298)"
    ax{0,1,2}_fbs       1        machine->0x108
    ax{0,1,2}_n         1        one IOGraphicsAccelerator2
    ax{0,1,2}_via       1        matched by the BASE class name
    ax{0,1,2}_size      8168     accelerator getClassSize()
    ax{0,1,2}_dmsize    408      display machine
    ax{0,1,2}_dpsize    15216    display pipe

**SO 2w4/2w5's ELIMINATION OF `pipe->0x298` IS REFUTED, AND THE
ACCELERATOR-ENABLED BIT IS ELIMINATED INSTEAD.** Exactly the opposite of two
milestones of deduction. `enabled 1` with `vram 1` and `vmap 1` is three
fields agreeing - `enableAccelerator()` is called only when
`accel->0x180 != 0`, and both are what they must be - so the pointer chain is
right and the reading is sound.

**WHY THE DEDUCTION FAILED: 2w3 MISCOUNTED `init_framebuffer_resource`'s
EXITS.** It claimed three failure exits, all logging at os_log type 0x11 =
FAULT, and three boots of FAULT-absence were then read as "it succeeded".
`IOAccelDisplayPipe::init_framebuffer_resource` (`0x14e5d7ca`) actually has
**five**, and **two are silent**:

    0x14e5d836  fb->vt[0x9f0]() != 0        -> xorl %r15d; jmp exit   SILENT
    0x14e5d866  fb->vt[0x9e8]() != 0        -> FAULT (fmt)
    0x14e5d94b  bitsPerPixel switch gave 0  -> FAULT (fmt_0, fmt_1)
    0x14e5d9d9  pipe->vt[0x858](0, res) ==0 -> je exit, r15 already 0 SILENT
    0x14e5da45  res->vt[0x170]() == false   -> FAULT (fmt_2)

Rule 14's sharper form: **the absence of a log is informative only once every
exit has been enumerated.** Three boots were spent on an enumeration that was
short by two.

The first silent exit is `getCurrentDisplayMode` and **ours returns
`kIOReturnSuccess`** (`RBAMDFramebuffer.cpp:515`), so it is not that one.

**THE SECOND SILENT EXIT IS THE VENDOR HOOK.** Call offset `0x858` = dump
`0x868` (rule 7) = `IOAccelDisplayPipe::initFramebufferResource(unsigned int,
IOAccelResource2*)`, and the live class overrides it:
**`AMDRadeonX6000_AMDAccelDisplayPipe::initFramebufferResource`**
(`0xbe49356`). It returns 0 - silently, every time - on any of:

    resource == NULL
    pipe->getFramebuffer() == NULL          (= pipe->0x98; ours, non-NULL)
    index != 0
    pipe->0x340 == 0        after  pipe->0x330->vt[0x138](fbIndex, index,
    pipe->0x348 == 0                        &pipe->0x340, resource)
    pipe->0x35f != 1        on the alternate branch
    pipe->0x380 == 0        the value it returns

`pipe->0x330->vt[0x138](...)` is the one that writes `0x340` and `0x348` -
an address and a size - and is the next thing to read.

**WHAT IS NOW FIXED, NOT INFERRED:** the accelerator is enabled, its VRAM
descriptor exists and its map succeeded, so `getVRAMRange()` and everything
built on it are **correct** and `find_vram_descriptor` is off the list. The
failure is one level down, inside AMD's own `initFramebufferResource`, and it
is silent by construction.

## 2w9 — boot 189: the accelerator reads two properties off the framebuffer, and we publish neither

Capture `logs/20261027-233944-plugin`, build `C025F308`, `rbgpu-boot` 189.

Arm verified first (rules 8/15/34): `rbgpu-boot` 189 (was 188), `kexts.txt`
shows `com.rembrandtgpu.plugin ... C025F308-4D1D-3329-BF0E-35696F851631`
matching `build/out`, `agdc_oneshot 0`, `iop_oneshot 0`, `agdc_error 0`,
`armed 1`, `diag_used` **658** of 768 — so absences are informative.
`ax_say` present, and all three samples (25/45/75 s) are byte-identical.

### What the probe measured

    ax0_w / h / bpp / fmt   1920 / 1080 / 4 / 4   getPixelInformation SUCCEEDED
    ax0_pfb                 1                     pipe->0x98 (getFramebuffer) non-NULL
    ax0_pres                1
    ax0_hw328 / hw330       1 / 1                 Navi21Hardware -> HWDisplay chain up
    ax0_b35e / b35f         1 / 1
    ax0_fi348               8294400               = 1920 * 1080 * 4 EXACTLY
    ax0_fi340               0                     *** the address is ZERO ***
    ax0_fi34c               0
    ax0_enabled / defer     1 / 0                 both still eliminated
    ax0_active / gate       0 / 3                 "pipe NOT active (0x298)"

Display log (4417 lines, 461 `[INFO]`, 599 kernel, 26 `display_change_handler`
as the kernel-half control): `Failed to submit transaction` **140**, all
`IOReturn: 0x2d8`, `Fallback` 69, `init_framebuffer_resource` 0, `no gamma` 0,
`event timeout` 41, `bad bits` 4.

So the base's half of the work is **done and correct** — 1920/1080/4/4 is
`getPixelInformation` answering properly — and the failure is unambiguously
inside AMD's hook, as 2w8 predicted.

### The chain, read end to end (no boot spent)

2w7 said `configureDisplay` must fill `0x340`/`0x348`. **That is corrected.**
`AMDRadeonX6000_AMDHWDisplay::configureDisplay` (`0xbe87bd4`) *is* the real
target of call slot `0x138` (rule 7: dump `0x148`), but it **never touches its
`_FRAMEBUFFER_INFO*` argument** — `%rcx` is clobbered at `0xbe87c34`, and the
`%rbx` it writes `0x1b4`/`0x1b9`/`0x1ba`/`0x1bd`/`0x1dc` into is the
**`IOAccelResource2`**, the fifth argument. The filler is one slot earlier.

`AMDRadeonX6000_AMDAccelDisplayMachine::set_display_mode_and_vram`
(`0xbe48604`), the vendor gate 2w4 named, per pipe:

    r13   = pipe + 0x340                       *** the _FRAMEBUFFER_INFO IS &pipe->0x340
    0x35d = hwd->vt[0x128](i, fb)              = isDisplayEnabled
    ok    = hwd->vt[0x130](i, 0x35d, 1, fb, r13)  = getDisplayInfo
            pipe->initAffineTransform()
    if (!ok)                     fail          (0xbe4870e)
    if (pipe->0x35d != 1)        fail          (0xbe4871c)
    if (pipe->0x340 == 0)        fail          (0xbe48727)

where `hwd` is `machine->0x188`. Rule 7 on `AMDRadeonX6000_AMDHWDisplay`'s
vtable: call `0x128` → dump `0x138` = `isDisplayEnabled(unsigned int, void*)`;
call `0x130` → dump `0x140` =
`getDisplayInfo(unsigned int, bool, bool, void*, _FRAMEBUFFER_INFO*)` — a
signature that matches the five registers exactly.

**`getDisplayInfo` (`0xbe8700e`) fills the struct from two registry properties
on the framebuffer.** It zeroes `info+0x00/08/10/18/1e` at entry
(`0xbe870bf`), then:

    0xbe87192  rax = fb->vt[0x2b8]("ATY,fb_offset")        getProperty
    0xbe871bb  rax = OSMetaClassBase::safeMetaCast(rax, <class>)
    0xbe871cb  rax = rax->vt[0x178]()                      getBytesNoCopy
    0xbe871d9  *(uint64_t *)(info + 0x00) = *(uint64_t *)rax

    0xbe871e9  rax = fb->vt[0x2b8]("ATY,fb_size")
    0xbe8720c  rax = rax->vt[0x178]()
    0xbe87219  *(uint32_t *)(info + 0x0c) = *(uint32_t *)rax

    0xbe8722b  r13 = fb->vt[0x9a8](0)      0xbe87240  r12 = fb->vt[0x9b0]()
    0xbe87257  if (r13 && r12) info+0x1e = 1

`0x9b0` is `getVRAMRange` (2pq's slot), so the aperture/VRAM pair is read here
too and both of ours are non-NULL (boot 188's `ax_vram`/`ax_vmap` = 1/1).

**And the second property gates `0x35d` as well.** `isDisplayEnabled`
(`0xbe86f9c`) in full:

```c
bool AMDHWDisplay::isDisplayEnabled(unsigned int idx, void *fb) {
    if (this->0x58 <= idx) return false;            // 0xbe86f9f
    bool a = this->vt[0x248]();
    if (a || !fb) return a;                         // 0xbe86fbb
    OSData *d = OSDynamicCast(OSData, fb->getProperty("ATY,fb_size"));
    if (!d) return false;                           // 0xbe86fe5
    void *p = d->getBytesNoCopy();
    if (!p) return false;                           // 0xbe86ff6
    return *(uint64_t *)p != 0;                     // 0xbe86ff8
}
```

**So both properties are hard gates and both values must be NON-ZERO.**

### `fb_offset` is an OFFSET, not an address

`AMDRadeonX6000_AMDAccelDisplayPipe::initFramebufferResource` (`0xbe49356`),
on the path past the two checks:

    0xbe49424  rdi = pipe->0x328
    0xbe4942b  r12 = pipe->0x340
    0xbe49435  rax = rdi->vt[0x2d8]()         = hw->0x370
    0xbe49441  rax = rax->vt[0x1e0]()         = mem->0x50
    0xbe49447  r12 += rax                     *** a BASE is added ***
    0xbe49456  reserveFrameBuffer(pipe, r12, max(0x34c, 0x348), resource)

`pipe->0x328 = accel->0x1a38` (`0xbe49051`, in
`AMDAccelDisplayPipe::init`), and `accel->0x1a38` is built by
`AMDGraphicsAccelerator::createHWInterface` → `vt[0xb48]` →
`AMDNavi21GraphicsAccelerator::newHWInterface` (`0xbe82fda`) →
`new AMDRadeonX6000_AMDNavi21Hardware` (size `0x20850`). Its `vt[0x2d8]`
returns `hw->0x370` and its `vt[0x2f8]` returns `hw->0x398` — which is
`pipe->0x330`, the HWDisplay, closing that loop. `hw->0x370`'s `vt[0x1e0]`
returns `mem->0x50` (the accessor at `0xbe9aae2`, inside
`AMDGFX10HWMemory`'s table), the VRAM base.

So `ATY,fb_offset` is a **byte offset relative to the VRAM base**, and
`max(info+0x08, info+0x0c)` is the length reserved — `info+0x08` is already
correct at 8294400, so `ATY,fb_size` is belt-and-braces for the length and
load-bearing only for `isDisplayEnabled`.

### We publish neither, and the control is valid

`grep -c ATY framebuffer.plist` = **0**, against a control in the same file:
`IOFBMemorySize`, `IOFBGammaCount` and the whole `RBFB*` family are present
(rule 26 — the first version of this check had no control and proved nothing).
`ax0_fi340 = 0` and `ax0_fi34c = 0` are **exactly those two absences
agreeing** — two fields, one cause.

Counted with a control across the extracted kexts (`ATY,SurfInfo` present in
`AMDSupport`, absent in `AMDFramebuffer`):

| kext | `ATY,fb_offset` | `ATY,fb_size` | role |
|---|---|---|---|
| `AMDFramebuffer` | 1 | 1 | producer |
| `AMDRadeonX6000Framebuffer` | 1 | 1 | producer |
| `AMDRadeonX6000` | 1 | 1 | consumer |
| `AMDSupport` | 0 | 0 | — |
| `IOGraphicsFamily` | 0 | 0 | — |
| `IONDRVSupport` | 0 | 0 | — |

**Neither string exists in `IOGraphicsFamily` or `IONDRVSupport`**, so the
`IONDRVFramebuffer` desktop could never have obtained a hardware display pipe
either. That is an independent corroboration from the opposite direction, and
it retires the long-standing puzzle of why the software compositor was never
one flag away.

`AMDFramebuffer` publishes them in `initializeSetDisplayMode` (`0x2a34e0`) and
`resetDriverModeParameters` (`0x2afa10`) via `vt[0x288]` =
`setProperty(key, bytes, length)` with **`ecx = 8`** for both:
`&this->0x7e0` for the offset, and for the size
`(this->0x800 ? this->0x800 : this->0x818)` where
`this->0x818 = this->0x850 * this->0x870`.

**The class is `OSData`, established from the use and not from the GOT**: the
consumer calls `vt[0x178]` and then *dereferences* the result, which is
`getBytesNoCopy()` returning a pointer. An `OSNumber` would have returned the
value itself. Rule 13's habit applied to a type.

### The change, and the one thing it deliberately gets wrong

Build **`59124B3A`** (fbkext) publishes both as 8-byte `OSData` behind
`-rbgpufbaty`, offset defaulting to **16 MB** and tunable with
`rbgpufbatymb=<1-3072>` (refusal publishes the refused value, rule 19). Rule 30:
`-rbgpufbaty` neither prefixes nor is prefixed by `-rbgpufbvbl`,
`-rbgpufbvram`, `-rbgpufbvramrange`, `-rbgpufbaccel`, `-rbgpufbmatch` or
`-rbgpufbnocrumb`.

**The truthful offset is 0 and 0 cannot be used.** Our scanout *is* at VRAM
offset 0 — the GOP framebuffer is BAR0 offset 0 (2pr) and the aperture is
`withSubRange(bar0, 0, kApertureBytes)` — but the gate is
`cmpq $0x0, (%r15); je fail`, so an offset of 0 is indistinguishable from the
property being absent, and AMD's own driver never puts the scanout there.

**So state the expected outcome before the boot**: the display engine keeps
scanning offset 0 while the compositor is told the framebuffer lives at 16 MB.
If the chain works, the pipe goes **ACTIVE** and the panel shows a **stale or
wrong image**. That is a working PIPE with a wrong IMAGE, and it is the point
of the boot — SSH and the probe are the instruments, not the screen. Nothing
is written to the display engine, so this cannot wedge DCN; it is reversible by
removing one boot-arg. Pointing the scanout at the same offset means writing
the DCN 3.1.2 primary-surface registers, which this kext has never done, and is
a separate and much narrower step **once the chain is proven**.

Also added: `ax*_b35d`. `pipe->0x35d` was never probed and is now known to be
a gate; it is `1` iff `ATY,fb_size` is published non-zero, so it separates
"the property landed" from "it did not" without inference.

Plugin build **`64D3D687`**. `SystemKernelExtensions.kc` count 0,
`IOGraphicsFamily` in the plugin's `Info.plist` 0.

### Predictions for boot 190, written down first

- `ax0_b35d` **1** (was unread; 0 would mean the property did not land)
- `ax0_fi340` **0x1000000** (16 MB), `ax0_fi34c` **8294400**
- `ax0_active` **1**, `ax0_gate` **0**, `ax0_say` "ALL THREE OPEN"
- `Failed to submit transaction` / `IOReturn: 0x2d8` → **0**
- `fb_vbl_ot_armed` **present for the first time** — a transaction finally queued
- `RBFBAtyArmed Yes`, `RBFBAtyOffset 16777216` in `ioreg -rl -c RBAMDFramebuffer`
- the screen wrong or stale, by construction

If `b35d` is 1 and `fi340` is 0x1000000 but `active` is still 0, the remaining
suspects are `index != 0` and `reserveFrameBuffer` failing, both inside
`initFramebufferResource`, and `r380` names which.

## 2wa — boot 190: the fbkext never changed, and `ATY,fb_size` is NOT a gate here

Capture `logs/20261028-001439-plugin`, `rbgpu-boot` **190**, armed, both
one-shots **0**, `diag_used` **662**/768, 21 files (the capture completed).

### Rule 15 failed, on the second kext

    plugin   64D3D687-62CB-3D4C-BE3F-B9541E2E1E4F   = build/out   CORRECT
    fb       45588775-2890-3382-A5FE-BBFB108B49B2   build/out has 59124B3A   STALE

`-rbgpufbaty` **was** in boot-args, and the framebuffer properties are absent:

    ATY,fb_offset   absent        IOFBMemorySize   PRESENT   (control)
    ATY,fb_size     absent        RBFBCrumbOn      PRESENT   (control)
    RBFBAtyArmed    absent        VRAM,totalMB     PRESENT   (control)

**`RBFBAtyArmed` is published unconditionally by the new code** — outside the
`if (atyOn)` — so its absence establishes the old binary independently of the
UUID. Two-way confirmation, which is what rule 15 is for.

**Why it was stale, and it is not `fbload.sh`.** `fbload.sh` does
`rm -rf "$stage"; cp -R "$src" "$stage/"` every run, so it always stages the
current build. The kext that **owns the panel** comes up at boot from the
**auxiliary collection**, i.e. from an **installed** copy:

    /Library/Extensions/RBAMDFramebuffer.kext/Contents/MacOS/RBAMDFramebuffer
        UUID 45588775-2890-3382-A5FE-BBFB108B49B2

Rebuilding `build/out` never touches it. **This is 2w6's lesson repeated for
the second kext, and 2w9's handoff contained the same omission it was written
to fix**: it listed `sudo tools/efi.sh install` for the plugin and said nothing
about refreshing the installed framebuffer. An install is the user's step, so
the handoff has to *name* it. Generalised in rule 15: **every artifact a boot
loads has its own install path, and a rebuild refreshes none of them.**

### What the boot did buy: `ax0_b35d = 1`

All three samples identical and, apart from the new key, byte-identical to
boot 189's — a clean control on the probe extension itself, since the plugin
changed and no reading moved:

    ax0_b35d   1        *** NEW ***
    ax0_fi340  0        ax0_fi34c 0        ax0_active 0        ax0_gate 3
    IOReturn: 0x2d8  148      Fallback 73      init_framebuffer_resource 0
    display_change_handler 26 (control)       [INFO] 483

**`pipe->0x35d` is 1 with `ATY,fb_size` absent, which 2w9 predicted was
impossible.** The reason is the early-out this journal quoted and then
reasoned past:

```c
bool isDisplayEnabled(unsigned int idx, void *fb) {
    bool a = this->vt[0x248]();
    if (a || !fb) return a;              // 0xbe86fbb  <-- taken
    ... the ATY,fb_size read ...
}
```

`vt[0x248]` (rule 7: dump `0x258`) is
**`AMDRadeonX6000_AMDDCNDisplay::isDisplayControlEnabled(unsigned int)`**
(`0xbec012e`), and it is a **live register read**, 17 instructions:

    0xbec0137  rdi = this->0x28                  the register accessor
    0xbec0141  esi = this->0x5c0 + 0x38 * idx    the register id
    0xbec014b  eax = rdi->vt[0x118](id)          vt[0x118] = READ (2fd/2fg)
    0xbec0151  return (eax & this->0x6f0) != 0

So the **firmware-lit panel satisfies this gate for free** — OTG0 is already
running here (`OTG0_CONTROL = 0x00011201`, master enable set). It is the
hardware answering, not a property of ours.

**2w9 IS CORRECTED: `ATY,fb_size` is not a gate on this machine.** It still
feeds `info+0x0c`, but `initFramebufferResource` reserves
`max(info+0x08, info+0x0c)` and `info+0x08` is already 8294400, so it is
optional. **Only `ATY,fb_offset` is load-bearing**, and `pipe->0x340 == 0`
remains the single fatal check. The fix narrows rather than changes: publish
both (harmless and consistent), but the one that matters is the offset.

That is the fifth time a correct disassembly was attached one link off, and
the second time in two milestones that the probe caught it. The pattern is
specific enough to name: **when a function has an early-out above the branch
you care about, read what makes the early-out fire before claiming the branch
is reachable.** 2w9 had the instruction (`if (a || !fb) return a;`) in its own
quoted listing and still called both properties hard gates.

### Boot 191 — no new build needed

`build/out` already holds fbkext `59124B3A` and plugin `64D3D687`. The
framebuffer kext has to be **installed**, which is the user's step. Predictions
are 2w9's, minus `b35d` (already 1, and now known to come from the hardware):

- `RBFBAtyArmed Yes`, `RBFBAtyOffset 16777216` in `ioreg -rl -c RBAMDFramebuffer`
- `ax0_fi340` **16777216**, `ax0_fi34c` **8294400**
- `ax0_active` **1**, `ax0_gate` **0**
- `IOReturn: 0x2d8` → **0**, `fb_vbl_ot_armed` present for the first time
- the picture wrong or stale, by construction (the scanout still reads offset 0)

### 2wa addendum — the AuxKC rebuild ERRORED and SUCCEEDED, and 2sy's KDK claim is refuted

`sudo kmutil create -n aux -z --volume-root /` printed:

```
No variant specified, falling back to release
Error Domain=KMErrorDomain Code=34 "Missing Developer Kit: As of macOS 13.0,
you will need to install a KDK matching your build 24H32 to rebuild kernel
collections."
```

**2sy's "The AuxKC alone needs none" is wrong on this machine** — `-n aux` is
demanded a KDK too, and `/Library/Developer/KDKs` is still empty. (`kmutil
create` does carry `--allow-missing-kdk` and `--kdk`; neither was needed.)

**But the collection was rebuilt anyway.** Read from the artifact instead of
the exit status:

    /Library/Extensions/...RBAMDFramebuffer   UUID 59124B3A   (the new build)
    AuxKC mtime                               00:21:25
    installed bundle mtime                    00:21:15        -- 10 s earlier

and searching the 18 694 144-byte
`/Library/KernelCollections/AuxiliaryKernelExtensions.kc` for the raw UUID
bytes, with controls:

    NEW 59124B3A   1 occurrence      com.rembrandtgpu.fb    5   (control)
    OLD 45588775   0 occurrences     com.nullmoth          22   (control)

    1  /Library/Extensions/RBAMDFramebuffer.kext
    0  /private/var/tmp/RBAMDFramebuffer.stage
    0  RBAMDFramebufferBeside
    1  /Library/Extensions/NVRMFB.kext                          (control)

So the collection carries **exactly one** copy of our bundle, the installed
displacing one, the old build is **gone**, the staged `beside` copy 2sp said to
remove first is **not present**, and the user's nullmoth RTX driver survived
the rewrite. Which agent did it is **not established** — either
`kernelmanagerd` auto-rebuilt on the `/Library/Extensions` change (2sp's
option 1, which is also how `45588775` got in, since `kmutil` never once
succeeded) or `kmutil create` wrote the aux collection and then failed on a
different variant. The timestamps fit both.

**The reusable form, and it is the inverse of 2so's.** 2so recorded that a
tool's *exit code can be its verdict* — `make useiop && …` reported failure
under a perfectly good report. This is the mirror: **a loud, specific,
correct-sounding error can sit on top of a write that landed.** Verify the
artifact, never the exit status, in both directions. Rule 26 gains the
sentence; the instrument here was a raw-byte search of the collection with
four controls, which took one command.

So **no further install step is needed** — arm and reboot.

## 2wb — BOOT 191: THE PIPE GOES ACTIVE, AND TRANSACTIONS FLOW FOR THE FIRST TIME

Capture `logs/20261028-002545-plugin`, `rbgpu-boot` **191**, armed, both
one-shots **0**, `diag_used` **661**/768. Only 6 files — the box was rebooted
at 00:26:17, ~52 s into `plugin_check.sh`, so there is no `display-log.txt`
and no `kexts.txt`. Both gaps were recovered; see below.

### Rule 15, satisfied without `kexts.txt`

`framebuffer.plist` carries `RBFBAtyArmed = True`, and that key is published
**unconditionally** by the 2w9 code, outside the `if (atyOn)`. Only build
`59124B3A` can produce it. 2wa's own prescription, used in anger one boot
later. The raw property bytes are right too:

    ATY,fb_offset  00 00 00 01 00 00 00 00   = 0x0000000001000000 = 16777216
    ATY,fb_size    00 90 7e 00 00 00 00 00   = 0x00000000007e9000 =  8294400

eight bytes each, little-endian, exactly the `OSData` shape `getDisplayInfo`
dereferences.

### The gate is OPEN. All three samples, 25/45/75 s, identical:

    ax0_fi340   16777216   *** was 0 ***        ax0_b35d   1
    ax0_fi348    8294400                        ax0_b35e   1
    ax0_fi34c    8294400   *** was 0 ***        ax0_b35f   1
    ax0_r380           1   *** was 0 ***        ax0_enabled 1
    ax0_active         1   *** was 0 ***        ax0_defer   0
    ax0_gate           0   *** was 3 ***
    ax0_say   "ALL THREE OPEN - NotReady is elsewhere"

`r380 = 1` is `initFramebufferResource`'s own return value, so it did not take
any of its seven silent zero-exits; `active = 1` is `pipe->0x298`, which only
`init_framebuffer_resource` writes. **`IOAccelDisplayPipe::isActive()` is true
for the first time in this project.** Every prediction written down in 2w9 and
2wa landed.

### The submit failures COLLAPSED, measured at a level that survives a reboot

The live machine is **not** boot 191 (rule 33): `kern.boottime` 00:26:17 vs the
capture's 00:24:16, different `kern.bootsessionuuid`, and `rbgpu-boot` still
reads 191 because the following boot was unarmed. So INFO is gone — which means
**`Failed to submit transaction` / `IOReturn: 0x2d8` reading 0 is NOT a
result** (rule 14/36: that message is INFO-level, 2w2). `Fallback ... submission
failed` is **ERROR**, and 2w2 established that ERROR persists by recovering boot
184's 56-line control after a reboot. Re-queried by sender over
00:24:10-00:26:17, one pid (`WindowServer[162]`), 596 lines:

| | boot 189 | boot 190 | **boot 191** |
|---|---|---|---|
| `Fallback ... submission failed` | 69 | 73 | **3** |
| `display_change_handler` (control) | 26 | 26 | **26** |
| `init_framebuffer_resource` | 0 | 0 | 0 |

And the three are not scattered — they are at **00:24:23.762, .766 and .849**,
inside 90 ms, at the same instant as the **last** `display_change_handler`
(00:24:23.762484). After 00:24:23.857 CoreDisplay says nothing further for the
remaining **113 seconds** of the boot. That is the shape of "it failed until
the pipe went active, then stopped", not of a count that happened to be low.

### THE NEW FRONTIER, AND IT IS PAST EVERYTHING WE HAVE EVER REACHED

113 lines after 00:24:24, two messages, **122 occurrences each** across the
boot, from 00:24:23.734 to 00:25:25.045 — a full minute:

```
IOAccelDisplayPipeTransaction2::set_transaction_args(sIOAccelDisplayPipeTransactionArgs *)
    returning error 0xe00002c7 for transaction(N).
AMDRadeonAccelerator [0]: transaction ID (N) generated error (0xe00002c7).
    dirtyBits=0x3c1, options=0x801
```

`0xe00002c7` is **`kIOReturnUnsupported`** (`IOReturn.h:109` on this machine;
`0x2d8` on line 126 is the old `kIOReturnNotReady`, for contrast).
`options` is `0x801` ×120 and `0x800` ×2; `dirtyBits` is `0x3c1` throughout.

**Transactions are being created, numbered and handed to the kernel.** Since
2s9 (boot 168) every milestone has recorded `fb_vbl_ot_armed` absent and "no
transaction has EVER been queued" — across boots 168, 171, 177-191. That
statement is now **false**, and the thing that changed is one 8-byte registry
property. It also explains the other new reading in this capture:
**`RBFBVBL1Fires = 1`**, where 2w0 measured Apple's handler 1 registered,
disabled and at **0 fires** over 375 s. `transaction_queue_gated` →
`enableTransactionInterrupt` → `enableVBLInterrupt` (2s5) fired at last.

**Rule 13 applies before anything is built on `kIOReturnUnsupported`**: a named
constant says what the NAME means, not what the function meant by it, and this
project has already been burned by precisely this code — request 0x1B's
*success* path returns `kIOReturnUnsupported` (2ha). `set_transaction_args`
must be disassembled before a single line is written against it.

### What has NOT changed

The wedge is intact and unexplained: 22 `event timeout`, 33 `checkGPUProgress`
hardware-error signals, 22 `no channel associated with stamp_idx`, 22 `channel
N is not hung, keep running`. First `event timeout` at 00:24:29.6, still
~6 s after the display activity. `bad bits` still 4. Whether it is a
consequence of the display path or an independent second defect remains
**not established** — but it now has a competitor for the frontier.

### Not measured

What the screen showed. By construction it should be wrong or stale: the
compositor was told the framebuffer is at VRAM offset 16 MB while OTG0 still
scans offset 0. The user rebooted two minutes in, which is consistent with a
bad picture but does not establish one.

### Next

Disassemble `IOAccelDisplayPipeTransaction2::set_transaction_args` in
`IOAcceleratorFamily2` and find every path returning `kIOReturnUnsupported`,
with `dirtyBits = 0x3c1` and `options = 0x801` as the measured inputs. No boot
needed for that. Rule 35: if the chain ends at our own code again, instrument

## 2wc — `kIOReturnUnsupported` IS ONE FRAMEBUFFER ATTRIBUTE WE NEVER ANSWERED

Static read, no boot. 2wb's frontier is closed, and the defect is in our own
kext.

### The chain, end to end

`IOAccelDisplayPipeTransaction2::set_transaction_args` (`0x14e5ea68`,
`IOAcceleratorFamily2`) is 0xae8 bytes with **one** `retq` returning `%r14d`.
Three writers reach it: the literals `0xe00002c2` (`0x14e5f0df`) and
`0xe00002bd` (`0x14e5f11f`), each after its own `os_log` at type `0x11`, and

    14e5f4b5  rdi = this->0x28                  /* the IOAccelDisplayPipe   */
    14e5f4bf  callq *0x8a0(%rax)                /* pipe->vt[0x8a0](this)    */
    14e5f4c5  if (eax == 0) -> r14 = 0, return  /* 14e5f4ff                 */
    14e5f4c9  r14 = eax
              log "%s returning error 0x%x for transaction(%d).\n"
              return r14

so that call is the **only** site in the function that can return an arbitrary
code, and the message we measured 122 times is its own. Rule 7: call `0x8a0`
→ dump `0x8b0` = `IOAccelDisplayPipe::validateTransaction`, whose base is
`xorl %eax,%eax; ret` (`0x14e61146`) — the slot above it,
`IOAccelDisplayPipe::performTransaction` (`0x14e6114e`), is
`movl $0xe00002c7,%eax; ret` unconditionally, which is worth knowing because
it is the kext's own idiom for "not implemented".

The override is `AMDRadeonX6000_AMDAccelDisplayPipe::validateTransaction`
(`0xbe49a9e`): a kdebug-signposted wrapper (`0x85ad2009` before,
`0x85ad200a` after) around

    AMDRadeonX6000_AMDAccelDisplayPipe::executeTransaction(txn, false)

(`0xbe49b54`, 0xc40 bytes), and it returns that call's value unchanged.

### The sixth `kIOReturnUnsupported`, and why a grep could not see it

`executeTransaction` has **five literal** `movl $0xe00002c7` sites —
`0xbe49c40`, `0xbe49f99`, `0xbe4a17a`, `0xbe4a34a`, `0xbe4a47e` — and a
**sixth** that the assembler writes as arithmetic:

    be49b87  r13 = this->getFramebufferIndex()            /* 0x14e5d52c */
    be49b94  al  = this->0x330->vt[0x190](r13)
    be49b9d  if (txn == NULL) -> be49c78
    be49ba5  if (!al)         -> be49c78
    ...
    be49c78  xorl %eax,%eax; testq %r14,%r14; setne %al
    be49c80  leal (%rax,%rax,4), %r12d
    be49c84  addl $0xe00002c2, %r12d       /* 0x2c2 + 5 == 0x2c7 */

`0xe00002c2` is `kIOReturnBadArgument` and `0xe00002c2 + 5` is
`0xe00002c7` = `kIOReturnUnsupported`. So **a non-NULL transaction whose
`vt[0x190]` answers false gets kIOReturnUnsupported on the function's first
test, before a single dirty bit is looked at.** `grep -n '2c7'` over the
disassembly returns five sites and misses this one — **rule 26 again, and the
sixth recorded instance**: a constant can be a sum.

### Enumerating the other five against the measured inputs

Boot 191 measured `dirtyBits = 0x3c1` and `options = 0x801`, and
`validateTransaction` passes the `bool` as **0**. `0x3c1` is bits 0, 6, 7, 8,
9. With `r12 = txn->getTransactionDirtyBits()` (`0x14e608fa`) and
`txn->getTransactionOptions()` (`0x14e60904`):

| site | guard | with 0x3c1 |
|---|---|---|
| `0xbe49c40` | `dirtyBits == 0x100` exactly, then `getPlaneResource(0,0)` NULL | not taken |
| `0xbe49f99` | `dirtyBits & 0x4`, `getPlaneGammaTable(0)` count > 0x100 | bit clear |
| `0xbe4a17a` | `dirtyBits & 0x20`, `getPipePreGammaTable()` count > 0x100 | bit clear |
| `0xbe4a34a` | `dirtyBits & 0x80`, **`getPipePostGammaTable()` count > 0x100** | **live** |
| `0xbe4a47e` | `dirtyBits & 0x400`, `getPipePostCSCGammaVID()` size/cid | bit clear |

Every count check is `cmpl $0x100, %r13d; ja`, i.e. **AMD refuses a gamma
table of more than 256 entries**, with `r13 = IOAccelDisplayPipeGammaTable2::
getTableCount()` (`0x14e62a92`). That made the post-gamma ceiling a real
candidate, and the capture settles it: counting the LUT CoreDisplay actually
submits in boot 190's dumps gives **71 of 256 entries and 2 of 1024**, and in
boot 189's **67 and 2**. A ceiling that two submissions in seventy-three
cross cannot produce 122 failures out of 122. (A `sort -u` of those lines had
shown both sizes and nothing else, which read as "1024 is what it sends" —
rule 26: a de-duplicated list is not a count.)

So the live candidate is the unconditional one.

### `vt[0x190]`, and the one thing that writes it

`pipe->0x330` is the HWDisplay (2w9). Rule 7: call `0x190` → dump `0x1a0`, in
both `__ZTV27AMDRadeonX6000_AMDHWDisplay` and
`__ZTV28AMDRadeonX6000_AMDDCNDisplay`; the control that fixes those tables'
alignment is dump `0x258` = `AMDDCNDisplay::isDisplayControlEnabled`
(`0xbec012e`), exactly where 2wa found it, and dump `0x138` =
`isDisplayEnabled`, exactly where 2w9 found it. The slot is an unnamed
accessor at `0xbec02ce`:

    bool f(unsigned idx) { return ((uint8_t *)this->0x40)[idx * 0xd0 + 1] & 1; }

`this->0x40` is `IOMalloc(this->0x58 * 0xd0)` in
`AMDRadeonX6000_AMDHWDisplay::init` (`0xbe86c66`), one 0xd0-byte state struct
per display, and `this->0x58` is the display count `isDisplayEnabled` bounds
against. Byte +1 bit 0 is **bit 8 of the dword at +0x00**. Of the forty
`imulq $0xd0` sites in the kext not one writes that dword — the sole writer
uses a precomputed index, inside **`AMDRadeonX6000_AMDHWDisplay::
getDisplayInfo` (`0xbe8700e`)**, forty bytes past the `ATY,fb_offset` read
2w9 traced:

    be870e2  orl  $0x40,       (%rax,%rbx)
    be87100  r = fb->vt[0xa30]('wsaa', &out)
    be87113  if (r)  andl $~0x80 ;  else { this->0x570[idx] = out; orl $0x80 }
    be87165  r = fb->vt[0xa30]('amtr', &out)
    be8717e  if (r == 0 || r == 0xe00002d8)  orl  $0x100,      (%rax,%rbx)
    be8718b  else                            andl $~0x100,     (%rax,%rbx)

Rule 7 on `IOFramebuffer`: call `0xa30` → dump `0xa40` =
**`IOFramebuffer::getAttribute(IOSelect, uintptr_t *)`**, and call `0xa28` →
dump `0xa38` = **`setAttribute(IOSelect, uintptr_t)`**. The four-character
codes decode as C literals: `0x77736161` = `'wsaa'` =
`kIOWindowServerActiveAttribute`, which is the **control** — it is a
documented IOGraphics attribute and it sits in the same instruction shape —
and `0x616d7472` = `'amtr'`.

`'amtr'` is a real `AMDFramebuffer` attribute, not an inference:
`AMDFramebuffer::setAttribute` and `::getAttribute` each have a `subl
$0x616d7472` case (`0x2a580b`, `0x2a6cb1`), four code references in all, and
`IOGraphicsFamily` has **zero** (the seven raw byte matches there are data —
rule 26). Their bodies give the whole protocol:

    getAttribute('amtr', out)                                0x2a6faa
        if (!(ctrl->0x31332 >> 9 & 1)) return kIOReturnUnsupported;
        if (getOutstandingDisplayPipeTransactions())  return kIOReturnNotReady;
        return kIOReturnSuccess;              /* *out is never written */

    setAttribute('amtr', value)                              0x2a65a4
        if (!value) return kIOReturnBadArgument;
        if (this->0xef0) this->0xe68 = 1;
        if (!tryAcquireIOPGuard()) return kIOReturnNotReady;
        this->0xe68 = 0;
        r = handleDisplayPipeTransaction((_AMD_PIPE_TRANSACTION *)value);
        releaseIOPGuardNotify();
        return r;

### So the defect is ours, and it is one selector

`RBAMDFramebuffer` declared `getAttribute` and `setAttribute` and handled
exactly one selector between them (`kIOHardwareCursorAttribute`), falling
through to `IOFramebuffer`'s base for everything else — which answers an
unknown attribute with `kIOReturnUnsupported`. That clears bit 8 on every
`getDisplayInfo`, which fails `vt[0x190]`, which returns
`kIOReturnUnsupported` from `executeTransaction`'s first test, which
`validateTransaction` passes through, which `set_transaction_args` logs. **122
transactions, 122 refusals, one cause, and it is a selector we never answered.**

This also explains the shape of boot 191 that nothing else did: the pipe went
**active** (`ax0_active 1`, `r380 1`) and transactions were **created and
numbered** — everything up to and including `initFramebufferResource` works —
and then every single one was refused identically with no variance across 62
seconds. A gate that depends on a table size, a plane count or a capability
reply would vary; a missing attribute cannot.

It is the **seventh** time a correct static chain was attached one link off
before the probe or the next read moved it, and the second time the answer was
in the same function as the previous milestone's (`getDisplayInfo` gave 2w9
the ATY pair and gives 2wc the `'amtr'` bit, forty bytes apart).

### What is in build `6F1EB613`

`-rbgpufbamtr`, off by default, in `src/fbkext`:

- `getAttribute('amtr', *)` → `kIOReturnSuccess`, counted in `RBFBAmtrGets`.
  It does **not** write `*value`, copying AMDFramebuffer, whose consumer
  presets its local and ignores the out-parameter.
- `setAttribute('amtr', value)` → `kIOReturnBadArgument` on a null value
  (AMDFramebuffer's own answer), otherwise `kIOReturnSuccess`, counted in
  `RBFBAmtrSets`, and the **first** call snapshots 0x80 bytes from `value`
  into `RBFBAmtrSnap`. Rule 19: the floor checked is the **kernel** base
  `0xffffff8000000000`, correct for a kalloc'd object, and a refusal publishes
  the pointer it refused in `RBFBAmtrRefused`.
- Neither handler allocates. They run on the accelerator's thread with its
  locks held; the VBL `thread_call` publishes the counters (rule 31), and
  `RBFBAmtrArmed` is published **unconditionally** in `start()` beside
  `RBFBAtyArmed`, which is rule 15's cheap independent identity check.

`value` is `&pipe->0x410` — `executeTransaction` ORs 0x1, 0x2, 0x4, 0x8,
0x10, 0x20, 0x40, 0x100 and 0x201 into the flag word there, puts the plane
resource at +0x10, the destination rect at +0x18/+0x20, the colour matrix at
+0x30 and the gamma tables from +0x220 — so `RBFBAmtrSnap` is the first
cooked display-pipe transaction this project has ever been handed, and the
surface address in it is what the scanout eventually has to be pointed at.

The hosttest shim (`tools/hosttest/fb_vbl_shim.hpp`) grew the same fields and
a blob `setProperty`, so `publishVBLState` stays host-compiled.

### Said before the boot

The transaction is **answered, not executed** — nothing is written to DCN, so
the panel keeps showing whatever it shows and the composited image lands
nowhere. A working PIPE with a wrong IMAGE is still the goal (2w9). Expect
`RBFBAmtrGets` > 0, `RBFBAmtrSets` > 0, `RBFBAmtrSnapped` true, and the
`set_transaction_args` error line **gone**. If the gets move and the sets do
not, validation passed and the submit path is gated somewhere else; if neither
moves, `getDisplayInfo` is not reaching us and the chain above the attribute
is wrong.

### Next

An armed boot of fbkext `6F1EB613`, **installed to the auxiliary collection**
(rule 15 — a rebuild refreshes nothing, and boot 190 was lost to exactly this
omission), with `-rbgpufbaty` and `-rbgpufbamtr` both in boot-args.

## 2wd — BOOT 192: `'amtr'` IS ANSWERED, THE REFUSALS DO NOT MOVE, AND 2wc WITHDREW THE WRONG EXCLUSION

Capture `logs/20261028-005656-plugin`, `rbgpu-boot` **192**, armed
(`armed 1`, `agdc_oneshot 0`, `iop_oneshot 0`, `agdc_error 0`), `diag_used`
**663**/768, **all 17 files** — the first complete capture in four boots.

### Rule 15 met on both kexts, for the first time since 2w6

`kexts.txt`: plugin **`64D3D687`**, `com.rembrandtgpu.fb` **`6F1EB613`** —
the new framebuffer, so the auxiliary-collection install worked and
`kmutil create`'s `Code=34` was again a loud error over a write that landed
(2wa, rule 26's mirror). `RBFBAmtrArmed = True` and `RBFBAtyArmed = True`
corroborate it from the registry. Boot-args carry `-rbgpufbaty` **and**
`-rbgpufbamtr`.

### The ATY chain is reproducible

All three probe samples byte-identical to boot 191's, and to each other:

    ax*_fi340 16777216   ax*_fi348 8294400   ax*_fi34c 8294400
    ax*_r380         1   ax*_active       1   ax*_gate        0
    ax*_b35d 1  ax*_b35e 1  ax*_b35f 1  ax*_w/h/bpp/fmt 1920/1080/4/4
    ax*_hw328 1  ax*_hw330 1  ax*_pfb 1  ax*_pres 1  ax*_n 1  ax*_fbs 1

So 2w9/2wb hold on a second boot. `IOAccelDisplayPipe::isActive()` is true,
`initFramebufferResource` returns success, and none of 2w3's three
`kIOReturnNotReady` gates is shut.

### `'amtr'` was asked for, and answered

From `ioreg -rl -c RBAMDFramebuffer`:

    RBFBAmtrArmed    True       RBFBAmtrSets      0
    RBFBAmtrGets     3          RBFBAmtrSnapped   False
    RBFBAmtrPtr      0          RBFBAmtrRefused   0

**Gets 3, Sets 0.** So `AMDHWDisplay::getDisplayInfo` did call
`fb->getAttribute('amtr', &out)` — three times, which is one per
`getDisplayInfo` — and our handler returned `kIOReturnSuccess` each time, so
2wc's chain down to the attribute is **confirmed as a real call path**. Zero
sets means nothing ever reached
`setAttribute('amtr', &pipe->0x410)`, which in `executeTransaction` sits past
the `bool` arm; the validate arm never calls it. No snapshot, and the refusal
published nothing because no pointer was ever refused.

### And the refusals did not move

| | boot 191 | **boot 192** |
|---|---|---|
| `set_transaction_args ... 0xe00002c7` | 122 | **132** |
| `transaction ID (N) generated error (0xe00002c7)` | 122 | **132** |
| `dirtyBits` / `options` | 0x3c1 / 0x801 | **0x3c1 / 0x801** |
| `display_change_handler` (control) | 26 | **26** |

Unchanged, with the same inputs. **So `vt[0x190]` is not, or is not the only,
thing refusing.** Boot 192 cannot separate "we opened gate 1 and met gate 2"
from "gate 1 was never shut": both give an unchanged count and an unchanged
code, and the error code is identical for the two sites. That is **not
established** and must not be written as if it were.

### What boot 192 DID settle, from the consumer's side

`Failed to submit transaction: IOPRESENTMENT_METHOD_FAILURE: IOReturn: 0x…`
appears 134 times, and the codes are **132 × `0x2c7`** and 2 × `0x2bc`
(`kIOReturnError`). Boots 185 and 186 measured that same message **118 and 152
times, all `0x2d8`** (`kIOReturnNotReady`). So the `kIOReturnNotReady` era is
over, confirmed from CoreDisplay and not only from the kernel: the ATY pair
moved the failure from `transactionEnd`'s three gates into
`executeTransaction`, and the new code propagates the whole way up.
`Fallback ... submission failed` is **66**, `DisplayPipeState` **66**, and
**132 = 2 × 66** — exactly 2w3's "Submit runs ~twice per Commit".

Also: `no gamma` **0** (2u6's fix still holds), `bad bits` 4 unchanged, the
wedge still present (34 `event timeout`, 53 `checkGPUProgress`), and
`RBFBVBLFires 13200` with `RBFBVBL1Fires` **0** — Apple's handler 1 did not
fire this boot where boot 191 saw it once. Not attributed.

### 2wc's EXCLUSION OF THE GAMMA CEILING IS WITHDRAWN — it was the wrong table

2wc enumerated `executeTransaction`'s six `kIOReturnUnsupported` sites against
`dirtyBits 0x3c1` and found one live besides the unconditional one: bit `0x80`,

    be4a271  rax = txn->getPipePostGammaTable()
    be4a28f  r13 = rax->getTableCount()
    be4a34a  r12 = 0xe00002c7
    be4a350  cmpl $0x100, %r13d
    be4a35e  ja  -> return kIOReturnUnsupported

and then dismissed it by counting the LUT in boot 190's `DisplayPipeState`
dumps: 71 of **256** entries, 2 of 1024 (67 and 2 in boot 189; 64 and 2 in
boot 192). **Those dumps are headed `Plane Index: 0`, and their `LUT` is the
PLANE gamma** — whose dirty bit is `0x4`, which is **CLEAR** in `0x3c1`. The
gate is on bit `0x80`, the **PIPE post-gamma**, and `DisplayPipeState` never
prints it. A per-plane number was used to retire a per-pipe line: **rule 33,
third recorded instance** (2u4's `Plane Index` for a plane count, 2v9's note,
now this).

### Where the pipe post-gamma's size comes from

`IOAccelDisplayPipeGammaTable2::getTableCount` (`0x14e62a92`) is four
instructions:

    movq 0x10(%rdi), %rax ; movl (%rax), %eax

— the **first dword of the `IOAccelDisplayPipeGammaTableData` the userspace
client supplied** (`withGammaTableData` `0x14e62682`,
`IOAccelDisplayPipeTransaction2::set_pipe_postgamma_table` `0x14e5e7e6`). So
the count is **CoreDisplay's choice**, not AMD's and not a hardware fact, and
the only lever this project holds on it is the one capability field that tells
CoreDisplay how large a table the pipe accepts: our AGDC attribute-`0x711`
type-2 entry `+0x28`, published as the dictionary key `MaximumSize`
(2u6/2v5), i.e. `RB_AGDC_GAMMA_CHANNELS`.

Boot 192 measured it live: **`agdc_gamma_elems1 = 1024`**, with
`agdc_gamma_entries 1`, `agdc_gamma_elems2 0`, `agdc_extcap_answered 15`,
`agdc_extcap_calls 48`. We are advertising 1024 to a consumer whose own
accelerator refuses anything above 256.

### The change: `RB_AGDC_GAMMA_CHANNELS` 0x400 → 0x100, plugin `0D1F953A`

One constant in `src/common/rb_agdc.h`. It is **still a substitute** (rule 17
— Apple reads it from `vt[0x1b8](0xf)` on an `AmdFbDisplayPath` we do not
have), but unlike 0x400 it is bounded by a **measured fact about the
consumer** rather than by the size of a table CoreDisplay happened to print.
It is non-zero, so 2u6's *"plane with no 3-channel gamma table support"* —
which fired only at **zero** — stays fixed; boot 192 counts it 0 as the
control.

The hosttest keeps asserting the **literal**, for 2v1's reason (a field
compared against the macro that wrote it is not a test), and gains the
consumer's ceiling as a second assertion of its own, so a future raise fails
on the host rather than on hardware.

`make plugin`: hosttest green, `kmutil libraries` 0 symbols from
`SystemKernelExtensions.kc`, `grep -c IOGraphicsFamily src/plugin/Info.plist`
0.

### Said before the boot

- `agdc_gamma_elems1` must read **256**. If it reads 1024 the plugin did not
  move and nothing else in the capture means anything (rule 15).
- If the post-gamma ceiling was the live gate, `set_transaction_args ...
  0xe00002c7` goes to **0** and `RBFBAmtrSets` becomes non-zero — because the
  only thing past the gamma block in the validate arm is the success return,
  and `setAttribute` is then reached on the submit arm.
- If it goes to 0 but `RBFBAmtrSets` stays 0, the transaction validates and
  CoreDisplay still does not submit; read `Fallback` and `DisplayPipeState`
  next, not the kernel.
- If it stays at ~132, the gamma ceiling is excluded *properly* this time and
  the unconditional `vt[0x190]` gate is back as the live candidate — in which
  case the next step is not another guess but the **probe**: publish
  `((uint8_t *)hwd->0x40)[fbIdx*0xd0 + 1]` and the whole dword beside it, so
  the bit is read instead of reasoned about. 2w7 and 2wa were both settled
  that way and 2wc was not.
- **The picture stays wrong either way** — nothing is written to DCN, and
  `-rbgpufbaty` still publishes a 16 MB offset while OTG0 scans offset 0. The
  user reported boot 191 as the Apple logo and progress bar with the OS live
  underneath over SSH, which is what a never-composited panel looks like.

### Next

One armed boot of plugin **`0D1F953A`** — **installed into the OpenCore EFI**
(`sudo tools/efi.sh install`; rule 15, the plugin's own path) — with fbkext
`6F1EB613` already in `/Library/Extensions` and unchanged. No boot-arg change.

## 2we — BOOT 193: THE DISPLAY PIPE ACCEPTS TRANSACTIONS. EVERY FAILURE IN THE CHAIN IS GONE.

Capture `logs/20261028-101029-plugin`, `rbgpu-boot` **193**, armed
(`armed 1`, `agdc_oneshot 0`, `iop_oneshot 0`, `agdc_error 0`,
`agdc_say "PUBLISHED"`), `diag_used` **664**/768, 20 files, complete.

**Rule 15 on both kexts**: plugin **`0D1F953A`** (new), fb **`6F1EB613`**
(unchanged). The experiment's own arm check: **`agdc_gamma_elems1 = 256`**,
`agdc_gamma_entries 1`, `agdc_extcap_answered 15`, `agdc_extcap_calls 48`.

### The whole failure cascade is at zero

| | 189 | 190 | 191 | 192 | **193** |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| `display_change_handler` (control) | 26 | 26 | 26 | 26 | **26** |
| `set_transaction_args … 0xe00002c7` | — | — | 122 | 132 | **0** |
| `transaction ID (N) generated error` | — | — | 122 | 132 | **0** |
| `Failed to submit transaction` | 152* | — | — | 134 | **0** |
| `Fallback … submission failed` | 69 | 73 | 3 | 66 | **0** |
| `DisplayPipeState` | 69 | 73 | — | 66 | **0** |
| `Attempting to get 3-channel linearization …` | — | — | — | 134 | **3** |

(*boot 186's count; 189's log was not captured at INFO.) The control is
identical in all five boots, so the zeros are zeros and not a dropped
predicate (rule 36). `IOReturn: 0x` has **no matches at all** — there is no
longer a failing submit to carry a code. 2v9 proved the dumps *are* the
failure's own diagnostic, so `DisplayPipeState` 0 follows from `Fallback` 0
rather than being a separate reading.

`Metal compositor activated` ×4 from SkyLight. `no gamma` 0 — 2u6's fix holds
at 256, as predicted.

### Transactions reach OUR framebuffer

    RBFBAmtrArmed    True        RBFBAmtrSets      13      (was 0)
    RBFBAmtrGets     29  (was 3) RBFBAmtrSnapped   True    (was False)
    RBFBAmtrRefused  0           RBFBAmtrPtr  0xffffff916784a410

**`setAttribute('amtr', &pipe->0x410)` is being called.** That call lives past
the `bool` arm of `executeTransaction`, i.e. on `submitTransaction`'s side, and
in boot 192 it was reached **zero** times. So the submit path runs now, and
2wc's `handleDisplayPipeTransaction` shape is the live one: Apple's accelerator
hands the cooked transaction to the framebuffer and we answer it.

### Both changes were load-bearing, and that is now established

Boot 192 (fbkext with `'amtr'`, `MaximumSize` still 1024): refusals 132,
sets 0.
Boot 193 (same fbkext, `MaximumSize` 256): refusals 0, sets 13.

Boot 192 could not separate "gate 1 opened and gate 2 met" from "gate 1 was
never shut" (2wd). Boot 193 settles it in the only direction consistent with
both: **the `'amtr'` answer was necessary and not sufficient.** It cannot have
been sufficient (192 still refused everything) and it cannot have been
unnecessary (the only path to `setAttribute` is through
`executeTransaction`'s first test, which `vt[0x190]` gates, and sets moved
0 → 13 with no other change to that code). Two sequential gates, both ours,
both now open.

### The transaction struct, confirmed field for field from the hardware

`RBFBAmtrPtr` is `0xffffff916784a410`, so the pipe is at
`0xffffff916784a000` and the pointer is **exactly `pipe + 0x410`** — 2wc's
reading of the argument, confirmed from a live pointer rather than from the
disassembly. `RBFBAmtrSnap`, 0x80 bytes from there:

| off | value | field | self-reference |
|---|---|---|---|
| +0x00 | `0x75` | `0x410` flag word | |
| +0x08 | `0x1` | `0x418` mode word | |
| +0x10 | `0xffffff916784d6b0` | `0x420` plane state | **= pipe + 0x36b0** |
| +0x18 | 0 | `0x428` | |
| +0x20 | `0xffffff916784d660` | `0x430` | **= pipe + 0x3660** |
| +0x28 | 0 | `0x438` | |
| +0x30 | `0xffffff916784d680` | `0x440` colour matrix | **= pipe + 0x3680** |
| +0x38 | `0xffffff916784c650` | `0x450` | **= pipe + 0x2650** |
| +0x40 | `0xffffff916784d8d0` | `0x460` | **= pipe + 0x38d0** |
| +0x48…+0x7f | 0 | | |

Every pointer is one of the `leaq 0xNNNN(%rbx)` addresses `executeTransaction`
loads — `0x36b0`, `0x3660`, `0x3680`, `0x2650`, `0x38d0`. The struct is a
table of pointers into the pipe object's own tail, and the snapshot agrees
with the disassembly at every one of them. That is five independent controls
on 2wc's field map in a single reading.

**And the flag word decomposes exactly as `dirtyBits 0x3c1` predicts** on the
submit arm, where every block runs:

    0x001 SET    plane resource          (0xbe49e02)
    0x002 clear  plane gamma             (0xbe49f01)   dirty bit 0x4   clear
    0x004 SET    plane dst rect          (0xbe49fc4)
    0x008 clear  pipe pre-gamma          (0xbe4a0e2)   dirty bit 0x20  clear
    0x010 SET    colour matrix           (0xbe4a1b8)   dirty bit 0x40  set
    0x020 SET    PIPE POST-GAMMA         (0xbe4a2b2)   dirty bit 0x80  set
    0x040 SET    pre-CSC linearization   (0xbe4a4c1)   dirty bit 0x200 set
    0x100 clear  postCSC gamma VID       (0xbe4a3bb)   dirty bit 0x400 clear

**`0x20` is set**, and `0xbe4a2b2` is the instruction immediately after the
ceiling test that was refusing every transaction four hours ago. The block
that returned `kIOReturnUnsupported` now completes and sets its flag.

### THE WEDGE IS AN INDEPENDENT SECOND DEFECT

First `checkGPUProgress` at **10:07:57.763**, fifteen seconds after boot, and
running the whole 2 m 48 s capture: 63 `Signaling hardware error`, 63
`GPURestartSignaled`/`Enqueued`/`Dequeued`, 36 `channel N is not hung, keep
running`, 36 `no channel associated with stamp_idx N`, 36 `GPURestartSkipped`,
26 `SDMA0_PAGE event timeout`, 9 `GFX event timeout`, 1 `VMPT event timeout`,
3 `GPURestartDeferred`.

2w4 recorded the wedge starting **six seconds after** the first submit failure
and could not say whether it was a consequence. **Boot 193 answers it**: there
are no submit failures at all and the wedge is unchanged in shape and slightly
larger in count. So it is **not caused by the display submit path** — a clean
differential, n=1 but the right shape. It is a stamp-retirement failure: work
is submitted, never retires, the hang check says not hung, and the restart
cannot find the channel.

`IOAccelSurface::set_id_mode: Surface mode contains bad bits` ×4, still
unexplained, unchanged across five boots.

### New shapes, not attributed

`Setting main display 0x… offline` ×7 and `Setting offline display 0x… main
in CGXConstructVirtualFramebuffer` ×7, both `[ERROR]`. They do not appear in
boot 192's log. Whether they are part of the normal mode-set sequence that the
earlier boots never reached, or a new defect, is **not established**.
`RBFBVBL1Fires` is **0** with `RBFBVBLFires 21218`, where boot 191 saw Apple's
handler fire once — also not attributed, and now less interesting, because the
transactions are not going through the VBL ring at all but straight to
`setAttribute`.

### What is NOT fixed, and why the screen is still wrong

Nothing is written to the display engine. `setAttribute('amtr', …)` returns
`kIOReturnSuccess` without doing the work, so the compositor believes thirteen
transactions landed and none of them did; `-rbgpufbaty` still publishes a 16 MB
offset while OTG0 scans VRAM offset 0. **The pipe is accepted; the picture is
not drawn.** That is exactly the state 2w9 said to aim for, reached.

### Next

`handleDisplayPipeTransaction` (`AMDFramebuffer` `0x2b4df0`) read against
`RBFBAmtrSnap`'s five pointers, to learn what each sub-struct holds — above
all the plane state at `pipe + 0x36b0`, which carries the surface the
compositor rendered into. That address is what the DCN 3.1.2
`HUBP*_DCSURF_PRIMARY_SURFACE_ADDRESS*` pair has to be pointed at, and taking
it out of the transaction is strictly better than inventing it. **No boot
needed.**

Then, separately and on its own risk: the first write this kext has ever made
to the display engine. And the wedge, which is now the only other defect left

## 2wf — the transaction is read end to end, and the surface address is already in it (static, no boot)

Static read only. `handleDisplayPipeTransaction` (`AMDFramebuffer` `0x2b4df0`)
against boot 193's `RBFBAmtrSnap`, as 2we's handoff named. The function is
compiled **unoptimized** — every local spilled to the frame — so unlike
`executeTransaction` it reads almost like source.

### The transaction struct is confirmed from the consumer side

`SUPPORTED_TRANSACTIONS` is a file-static at `0x2bec98`, 8 bytes, value
**`0x7d`**. The function's first act after its gates is

    flags = txn->0x00 & 0x7d;
    queueDisplayPipeTransactions(flags);
    if (this->0xe80) finishDeferredDisplayPipeTransaction();

and then one block per bit, highest first, each of the shape

    if (this->0x1198 & bit) { log; dequeueDisplayPipeTransactions(bit); }
    else if (flags & bit)   { ...handle... }

Boot 193 measured the flag word **`0x75`**. `0x75 & ~0x7d == 0`: **every bit
our transaction carries is a bit AMD supports.** Bit `0x2` (plane gamma) is the
one bit *not* in `0x7d`, and it is clear in `0x75` anyway. If any unsupported
bit were set the function logs a complaint against the `0x7d` literal at
`0x2b584f` — a line to grep for later.

Each handler dereferences exactly the pointer 2we's snapshot recorded, which
makes this an independent confirmation of that field map from the other side:

| bit | field | what the consumer does with it |
|---|---|---|
| 0x40 | `txn->0x40` | reads `+0x18` u16, compares to `0x10`, writes 0/1 to `this->0x1180` |
| 0x20 | `txn->0x38` | **`setGammaTable(_AMD_PIPE_GAMMA_TABLE *)`** (`0x2a5100`) |
| 0x10 | `txn->0x30` | `memcpy(this + 0x1130, p, 0x30)`; `this->0xd48 = this + 0x1130` |
| 0x4  | `txn->0x20` | floats at `+0x8`, against `this->0x1168/0x116c` |
| 0x1  | `txn->0x10` | the plane state — below |

NULL in any of them is `kIOReturnBadArgument` (`0xe00002c2`). `txn->0x08` is a
u32 **transaction ID**: the tail calls
`processDisplayPipeTransaction(txn->0x8, false)` with it. The four gates above
all of it are AMDFramebuffer's own state — `this->0x908` NULL and
`(this->0x820 >> 1) & 1` clear give **`kIOReturnOffline`** (`0x2d7`), a call on
`this->0xdd8` and `this->0xe00` give **`kIOReturnNotPermitted`** (`0x2e2`).

### The plane state is an `_AMD_PIPE_FLIP`, 0x220 bytes, and it is `txn->0x10`

    ps = txn->0x10;                         /* = pipe + 0x36b0 */
    if (!ps) return kIOReturnBadArgument;
    if (this->0xdf0 && enabled(this->0xdf0))
        switch (query(this->0xdf0, *(uint16_t *)(ps + 0x6))) {
        case 1: hw->vt[0xb58](fbIdx, 0); break;
        case 2: hw->vt[0xb58](fbIdx, 1); break;
        }
    memcpy(this + 0xf10, ps, 0x220);
    this->0xd40 = this + 0xf18;
    r = saveFlipTransactionPixelFormat(*(uint32_t *)ps);

**Three independent agreements on the size 0x220**, which is what makes it a
measurement rather than a guess:

1. the `memcpy` length here, in `AMDFramebuffer`;
2. `pipe + 0x36b0 + 0x220 == 0x38d0`, and `pipe+0x38d0` is the next pointer
   boot 193's snapshot already carries (`+0x40`, pre-CSC linearization) — field
   adjacency in a third kext's object;
3. `bzero(flip + 5, 0x21b)` at `0xbe88430` inside the **writer**: 5 + 0x21b =
   0x220 exactly.

The producer is `executeTransaction` at `0xbe49cf6`–`0xbe49dd2`:

    res  = getPlaneResource(txn, 0, 0);      /* 0x14e62430 */
    surf = getPlaneIOSurface(txn, 0, 0);     /* 0x14e5f936 */
    if (!res) return kIOReturnBadArgument;
    r9 = isSubmit ? pipe + 0x36b0 : NULL;    /* the out-parameter */
    r11 = isSubmit ? NULL : &scratch;        /* memcpy of pipe+0x3948, 0x220 */
    ok = pipe->0x330->vt[0x198](fbIdx, res, 0, mode, isSubmit, 0xff, r11);
    if (!ok) return kIOReturnError;          /* 0x2bc */
    txn->0x10 = pipe + 0x36b0;
    planeState->0x6 = (uint16_t) ...;

`pipe->0x330` is the **AMDHWDisplay** — the same object whose `vt[0x190]`
(dump `0x1a0`) is 2wc's `'amtr'` gate — so `vt[0x198]` is dump **`0x1a8`**, one
slot along, with 2wc's accessor and `isDisplayEnabled`/`isDisplayControlEnabled`
as controls on the table alignment. It resolves to

**`AMDRadeonX6000_AMDHWDisplay::getDisplayPipeTransactionFlip(unsigned int,
IOAccelResource2 *, IOAccelResource2 *, _eAMDSwapInterval, _AMD_PIPE_FLIP *,
bool, …PipeRotation, _AMD_PIPE_FLIP *)`** (`0xbe88392`).

The signature matches the call register for register, including the two
`_AMD_PIPE_FLIP *` out-parameters that the call site fills **one or the other
of, never both** — `r9` on the submit arm, the last stack argument on the
validate arm. So the plane state at `txn->0x10` *is* an `_AMD_PIPE_FLIP`, and
`flip->0x00` is the u32 format (`0/6/7/8/9` at `0xbe887cb`–`0xbe88807`),
`flip->0x04` the rotation byte, `flip->0x06` the u16 the caller fills after.

**2pf's "never called once in a whole boot" is not refuted and not relied
on.** It was measured when no transaction had ever executed — 2s9 through 2wd
all recorded that — so it says nothing about a boot in which `setAttribute`
ran 13 times. It is simply not evidence either way now.

### The address is computed by a leaf helper, and it is a GPU VA

`0xbe88846`, called on each `IOAccelResource2` (primary → `-0x80(%rbp)`,
secondary → `-0x60(%rbp)`):

    mem = res->0x88;  if (!mem) return 0;
    base = mem->vt[0x158](0, 0);
    k = (uint8_t)res->0x14;
    off = (k == 0 || k == 0x80) ? res->0xf8        /* u64 */
        : (k == 0x82)           ? (uint32_t)res->0xfc
        :                         0;
    return base + off;

So what lands in the flip is a **GPU virtual address**, not a VRAM byte offset
— which is a different kind of number from `ATY,fb_offset` (2w9), and worth
holding separate. Both addresses are then passed as `%rcx` and `%r8` to a
further `vt[0x230]` on a third object, three times over three branches, and
*that* is what stores them into the flip.

### Where this stops, deliberately

**The chain is NOT followed to the store offset.** Three more vtable layers in
three more classes separate the helper from it, and this project has now
attached a correct static chain one link off **seven** times (rule 33), with
2v9 spending five correct layers on the one link that was fine (rule 35). The
one address store seen directly is `flip->0x58` at `0xbe885a4`, on a branch
whose base also comes from a `vt[0x158]` call — a *candidate*, not a result.

It does not need to be derived, because **Apple has already filled the struct
before we are called.** `setAttribute('amtr', &pipe->0x410)` happens after
`getDisplayPipeTransactionFlip` has returned, so the real addresses are
sitting in memory we already hold a pointer to. Measuring beats deriving
(rule 17).

### And the AMDFramebuffer path could never have worked here anyway

A new and independent confirmation of 2sj. The last thing
`processDisplayPipeTransaction` does with the plane state is

    hw = this->0xdd8;
    hw->vt[0x8c0](this->0xd40);      /* 0x2b480e-0x2b481f */
    this->0xd40 = 0;

Rule 7: call `0x8c0` → dump `0x8d0` in `__ZTV13ATIController`, which is
**`0x975800`** — a filler shared by **122** slots of that vtable, i.e. the
pure-virtual stub. `ATIController` does not implement the plane-state program;
a subclass does, and the journal already recorded (line 34452) that no
controller personality matches `0x1681`, so none instantiates here. **Even
Apple's own `AMDFramebuffer` could not have completed this flip on this
machine.** The register write was always going to be ours; that is not a
consequence of having replaced the framebuffer.

### Build `A454F066`, no new boot-arg

`-rbgpufbamtr` now also follows `txn->0x10` and takes the whole `0x220` bytes.
`amtrFlipSnapped` is a **separate** flag from `amtrSnapped` so "header read,
plane state not" is distinguishable from "never called"; `RBFBAmtrFlipRefused`
publishes a pointer refused (rule 19, same kernel floor). Published:
`RBFBAmtrFlipSnapped/Ptr/Refused/Snap`, plus `RBFBAmtrFlipFmt` (+0x00),
`RBFBAmtrFlipRot` (+0x04) and `RBFBAmtrFlipA58` (+0x58) as named keys — the
three fields the static read **predicts**, so the boot tests that read instead
of assuming it.

**Said before the boot.** Bit `0x1` is SET in `0x75`, so `txn->0x10` is valid
and `RBFBAmtrFlipSnapped` must be **true**; false, or a non-zero
`RBFBAmtrFlipRefused`, would mean the flag word and the pointer disagree and
2we's decode is wrong somewhere. `RBFBAmtrFlipFmt` should be one of
`0/6/7/8/9` and `RBFBAmtrFlipRot` small. If `RBFBAmtrFlipA58` holds a
plausible GPU VA, the static read landed; if it is zero, the blob says where
the address actually is and nothing is lost — which is the whole reason the
blob is published beside the three fields. **The picture stays wrong either
way**: nothing is written to the display engine in this build.

Plugin stays **`0D1F953A`**, already installed in the EFI and proven by boot
193 — no plugin rebuild, no `efi.sh install`. Only the framebuffer kext
changed, so rule 15's install for this boot is the **auxiliary collection**.

## 2wg — boot 194: the surface address is measured, and it is a low/high pair

`rbgpu-boot` **194**, `armed=1`, both `ax0`/`ax2` samples all-open
(`gate=0 enabled=1 active=1 defer=0 vram=1 vmap=1`), `ax0_fi340=0x1000000`,
`ax0_w/h/bpp/fmt = 0x780/0x438/4/4`, `diag_used` **663** of 768 so absences
are informative, and the experiment's own arm check passed:
**`agdc_gamma_elems1 = 0x100` = 256**.

**Rule 15 met without `kexts.txt`.** The capture is only **6 files** (no
display log, no `ioreg`, no kext list — the box was rebooted early again), but
`RBFBAmtrFlipSnapped`, `RBFBAmtrFlipFmt`, `RBFBAmtrFlipRot` and
`RBFBAmtrFlipA58` **exist**, and only build `A454F066` publishes them. A key
the new code publishes is again the cheapest identity check.

**And rule 8 was met by differential, not by a bare read.** `RBFBCrumbBoot`
reads **192** in the boot-193 capture and **193** in this one — it lags
`rbgpu-boot` by exactly one in *both*, because the fbkext reads the nonce
before the peer increments it. The crumb advancing is therefore the nonce
advancing. `rbgpu-boot = 194` confirms it directly.

**A grep read the WRONG BOOT'S TABLE.** The first pass over `nvram.txt`
reported `armed=0`, `agdc_oneshot=2`, `agdc_error=3` and `diag_used=0xa3`, and
every one of those came from **`rbgpu-diag-prev`** — the *previous* boot's
table, sitting in the same flat file under a key whose name is a superstring
of the one being matched. It read exactly like an unarmed boot and would have
thrown the measurement away. Caught only by noticing that
`agdc_gamma_elems1` was published at all, which an unarmed bridge cannot do.
**Rule 26 again: a key name can be a prefix of another key's name, and a grep
with no line structure will cross the boundary.** Match `rbgpu-diag` anchored,
or read the value, never the file.

### The transaction struct, confirmed a third time and now live

`RBFBAmtrPtr = 0xffffff953cdba410`, `RBFBAmtrFlipPtr = 0xffffff953cdbd6b0`.
The difference is **0x32a0**, and `0x36b0 - 0x410 == 0x32a0`. Both pointers
give the same pipe base, `0xffffff953cdba000`, computed two independent ways.
So `txn->0x10 == pipe + 0x36b0` is now measured on hardware in a second boot,
at a different kernel address.

### The `_AMD_PIPE_FLIP`, measured

    +0x00  u32  6            pixel format
    +0x04  u8   0            rotation
    +0x05  u8   2
    +0x08  u32  0x1002a000   SURFACE ADDRESS, LOW
    +0x0c  u32  0x000000f4   SURFACE ADDRESS, HIGH
    +0x14  u32  1920         width / pitch in pixels
    +0x18  u32  4            bytes per pixel
    +0x28  f32  1920.0       width
    +0x2c  f32  1080.0       height
    +0x30  u32  4
    +0x38  u32  2
    +0x3c  u32  4
    +0x40 .. +0x21f          ALL ZERO

**`+0x28`/`+0x2c` decoding as exactly `1920.0f` and `1080.0f` is the control
that proves the whole struct is real** — two IEEE floats matching the panel's
measured mode, at an offset nothing predicted them at. `+0x14 = 1920` and
`+0x18 = 4` agree with `ax0_w` and `ax0_bpp` from a completely separate
instrument in the same boot. Four fields, two instruments, one mode.

**THE SURFACE ADDRESS IS `0xf4_1002_a000`.** The measured carve-out MC base is
`0xF4_0000_0000`, so the surface sits **0x1002a000 = 256.164 MB** into VRAM.
It is an **MC address**, not a GPUVM one (Apple's GPUVM space is `0xFF_BF..`),
which is what HUBP wants.

**And it is stored as a LOW/HIGH PAIR** at `+0x08`/`+0x0c` — exactly the shape
of DCN's `HUBP*_DCSURF_PRIMARY_SURFACE_ADDRESS` and
`..._SURFACE_ADDRESS_HIGH`. The struct holds it pre-split, in the register
pair's own layout. That is a strong independent corroboration of which field
it is: no other field in the struct is split that way.

### 2wf's prediction was WRONG, and the instrument absorbed it

`RBFBAmtrFlipA58` reads **0**. 2wf named `flip->0x58` (the one address store
seen directly, at `0xbe885a4`) as a **candidate, not a result**, and published
the raw blob beside it precisely so a wrong guess would cost nothing. It cost
nothing: the blob names `+0x08`. The `0xbe885a4` store is on a different
branch — a secondary/cursor path that did not run here, consistent with
`+0x40..0x21f` being entirely zero and with `executeTransaction` passing
`ecx = 0` for the second `IOAccelResource2`.

`RBFBAmtrFlipFmt = 6` **is** in the predicted set `{0,6,7,8,9}` and
`RBFBAmtrFlipRot = 0` is small, so two of the three predictions landed. This
is rule 35 working as intended: the static chain was instrumented at our own
end and the one link that was guessed is the one that was wrong.

### What this boot does NOT say

**The capture has no display log and no `ioreg`**, so every regression control
from 2we — `set_transaction_args … 0x2c7`, `Failed to submit transaction`,
`Fallback … submission failed`, `DisplayPipeState`, `no gamma`, the wedge
counts, `display_change_handler` as the control — **is uncheckable, and their
absence is not a result** (rules 14/36). What *is* positive evidence that the
chain still runs: `RBFBAmtrSets` **13 → 17** and `RBFBAmtrGets` 29 → 37, so
transactions are still being submitted to us.
`RBFBVBLFires` 23098, `RBFBVBL1Fires` still **0**, `RBFBGammaCalls` 0,
`RBFBAtyOffset` 16777216 — unchanged.

### The consequence for the write, stated before it is attempted

**The address is per-flip, not a constant.** We snapshot only the *first*
transaction, and 17 arrived; a compositor swap chain hands a different surface
each flip. So pointing the scanout at `0xf4_1002_a000` once is **not** the
fix — it would show one stale frame. The write has to happen **per
transaction**, and `setAttribute('amtr', …)` is exactly the hook that gets
called with each one. That is a design consequence of a measurement, and it
changes the shape of the next step from "write a constant" to "write the
address this transaction carries".

Also worth holding separate: the surface is at 256.164 MB while
`ATY,fb_offset` publishes **16 MB** (2w9's deliberately untruthful value, as
the gate rejects 0). Those two numbers have nothing to do with each other —
the ATY offset only has to be non-zero to open `initFramebufferResource`,
while the flip carries the real address. Do not try to reconcile them.

### Next

The first write this project has ever made to the display engine, as its own
milestone with its own boot-arg: take `flip->0x08`/`+0x0c` out of each
transaction in `setAttribute('amtr')` and program the DCN 3.1.2
`HUBP*_DCSURF_PRIMARY_SURFACE_ADDRESS` pair. Registers from
`docs/linux-ref/`, `DCN_VERSION_3_1` grouping, `dcn_3_1_2` offsets,
**grouping checked before adding one**. A readback and a restore path come
with it, because a wrong write blanks the panel and rule 12 says a black panel
is indistinguishable from a hang.

## 2wh — the first write to the display engine, built (fbkext `D07493B1`)

No boot yet. This is the write every milestone since 2w9 has been pointing at.

### What it does on the chip

HUBP is DCN's display-data fetch block.
`HUBPREQ0_DCSURF_PRIMARY_SURFACE_ADDRESS` and `_HIGH` are the address it reads
scanout pixels from — double-buffered, latched at the next vblank. Changing
them changes **which bytes in VRAM reach the panel, and nothing else**: no
timing, no clocks, no pipe topology, no power state, no PLL. OTG keeps
scanning at the same 143.833 Hz either way. A wrong value shows garbage or
black until the next correct write, and one boot-arg reverses the whole thing.

### Why this is the narrowest possible first write

Two measurements, taken a year of milestones apart, happen to agree:

| | 2os, boot 133 (the live pipe) | 2wg, boot 194 (the compositor's surface) |
|---|---|---|
| pitch | `HUBP0_SURFACE_PITCH 0x077f` = 1920 px | `flip+0x14` = 1920 |
| format | `HUBP0_SURFACE_CONFIG 0x0008` ARGB8888 | `flip+0x18` = 4 bytes/pixel |
| address high | `0x000000f4` | `flip+0x0c` = `0x000000f4` |
| address low | `0x00000000` | `flip+0x08` = `0x1002a000` |

**Pitch, format and the HIGH dword already match. Exactly one dword changes.**

**And the register takes an MC address, measured not derived.** The pair reads
`0xf4:0x00000000` today, which is the carve-out base — an MC address. 2os also
noted `mc2pa(0xf400000000) = 0x7_8000_0000` system-physical; that is the
*equivalent*, not what the register holds. **`mc2pa` is not applied here**, and
the reason is a reading of the hardware's own current contents rather than an
inference.

### Where the logic lives, and why

`src/common/rb_hubp.h` — pure, freestanding, every offset citing
`dcn_3_1_2_offset.h`. `src/fbkext/RBAMDFramebufferHUBP.cpp` is only the
mechanism. **Everything the kext decides, the hosttest decides first**, which
is the only honest way to write code that can blank the panel.
