SHORTER hold buys rate back at some flicker; `HoldExpired 0` says the bound is
never reached today, so shortening it would start truncating real holds, and no
measurement yet says that would help.

Stated before the boot:
- `RBFBVBLModeMhz` near **143830** at 143.83 Hz and near **60000** at 60 Hz
  means the -5 % was an artifact of animtest's window and there is nothing to
  fix. Near **57000** at 60 Hz confirms it is real and in our clock.
- `RBFBVBLModeEnables` scaling with `ModeFires` (~44/s either way) says the
  toggling is mode-independent; markedly higher per second at 60 Hz would make
  the enable path the cause and the next change obvious.
- `RBFBVBLModeNs` must track wall time since the last switch. If it does not,
  this instrument is wrong and nothing else here is readable (rule 16).

## 2y8a — the plugin UUID I quoted was not the one installed, and the UUID is deterministic

`sudo tools/efi.sh install` reported the EFI carrying **636F3584**, against the
**1AAABBA1** this session had just built and quoted. Rule 15 caught it before a
boot was spent reading results against the wrong binary.

**Mechanism, and it is by design.** `efi.sh install` deletes
`build/plugin/kern_start.o` and `RembrandtGPUPeer.o` and re-runs `make plugin`
itself, because GNU make 3.81 compares whole seconds and a same-second edit
could otherwise ship a stale binary. So it relinked; the UUID quoted was from
this session's earlier link.

**The check that matters passes.** 636F3584 is REPRODUCIBLE from the committed
tree - three independent relinks (the install's, a `touch`-driven rebuild, and
a clean-object rebuild) all produce it, and there is no `__DATE__`, `__TIME__`
or `__TIMESTAMP__` anywhere in `src/plugin`, `src/common` or the Makefile. So
the installed plugin is exactly what the committed source builds. 2y8 also
changed no plugin source at all - only `src/fbkext` and `tools/hosttest` - so
there was no plugin behaviour to lose either way.

**The part that stays open, because deterministic cuts both ways.** Since the
UUID is content-derived and stable, 1AAABBA1 and 636F3584 differ in CONTENT,
and this session cannot account for what. Not load-bearing (the installed
binary reproduces from the committed tree, which is the claim that matters),
but "unexplained" is not "fine" and a future session should not read a changed
plugin UUID as proof of changed source without this note. The useful general
fact in the other direction: the plugin UUID IS a valid identity check on this
toolchain, which is what makes rule 15 work for it at all.

## 2y9 (boot 257) — the -5 % was never real, and the instrument was wrong a SECOND time in the same tool

`RBFBVBLModeMhz` = **60033** against a requested 60002 - **+0.053 %**. The
first of 2y8's three stated outcomes: *"near 60000 means the -5 % was an
artifact of animtest's window and there is nothing to fix."* There is nothing
to fix. Published beside its own inputs, as required: `ModeFires` 1136,
`ModeNs` 18922736306 = 18.923 s, and 1136/18.923 = 60.034/s, which reproduces
the published mHz to four figures.

`RBFBVBLModeEnables` 593 over 18.923 s = **31.3/s**, LOWER than the 44.2/s the
cumulative counter implied. So the vblank-enable path is not elevated at 60 Hz
and the second lead dies with the first. Both hypotheses this session raised
for the "defect" are dead, and the defect with them.

**THE MECHANISM, AND IT IS RULE 31 AIMED AT ME.** animtest reads `RBFBVBLFires`
from a PUBLISHED PROPERTY, which `publishVBLState()` refreshes periodically and
which is therefore stale by design - the rule this project has written down
since 2sv and paid for again in 2xs. The tool then divided that
stale-bracketed counter delta by a FRESH wall-clock delta. The implied bracket
is **1.52 s of the 30.14 s window**, which is exactly a -5.0 % undercount. And
it scales with the publish interval measured in WALL time, which is why it
appeared at 60 Hz and not at 143.83 Hz, where the same staleness is a smaller
fraction of a faster count. Everything about the number was an artifact, and
2y7 escalated it to a hardware claim and then to a named cause (timer
coalescing) on the strength of it.

**Second defect in the same tool in two milestones.** 2y7 fixed animtest
dividing by a hardcoded 143.83; this one is a different error in the same
arithmetic - a mismatched TIME BASE rather than a mismatched rate - and the
first fix did not touch it. Rule 16 says the instrument is a suspect; what this
pair adds is that **fixing one bug in an instrument is not evidence about the
others**, and both of these inflated a result in the direction that made it
look worth reporting.

Fixed structurally rather than by correcting a number: `fbsnap()` now also
reads `RBFBVBLUptimeNs`, and every rate is counter-delta over
kext-uptime-delta **from the same ioreg pass**, so the staleness cancels in the
ratio instead of being charged to the framebuffer. Wall time is still printed
as the control, with the two compared explicitly and a loud marker when they
diverge by more than 3 % - so the next time the published counters lag, the
tool says so instead of inventing a defect.

**What this leaves standing from 2y7**, all of it independent of the bad
number: the corrected delivery figures (76.51 sets/s and 53.1 % of scanouts at
143.83 Hz against 54.58/s and 95.8 % at 60 Hz) came from `AmtrSets` and
`VBLFires` read in the SAME snapshot, so the stale bracket cancels in that
ratio - the 95.8 % is unaffected. The absolute sets/s figures carry the same
~5 % undercount at 60 Hz, so 54.58/s is really ~57.5/s, which moves nothing:
unique frames per second still FELL from 76.5 to 57.5, so the user's
"choppier" stands and its explanation stands. The ~76/s ceiling stands, and was
never this tool's measurement anyway.

Also now correct in `CLAUDE.md`: the frame-rate line said "not established
whether that is demand-limited or still gated", which 2xo had already answered
- 82/s with the hold against 112/s without it, recorded as the user's trade.

## 2z0 — the mode list is DERIVED from the panel, not written down (`D05FD4D9`)

The user's point, and it is the right one: 2y6 hardcoded one extra mode at
60 Hz, which is correct for a measurement and wrong for a driver. It would
offer 60 Hz on a 75 Hz panel and advertise 143.8 Hz on hardware that has never
run it. What a panel can do is three measured numbers - clk, H_TOTAL, V_TOTAL -
and every mode follows from them.

`rb_drr_build_modes()` in `rb_drr.h` builds the list; the hosttest decides it,
as everything in `src/common` must. Index 0 is always NATIVE and carries the
firmware's own V_TOTAL, which means *do not write the timing at all* - the one
thing worse than a mode that fails is a write that was never needed. Every
other entry is strictly slower, because V_TOTAL can only be LENGTHENED on a
live raster and nothing has established what any panel tolerates above its
native rate. The ladder is 120/100/90/75/60/50/48 and an entry appears only if
this panel can reach it.

Measured against three panel shapes in the hosttest:

    this panel (143.765 Hz)   native + 120/100/90/75/60/50/48   = 8 modes
    a 75 Hz panel             native +          60/50/48        = 4 modes
    a 60 Hz panel             native +             50/48        = 3 modes

The 75 Hz case is asserted explicitly, including that **nothing faster than
native is ever offered** - that is the defect the derivation exists to prevent.

**A design conflict the test caught before it shipped.** The first version
derived the native mode's advertised 16.16 rate like every other mode's. That
would have changed the advertised native refresh away from the `0x008fd53f` in
`.Display_boot`'s own live IOFBConfig, which every boot since 2sl has been read
against - and worse, it would be a DIFFERENT number every boot, because the
measured refresh moves ~0.05 % with DP spread-spectrum (2y6: 143843 against
143765). So `rb_drr_build_modes` takes the native rate as an argument, 0 meaning
derive, and the test asserts both paths AND that they differ. The derived clock
still drives every other mode's line count; only what native *advertises* is
the fixed constant.

**Modes the raster would refuse are dropped from the list rather than
advertised.** `modeSetup()` asks `rb_drr_check` per entry - the same question
`modeApply` will ask later - and keeps only those that pass. Rule 14: a refusal
a user can only discover by selecting the mode is indistinguishable from a bug.

**Native is a RESTORE, not a write.** `modeApply` on index 0 puts
MIN/MAX/CONTROL back to the values read at setup, CONTROL first, rather than
programming the native line count. The firmware set that timing before the kext
existed.

Two bugs found while wiring, both by the compiler rather than by a boot:
  - `setProperty("RBFBModeList", buf)` bound to the **bool** overload in the
    host shim, which would have published `1` for every string.
    `-Wpointer-bool-conversion` caught it; the real `IORegistryEntry` has a
    `(const char*, const char*)` overload and the shim now does too. A shim
    that is missing an overload does not fail - it silently picks another.
  - my own 75 Hz line count was 2166 by hand and **2165** by the code, and the
    assertion is the code's. Two line counts differ by 34 mHz of refresh.

Ids are now `kModeIDBase + index` and `modeIndexOf()` is the single place that
decides whether an id is ours, so the five query methods and `modeApply` cannot
disagree. Published: `RBFBModeListN`, `RBFBModeList` (lines@mHz per entry, so a
reading is checkable against its own inputs), `RBFBModeCurMhz`,
`RBFBModeCurLines`.

Control: forcing the native-rate override to be ignored fails exactly one
assertion, and restoring it passes.

Stated before the boot:
- `RBFBModeListN` **8** with `RBFBModeList` reading eight `lines@mHz` pairs,
  the first `1129@~143765` and the rest descending, is the list up. The 60 Hz
  entry's line count will be whatever THIS boot's clock gives - 2705 and 2707
  have both been measured - and a different value is not a finding.
- The Displays panel should now offer the whole ladder, not two entries.
- **75 Hz is the mode to try**, and it is also this session's open experiment:
  if throughput really caps near 76 frames/s, 75 Hz should be the first mode
  that is BOTH flicker-free and ~100 % fed, i.e. the best-looking desktop this
  machine can produce. `RBFBAmtrSets` against `RBFBVBLFires` in one animtest
  snapshot answers it.
- **120 Hz discriminates the two competing models** of the ceiling: an
  absolute ~76/s cap predicts ~76 sets/s and ~63 % fed, while a
  latch-phase/every-other-vblank defect predicts ~60/s and ~50 % fed. That
  distinction is what decides whether real 143.8 Hz is reachable at all, and
  it costs one mode selection rather than a boot.

## 2z1 — the mode list is up, and 60 Hz was a one-way door (boot 258)

**Boot 258 is the first boot of 2z0's derived mode list, and it both worked and
exposed a defect that the hosttest could not have caught as written.**

Identity first (rule 15): plugin `636F3584`, fb `D05FD4D9`, `rbgpu-boot` 258.

**The list is up and the derivation earned its keep.** `RBFBModeListN` 8,
`RBFBModeList` = `1129@143862 1354@119956 1624@100012 1805@89983 2166@74986
2707@60000 3248@50006 3384@47997`, and all eight are visible to CoreGraphics
(`tools/modeset.m`, new here) as ids 100..107. This boot measured the raster at
**143862** mHz against 143843 on boot 255 and 143765 on boot 256 - a 97 mHz
spread - giving `RBFBModeClkHz` **342 056 937** where the earlier boots derived
342 011 761 and 341 826 303. 143862 x 2106 x 1129 / 1000 re-derives that clock
exactly, and 2707 lines against it lands on **60000** mHz dead on where boot
256's clock gave 2705 lines. Three boots, three clocks, two different line
counts for the same requested 60 Hz: a hardcoded table would have been wrong on
at least two of the three.

**macOS remembered the mode across the reboot.** Nothing in the kext does this:
`RBFBModeCur` came up **105** with `ModeSwitches` 1 and `system_profiler`
independently reporting `1920 x 1080 @ 60.00Hz`. WindowServer restored the
user's last selection through `setDisplayMode` on its own. Worth recording
because it means **a mode selection is durable state the kext does not own**,
and a boot can therefore come up in a non-native mode before anything has
asked it to.

**The defect: every mode -> mode transition refused with RB_DRR_FW_DRR.**
Asking for 120 Hz moved `RBFBModeLastAsked` to 101 and `ModeApplies` 3 -> 4,
left `ModeCur` at 105, and set `ModeRefuse` **2**. The Displays panel refused
identically (`ModeApplies` -> 5), and CoreGraphics snapped its own idea of the
current mode back to 105. So 60 Hz was the last mode the boot could reach, and
with WindowServer restoring 60 Hz at login the machine came up already inside
the trap.

The cause is one argument. `modeApply` re-reads `V_TOTAL_CONTROL` live, which
is right (rule 41), and then passed that live value to `rb_drr_check`, which
refuses any non-zero CONTROL on the grounds that the firmware must own DRR and
the restore values are therefore unknown. That reasoning is correct for the
FIRST write and false for every one after it, because **our own arming is what
makes CONTROL non-zero**: `rb_drr_ctl_on(0)` = 3, and the check then reads our
own SEL bits as a stranger's. The precondition had become its own violation.

Two separate things were wrong and both are fixed:

1. `rb_drr_check_owned(htotal, vtotal, ctl, ctl0, lines)` takes the live value
   AND the setup snapshot. If the live value is `ctl0` or exactly
   `rb_drr_ctl_on(ctl0)`, the restore values are known and the decision is the
   one `ctl0` implies; anything else is a third party and still refuses. The
   refusal the check exists for survives - including a boot whose firmware
   really does own DRR (`ctl0 != 0` refuses from either state) and a PARTIAL
   arming (MAX_SEL alone is not ours).
2. The live CONTROL is now read only to be **checked**, never built on.
   `modeApply` writes `rb_drr_ctl_on(modeCtl0)` and restores `modeCtl0` on a
   lost write. Using the live value as the write base is how arming became its
   own precondition, and the setup snapshot is the only value that can put the
   firmware's timing back.

**Why the hosttest passed 2z0.** `modeSetup` filters the ladder with
`rb_drr_check(htotal, vtotal, modeCtl0, lines)` - the BOOT snapshot, which is
0 - and the test exercised that call. `modeApply` uses the live register. The
two call sites disagreed about which value they meant and the test only ever
saw the one that was right. The new cases assert the old call and the new one
on identical inputs, so the regression is stated rather than described, and the
control confirms they discriminate: breaking `rb_drr_check_owned` to delegate
with the live value fails exactly the three mode -> mode assertions while
**"native -> mode still passes" stays green**.

**`tools/modeset.m` (new).** `modeset` lists what CoreGraphics reports with the
current mode marked, `modeset <hz>` selects the nearest. Pure userspace
CoreGraphics, no kext and no reboot. It earned itself immediately: it is what
showed `CGCompleteDisplayConfiguration` returning success over a mode change
that never happened - rule 13 on an Apple API, and the reason the first 120 Hz
`animtest` run of this boot is a 60 Hz measurement wearing a 120 Hz label.

**The 60 Hz baseline for this boot** (the only honest number taken so far):
52.87 amtr sets/s, **88.2 % of scanouts fed**, 1809 VBL fires at 60.00/s
against 60.00 asked. The time base now agrees with wall clock to +0.02 % over
30 s, so 2y9's fix holds and animtest can be believed.

**Still open and now actually reachable: the 120 Hz discriminator.** Nothing
below has been measured, because no 120 Hz measurement exists yet.
- An absolute ~76 frames/s cap predicts ~76 sets/s and ~63 % fed at 120 Hz.
- A latch-phase defect - flips missing the vblank latch window and landing on
  the next one - predicts ~60/s and ~50 % fed.
That number decides whether genuine 143.8 Hz is reachable at all. 75 Hz is the
other mode worth a run: if the cap model holds it should be the first mode both
flicker-free and ~100 % fed.

fbkext `D669FE2E-DEFD-3D2E-A7AD-0F0A4A9883EF`. Needs a boot.
